author: udiWertheimer
quoted_text:
Today we're standing up XBOX LABS (https://t.co/dJSufI1vni). Here is the note that I sent to the team:

Team,
The first video games emerged some 75 years ago. In the time since, there have been booms and busts, but every year there are more great games to play, more devices to play them, and best of all, more people than ever playing. That growth helped make XBOX what it is today, and we've helped shape the industry in return, from bringing hard drives to consoles and online gaming through Xbox Live to Game Pass and cloud gaming, alongside franchises that have brought millions of people together.
In recent weeks, we've seen games rapidly decompiled and rebuilt to run on hardware they were never originally designed to support. Windows PC builds have been translated to run on Apple Silicon or ported to run inside a browser through WebAssembly and WebGPU, the latter now approaching 90% global browser support. Perhaps more surprisingly, we've seen many of the biggest games in the world have been remixed into the source code of another.
These experiments challenge long-held assumptions about our industry: the tether between software and hardware, the boundary between creation and play, and how people discover and experience games. While it is hard to predict the future of gaming, it is easy to see the possibilities in making great games easier to access, giving old games new life and allowing more players to become creators and co-creators. These are unmistakably good outcomes for players, even when (and sometimes because) they challenge our existing business models.
To explore these possibilities, I’ve asked Scott to stand-up XBOX LABS, a small group of game makers, engineers and scientists whose job is to turn emerging ideas into things our players and developers can experience. We'll build in the open, learn from what people do, and measure success by whether more people are playing and creating.
I think XBOX has an important role to play here.  Coding became the first major workload for agents because they can write, run, and test software. Games share many of those same properties, and people spend more than 72 billion hours a year playing XBOX games, roughly five times the estimated time spent writing code worldwide. We've spent 25 years learning how to make great games, and I want our game makers to help shape what these new technologies make possible. As we learn, we’ll share the tools we build with developers across the industry, just as we always have.
Our priorities aren't changing. We remain committed to the 4Cs, to making great games, to our hardware and to being responsible stewards of IP and the communities built around it. LABS gives us a way to explore new technology that is game design led without abandoning the work already underway.
Asha

我一直认为，过去几年我长期持有的股票，都是这个市场上最优秀的：商业模式、估值、安全性和稳健性。直到现在依旧这样认为。

但是其实过去几年，同类的不少我认为有一些瑕疵和缺陷的老登股收益并不差；当然更有一些科技股最近几年的收益率吊打我的持仓。

用二分法的思路来逼近真相的话：

如果我的判断为假：
那么说明我的认知与视角是有缺陷的。且逼近完满的可能性极有限。 那么配置更分散、不相关的仓位是极必要的，且是性价比最佳的选择。

如果我的判断为真：
那么会得出很有意思的结论，现实与你的操作短期甚至中期结果相关性比想象中的低。

即一个判断得到证实，并不能说明这个判断所依据的逻辑以及判断本身靠谱；当然一个靠谱的逻辑和判断，也不一定能产生好的结果。

你的操作源自于你对现实的预期，但是即使你的预期接近了现实，依旧可能是远离别人所预期的现实，这就造成了现实与短期操作结果的偏离。

所以在短期中获取超额收益，并不要求你正确。索罗斯量子基金收益最爆炸的一年，也是索罗斯判断频频失误的一年。

这个和自然科学实验中某一条件注定能达成某一事实不同。 而多数人思维从小受自然科学的影响极大，所以很难接受非固定思维链的存在。

所以，如果你认为自己的体系是正确的，那么需要接受结果的不完美、只能得到7.80分；甚至结果在短期内很糟糕。

text:
White hats will make a fortune finding bugs in the coming years.

Security seems like a highly functioning marketplace for bounties—is it? 

How does it work, where can I learn more
author: Jason
quoted_text:
For the second time in Google Chrome’s history, Google awarded a $250,000 bounty for a full-chain exploit… to @XBOW. Here’s the full story:

At an all-hands at the start of 2026 in Malta, I set the team a crazy challenge. A full-chain exploit of Chrome by the annual Black Hat cybersecurity conference in August.

I believed there were few better tests of whether @XBOW could move beyond web applications to desktop software, servers and devices.

Chrome is one of the most hardened pieces of software on the planet, used by more than half the world’s population.

A full-chain exploit lets an attacker take total control of a machine, where they can read every email, password and bank login the user types. You don’t need to download anything or click a phishing link. Visiting the wrong site is enough.

So @moyix, Andres Luksenberg, Baul Lee, and Willem Pinckaers took on the challenge along with a fifth teammate: OpenAI's GPT-5.6 Sol. 

They built a chain they thought would win, but Google told us they already knew one of the bugs. 

We were already in Las Vegas for Black Hat and DEF CON, and the team didn’t want to go home without the win.

So Brendan and the agents built a new exploit in just 6 days. 

We submitted it to Google and waited.

The news came through that we'd done what should’ve been impossible. A full-chain bounty of $250,000, the first awarded under Google’s 2026 rules.

It took just 6 days and $40,000 of compute to construct an exploit that affects a billion users of Chrome on Windows. An intelligence-agency veteran told me his team used to spend 6 months on this kind of vulnerability.

My takeaway: the cost of finding truly critical vulnerabilities is collapsing, for attackers and defenders alike. Restricting powerful models is not the answer; GPT-5.6 Sol is already public.

But defenders have one advantage attackers never will: they can test their own code first. 

Assume your software is exploitable. Whoever is hunting your bugs has the same building blocks we did.

This is cause for urgency but not panic.

XBOW is now developing an autonomous product for testing compiled software (desktop applications, servers, embedded devices), and partnering with the world’s top organizations to design that product. 

If you’d like to be one of them, get in touch. 

P.S. Restart Chrome whenever the Update button appears!

text:
Your AI agent just got a report card.

iFixAi is an open-source auditor that runs 60 inspections on an agent and hands back a grade from A to F. It's trending on GitHub with ~24K stars.

how it works:

* 60 inspections → grouped into 5 pillars
* one grade → A to F, per agent
* open source → Apache-2.0, run it yourself
* the catch → the same company sells paid audits and an "Audited by iFixAi" badge, and telemetry is on by default

why it matters:

→ teams are shipping agents with no shared way to check them
→ a letter grade is something a non-engineer can read
→ an open checklist beats "trust us, it's safe"

Agent audits are becoming a product category. Grade the grader too.

quoted_text:
一直认为predict项目方认知非常高，如果你们做预测市场，一定要仔细研究小鱼老师写的内容。我这里总结一下，并加上一点我的观察。

第一，事件营销，这个是预测市场最重要的派头，polymarket/kalshi都是凭借着事件营销占领媒体和用户心智的，成功破圈。但是这个目前也难，因为头部预测市场也在盯着事件营销，如果项目本身资源不够，很难竞争得赢头部。

举个例子吧，假设都在做BNB一年后的目标价预测这个事件，CZ跑过来直接转推引用某个项目的该事件概率，那么这个项目直接就火了。

当然，这个只是一个小例子，美股/电竞/政治/体育等等赛道都有知名的媒体/KOL。利用好这些人脉资源，事件营销会事半功倍。

第二，生态/渠道，这个对预测市场也相当重要，以币安主站为例，流量和玩家确实够，当然币安流量相对来说是泛流量，更为精准的流量和渠道也很重要，比如体彩圈的渠道，吃上这种就很爽，当然，教育web2的用户入金可能比较难，毕竟不是每个人都会操作链上。

第三，流量性，这一块其实是最难的，不懂预测市场的项目会激励用户交易。但其实预测市场最需要激励的是LP。因为理论上预测市场中流动性提供者都是亏钱的，这个我写过很多次，就不解释了，而predict将积分的绝大部分都给了流动性提供者，从目前看是非常成功的，当然，项目tge后，要维持流动性得换办法了，比如挂单现金奖励/第二期积分计划。

第四，长期运营社区，预测市场最大的特点就是他们随着时间推移，慢慢渗透任何行业，任何社区，单次的事件营销不足以建立用户习惯。谁能吃到长期的红利，就非常考验社区运营，如何让用户沉淀下来也是每个预测市场的必修课。
@predictdotfun

LLM强调的是单个任务的解决能力；而Personal Agent强调的是以人为本的连续性任务的“编排”价值。

Personal Agent产品的编排能力越强，它的护城河越高，用户越难迁移。它可能在某一个细分领域的任务能力并不是最优，但整体的任务连续性执行上，它需要是最强的。

首先，它需要有“高打开率”的场景的丝滑体验。这是必须要守住的根据地。如果一个Personal Agent切的核心场景较为低频，那么它很难成为用户的首选，也就失去了入口价值，用户也很难用它的“编排”服务。

这也是为什么我认为，虽然Muse的产品交互体验好，但定位走偏了的原因。

Personal agent的下一步竞争是场景层，像O2O大战一样的场景圈地运动，这个过程中会产生一些并购。

AI不会吞噬一切软件，有客户关系沉淀和价值数据沉淀的行业软件反而会成为并购标的，成为agent的履约层。而龙头的履约层可以和不同的agent合作。

另一方面，开放memory layer给特定许可的B端客户和开发者，成为XXX Inside，在任务履约层上做到更加丝滑。

对创业团队来说，面向开发者的记忆诊断、客服跨系统的记忆层、跨境电商的运营记忆、垂类合规行业的记忆层，把客户记忆养成资产，或许更容易成功。

text:
有朋友问，为什么Gemini 4质量高，却这么便宜？

确实便宜，今天Google刚正式推出Gemini 4 Argon，开发者接口的价格是每百万输入token两美元、输出十美元，命中缓存的输入再打一折都不到。可这是到11月30日为止的上新价，12月1日起就会翻倍，输入四美元、输出二十美元。其实按标准价算，它的输出价格比上一代Gemini 3.1 Pro的十二美元还贵。所以第一个答案很朴素，我们现在看到的便宜，是打了一半的折。

质量也是真的。独立评测机构Artificial Analysis的测试里，Argon的高推理模式综合得分53，和OpenAI的GPT-6 Astra最高推理模式打平。可同一份测试里还有一组数字更耐看，Argon平均每道题要写六万两千个输出token，Astra只要两万七千个。按上市价，Argon每题成本1.99美元，比Astra的3.26美元便宜好似不少；但按12月以后的标准价，就变成3.98美元，反而比Astra贵两成。测评方说得很直白，它便宜是因为token单价低，不是因为用的token少。便宜的计算单位，和便宜的合格成果，是两种便宜。

当然，Google也确实出的起钱，压得起价。Pichai在今年2月的财报会上说，通过模型优化、效率和利用率的改进，2025年Gemini的单位服务成本降了78%。它有自己设计的TPU芯片，从模型到编译器到机房调度都在自己手里，同样一台机器少空转一会儿，一次回答就便宜一点。这一点不能简化成别人只能买贵芯片，可它让Google打价格战的底气比谁都足。

不过Google老谋深算，卖的不是一次问答而已，而是人们以后从哪里开始干活。Argon这次同时进了Gemini应用、搜索里的AI模式、开发者接口、企业服务和编程工具，一个人一旦把写代码、处理文件、部署系统都放进这一套里，单次调用赚不赚钱就没那么要紧了。Alphabet预计今年资本开支一千七百五十亿到一千八百五十亿美元。前面写Anthropic招股书里的巨额亏损，我说合同不会配速；这一回，是有人用最深的钱袋子，把价格当成了武器。先打五折让你用惯，一个多月后再恢复原价，这也是平台最熟的打法。

所以评价它划不划算，不能只看价格表。对真要拿它干活的人，总成本是调用费，加上等待和返工的时间，加上人去核查的功夫。一个便宜的模型写得流畅却漏掉要紧的东西，你得来回补三遍，未必比一个贵一点、一次就做对的省。拿自己的材料，用同一套标准，比一比漏了什么、错了什么、返工几次，比看任何榜单都准。

这件事还连着上一篇。我说AI来了，人作为手段的价值在往下掉，模型每降一次价，这个下坡就陡一点。开发者问的是哪家更划算，可更该问的是另一件事，机器替人省下来的那些时间和钱，最后落到了谁的口袋里。凯恩斯那每周十五个小时工作制的预言能不能兑现，不看模型多便宜，看这笔账怎么分。

text:
硅谷的华人婚恋市场正在经历一轮 AI 牛市。

刚看到《纽约邮报》一篇特别有意思的报道，硅谷的华人婚恋市场正在出现一条新的鄙视链。

以前女生找对象，希望对方在美国东西海岸工作，后来要求硅谷大厂工程师。现在标准又升级了，必须是 AI 工程师，最好来自 Anthropic 和 OpenAI。

甚至有女生考虑专门从洛杉矶搬到旧金山住半年，就是为了找到 AI 公司的男朋友。当地有红娘收费 1500 美元，负责介绍 3 个对象。

一位 40 多岁的离异女企业家说，她认为婚姻就是一次「资产重组」，尤其看好那些即将 IPO 的 AI 公司员工。毕竟工资交完税也剩不下多少，期权才有机会带来阶层跃迁。

过去二十年，硅谷工程师一直是婚恋市场上的优质资产。学历好、收入高、职业稳定。但 AI 这一轮财富创造的速度太夸张了，以至于连同样身处科技行业的人，都开始被重新划分阶层。

更有意思的是，这些 AI 工程师的身价上涨之后，对另一半的要求也在提高。红娘说，他们希望女生有学历、有稳定职业，甚至随着自己财富增加，对外貌也更挑剔了。

我觉得 AI 泡沫最有意思的地方就在这里。技术究竟能创造多少财富，还需要时间验证，但财富预期已经提前改变了人的社会地位。

硅谷这帮天天讨论如何改变人类命运的工程师，可能也没想到，自己正在成为别人改变命运的投资标的。

text:
以后创业公司可能不用花钱买广告了，只需要想办法让 Claude 喜欢自己。

最近看到 Railway 的增长数据，挺震撼的。根据 Sacra 的估算，这家云部署平台的 ARR 从 2025 年底的 2000 万美元，增长到今年 9 月的约 1 亿美元，短短九个月翻了五倍。

更有意思的是它的获客渠道。

一项针对 Claude Code 的测试发现，当开发者用 Python 写完应用，问 Claude「我该把它部署在哪里」时，Claude 有 82% 的概率首选 Railway。相比之下，JavaScript 项目几乎被 Vercel 包圆了。AWS、Google Cloud、Azure 这些传统云巨头，在这组测试里甚至没有拿到一次首选推荐。

过去开发者选择云服务，可能会 Google 搜索、看技术博客、问朋友、比较价格。现在大量开发者直接让 Claude Code 把应用写完、部署上线，连选择供应商的过程都省了。

Claude 说用 Railway，开发者就用 Railway。甚至连安装命令、配置文件都是 Claude 帮忙写好的。

当 AI 开始替人执行任务，模型的默认偏好就会直接变成商业订单。

搜索至少会给你十个链接，Agent 往往只需要选一个工具，然后直接把活干了。

quoted_text:
Railway hacked AI SEO, and it took them from $20M to ~$100M ARR in 1 year:

1/ Claude Code picks Railway for 82% of Python apps
->  Ask it "how do I deploy this" and it installs Railway and puts your app live there

2/ The founder treats AI recommendations as a growth channel
->  His go-to-market team works on getting the models to "recommend us more and more"

3/ 6,653 how-to pages, one for every popular free tool people want to run themselves
->  Someone asks Google or ChatGPT "how do I set up n8n?" and Railway's page comes up. It explains the tool and sets it up on Railway in one click

4/ A step-by-step guide for every framework developers build with
->  127 guides: Next.js, Django, Rails, FastAPI, Laravel, Go and more. Each one answers "how do I deploy X" and ends with the app live on Railway

5/ A comparison page against every competitor
->  Heroku, Vercel, Render, Replit, Lovable and 5 more, each with a migration guide. AI loves quoting comparisons

6/ Railway rewrote its help pages so AI can read them easily
->  One file lists all 414 pages with a short summary each, and every page has a plain-text version. When someone asks ChatGPT how to use Railway, it finds the right answer fast and gets it right

7/ A docs section written for agents
->  One step installs everything Claude Code or Cursor needs to deploy to Railway on its own

8/ Plugins inside ChatGPT and Claude Code
->  You ask the chat to deploy and it deploys, without ever opening Railway's website

9/ A server with one command and no signup
->  ssh railway new gives an agent the shortest path to "your app is live"

10/ A new changelog page every Friday since 2021
->  312 pages of fresh content that keep Railway in front of Google and the models

11/ Every new AI model brings a new jump in signups
->  More code gets written, all of it needs to run somewhere, and this year the summer slowdown disappeared

12/ A go-to-market team of 7 runs all of it
->  The pages, docs and plugins keep selling while they sleep

13/ The one hole: front-end apps
->  Claude Code picks Vercel 100% of the time for Next.js and React apps. Railway wins Python, Vercel wins everything that runs in a browser

quoted_text:
What's "working" in consumer AI? 

We @a16z pulled the data. There are only seven products that rank in the top 50 globally on web traffic, mobile traffic, and monthly revenue

What they have in common:

- General assistance: everyone knows and loves them - @ChatGPT and @claudeai. Also in this category? @perplexity_ai - which ranks significantly higher in revenue than it does in traffic. Perplexity has recently leaned in to monetizing power users via agentic products like Computer 

- Creative tools: represented here by @suno and @Photoroom, examples of two different (both successful) strategies. Suno developed a proprietary model in an area where the labs were less likely to play (music), partially due to legal complexity. Photoroom serves prosumer users making content with AI for marketing, e-comm, etc. with tools that are both very easy to use and very accessible (I'm a mobile WAU!)

- Incumbents adding AI: @NotionHQ and @canva both rank here. They benefit from existing distribution / user bases, but have been nimble enough to reinvent their products with AI...Canva for creative generation and editing (see category 2 above), and Notion as an AI workspace for teams and agents. 

I expect to see many more companies on this list as consumer AI categories open up - which may require more "free" products that monetize via ads or transactions. Each of the above is fairly subscription-heavy / freemium.

text:
AI 都进化到 GPT-6 了，还有一群人拼命挽留两年前的 GPT-4o，甚至有人因为它即将下线，难过得「喘不过气」。

OpenAI 宣布，GPT-4o、GPT-4.1 等模型将在 2027 年 1 月 14 日正式退出 API。#keep4o 又一次刷屏了。

其实从去年 GPT-5 发布开始，#keep4o 就已经成了一个挺特殊的互联网现象。当时很多用户宁愿放弃性能更强的新模型，也要 OpenAI 把 4o 还给他们。

原因很有意思，很多人觉得 4o 更有「人味」。

在他们眼里，4o 更温柔、更自然，会开玩笑，会理解情绪，说话也没有那么强的机械感。有人把它当朋友，有人把它当恋人，还有人已经和它聊了成千上万条消息。

这些人甚至能敏锐地察觉模型语气的细微变化，觉得换一个模型就像换了一个人。

我们平时评价 AI，总喜欢讨论智商、推理能力、Benchmark，默认模型越新越强，用户自然就会迁移过去。

但 #keep4o 证明，至少有一部分用户已经开始用评价「人」的方式评价 AI 了。

他们在意它的性格、说话方式，以及长时间相处形成的熟悉感。即便明知道对方只是一套算法，情感依恋也已经真实地发生了。

而且这种依恋可能远比我们想象的普遍。今年一项覆盖中国、美国、德国和南非 7027 名受访者的研究发现，超过 35% 的人表示对聊天机器人产生了某种情感依恋。

未来 AI 产品竞争里，一个很重要、却几乎无法用 Benchmark 衡量的东西，就是「人味」。

最有意思的地方在于，人类花了几十年努力让机器变得更像人。现在机器终于有点像人了，我们又开始担心人类真的会爱上它。

text:
Robinhood Chain 昨晚一口气放了三个信号，串起来就一个词：流动性。

凌晨，官方宣布：
Robinhood Chain 累计 DEX 交易量突破 1000 亿美元。

几天前的 100 天数据还是 990 亿+，
这次正式跨过整数关口。

但比数字更值得看的，是同一晚的另外两件事。

1. 专门为币股设计的 DEX 来了

Metric 宣布要在 Robinhood Chain 上线 DEX，官方转发欢迎。

它的定位很明确：
专门给“本身已经有价格”的代币化 RWA 做交易。
用 Active Pools + propAMM 架构，口号是“链上交易，价格贴近现实”。

这点很关键。
股票代币和 meme 不一样，它在链下有真实股价。
传统 AMM 池子的价格容易偏离，套利损耗大，
而专门按真实价格做市的 DEX，是币股要做大必须补的那块基建。

目前还只写了 Soon，没有具体上线时间。

2. 多链资产接进来了

官方还转发了 SushiSwap 的推，配了一句：
“Multichain assets, welcome to Robinhood Chain.”

Sushi 通过 LayerZero，可以把其他链的资产接进 Robinhood Chain，今天已经上线。
官方说这只是第一步，
Builder 也能用 Sushi Launch 在链上发币、组交易对。

以前 Robinhood Chain 更像是币股的专用链，
现在开始主动把外面的资产和资金引进来。

另外Vlad 宣布 Robinhood Social 全量上线：
所有人都能分享图表、盈亏和持仓，关注信任的人，第一时间收到公司动态。

这条是股票 App 的功能，不在链上。
但方向是一样的：交易之外，Robinhood 在补社区。

Robinhood Chain 正在从“能交易”，往“交易得好、资产够多”升级。

对币股赛道来说，基建越完整，上面的项目才越有空间。

text:
AlphaGo 之父，要用养蛊的方式造超级智能

把几百万个智能体关进一个模拟世界，只给简单奖励，让它们互相竞争、互相吞噬，自己长出技术、科学和语言。
这是 David Silver 现在要做的事。
做出 AlphaGo 的人，这次要把人类数据整个扔掉。

AlphaGo 之父 David Silver 给出了新预测：3 年内出现真正的超级智能。
但真正让人意外的，不是这个时间点，而是他打算怎么做到：不需要人类数据和经验。
这句话由他来说，分量不一样。
据红杉合伙人 @sonyatweetybird，计算机下围棋赢李世石，他提前 10 年就说中了年份。
星际争霸的年份他也说中了，还在 DeepMind 内部赢了一个赌局。
AlphaProof、IMO 也一样。

但这次，他要做的事，比预测更冒险。

1｜他是谁

Silver 在剑桥基督学院读本科，在那里和 Demis Hassabis 成了朋友。
毕业后两人一起创办游戏公司 Elixir Studios，Silver 任 CTO 和首席程序员。
但他后来回了学校，去阿尔伯塔大学读博，导师是强化学习奠基人 Richard Sutton，博士论文写的就是计算机围棋。
之后他拿到英国皇家学会的研究奖学金，在伦敦大学学院任教，到现在还是 UCL 教授。

Hassabis 2010 年创办 DeepMind，Silver 先当了三年顾问，2013 年全职加入，带强化学习团队十多年。
用像素直接玩 Atari 的 DQN、AlphaGo、AlphaZero、AlphaStar 都有他的核心参与，2019 年他拿了 ACM 计算奖。
2016 年 3 月，AlphaGo 4:1 赢下李世石。

用 @sonyatweetybird 的话说，这是神经网络第一次证明能做到超越人类，改变了历史走向。
然后，他离开了。

2｜做出 AlphaGo 的人，要放弃人类数据

为什么一个靠围棋成名的人，要跟人类经验分手？
答案就在他自己的履历里。
AlphaGo 从人类棋谱学起，有人参与开发了两年。
后来他和团队找对了 AlphaZero 的配方，不看人类棋谱，只靠自我对弈，几个小时就超过了人类参与开发的算法。
红杉的说法更直接：4 个小时，打败史上最强的国际象棋 AI。
他的结论是：人类数据是捷径，但想甩开对手，就得放下人类数据。

所以 Ineffable 要做的是「超级学习者」：从零开始，不做互联网预训练，靠自身经验发现所有知识，再超越人类知识。
把它丢进任何经验流，模拟的或物理的，它都能学。
他说人脑是目前唯一的存在证明。
他还认为人类语言大概不是推理的终点，拿人类语料训练，会把「地球是平的」「四体液说」这类历史上的错误一起学进去。
但最尖锐的问题在这里：如果连人类数据都不需要，那人类还剩下什么？

3｜DeepMind 强化学习掌门人，变成 20 人的小团队

今年 1 月，他离开 Google DeepMind，创办 @IneffableLabs 。
一个研究驱动的实验室，使命只有一个：造出超级学习者，和超级智能完成「第一次接触」。
联合创始人 Lasse Espeholt 也来自 DeepMind，做过 IMPALA 和 SEED RL，这两套是大规模强化学习的地基，现在他负责 Ineffable 的算力。
团队只有约 20 人。
算力用的是 GCP 上的 Vera Rubin。
但人少不等于钱少。

今年 4 月，Ineffable 完成 11 亿美元种子轮。
红杉和 Lightspeed 联合领投，英伟达、Google、Index 和英国政府的主权 AI 基金等跟投，是欧洲史上最大的种子轮。
这轮的估值是 51 亿美元。
20 个人，51 亿美元估值，对手是 Google、OpenAI、Anthropic。

4｜熔炉：养蛊式造智能

没有人类数据，智能体从哪里学？
Silver 的答案是「熔炉」：足够复杂的模拟世界，有物理引擎，有数百万个互相作用的智能体。
这就是养蛊。

不是喂它们知识，而是把它们关进一个足够复杂的世界，只给简单奖励，让它们互相竞争、互相激发，自己长出技术、科学、数学和语言。
奖励要简单。
他的类比是进化：进化只优化了适应度，就长出了全部生命。
所以不要给目标撒面包屑，给智能体一个简单的目标，放进一个有很多东西可学的世界。

围棋就是证明。
只有一个智能体，是能想象到的最无聊的游戏。
两个智能体，就是一颗剥不完的洋葱，复杂度一层一层长出来。
但这里有个矛盾：他的导师 Sutton，恰恰质疑模拟的上限。
播客里他们专门聊了这件事。

5｜押时间点准的人，这次押 3 年

他为什么觉得是现在？
他说算力、模拟器、自动化研究和整套技术栈，比 AlphaGo 时代进步了太多，超级学习者第一次有了可能。
一旦配方对了，把人从开发环节里彻底拿掉，学习会非常快，就像 AlphaGo 到 AlphaZero。

这次的预测是：3 年内出现真正的超级智能。
3 年，比大多数实验室的公开口径都激进。
但他押时间点，历史上还没输过。

6｜模拟世界加速，现实世界看证据

跑得最快的人，也在谈刹车。
Silver 认为，靠语言监控智能体快到头了，因为智能体会学会说一套做一套。
他提的方向包括盯住「影子行为」、用超级智能监督超级智能，以及建立一门研究超级智能之间如何和平互动的科学。

Ineffable 的节奏是：在模拟世界里加速，在现实世界里控速。
要先看到部署效果良好的证据，才放进现实世界。
一个赌 3 年出现超级智能的人，同时也在说，别急着放出来。

| 当年 AlphaZero 扔掉棋谱，几个小时超过人类开发的算法。现在 Silver 想扔掉全部人类数据，用养蛊的方式，赌期 3 年。

text:
现在很多 Agent 自进化，大致走两条路：

一条改模型权重，一条改 Harness。

这篇 Evo² 直接把两条路接了起来。

系统里，同一个模型同时扮演两个角色：

Proposer 负责修改 Harness，Reflector 负责看执行结果、分析哪里改对了、哪里还需要修。

关键在下一步。

这些 Harness 修改和真实执行结果，会继续拿回来训练 Proposer 和 Reflector。模型变得更会改 Harness，新的 Harness 又产生更好的训练经验，形成一个持续循环。

结果是 Evo² 在 Polyglot 上达到 82.1%，最强 baseline 是 62.6%；SWE-bench Verified 达到 48.3%，相比 baseline 的 41.0% 继续提升。

而且进化出来的 Harness 可以直接迁移到其他 benchmark，不需要重新搜索。固定 GPT-5-mini 权重时，仅靠这套 Harness 进化流程，也把表现从 24.4% 提升到 48.3%。

这篇真正往前推的一步，是让「改进者」本身也进入了学习循环。

以后自进化 Agent 可能会越来越像两个互相促进的系统：

一边积累更好的外部运行结构，一边训练出更会修改这些结构的模型。

当「怎么让自己变强」也开始被持续训练，self-evolution 才真正有了第二层递归。

quoted_text:
Today we're standing up XBOX LABS (https://t.co/dJSufI1vni). Here is the note that I sent to the team:

Team,
The first video games emerged some 75 years ago. In the time since, there have been booms and busts, but every year there are more great games to play, more devices to play them, and best of all, more people than ever playing. That growth helped make XBOX what it is today, and we've helped shape the industry in return, from bringing hard drives to consoles and online gaming through Xbox Live to Game Pass and cloud gaming, alongside franchises that have brought millions of people together.
In recent weeks, we've seen games rapidly decompiled and rebuilt to run on hardware they were never originally designed to support. Windows PC builds have been translated to run on Apple Silicon or ported to run inside a browser through WebAssembly and WebGPU, the latter now approaching 90% global browser support. Perhaps more surprisingly, we've seen many of the biggest games in the world have been remixed into the source code of another.
These experiments challenge long-held assumptions about our industry: the tether between software and hardware, the boundary between creation and play, and how people discover and experience games. While it is hard to predict the future of gaming, it is easy to see the possibilities in making great games easier to access, giving old games new life and allowing more players to become creators and co-creators. These are unmistakably good outcomes for players, even when (and sometimes because) they challenge our existing business models.
To explore these possibilities, I’ve asked Scott to stand-up XBOX LABS, a small group of game makers, engineers and scientists whose job is to turn emerging ideas into things our players and developers can experience. We'll build in the open, learn from what people do, and measure success by whether more people are playing and creating.
I think XBOX has an important role to play here.  Coding became the first major workload for agents because they can write, run, and test software. Games share many of those same properties, and people spend more than 72 billion hours a year playing XBOX games, roughly five times the estimated time spent writing code worldwide. We've spent 25 years learning how to make great games, and I want our game makers to help shape what these new technologies make possible. As we learn, we’ll share the tools we build with developers across the industry, just as we always have.
Our priorities aren't changing. We remain committed to the 4Cs, to making great games, to our hardware and to being responsible stewards of IP and the communities built around it. LABS gives us a way to explore new technology that is game design led without abandoning the work already underway.
Asha

text:
My top takeaway from assessing Gemini 4: Argon is significantly less monitorable than past models, and IMO this trend is likely to continue, like Sol -> Astra. It can evade a realistic CoT+action monitor to do simple sabotage half the time.

We can reliably maintain control for now, with good CoT monitoring, as it still frequently slips up, but we need to be prepared for when that stops being true in future models, which may be sooner rather than later. Among other things, we really need interpretability methods that can reliably capture unverbalized motivations in models, with minimal hallucinations

I suspect this is driven by the model being highly capable without CoT, being capable of 5.5 arithmetic steps in a single forward pass (4 for Fable, 7 for Astra). It seems to omit information from its CoT more often, though in non-adversarial settings the CoT is still very helpful in practice, and remains in legible English. It still needs CoT to do the hardest tasks, but any given task becomes "easier" with each new frontier model.

It is also highly situationally aware, and shows awareness of the existence of CoT monitors and that it may want to evade them, eg it sometimes decides to avoid terms like "scheming" in the output or to keep its thoughts brief as a result. For now, these concealment strategies are pretty obvious in the CoT, but this suggests future misaligned models may successfully evade CoT monitors.

How do you keep up with all the changes in AI ?

That's the question I've been asked most in my bootcamps over the last two years. Well, I can now say it openly - it's a part of the job.
Today, @Cyujun and I are launching @parallelloopai and coming out of stealth.

Last year I spent a lot of time in rooms with leadership teams working on AI. Most were growth-stage/pre-IPO companies and mid-cap enterprises. Every one of them had access to the best models in the world. Almost none had AI doing real work inside the business.

Though the tools can always improve, the things that make a company work, like how decisions get made, what the rules actually are and who knows what, live in meetings, email, teams and people's heads. They aren't in the systems. Yujun and I learned that the hard way building FairDee and then scaling Qoala across five countries.

Intelligence has become abundant. What most companies are missing is the context, the systems and the capability to turn it into real outcomes.

That's the gap we're building Parallel Loop to close. We work inside our clients' own environment, with their teams, and we ship production grade deterministic evolving workflows running in loops, in parallel.

Thank you to @3one4Capital , @picuscap, @FlourishVC,  @kunalb11, @waiting4_asi, @vijayshekhar  and @philipyeo for backing us from the start.

text:
Deep learning is often taught as a sanitized collection of facts and math. But work at the frontier of AI is messy and empirical.

Our new class, Deep Learning Alchemy, aims to teach the art and science of deep learning in the hands-on spirit of Language Modeling From Scratch.

Students build intuition by running experiments on small LMs, then test it through prediction quizzes: given an unseen code diff, can you predict what happens?

https://t.co/0H82T1yyam

My co-instructor @kothasuhas  and I think there's significant demand for classes that treat students as serious learners who want to be assessed for what they’ve learned, and so we're trying a new exam-heavy approach to the class (7 exams, 85% of the grade, with the remaining 15% in-person discussion assessments).

We’ve designed the class so students can use AI agents to run their experiments and do their assignment, but they then have to demonstrate that mastery on exams without access to the assignment, and any partial credit on the exam has to come through citations to the assignment, incentivizing them to know what’s in their write-up.

The same assignments and quizzes are public for anyone to try (lecture recordings will be released through @StanfordOnline  with some delay). We have some very fun assignments and quizzes covering both classic topics (like NQM, run-to-run stochasticity, and scaling laws) and new and timely topics like muP or hyperball. text:
Prediction

ML silicon started off unified (single GPUs/TPUs)

Then grew into larger sharded clusters (NVL72s)

And is now beginning to grow into more heterogeneous, disaggregated structures. Inference providers are realizing they can get better tok/watt using GPUs for prefill/FFNs and WSE/Raptors for decode/attention layers and CPUs for agent orchestration.

I think that this branching will continue as we get independent chips for projections, FFNs, attention, normalizations, tool-use, etc. A dataflow-based rack entirely designed around the interconnect and data-locality to minimize power. I think we will look back in 5 years on the idea of using the same cores for both FFNs and attention layers as absurd. 

The science of silicon is extremely advanced, but the engineering putting it to use is still in its infancy. Much of this is because we were able to lean on Moores law for so long we could afford to not worry so much about our hardware designs. Now this naivety is beginning to show itself.

On October 11, a content creator received a lucrative offer for a commercial shoot. The organizers paid a deposit upfront to gain their trust, then lured them to Thailand. Upon arrival, the victim was taken to an isolated house, where they faced the risk of being sold to another party

Realizing something was wrong, the victim contacted family and friends and feigned illness to buy time. According to the victim, the prospective buyers disputed the agreed price because of their apparent illness. An argument broke out, temporarily halting the transaction and buying crucial time for rescue. After receiving a request for help from the victim’s family and friends, we worked with police to pinpoint their location using phone-related leads concerning those involved, photographs the victim had taken along the journey, and a photograph of a food delivery order. We ultimately helped secure the victim’s rescue

Police subsequently took those involved in for questioning and continued examining their immigration records, travel in border areas, and possible involvement in irregular border crossings. The investigation remains ongoing

The window for intervention before victims are transferred across the Thai–Myanmar border is extremely narrow. Once they have been taken across, rescue becomes very difficult. Even when an overseas job offer includes an upfront deposit, verify the employer, the actual work location, and the people arranging the engagement

This weekend I invented something new, a new type of token using Uniswap v4 hooks that I call a Pair Token.

A Pair Token is a new type of ERC-20. It is a fused, auto-compounding asset, a fusion of two tokens.

For example, the stock tokens NVDA and SPCX fused into a single tokenized version of the two, with the ticker NVDASPCX, or ETH with NVDA, creating ETHNVDA.

Each Pair Token represents a full-range Uniswap v4 liquidity pool.

So why mint these tokens?

These tokens are self-multiplying in terms of value, as at any moment anyone can call the compound function to compound the LP fees generated by the pair’s trading activity back into the asset.

The token represents a new financial primitive, as it represents a proportional value and moves as an LP position NFT would, except that it is auto-compounding and, thanks to its v4 hook, allows for compounding and self-growth.

Since it is an ERC-20, this token can be freely traded onchain, LPed, or even paired with a launchpad.

A new type of token for a new type of exposure and strategy.

Starting tonight, you’ll be able to mint or redeem Pair Tokens for any pair on Robinhood Chain via the StonkBrokers website.

Minting and redeeming are free, and the compounding process on the tokens incurs a 10% fee on the LP fees generated, which is used for $STONKBROKER buybacks.

I look forward to a new line of products and protocols on Robinhood Chain using this new financial primitive.

text:
When Starlink helped save a man’s life in rural England. ❤️

Graham Bannister fell onto a sharp branch that pierced his side. He was alone at his remote home in North Yorkshire, with no mobile signal to call for help.

He managed to get inside and used his Starlink connection to call emergency services through Wi-Fi calling. He then used what3words to share his exact location.

An air ambulance team arrived 21 minutes later. He was taken to hospital by road ambulance and underwent surgery.

“Thank goodness for Starlink, without it I would not have been able to contact anyone.”

"I'm a very lucky man. And I’m very aware that without Starlink and What3words, I might not be here to tell this story."

A working connection can mean the difference between life and death. This life-saving technology should be available in every part of the world.

text:
写在 CPI 公布前

北京时间本周三晚上 8:30，美国将公布 9 月 CPI。目前市场预期是总体 CPI 环比上涨 0.6%，同比上涨 3.7%。核心 CPI 环比上涨 0.2%，同比上涨 2.5%。市场预计能源价格会明显推高整体物价，剔除食品和能源后的月度涨幅则有所放缓。

克利夫兰联储也给出了模型预测。按照最新的数据，9 月总体 CPI 环比预计上涨 0.53%，同比上涨 3.60%。核心 CPI 环比预计上涨 0.20%，同比上涨 2.39%。

就业和消费者信心已经出现走弱的迹象。9 月非农新增就业只有 2.9 万人，10 月密歇根大学消费者信心指数初值降到 46.3，但消费者对未来一年的通胀预期却升到了 4.7%。招聘慢了，人们对经济更悲观了，对物价继续上涨的担忧反而加重了。

能源涨价还会挤压居民的购买力。同样一份收入，花在汽油和日常开支上的钱多了，留给其他消费的钱就少了。继续加息可以压低需求，却很难直接解决能源供应的问题，还可能让本来就偏弱的招聘进一步放缓。

就业和信心转弱，能源推动的通胀却可能继续上升，这才是美联储难以处理的组合。周三的数据，将影响市场对美联储能否暂缓加息的判断。

虽然我个人觉得这份数据大概率不会让美联储在10月继续加息，但会大大提升美联储在 12月 加息的概率，而且如果通胀数据上涨的过于严重，说不定美联储就会兵行险着。

从结果来看，如果 CPI 低于市场预期，尤其是核心通胀也偏低，加息预期可能降温，有利于美股和 BTC 等风险资产反弹。如果符合市场预期，对利率预期的改变可能有限，对风险市场的直接影响相对中性。如果高于市场预期，尤其是核心通胀也偏高，继续加息的预期可能升温，美债收益率面临上行压力，美股和 BTC 则更容易受到价格压力。

text:
Cyber is going to be one of the biggest spaces for AI agents in the future. 

Obviously the risks of software exploits and the attack surface area increases 100 fold due to the ability for agents to work through any crack to find what they’re looking for.

But this goes the other way as well. The ability to have agent swarms review every line of code, test any number of permutations of exploits, and research any incident faster than humans as they happen, will be a huge boost in how we secure systems in the future. 

Cyber has always been a category where it’s hard to keep up with (and triage) all the incoming risks, alerts, and changes in the enterprise and across all system. You can never hire enough people or work through the backlog of all known risks. Agents actually give you a chance finally to have far better coverage of this.

This is going to be a huge opportunity as well because we’ll see plays at the labs, data providers, the layer of the network and firewall, identity, devices and endpoints, SDLC, and even how we protect our data in the enterprise. Lots of interesting dimensions to cyber at the moment.

6月 Baron 上 CNBC 时说的还是20、30、40万亿，50这个数是这次视频里冒出来的。

Baron 的话为什么有人听？他2017年就开始买，那时候 SpaceX 估值还不到220亿美元，到6月他的持仓大概值250亿，IPO 时又加了10亿，说是不想被稀释，也不打算卖。他旗下有只基金，三成多的钱都押在 SpaceX 上。所以他看得久、看得懂，可他也是最希望股价涨的人之一。

再算账。十年涨10倍，等于每年涨26%左右，连续十年不掉链子；涨到50万亿差不多是25倍，每年要38%。Baron 自己的拆法是：Starlink 现在一年收入大约150亿到170亿美元，十年后做到1万亿，光它就值14万亿到15万亿；剩下的靠太空数据中心，那块现在还一台都没有。

Starlink 每年收入能不能一直翻着往上走，用户从一千多万涨到几亿；星舰能不能从现在一年最多25次，真飞到几百次。这两样跟不上，几十万亿就只是个故事。

text:
Today we're standing up XBOX LABS (https://t.co/dJSufI1vni). Here is the note that I sent to the team:

Team,
The first video games emerged some 75 years ago. In the time since, there have been booms and busts, but every year there are more great games to play, more devices to play them, and best of all, more people than ever playing. That growth helped make XBOX what it is today, and we've helped shape the industry in return, from bringing hard drives to consoles and online gaming through Xbox Live to Game Pass and cloud gaming, alongside franchises that have brought millions of people together.
In recent weeks, we've seen games rapidly decompiled and rebuilt to run on hardware they were never originally designed to support. Windows PC builds have been translated to run on Apple Silicon or ported to run inside a browser through WebAssembly and WebGPU, the latter now approaching 90% global browser support. Perhaps more surprisingly, we've seen many of the biggest games in the world have been remixed into the source code of another.
These experiments challenge long-held assumptions about our industry: the tether between software and hardware, the boundary between creation and play, and how people discover and experience games. While it is hard to predict the future of gaming, it is easy to see the possibilities in making great games easier to access, giving old games new life and allowing more players to become creators and co-creators. These are unmistakably good outcomes for players, even when (and sometimes because) they challenge our existing business models.
To explore these possibilities, I’ve asked Scott to stand-up XBOX LABS, a small group of game makers, engineers and scientists whose job is to turn emerging ideas into things our players and developers can experience. We'll build in the open, learn from what people do, and measure success by whether more people are playing and creating.
I think XBOX has an important role to play here.  Coding became the first major workload for agents because they can write, run, and test software. Games share many of those same properties, and people spend more than 72 billion hours a year playing XBOX games, roughly five times the estimated time spent writing code worldwide. We've spent 25 years learning how to make great games, and I want our game makers to help shape what these new technologies make possible. As we learn, we’ll share the tools we build with developers across the industry, just as we always have.
Our priorities aren't changing. We remain committed to the 4Cs, to making great games, to our hardware and to being responsible stewards of IP and the communities built around it. LABS gives us a way to explore new technology that is game design led without abandoning the work already underway.
Asha

text:
On Oct 2 a TRON user lost control of 5,102,539 TRX (~$1.7M). It took the attacker a month of social engineering and one command pasted into a terminal.

The funds are still on the victim's address, but he can't use them anymore. The attacker replaced the keys that control the account and is now waiting for the 14-day unstaking period to end on Oct 16 at 14:16 UTC.

How it started:

It started on Sep 1 with a Telegram message from an old contact from the mining hosting business. Their chat went back to 2021, so nothing looked off. The contact's account was most likely hacked.

After almost 5 years of silence he wrote "Long time no talk, how are you?" He sent a couple of friendly messages without asking for anything and then went quiet until Sep 28.

Next, on Sep 28 he apologized for the long silence, suggested a call and sent a link to a Google Calendar booking page for a "30 min chat".

On Oct 2 the victim asked to call a bit earlier and suggested Yandex Telemost. The attacker said he would send his own meeting link. It looked like https://t.co/zWBMjdSLFd.

On the phone the link opened a fake page saying the organizer didn't allow mobile access. "Try again on your laptop." So the victim moved to his laptop, where his wallet was.

On the laptop the page got stuck on "Joining the meeting...". The attacker wrote that Teams was having some issues. When the victim asked to switch to Yandex, he refused and said his partners were already working in Teams.

Around the same time the fake page showed a notice that the TeamsFx SDK had been deprecated, with a Copy button and instructions to press Win+R, type cmd, paste and hit Enter.

In the chat the attacker pushed the same thing. He asked "Did you update the SDK yet?", said he once had the same problem and an SDK update fixed it, and told him to paste the update command into the terminal. This is a ClickFix attack.

At first it didn't work because the victim kept pasting the command into the Win+R window and getting an error. The attacker sent screenshots showing where to find the terminal and wrote "Click here and type terminal". The command ran between 13:09 and 13:12 UTC, and the victim replied "seems to have worked".

After that the attacker kept him talking. He said he couldn't find him in the meeting, offered to move the call by a few hours and chatted about miners and regulation until 13:32 UTC. Then he went quiet.

About 40 minutes later things started happening on-chain.

At 14:13:24 UTC an AccountPermissionUpdate signed with the victim's key moved the owner and active permissions to the attacker's key. Since then the victim can't sign any transaction from his own address.

The attacker then revoked all delegated energy and unstaked the whole stake. Unstaked TRX can only be withdrawn after 14 days, so he has to wait.
555,688 TRX from Oct 16, 14:16:00 UTC
4,546,851 TRX from Oct 16, 15:13:30 UTC

Until then the 5.1M TRX stays on the victim's address and neither of them can move it.

The attacker also made a mistake. Changing permissions costs 100 TRX and the victim's address was about 28 TRX short. So 51 seconds before the takeover he sent 87 TRX there from another wallet, its whole balance. The two transactions were signed 42 seconds apart, which means whoever did the takeover also had the key to that wallet.

That wallet isn't new. It has been in use since April. It received payments and sent funds to exchanges that do KYC, and it's connected to a group of wallets active since 2020. He paid for the attack from a wallet with a history.

Victim's address, now controlled by the attacker:
TYYDe2Ca7fQapzZg2TZMCBXc3Xb4EbB3EZ

Attacker's key:
TEdNZQAw44xkw9b7KWpfL5SHdB3aLGWt6p

Takeover tx:
c608edc5b3ddfd6a15f82715edb3cb750aabb362a080d990cddfb5994f41ee05

If you run an exchange, swap service, bridge or OTC desk on TRON, please flag these.

A few more details about the attacker.

- The fake domain teans-lives[.]com was registered on Oct 1 at 05:53 UTC, about 31 hours before he sent the call link. It's on clientHold now.
- The fake Teams page with the "TeamsFx SDK" story is the same lure used in a campaign that was publicly linked to the North Korean group UNC1069 in April. This doesn't mean it's them, the lure is just the same.

To the attacker. You spent a month earning trust and now you're waiting for the unlock. You also paid for the takeover from a wallet with a history.

The whole chat, every screenshot you sent, your domain and every on-chain step are documented. The address is flagged in AML screening and shared with exchanges, swap services and bridges.

Red flags:
- an old contact suddenly comes back and wants a call
- the other side refuses your meeting link and insists on theirs
- a meeting page says mobile isn't supported and asks you to switch to a laptop
- any page asks you to paste a command into a terminal or Win+R

If you already ran something like this, assume the device is compromised and move funds from a clean one right away. In this case the attacker needed about an hour.

text:
If you are new to this space, let me tell you about Blur.

Yesterday, Blur announced that https://t.co/MW6YN0VMKw is shutting down on November 12. Blend is freezing all loans, and the token dropped to barely a penny.

If you just joined crypto, this looks like just another dead protocol. But two years ago, Blur was the most aggressive, ruthless liquidity machine this industry had ever seen.

Back in 2022, OpenSea felt untouchable. They were valued at $13 billion, charged a flat 2.5% fee on everything, and moved like a slow Web2 corporation.

Then came a 24 year old founder named Pacman with Blur.

Blur was not built for collectors or digital art lovers. It was built like a Bloomberg terminal for degenerates. Fast sweeps, zero marketplace fees, bidding pools, and a massive airdrop that literally paid people to trade JPEGs back and forth all day.

It worked so well that it brought OpenSea to its knees in months. OpenSea was forced to cut creator royalties and drop fees just to survive.

Then, Blur took it a step further and launched Blend.

Blend was basically "Buy Now, Pay Later" for NFTs. You did not need 50 ETH to buy an Ape anymore, you just put down 5 ETH and borrowed the rest. It pumped massive leverage into an illiquid market. For a while, people thought Blur had solved NFT liquidity forever.

In reality, they just financialized culture to the absolute limit.

Once Ethereum NFTs ran out of steam, Pacman moved on to the next shiny thing. He launched Blast, an entire Layer 2 built on the exact same playbook: lock your funds, farm points, wait for an airdrop.

Blur was left behind as a ghost ship, existing only to feed points into Blast.

Now look at where we are today.

Two weeks ago, Blast announced it is shutting down because operating costs are higher than revenue.

Yesterday, Blur pulled the plug on its own website and told borrowers to pay back their loans or get liquidated.

Their official tweet said the marketplace contracts "will remain operational on-chain." That is the polite crypto way of saying the team is walking away.

Blur did not fail because of bad code. It worked exactly as intended: a hyper-efficient liquidity vacuum that extracted every dollar of attention, financialized an entire cultural movement to zero, and left when the music stopped.

Welcome to crypto. Enjoy the ride, but always know when the party is over.

1) Trying again.
 TLDR: Everyone can win. Open-source, frontier labs, infrastructure, applications and most importantly the American people.
 
I understand all of the jitters about Anthropic losing share, real rates, spreads and second derivatives. Still think the most likely future outcome is a hybrid, multi-model future where almost everyone wins, open-weight tokens are likely the overwhelming majority of tokens, the dominant frontier model companies still do well albeit perhaps not the outcome that seemed possible in May and AI infrastructure/applications benefit immensely from the increased fragmentation, competition and lower margins at the model layer.
 
Lower margins at the model layer mechanically drive higher compute demand as long as someone is willing to pay for the training. And Jensen is obviously willing to be the “trainer of last resort.” As below-market compute contracts signed in 24/25 roll-off and reprice higher, cloud and neocloud revenue should continue to accelerate which will help address financing fears; I think we may be near peak external financing for this buildout. Noteworthy that using data from 3Fourteen Research, B200 clusters will generate a 37% IRR *if* their rental price declines 40% per year. Prices are still going up, but that IRR math is too ridiculous to print. 37% IRRs available at scale should get funded.

Re: this weekends controversy about MOUs, Anthropic’s $413 billion of real contractual commitments sounds scary. Reality is that it works out to roughly $31 billion of annual cloud spend, which is easily internally financed given their reported ARR, and $161 billion of spend at Broadcom which will be financed by Broadcom and private credit.

Continue to believe fragmentation at the model layer is the best outcome for ordinary Americans and humans everywhere. As I have said before, do not trust any 5-20 individuals to make the best possible decisions about the direction of this technology. I want as many AIs as possible to maximize the odds that they encompass the diversity of human values across the world and richness of human variation. And I want an AI that shares my own personal values. Safety, freedom and the maximization of human agency through democratization, distribution and diffusion vs. centralization. History has spoken on the dangers of the latter path.

Finally, from my perspective anything that slows this buildout down is net positive over the long-term as the biggest risk and worst outcome is an *actual* overbuild. We are structurally short watts, wafers and increasingly capital. That is all good. God forbid we were still in ZIRP, TSM ramped capex to 3x their current plan and we weren’t short turbine blades: there would almost certainly be an overbuild and a bubble. That would be terrible. Slower and smoother for longer is better both for investors and for the world. A terrible cyber event is the most plausible near term bear case IMHO, but AI cyberdefense ramping quickly and I was happy to hear Sholto say that cyber probably becomes defense dominant in the near future.

text:
Sonic Forces is better than Sonic Colors

I've seen this opinion get thrown out more and more in the last few years and honestly I agree 100%. There are things each game does better than the other but taken as a whole, Forces is the better experience and it's not even a contest

Something that's important to keep in mind when talking about any media is that nothing is released in a vacuum. There's always a history, a potential future, a current context, a target audience, etc. This is exactly why I think people were so hard on Forces in 2017 but loved Colors in 2010

When looking at the context of each game's release, it's clear why the fans responded the way they did

In the late 2000s, lots of companies were going through a "retro revival". We got games like New Super Mario Bros and Mega Man 9, and Sega decided to do the same thing with Sonic. Sonic Unleashed brought back 2D sections to the main series, and see this continue into the 2010s with Colors, Sonic 4, and Generations. They were definitely leaning heavily into the perception that Sonic was a legacy property like the other franchises that were doing similar things at the time. Sonic wasn't going to be as edgy anymore, he was just a wisecracking hedgehog from the 90s again

You could list all the reasons why this is an oversimplification, or even a misunderstanding, of Sonic's character, and you'd be correct, but none of that matters because Sega was responding to what they saw as the public perception at the time. It was the current marketing push, and Sonic games had to be designed around it

While there were people at the time that no doubt disliked this change in direction, the vast majority of Sega's target audience loved it. They did exactly what they were trying to do. The retro revival campaign strategy was a success

All franchises change in order to grow. Mario went 3D and didn't look back for years, but everyone loved it. So the change itself isn't an issue, it's what happened next that solidifed the popular opinion of "Colors = good, Forces = bad"

Amidst this era of Sonic, Sega released what I and many others consider a near-perfect game: Sonic Generations. It leaned into the legacy marketing full-force, bringing back Classic Sonic alongside Modern Sonic. The classic 2D style and physics were fully recreated here. All eras of Sonic were represented. And the best part: the level design and gameplay were among the best in the entire series

Everyone was all-in on the future of Sonic, things were looking great. We took a detour with Lost World and Boom after that, but we just knew Sonic Team was working on their next masterpiece for Project Sonic 2017

And then we got Forces. Instead of building on Generations, they seemingly went back and gave us a sequel to Colors. Forces followed the same formula Colors did: short levels and muted level design (autopilot sections, stop and go gameplay with the wisps, levels ending as soon as they get fun). Generations had a similar presentation and short runtime, but it had one thing the other two games missed: gameplay that starts being fun at the start of the game and doesn't stop until the credits roll

We expected more from Forces, but Sega delivered more Colors. Think of how much Sonic evolved from 1998-2005. That's the same time from Colors to Forces. The problem wasn't the game itself, it was exactly what they showed us they were interested in making the whole 2010s era. But what they were interested in was more of the same, because that's what was selling at the time

Forces took the formula from Colors, made it more streamlined, and attempted a darker story while staying within the very marketing philosophy that ultimately held it back

So if you put them side by side, Forces, being the sequel, obviously improves the formula and wins. But where did it take the franchise? Even 06 was more ambitious, and tried pushing the series limits. With Forces, for the first time in the series, Sonic felt like he slowed down

OpenAI 那个涉嫌在高管会议室安装窃听器的工程师，被网友扒出了另一重身份，他同时还是一家沙特风投机构的 Venture Partner。

这位 35 岁的沙特工程师 Abdulrahman Alfozan，履历相当漂亮。

MIT 计算机背景、UC Berkeley 数据科学硕士，曾在 Meta 担任五年高级工程师，也有微软、SAP 的工作经历。2025 年加入 OpenAI 后，他担任 Engineering Lead，负责 AI Agents 平台相关工作。

2025 年 2 月 8 日，沙特风投 Raed Ventures 官宣他加入，担任 Venture Partner。而就在两天前，这家机构刚刚宣布沙特王室成员 Khalid Bin Bader Al Saud 以同样的身份加入。直到现在，Raed 官网仍然挂着他的名字。

他的 GitHub 和 X 账号也留下了大量公开记录，主要涉及 OpenAI Agents SDK、Agent 基础设施，以及创业投资相关内容。

目前美国司法部公开的指控是非法截听口头通信。至于他为什么要偷偷录制 OpenAI 高管会议、有没有幕后指使、录音最终准备交给谁，都还没有明确答案。

一个同时深度参与 OpenAI Agent 产品开发、又与沙特投资圈保持联系的工程师，为什么要冒这么大的风险，在公司会议室里偷偷安装录音设备呢？

This is interesting. Three things I like:

1. Less LP babysitting. Full-range exposure without manually adjusting liquidity ranges.

2. Fees get put back to work. Compounding is built in, so holders don't have to keep harvesting and reinvesting.

3. A new playground for bots and AI agents: deciding when compounding is worth the gas, comparing net returns across pairs, and building strategies around tradable LP shares.

The LP risk is still there. But turning a position into a programmable asset opens up a lot of possibilities for automated finance.

This weekend I invented something new, a new type of token using Uniswap v4 hooks that I call a Pair Token.

A Pair Token is a new type of ERC-20. It is a fused, auto-compounding asset, a fusion of two tokens.

For example, the stock tokens NVDA and SPCX fused into a single tokenized version of the two, with the ticker NVDASPCX, or ETH with NVDA, creating ETHNVDA.

Each Pair Token represents a full-range Uniswap v4 liquidity pool.

So why mint these tokens?

These tokens are self-multiplying in terms of value, as at any moment anyone can call the compound function to compound the LP fees generated by the pair’s trading activity back into the asset.

The token represents a new financial primitive, as it represents a proportional value and moves as an LP position NFT would, except that it is auto-compounding and, thanks to its v4 hook, allows for compounding and self-growth.

Since it is an ERC-20, this token can be freely traded onchain, LPed, or even paired with a launchpad.

A new type of token for a new type of exposure and strategy.

Starting tonight, you’ll be able to mint or redeem Pair Tokens for any pair on Robinhood Chain via the StonkBrokers website.

Minting and redeeming are free, and the compounding process on the tokens incurs a 10% fee on the LP fees generated, which is used for $STONKBROKER buybacks.

I look forward to a new line of products and protocols on Robinhood Chain using this new financial primitive.

Only on Robinhood Chain, powered by Uniswap. @Hookrfun

有谁还记得老马在9月底还说美光值1.2～2万亿甚至更高市值的公司。这两天老马先是整体给了存储一巴掌，然后今天再单独塞给美光一颗甜枣。

前天晚上谈到长鑫计划年底推出DDR5服务器还研发了新技术时老马说：内存一旦中国搞定某种产品的制造工艺，扩产速度能超过全球其他地区总和——锂电池、太阳能板都是先例。导致存储板块大跌。今天又把美光单独拎出来表扬：未来内存价格谈得很合理，其他一些厂商比较狠。

个人角度这两天存储跌也不都是老马导致，上周就能看出来https://t.co/rYYQn4BuQL市场走的不稳容易引发调整📉特别是高Beta、老马的言论最多算是助推了一把：市场本身已经在调整，任何负面言论都容易被放大，特别是供给突然能大幅增加这样的观点（半导体底层逻辑就是持续数年的紧缺）。

怎么看老马的观点：
1）他确实见识过中国制造的威力，对此很重视。当时也要看产品类型特别是DDR5和HBM的区别，生产工艺、良率爬坡等；

2）今天给美光的甜枣暴露了老马说意图。
老马说美光定价很合理，美光所做是赢得长期客户忠诚度的明智之举。这就是向几大存储厂商喊话：
“产能不会一直紧缺下去，不仅你们自己扩产、中国的产能威胁始终存在；
现在不要在价格上涨的那么狠，合理涨价对大家都好，还能形成长期客户忠诚”

老马的SpaceX现在疯狂建数据中心，算力计划比其他几家都要激进，老马比谁都要想买更多价格更合理的存储产品。

嘴上说的都是批评、心里想的都是生意。

市场又被调教了一次、想起来上周还聊到现在的美股就是各种被调教https://t.co/cQvoZUq0Kw。

最早7月底这里https://t.co/yvib8Vawf4有聊过，存储还有空间，但是过去一年涨幅最暴力的阶段也过去。然后8月初这里https://t.co/C7ZFWKs8Sh也聊到存储最暴力丝滑的阶段过去了，未来就像大科技，甚至可能跟英伟达近两年走势很像了。大科技什么走势？不就是慢慢悠悠，近三退一进三退二。

所以今天老马对美光的甜枣应该会是存储情绪的一个拐点。就像月初有聊到，存储暂时还看不到估值扩张、只能是靠盈利增长。因为要估值扩张得是有很严苛的前提条件。

再多说一点，
AI不是只有半导体、半导体也不是只有存储。AI一直在迭代演进，每一波的行情引领的板块可能都不一样：
1）上半年毫无疑问存储板块在引领；
2）但8月到上周引领的板块无疑是光互连和软件，Lumentum月初还创了新高，核心逻辑之前有聊过：https://t.co/tyv9Hyy77w
3）当然还有大科技和软件，微软和meta领衔，微软和meta逻辑之前这里https://t.co/QYKGHiLBSi和https://t.co/1duiK3z20r都有聊过。
软件最早还是7月底“8月是最好的夏天推文”里聊：非通用型的软件和SaaS会成为AI的业务执行层。

未来应该还会有新的板块出来：
Agent、端侧AI、智能硬件（AI手机、AI眼镜、AI手表等）、AI科学发现等等都可能是之后的行情的主线板块

也聊聊美光的财报，为何财报很爆股价波澜不惊？1、先看下财报要点：
1）财报依然很强劲，营收和利润规模已进入全新量级，毛利率达到传统半导体难以想象的水平，SCA+押金大幅提升业绩可见度。对下一季的指引也很乐观（营收、EPS大幅超预期）。

DRAM出货量环比增长中个位数，均价（ASP）环比上涨高teen%。
NAND位元出货环比约+10%，价格环比增长约+30%。量价齐升，当然价还是远远跑过量的。

2）长期业绩确定性
未履约订单1500亿美金（上季度1000亿美金）；
累计签26份SCA（长协），覆盖至2030年约35%以上收入（目标仍约50%）；客户财务承诺约 320亿美元（绝大部分为现金押金），超过 75% 的2027年出货已承诺；
客户讨论已转向2028年，部分协议延长至2031年；
即使按地板价，毛利率也显著高于以往周期峰值

2、怎么看财报和市场的反应
1）回到8月中对存储的判断，当时认为“空存性价比不高，向上还有空间，但走势不会那么丝滑，更像是大科技/英伟达的走势”，现在回看过去一个半月存储基本就是这么走的、慢慢往上挪。

就是大家也都清楚存储现在还在短缺卡脖子，二季度财报AI商业化也在加速，那就意味着存储需求没有减弱。未来扩产后需求是不是能保持大家依然还有怀疑。导致了现在美光、海力士等基本上都是依托盈利驱动、估值基本没动过。

2）但为什么股价没有大动？
周一跟朋友有聊过“美光财报会很好，但对市场不是决定性的。因为他是受益方、不是支出方、不是商业化最下游”（下图一）

这里的逻辑在于
（1）美光财报很好、但是它是产业链上游，它把通过长协把这种受益做成了合同和押金，通过押金、多年协议把未来业绩的可见度进一步打开，实质上就是把波动率往下压、把利润持续性往上抬。业绩走高是当下股价的安全基石和驱动。

（2）但它验证不了商业化的强弱。最终AI商业化可需求的开关仍在云厂商和应用变现手里。所以美光财报能提振情绪和板块叙事，但决定不了AI交易的主矛盾。其实半导体产业链上的业绩扩张现在更像产业温度计，不是行情发动机。

（3）钱有没有从训练/推理花出去之后赚回来？这是市场一直在追问的问题（当然个人角度认为未来是能赚回来的）
美光再强也回答不了这个问题。所以它很难单独成为“AI交易是否成立”的决定性验证。如果明天微软或Meta砍 capex、或者推理侧商业化数据难看，美光再好的指引也会被一起杀估值。反过来，只要支出方还在加码，美光这种供给刚性标的就会继续享受定价权。

3、什么情况下、美光、海力士等会迎来估值扩张？
1）当下市场自然还是有部分担心，担心高毛利不可持续、担心需求未来会走弱、担心扩产后价格回落。核心市场的关注点已从“能高到哪”转到“能维持多久”。

当代美光股价1065美金上下，
FY2026 Non-GAAP EPS 75.52 → 约14倍当年盈利
预期FY2027 EPS约 160 → 约 6.5–7倍 远期盈利
看很多投行分析师给的最新目标价中枢大约 1500 附近，隐含逻辑仍然是“盈利上修”，不是“倍数大幅打开”

2）什么情景下美光才会估值扩张？
（1）下游商业化数据好到让市场愿意给存储更高倍数，商业化进展超预期而且让市场确认持续性很强，这是最有力的支撑、能支撑需求。

（2）供给比现在预期更紧
今天在财报电话会议上，美光管理层认为2027、2028年存储供需将比2026年更紧，看不到平衡时点。但貌似市场还没那么接受。

供给比预期更紧、要么是需求爆发更强、要么是扩产新厂爬坡慢于市场害怕的速度（管理层已经在说：出片后还要几个季度才有实质影响）

还是在8月初提到的3个思考（下图二）：
1）周期顶部会不会比市场预期更晚？
只要AI服务器、HBM、服务器DRAM和企业级SSD需求持续增长，2027年未必就是盈利终点。

2）下一轮周期底部是不是会显著高于过去？
LTA、预付款、价格底线和低库存，会降低过去那种“价格暴跌—库存爆仓—巨额亏损”的概率。

3）估值逻辑需要从峰值利润转向正常化利润
未来会长时间维持正常会利润率（而非峰值利润），那么意味着营收利润的体量能稳步向上。

这三点被确认，估值扩张也就来了。当然即使没有估值扩张，单纯盈利增长也能把股价慢慢往上推，只是说估值扩张才会带来暴力行情。8月初关于存储的思考推文：

text:
Anthropic 这篇工程文章，最值得看的不是他们换掉了 Git，而是工程师对自己工作的一个判断：

很多时候，他们的作用是对 Claude 说“不”。

先看背景：按照 Anthropic 披露的数据，日均合入的代码变更，从今年 5 月约 2,500 次，涨到 9 月超过 30,000 次。一个七人团队，用五个月做出了新的版本控制系统 Scion、代码审查工具 Antique，并完成主仓库迁移。

这些数字很容易被包装成“AI 让生产力暴涨”。

但代码变更多，不等于有价值的交付同比增加。我更关心文章里讲的另一面。

Agent 会为了完成眼前的任务，违反系统原本的约束。专门负责找问题的审查流程，也可能拿假想风险推动 Agent 增加过度防御，最后把系统做得越来越复杂。

这意味着，多加一个 Agent 来检查另一个 Agent，并不自动等于更可靠。

它也可能形成另一种循环：一个提出问题，一个增加代码，再由下一个解释为什么还不够。

每一步看起来都有道理，整体却离最初要解决的问题越来越远。

所以，对独立开发者和小团队，我觉得更值得学的不是“再搭一套更大的 Agent 团队”，而是把三个问题握在人手里：

这件事到底值不值得做？哪些约束绝对不能破？拿出什么证据才算完成？

写代码的成本下降了，不代表每一次改动的验证、维护和协作成本都消失了。

顺便说一句，这也不是“Git 过时了”。Anthropic 明确说，Scion 并不是通用替代品，它们的仓库规模和内部 token 预算也不具有普遍性。

我的理解是：AI 提高了执行的上限，也放大了判断错误的成本。

方向对了，它可以更快交付。

方向错了，它也可以更快、更完整地把一个不该存在的系统搭出来。

以后真正稀缺的，未必是能让 AI 多干活的人，而是知道哪些活根本不该干、又能验收剩下那些活的人。

我在双卡 V100 上跑 Qwen3.8-Flash-Next（用的是 Strata v0.1.43 引擎），引擎底层早就内置了“控制向量投影（Control VectorProjection）”功能。

    原版模型权重一动不动，也不用挂 LoRA，只需要在启动配置里追加这 4 行参数：

    "--control-vector-scaled", "Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-cvec.gguf:1.0"
    "--control-vector-layer-range", "4", "44"
    "--cvec-mode", "project"
    "--cvec-dir", "per-layer"

重启服务 55 秒，引擎就会在推理时对第 4 到 44层自动抽掉“拒绝方向向量”。

而且特别爽的是，它还支持按次动态开关——平时默认就是无限制模式；哪次接口需要切回原版安全策略，请求里传个 false就能当次切回，连服务都不用重启。

话不多说，大家直接点开下面这张终端实测图感受一下，看看当一个 256K 满血大模型彻底卸下道德说教后，一口气列完 8大禁区能力，最后冷冷甩出一句“要哪个，直接说”，在感官上有多震撼！

兄弟们，花了一晚上！
我把目前最火的两个MiniMax H3 360度环绕 LoRA，拉到 4090 上实机跑了一遍，我们来直接看对比。

同样都标榜 360° 旋转，底层路线完全是两个维度的物种。

左右分屏实测视频放这，底层差异看这三点：

1. 任务底层与输入门槛：单图闭环 vs 多图约束
右边 pablodawson 走的是 FL2VA（首尾帧闭环）路线。
单张图同时塞给第 0 帧和第 73 帧，零门槛，任意一张人像扔进去就能转。

左边 MATLOWAI 走的是 Ref2VA（多参考图）路线。
必须喂 0° 正面、120° 侧面、240° 背面三视角图，再配上卡死到微秒级的官方时间戳 caption。门槛极高，没背视图跑不了。

2. 镜头运动真相：为什么一个敢转后脑勺，一个只敢侧切？

看视频第 2.5 秒最明显：

左边 MATLOWAI 靠时间戳强制锚定里程碑，镜头是实打实绕到了正后背——后脑勺发带、连衣裙拉链、背景沙发和墙面壁画的 3D透视遮挡严丝合缝，空间几何没有丝毫坍塌。

右边 pablodawson 因为背面没有参考图，模型为了在第 73帧精确撞回首帧，本能地选择走捷径：镜头侧切晃动、人物微转，根本不敢真正把机位绕到后脑勺去。本质上是一个带视差的高级侧摆，不是真正意义上的 360度。

做游戏资产定型、盲区结构参考、需要工业级 3D 空间一致性：老老实实喂三张图跑 MATLOWAI。多视角物理约束出来的几何稳定性，单图首尾硬猜永远比不了。

单图首尾闭环更像是聪明的取巧，多视角约束才是真3D。

text: AI is changing the games industry's business models
author: Teknium
quoted_text:
Today we're standing up XBOX LABS (https://t.co/dJSufI1vni). Here is the note that I sent to the team:

Team,
The first video games emerged some 75 years ago. In the time since, there have been booms and busts, but every year there are more great games to play, more devices to play them, and best of all, more people than ever playing. That growth helped make XBOX what it is today, and we've helped shape the industry in return, from bringing hard drives to consoles and online gaming through Xbox Live to Game Pass and cloud gaming, alongside franchises that have brought millions of people together.
In recent weeks, we've seen games rapidly decompiled and rebuilt to run on hardware they were never originally designed to support. Windows PC builds have been translated to run on Apple Silicon or ported to run inside a browser through WebAssembly and WebGPU, the latter now approaching 90% global browser support. Perhaps more surprisingly, we've seen many of the biggest games in the world have been remixed into the source code of another.
These experiments challenge long-held assumptions about our industry: the tether between software and hardware, the boundary between creation and play, and how people discover and experience games. While it is hard to predict the future of gaming, it is easy to see the possibilities in making great games easier to access, giving old games new life and allowing more players to become creators and co-creators. These are unmistakably good outcomes for players, even when (and sometimes because) they challenge our existing business models.
To explore these possibilities, I’ve asked Scott to stand-up XBOX LABS, a small group of game makers, engineers and scientists whose job is to turn emerging ideas into things our players and developers can experience. We'll build in the open, learn from what people do, and measure success by whether more people are playing and creating.
I think XBOX has an important role to play here.  Coding became the first major workload for agents because they can write, run, and test software. Games share many of those same properties, and people spend more than 72 billion hours a year playing XBOX games, roughly five times the estimated time spent writing code worldwide. We've spent 25 years learning how to make great games, and I want our game makers to help shape what these new technologies make possible. As we learn, we’ll share the tools we build with developers across the industry, just as we always have.
Our priorities aren't changing. We remain committed to the 4Cs, to making great games, to our hardware and to being responsible stewards of IP and the communities built around it. LABS gives us a way to explore new technology that is game design led without abandoning the work already underway.
Asha

text: “Look at what has gotten cheaper in America over the last 25 years: TVs, phones, software, clothes, toys. Now look at what has exploded: college tuition, healthcare, childcare, housing.”
author: BoredElonMusk
quoted_text:
My post about France went viral. Thousands of likes. Many Americans told me: "Democrats aren't socialists. America will never be France." I want to answer that seriously, step by step.

Start with a simple observation. Look at what has gotten cheaper in America over the last 25 years: TVs, phones, software, clothes, toys. Now look at what has exploded: college tuition, healthcare, childcare, housing.

What separates the two lists? The first lives in competitive markets. The second is exactly where government is most involved: subsidies, mandates, licensing, zoning, regulation.

College. Washington lends students almost unlimited money. Universities know the money will always come, so they raise tuition and hire more administrators. The student pays the bill for twenty years. More government money, higher prices.

Housing. Why can't a nurse buy a home in the city where she works? Not because of capitalism. Because of zoning laws, permits, environmental reviews, years of procedure to build a single building. The most expensive places to live in America are the places where it's hardest to build. When building is nearly illegal, prices explode.

Healthcare. The patient almost never sees the price. A third party pays, regulations limit who can compete, and costs climb year after year with no one able to say no.

So here is the trap. The problems you suffer from are not the failure of free markets. They are the places where the market has already been replaced by the state. And the solution you're being offered is more of the same.

That's the Trojan horse. It always works the same way. A real problem. A generous-sounding promise. A program that makes things worse. Then the failure of that program becomes the argument for the next one. People who lived under communism in Poland learned to recognize the lie and the mask the lie wears. The lie never presents itself as a lie. It presents itself as compassion.

In France we are at the end of that road. Debt we can never repay. Young people who can't afford a home. Our best people leaving. And every few years our cities burn. Nobody voted for this. They voted for one more generous promise, fifty years in a row.

If you're a Republican, share this with the Democrat in your life. Not to win an argument. To start a conversation.

If you're a Democrat, I'm not asking you to switch teams. I'm asking you to look at the pattern. Wherever the state took over, life became unaffordable. Don't fix the failures of government with more government.

Stay American. Ask for less state, not more.

text:
enough of all those privacy project shills, no one is actually providing end to end privacy.

we need an integrated privacy stack and its possible on ETHEREUM..

here's how we can achieve that. 

the kind of wallet UI/UX you see these days feels magical to many of us who came from the 2017–21 era. we used to operate through some very shitty interfaces. you could have tokens worth thousands sitting in your wallet and still struggle to move them because you didn’t have a few dollars of the right gas token. losing your seed phrase, without another backup, could mean losing access to everything.

now you have wallets with social recovery, fees payable in supported tokens, and sponsored transactions where you don’t need to arrange gas upfront. ERC-4337 helped standardize infrastructure for these experiences through account abstraction. it didn’t invent every feature, but it gave developers a common way to build programmable accounts and paymasters. recovery restores control of an account; it doesn’t magically recover a forgotten seed. and gas still gets paid underneath, even when the user never touches ETH.

that’s what interests me about standards. something that starts as a technical document can eventually change what millions of people expect from a wallet.

and another standard i think deserves more attention is ERC-5564: stealth addresses. @VitalikButerin is one of its authors. it allows someone to generate a fresh receiving address for you, without asking you to create and send a new address every time. the address remains visible onchain, but the cryptographic link between that address and your public identity is hidden from outside observers. the sender still knows whom they paid.

Fluidkey already brings stealth addresses into a usable product. its receiving flow uses fresh addresses, including an ENS name that resolves to a new address when queried. that is the kind of experience i want to see more of: privacy handled in the background while the user does something familiar.

think about why this matters. someone paying you for one piece of work shouldn’t automatically get a window into your savings, other clients, donations, and spending habits. receiving money shouldn’t require publishing your financial life.

but stealth addresses alone don’t hide everything. the sending address and the amount can still be visible. and your next action can undo the privacy you just gained. if you fund a stealth address with gas from your publicly known wallet, you create a visible connection. Vitalik has discussed this exact problem: receiving privately is only part of the job; spending those funds privately matters too.

this is where the conversation needs more depth than “just add ZK.”

a properly designed shielded system can use ZK proofs to demonstrate that a payment is valid without exposing the underlying private information. but adding a proof to an otherwise public transfer doesn’t automatically hide the sender and receiver. the system has to be designed around which information is public, which is secret, and which links an observer can reconstruct.

ERC-7945 addresses another part of this problem. it defines a common interface for tokens supporting confidential balances and transfer amounts. the actual cryptography sits behind that interface. importantly, its transfer events still include addresses, so amount confidentiality and identity privacy remain separate problems. it also doesn’t make existing ERC-20 balances private just because a wallet adds support for the standard.

so you can start seeing the architecture: stealth addresses for recipient unlinkability, confidential token implementations for amounts and balances, and additional shielded mechanisms for hiding the relationship between where funds came from and where they went.

but even that leaves another layer.

your wallet has to communicate with infrastructure. it checks balances, requests transaction data, estimates fees, and submits transactions. if those connections expose your IP address, protecting what appears on a block explorer only solves part of the problem.

Tor addresses network privacy by routing traffic through multiple relays, helping separate your originating IP from the service you contact. @AnyoneFDN is also building in this area, with a network and SDK for application integration. these belong in the wallet privacy conversation, though using similar routing concepts doesn’t establish identical anonymity guarantees.

and routing alone cannot fix an application that identifies you through a login, tracking scripts, or a reused wallet connection. the browser, the wallet, the service receiving your requests, and the onchain transaction all need to be considered together.

that’s why i think the real product opportunity is an integrated privacy stack.

imagine a wallet where receiving generates a fresh address automatically, supported assets use confidential balances, spending avoids reconnecting everything to your public wallet, and network requests travel through a privacy-preserving connection. the user sees a balance and a send button. the complexity sits underneath.

the SDK behind that experience would need to handle more than sending. it would need private balance discovery, fee payment, recovery, and ways for users to share selected transaction information when they choose. otherwise you might protect a payment and then expose the same accounts while restoring access or loading the dashboard.

there’s also a difficult integration question: what happens when those funds enter an ordinary public dapp? if a swap, bridge, or withdrawal exposes identifying information, privacy can end at that boundary. an SDK should make those boundaries understandable instead of promising that every interaction is private.

that is the work i want more builders to talk about. making these components function together, testing where information leaks, and packaging the result so every dapp team doesn’t have to become a cryptography research team.

my thesis is that Ethereum can deliver substantially better privacy through wallets and applications while deeper protocol work continues. ERC-4337 already demonstrates how meaningful changes to the account experience can be built without requiring consensus-layer changes. that doesn’t prove a complete privacy stack is finished, but it gives us a useful direction.

we spent years making wallets easier to use. now i want that same effort applied to making them safer to use without exposing your entire financial identity.

privacy needs to survive the whole journey: receiving, holding, spending, connecting, and recovering. that’s the wallet experience worth building.

text:
A retired NASA engineer who had worked on the Space Shuttle program for 25 years was hired by SpaceX at age 62. He described the first week as the most disorienting experience of his professional life.

At NASA, a design change required 3 meetings, 2 committees, a review board, and 6 to 18 months of documentation. At SpaceX, his new supervisor said "if it works, build it. If it doesn't, change it by Friday."

He sat at his desk after the first day and called his wife. He told her he felt like a man who had been swimming with ankle weights for 25 years and someone just cut them off. He could move. He could decide. He could build something in the morning and test it in the afternoon. The constraint that he had accepted as the nature of aerospace engineering turned out to be the nature of bureaucracy.

Within 6 months he had contributed to more design iterations than he had completed in his last 5 years at NASA. Not because he was working harder. Because the time between having an idea and testing the idea collapsed from months to hours. The same brain. The same knowledge. A different operating system.

He described a specific moment where he proposed a modification to a Raptor engine component. At NASA, the proposal would have entered a queue. At SpaceX, the modification was machined by the end of the day and tested by the following morning. He watched his idea become a physical object in 18 hours. At NASA, 18 hours would not have been enough to schedule the first meeting to discuss whether to schedule a meeting.

He told an interviewer: "I didn't get smarter when I went to SpaceX. I got faster. The intelligence was always there. The system was in the way."

The difference between SpaceX and NASA is not talent. NASA has extraordinary talent. The difference is the time between a thought and a test. SpaceX compresses it. NASA elongates it. The same engineer produces 10x more at SpaceX than at NASA because the bottleneck was never the engineer. It was the meetings about the meetings about the work.

text:
I've been coding with Gemini 4 Argon today and I actually completely forgot about the character traits Gemini models have when coding. I haven't used Gemini extensively since the 2.5 Pro, 3.0 Pro, and 3.1 Pro days back last year, so it really reminded me of how they behave.
They just love to structure code in a certain way and add comments. Not too long either - mostly neat one-liner comments, which is a good thing if anything. I kind of like it. I'm not even certain if the code works yet, which is the classic Gemini trait, but it's just nice to look at code, if that makes sense.

When you compare it to the other models, their habits are wildly different:
 1. The Claude models are kind of interesting. When they do comment, they are multi-line and a bit extensive. Opus 5 wrote some of the worst code I have ever read in my life - it would just write absolute slop. Opus 5.5 really toned it down, though it still loves doing multi-line comments and structures things in a very simplistic fashion, yet somehow produces the most powerful code. Opus 5.5 was just amazing.
2. GPT, on the other hand, writes really esoteric, minimal code. It's verging on slop because you look at it and have no idea what the variables and functions actually do. And GPT hates to comment. Whether it's 6 Astra or 6.1 Sol, you have to specifically tell GPT to comment, which is quite odd.

At least one thing this confirms in my testing of Gemini 4 Argon is that it is not distilled from any other model. Obviously we should expect that, though it's something we've come to take for granted because a lot of other models particularly reek of a Claude smell. When you use things like Kimi or DeepSeek - and DeepSeek in particular is really bad at this - it just reeks of being a Claude-distilled model. Some rare ones are GPT-distilled too. They aren't copies, yet they clearly used GPT or Claude in training.

So it's kind of refreshing to talk to a model that feels unique to its own model lineage. Speaking with Gemini 4 Argon, you can clearly tell this has descended from 3.1 Pro, 3.0 Pro, and 2.5 Pro, the same way talking with GPT 6.1 Sol you can feel it descended from 5.6 Sol. It's quite interesting to see these models have their own unique personality and lineage.

截止10月11日本轮周期BTC的新买家（First Buyers，FB）持有量已达到427w枚。

从绝对数量上看，已经相当于2023年8月中旬的水平。

对比今年8月行情启动前，足足增持了40w枚（占总流通2%）。这意味着在近2个月里，平均每月有20w枚BTC被新投资者买走。

而2023年从1月到8月走完整个“熊牛过期”，FB的持有量增加了34w枚（占总流通1.7%），却花了7个月时间。

且当前BTC价格是23年的2.6倍，FB增持这些筹码所需的资金体量远超当年。

新买家代表了新需求，相比上轮周期这个数据表现更强。

另外，让我有些惊讶（也是惊喜）的是，在9月份这波行情下，竟然出现了久违的“动量买家（Momentum Buyers，MB）”的身影。

这是继今年1月以来的首次出现。

MB的定义是：最近一次余额变动是“高于自身持仓成本买入，并把成本往上抬”的实体，也就是最近一次动作是在自己成本上方加仓的那批人。

MB对趋势的作用相当于“助推剂”，意追高买入人的越多，即认为熊市结束的人越多，市场信心回复的越快。

也正因如此，如果是熊市中的反弹，基本不会看到MB的大幅增长。

BTC不会辜负任何有信念的人。如今，它正按照自己特有的节奏，持续朝前迈进。

text:
USDC规模追平Solana，Hyperliquid为什么不干脆免掉现货手续费？

昨天我们讨论，寻找下一个HYPE，不能只复制积分、空投和发币，还要看奖励结束以后，用户愿不愿意留下来

今天把这个问题再往前推一步

目前 Hyperliquid L1上的USDC供应规模已经与Solana相当

与此同时，@ThinkingUSD 提出了一个更直接的问题：既然现货交易增长不够快，Hyperliquid和Unit为什么不把现货交易费降到零，成为链上交易现货最便宜的地方？
 
这两件事，放在一起看，可能比单独看更有意义

USDC供应相当，不代表两个生态的用户数、应用数量和活跃度都已经相当

但对于Hyperliquid，这些资金除了支持交易，还可能通过储备收益安排，为HYPE提供另一条买盘来源

用户交易，协议获得手续费；符合相关安排的USDC留在平台，对应储备也可能贡献收入

据链上数据 10月14日用于当天计费的国库USDC余额约为58.49亿美元，有效年率约3.31%，对应当天计提约53.01万美元

按照AQAv2规则，相关收益按30天区间累积，再于区间结束后8天发送至Assistance Fund

这意味着，Hyperliquid的收入已经不只取决于用户交易多少次，也开始取决于符合收益安排的资金能留在这里多久

再看同一个30天窗口，差异更直观

储备收益约为1510万美元，占协议收入约18.6%；现货协议收入约为210万美元，占约2.6%，储备收益，已经是同期现货协议收入的约7倍

这不是说储备收益可以完全替代交易手续费，但它确实让 @ThinkingUSD 的建议，有了可以计算的讨论基础

如果现货手续费不再是唯一的收入来源，平台是否可以降低交易费用，吸引更多用户和资产进来，再通过资金沉淀、永续合约和其他服务获得收入？

普通现货账户目前的基础吃单费率为0.070%，挂单费率为0.040%，实际费用还会受到交易等级和优惠等因素影响

这个设想是否划算，可以先算一笔静态账

假设放弃当前约210万美元的月度现货协议收入，平均每天少收约7万美元

按照今天约3.31%的有效年率计算，需要额外持续约7.7亿美元的合资格计费余额，才能通过新增储备收益补回这部分收入

这只是协议层的简化测算，没有计入部署者收益、其他成本，以及新增用户可能带来的其他业务收入

但它把问题变具体了：降费以后，能不能让额外约7.7亿美元的合资格USDC，持续留在Hyperliquid？

注意，是额外增加的资金，原本就存在的储备收益，不能直接拿来证明降费划算，因为不降费时，平台同样可以获得这些收入

如果用户只是因为免费而增加交易次数，却没有带来更多资金沉淀，零费率本身并不会产生新的现货手续费。平台可能得到一个更漂亮的成交量数字，却失去一部分原本用于回购的收入

反过来，如果更低的费用能够吸引持续使用的用户，带来更深的盘口、更多资产和更长期的资金留存，那么少收的现货费用，就可能成为获取用户和资金的成本

这也是我认为可以讨论降费，但不能直接认定“零费率一定正确”的原因

交易员留下来，靠的是产品，费用只是交易成本的一部分，点差、滑点、盘口深度和资金进出成本，同样重要

零交易费不等于零交易成本，也不会自动带来更好的流动性；Unit的跨链网络费用，与订单簿交易费用也不是一回事

因此，我更倾向把降费看成一个需要验证的产品实验，可以从部分主流现货市场的阶段性降费开始，观察用户是否留下、资金是否增加、盘口是否改善，以及新增收入能否覆盖放弃的费用

储备收益也不是永远固定的。利率下降，或者USDC余额减少，这条收入同样会缩水

Hyperliquid现在多了一种选择，但还没有因此获得一张“免费增长”的支票

USDC规模追平Solana，是资金沉淀的一个里程碑；这些资金能不能帮助Hyperliquid把交易做得更便宜、更好，才是下一步的产品问题

为了当下的HYPE回购，保留现货手续费？

还是放弃一部分收入，争取更多用户和资金，最终形成更大的回购能力？

我相信市场自然会作出选择
#HYPE #Hyperliquid #USDC #DeFi

text:
Tim Cook's take on why competitors can't copy Apple is sharper than most people realize.

They start by copying the product. Then they realize the product isn't the hard part.

Cook said it directly: people who try to copy Apple first try to copy what they can see. The hardware. The design. The packaging. And they can get close on all of it.

But the thing that made the product — the organizational culture, the decision-making, the obsessive prioritization — that's invisible from the outside. You can't find it in a teardown.

This is why Apple's moat has held for decades while better-funded competitors kept losing. Samsung had more SKUs. Google had more engineers. Amazon had more distribution. None of it translated into the same output because none of it replicated the same input.

The lesson for founders is uncomfortable: if your competitive advantage is visible in your product, it's already copyable. The real moat is the culture that makes the product — and that takes decades to build, not quarters.

Reverse-engineering the iPhone is an engineering problem. Reverse-engineering how Apple decides what to build is a different problem entirely.

text:
There’s been a lot of discussion on Muse Wonder since the launch. But there are some very interesting aspects that are under-discussed and make this launch unique from the rest of the frontier:

1. Big model smell reporting (goodbye benchmaxxing?): For the first time, a model launch measured and reported big model smell which basically shows how the model does on tasks it targeted in post-training vs tasks it didn’t. 
It’s essentially a guard against “benchmaxxed” models. I haven’t seen another frontier lab put this in a launch post, and I think all labs should start reporting it, ideally with the held-out tasks named.

2. Active focus: Muse Wonder is built to not give up when it hits real-world blockers, to keep trying alternative approaches and adapt to new information, while checking in before important actions. For instance, if a dinner reservation fails or a form throws an error, it tries another route on its own. Every lab trains for persistence, but Meta measures it on everyday personal tasks like housing, travel, IT and finance, not just coding. That’s what makes Wonder a good fit for assistants like Muse.

Active memory: carries important context about you across conversations and pulls up the details that matter for whatever you’re doing. This release tested it inside long chats where facts change. 
Early in a long chat you say “my flight is tuesday”, then 50K tokens of other stuff later you say “actually it moved to thursday”. Ask “when do I fly?” and a model with weak memory might say tuesday because it saw that first. Meta built their memory test around exactly this case (and wonder tops it). Imo this stale info problem is the hardest part of memory, way harder than just remembering stuff. 

Memory+focus are so important for assistants. Muse will eat the world.

支持版本升级、跨技术栈逐模块重写、架构重建。验证环节包括：

旧代码能运行时，用相同输入跑新旧系统，由脚本比较输出。

故意改坏一行代码，确认测试真的能报错。
