text:
The analysis point of this tweet is: $BORDR fundamentals are strengthening, and the market is starting to reprice the programmable token standard on Solana.

6Mix12LiHrQFojaQEnfPUC65Qkwd6X4Y5Qg93oFbordr 

Compared with our previous analyses, I believe Bordrless’s fundamentals have genuinely improved. What matters this time is not another batch of token-launch features, but the project’s attempt to redefine what a token can be on Solana: not merely an asset that records balances, but one that can carry its own execution rules and enforce them during transactions.

That is the central idea behind Bordrless’s latest article, “Every Solana Token Is the Same Token.”

In the traditional Solana ecosystem, most SPL tokens rely on a generic Token Program to manage balances and transfers. Token-2022 introduced extensions such as transfer hooks, but many complex mechanisms—including taxes, buybacks, rewards, burns, and automated distributions—still require external bots, servers, or other programs to operate.

Bordrless is trying to change that by making the token itself part of the rule-execution process, then connecting transactions, holder state, and fund management through its own DEX and Companion programs.

It does not automatically add features to every existing Solana token. Instead, it establishes a separate token standard that allows newly launched tokens to support more sophisticated economic mechanisms.

The important development is that Bordrless is connecting its Token Standard, DEX, Companions, and Workshop into a complete infrastructure stack.

Token hooks can execute rules during transfers, minting, and burning, while recording certain information about each holder, such as entry price, holding duration, and rewards already paid. They can deduct fees from transferred amounts or reject transactions that violate predefined rules, but they cannot independently obtain a user’s signature or move more assets than the original operation allows.

However, a transfer hook alone cannot necessarily determine whether a transfer represents a buy, a sell, or an ordinary wallet transfer. That is why Bordrless built its own DEX, where pool hooks can access the full transaction context, including direction, amount, price, trader, recipient, and pool state, and enforce rules before and after a swap.

This creates a path for mechanisms that previously depended on project promises or off-chain scripts to become part of transaction execution itself.

The platform already supports creator fees, sniper fees of up to 80% during the first 30 seconds, different buy and sell rates, buy-side burns, maximum wallet limits, early-buyer locks, and SOL rewards for holders.

Companions manage creator-fee treasuries and can execute predefined strategies involving market making, buybacks, burns, holder rewards, and game-related spending. Hooks enforce rules and record state during transactions, while Companions manage funds according to those rules. Together, they reduce the need for project teams to rely entirely on external bots running continuously.

Bordrless has also opened up its SDK and Workshop. Developers can use Rust, the SDK, or AI coding agents such as Claude Code and Cursor to build their own hooks and companions, then submit source code and testing materials for review. Approved components can be selected by other token launchers, and developers can earn 50% of the creator fees generated by subsequent launches that use their components.

This means ecosystem growth no longer has to depend entirely on the official team shipping more features. Bordrless is attempting to create a system in which third-party developers supply components, other launchers reuse them, and developers earn revenue when their work gets adopted.

If this structure takes off, Bordrless’s competitive position could expand beyond a launchpad into infrastructure capable of supporting many different token mechanisms. That is what makes it more interesting than an ordinary launchpad.

And this time, the progress is not limited to a stronger narrative. Platform metrics have also improved.

In our previous analyses, the website showed 93 total launches and approximately $222.5K in 24-hour trading volume. The latest snapshot shows 114 launches and approximately $469K in 24-hour volume. Cumulative holder distributions increased from 28.5 SOL to 37.6 SOL, cumulative launch fees rose from 99.4 SOL to 159.8 SOL, and the reported cumulative value of rule-triggered burns increased from 17 SOL to 22.5 SOL.

These figures indicate that launches, trading activity, and economic mechanisms are operating in practice. The simultaneous increase in launches and trading volume is particularly meaningful compared with simply announcing new features.

However, these are website snapshots taken at different times, not a continuous independently audited dataset. Automated strategies may also contribute to trading volume, so platform turnover should not be treated as equivalent to genuine buying and selling by independent users.

The website’s displayed BORDR buyback value has also increased from approximately $9.31K to $26.26K, but this requires caution. According to the official tokenomics documentation, the displayed dollar value represents bridged BORDR held in the treasury at the current market price. A rising token price can increase that figure by itself, so it cannot be interpreted as proof that actual buyback spending has increased by 2.75 times. The figures that matter are the SOL actually spent, the number of tokens purchased, and the corresponding on-chain transactions.

This brings us to BORDR’s value-capture mechanism.

According to the official tokenomics, BORDR has a fixed total supply of 1 billion tokens. Half of protocol revenue remains in the treasury for operating expenses, while the other half is used to buy back BORDR. The purchased tokens are bridged into the treasury and held; they are not burned. The buyback process is executed by an off-chain keeper, with the official mechanism designed to run every 10 minutes. If the keeper stops operating, incoming revenue remains in the treasury until further processing.

Therefore, BORDR’s economic thesis is based on potential recurring buying pressure generated by protocol revenue, not deflation through token burns.

For product growth to translate into stronger token demand, it must generate sustained protocol revenue that leads to actual buybacks. Higher platform trading volume does not mean every dollar of turnover becomes protocol revenue, and the website’s displayed buyback value is not the same as the amount spent on purchases during the current period.

So why did BORDR suddenly rally?

My interpretation is that the move likely reflects a combination of a stronger narrative, product delivery, and growing platform activity rather than a single tweet acting as the sole catalyst.

The latest article reframes Bordrless from a platform for launching tokens with taxes and rewards into a programmable token standard. That gives the market a different way to value the project. Traders are no longer looking only at the number of launches; they are beginning to consider whether other developers will adopt the standard to build their own token economics.

Meanwhile, SDK 0.10.0 has been released, and Companion and scripting capabilities have continued to improve. This indicates that the product is being delivered rather than remaining on a roadmap. Combined with the increases in launches and trading volume, these developments give the market a reason to price in potential ecosystem expansion ahead of time.

I believe the market is primarily betting on three things.

First, Solana could gain a token standard capable of supporting complex economic mechanisms. If developers build custom taxes, rewards, automated market-making strategies, and treasury-management systems on top of Bordrless, it could become infrastructure used by applications rather than just another launchpad.

Second, AI coding agents could lower the barrier to building on-chain mechanisms. Developers can publish components through the SDK and Workshop, then earn a share of fees when other projects adopt them. If independent developers, reusable components, and actual deployments continue to grow, a genuine network effect could emerge.

Third, platform growth could translate into BORDR demand through protocol revenue and buybacks. More launches and trading activity could generate more revenue and increase the funds available for buybacks. But because purchased tokens are held in the treasury rather than burned, the key is growth in actual revenue and the number of tokens bought—not simply describing the mechanism as ongoing deflation.

Going forward, I would focus on four areas.

The first is third-party developer adoption. SDK downloads do not equal independent developers. More meaningful indicators include the number of developers who successfully deploy components, the number of hooks and companions reused by other projects, and the fees those components actually generate.

The second is integration with external trading venues. Axiom has already provided an external trading entry point, but the broader distribution thesis depends on whether more terminals and aggregators integrate and how much incremental trading volume they bring.

The third is whether platform trading volume and protocol revenue continue to grow together. Reaching 114 launches and approximately $469K in 24-hour volume is encouraging, but automated trading must be distinguished from genuine user demand before the figures can validate sustainable revenue growth.

The fourth is whether buybacks can be independently verified. Only by checking actual on-chain spending, purchased token quantities, and treasury balances can we determine how much platform growth is translating into genuine buying pressure for BORDR.

The risks remain significant. Bordrless uses a separate token standard, meaning other trading venues must support its execution rules. Greater technical capability does not automatically mean lower adoption barriers. Open development also introduces code-quality and security risks, while automated trading strategies can contribute to headline volume. Given the sharp price increase, the market may already be pricing in a substantial portion of the anticipated ecosystem growth.

My conclusion is that Bordrless’s fundamentals have strengthened compared with our previous analyses, particularly in the completeness of its product architecture, the delivery of its SDK and Companion capabilities, and the growth in launches, trading activity, and reported economic-mechanism execution.

The central bet behind this rally is whether Bordrless can evolve from a technically differentiated launchpad into a programmable token standard that third-party developers consistently adopt across Solana.

But product progress and commercial validation must remain separate. The latest article presents a more complete explanation of the architecture, while growth in launches and trading activity provides encouraging evidence. Neither, on its own, proves that a developer network effect has already formed.

What ultimately determines whether BORDR deserves further repricing is sustained adoption of third-party components, the conversion of platform activity into recurring protocol revenue, and transparent evidence that buybacks are growing alongside the ecosystem.

If those indicators continue improving, Bordrless could evolve from a launchpad into infrastructure supported by a real developer ecosystem and recurring revenue. If price and attention continue rising while adoption and revenue fail to keep pace, however, the rally will be more likely to reflect expectations being priced in ahead of fundamentals.

quoted_text:
$BORDR Fundamentals Are Strengthening, but the Next Stage Depends on Whether the Ecosystem Can Truly Gain Traction

6Mix12LiHrQFojaQEnfPUC65Qkwd6X4Y5Qg93oFbordr 

Bordrless's fundamentals have improved significantly. The changes go beyond adding a few features. The project is expanding from its own token standard, DEX, and launchpad into an open developer platform and an external trading distribution network.

What we can confirm so far is that product delivery and infrastructure development have made progress. However, the scale of the developer ecosystem, the actual trading growth generated by external integrations, and the long-term value capture of BORDR still need to be validated with data.

The most notable aspect of this update is that three developments are happening simultaneously: Axiom integration is live, the SDK and Workshop are lowering barriers to developer participation, and mainnet programs have added fee distribution and scripting capabilities. If these components work together, Bordrless could evolve from a technically differentiated launchpad into infrastructure that other projects actively use.

What Has Changed in This Update?

1. From Its Own Trading Interface to External Trading Distribution

Axiom has integrated the Bordrless Token Standard and DEX. According to the official team, all tokens launched on Bordrless can now be traded on Axiom while retaining the corresponding Hooks. This means trading is no longer limited to Bordrless's own website, and other trading terminals and aggregators are also planned for integration.

This is one of the most important changes in this update. It addresses product distribution rather than simply improving the interface. The more external trading entry points there are, the more opportunities launched projects have to reach traders. However, completing an integration does not guarantee significant additional trading volume. That still needs to be demonstrated through actual trading data.

2. From an Official Development Product to an Open Developer Ecosystem

The SDK allows developers to create custom Hooks, trading pools, and Bonding Curves. They can also add liquidity and use bridged assets as quote assets. Hooks can execute custom rules during token transfers and trading, such as taxes, holder rewards, transfer restrictions, or burns. Companions manage creator fees according to predefined schedules and rules, supporting functions such as market making and buybacks.

The team is also shifting the Studio development workflow toward developers building independently with AI coding agents such as Claude Code and Cursor, then submitting their work to the Workshop. The platform reviews, builds, simulates, and deploys approved projects. AI explains what the code does and how much it charges in plain language. Approved Hooks and Companions can then be selected by other token launchers, and developers can earn 50% of the creator fees generated by subsequent launches that use their configurations.

This means developers no longer have to be merely users of Bordrless products. They can become providers of ecosystem components. The real growth signal is not how many people download the SDK, but how many third-party tools pass review, get adopted by other launchers, and generate recurring revenue.

3. Mainnet Upgrades Are Improving Fee Distribution and Ecosystem Incentives

The mainnet upgrades announced by the team include the release of SDK 0.10.0; the ability for terminals, bots, and wallets to add integration fees of up to 1% to Bordrless trades they route; the ability to split a token's creator fees among up to 10 wallets at fixed percentages; scripts that can pay SOL to eligible wallets when the launcher enables the feature in advance; and the option for Workshop developers to publish their Hooks with a 0% fee.

These capabilities serve different purposes: monetizing trading entry points, splitting fees among project teams, automating on-chain payments, and encouraging developer participation. Creator-fee distribution and programmable scripts are particularly useful because they allow teams, treasuries, partners, and automated strategies to participate in a project's economic flows.

One distinction matters: integration fees collected by third parties do not automatically become BORDR revenue, and creator fees earned by developers are not equivalent to returns for token holders. These are initially economic mechanisms for the platform and ecosystem participants. They can indirectly benefit BORDR only if they generate revenue that the protocol can capture.

4. A Quick-Trade Panel and Builder Competition Improve User Experience and Incentivize Supply

The new web trading panel floats over the chart and combines buying, selling, preset amounts, estimated tokens received, and trading rules. Trading wallets can sign without an additional prompt. The goal is to let users trade directly while viewing market data and to prepare for future terminal integrations.

The team also announced a $5,000 Builder Race, with the top three projects receiving $2,500, $1,500, and $1,000 after 72 hours. The competition aims to attract early developers to build Hooks, Companions, and other tools, but the prize money itself does not prove that sustained ecosystem demand already exists.

Following these updates, the product's core positioning has become clearer. Bordrless is not just a launchpad. It is building its own token standard, DEX, and launchpad on Solana, allowing token rules to be executed through Hooks. The official documentation lists the mainnet programs and explains how they differ from Token-2022 transfer hooks.

External integrations are also beginning to address the distribution bottleneck. An in-house DEX can execute complex rules, but if tokens depend entirely on the project's own website, trader reach and liquidity may be limited. Axiom's integration demonstrates that external distribution is no longer entirely theoretical. The next question is whether other terminals and aggregators follow through and how much trading volume they bring.

Finally, developer incentives are becoming more complete. The SDK, AI coding agents, Workshop review and deployment, reusable Hooks, and creator-fee sharing are beginning to form a loop. In theory, developers have an incentive to build better trading rules and fee-management tools, while launchers can use those tools directly. The wider the adoption, the more fees developers can earn.

However, open development capabilities do not mean a developer network effect has already formed. Sustained third-party output, genuine adoption, and verifiable fee distributions are needed before this mechanism can be considered commercially validated.

Has BORDR's Value Capture Improved Alongside the Product?

A stronger product does not necessarily translate into proportionally stronger demand for its token.

According to the official Tokenomics documentation, half of protocol revenue is retained in the treasury for operating expenses such as development and deployment, while the other half is used to buy back BORDR every 10 minutes. The purchased tokens are bridged into the treasury and held; they are not burned. The team also states that buybacks are executed by an off-chain keeper operated by Bordrless. If the keeper stops, revenue remains in the treasury until processing resumes.

Current project metrics displayed on the Bordrless website:

Total launches: 93
Platform 24-hour trading volume: $222.50K
Displayed cumulative buybacks: $9.31K in BORDR
Cumulative fees from launch rules: 99.4 SOL

These figures indicate that the product is generating real trading activity, launch fees, and buyback activity rather than remaining a white-paper project. However, 93 launches are not enough to establish a strong network effect. The $9.31K in buybacks also needs to be evaluated against the token's market cap and future protocol revenue to assess its actual impact on supply and demand.

Protocol fees primarily come from LP fees on launch pools, launch fees, and protocol fees on regular DEX pools. The typical rules listed in the official documentation include a 0.3% LP fee on launch-pool trades, a 0.01 SOL fee per launch, and a 1% protocol fee on the quote-asset amount traded in regular pools.

Therefore, the important question is not how many new fee mechanisms are added, but whether external integrations can expand effective trading volume and consistently convert that activity into protocol treasury revenue and actual buybacks. The up-to-1% integration fee that terminals can charge belongs to the integrators; it does not all flow into the BORDR buyback mechanism.

What Is the Market Betting On?

I believe the market is primarily trading three narratives.

First, a programmable token standard on Solana.

Bordrless aims to make rules for taxes, rewards, burns, and holding restrictions take effect directly during token transfers or trading, rather than requiring each project to maintain its own off-chain scripts. This is its most important technical narrative relative to ordinary launchpads.

Second, ecosystem expansion driven by AI developers.

If developers can use AI coding agents to build their own Hooks, publish them through the Workshop, and have other launchers adopt them, the supply of ecosystem tools could grow rapidly. What the market may be pricing in ahead of time is the potential developer network, rather than developer revenue already realized today.

Third, a growth loop between external trading distribution and fee-based buybacks.

More terminal integrations could bring more trading. A wider range of tools could attract more launchers, increasing platform activity and revenue. The protocol's allocation of half its revenue to BORDR buybacks also creates a potential channel of demand linked to the platform's business.

Among these three narratives, the token standard already has tangible product support, the distribution network is only beginning to expand, and developer network effects and sustained revenue growth remain unproven.

What Could Become the Next Catalysts for Price Appreciation?

I believe the real catalysts would be:

More terminals and aggregators officially integrating. Axiom is already live, and the team has said more terminals and aggregators would integrate that week. Concrete integrations, trading volume generated by those integrations, and verifiable protocol revenue would be meaningful catalysts. Announcements alone are not enough.

Sustained adoption of third-party Hooks and Companions. SDK 0.10.0, the Workshop, developer-fee sharing, and the $5,000 Builder Race could encourage more participation. If more third-party tools are adopted by other projects and generate recurring developer revenue, the ecosystem narrative would gain further validation.

Companions and fee automation becoming fully operational. Managing creator fees through scripts could support automated market making, buybacks, and other on-chain strategies, allowing funds generated by launches to be actively deployed rather than sitting idle. However, some screenshots described Companion upgrades as “coming soon,” while official development documentation linked them to the October 12, 2026 program upgrade. Mainnet deployment and actual invocation records should be verified before treating the entire feature set as fully operational.

Sustained growth in protocol revenue and buybacks. This is the catalyst most directly connected to token value capture. If platform trading volume grows alongside treasury revenue and verifiable on-chain buyback amounts continue to increase, the market would have a stronger basis for valuing BORDR as an asset supported by business activity rather than just a technical narrative.

My conclusion is that this update represents a genuine improvement in fundamentals, but not yet completed commercial validation. Bordrless is moving beyond its programmable token standard and in-house DEX by adding external distribution, third-party development, fee automation, and ecosystem incentives.

The next stage depends on three things: whether other terminals bring incremental trading volume, whether third-party developers' tools achieve sustained adoption, and whether additional trading activity translates into recurring protocol revenue and buybacks.

If all three improve, stronger fundamentals could become a sustained catalyst for the token. If product announcements and downloads grow without corresponding adoption and revenue, market expectations may run ahead of reality.

A router meant to reach one API had quietly become an API anyone could steer.

In Pashov Audit Group’s Initia review, the team—including Carlos as an external contractor—found two unauthenticated wildcard routes forwarding raw HTTP requests to the Skip API.

There was no path, method, header, or body filtering. A caller could choose arbitrary outbound API calls and payloads.

The fix restricted the proxy to an allowlist, validated request bodies, and required authentication. Initia resolved the finding.

text:
近期 Ledger 爆发的经销商供应链攻击事件，让大家对冷钱包的安全产生了焦虑。

社媒上因此重新流行起各种“拿台旧 iPhone 断网当冷钱包”的方案。

但简单把旧手机开个飞行模式，真的就绝对安全了吗？

Onekey 的@ohyishi 今天写的这篇长文教程值得一读，里面其实提到了一个底线：

如果你真想拿 iPhone 存大额资产，硬件至少得从 iPhone 17 起步，系统必须在 iOS 27 以上，而且每一到两年就要迁移一次设备。

同时这个文章里还有些其他干货，建议收藏：

1.老旧 iPhone 为什么不能用？
更老的苹果机型（如 A5-A11芯片）存在 checkm8 等无法通过系统升级修复的硬件级 BootROM 漏洞；

直到 iPhone 17 搭载 A19 芯片，苹果才首次在硬件层引入了内存完整性强制（MIE）和增强型内存标记（EMTE），能从底层阻断灰产取证工具常用的内存损坏攻击链，这是老手机靠升系统永远补不上的硬件代差。

2.非要用的话，不用时必须彻底关机
在成熟的手机取证产业面前，手机分为 BFU（开机后首次解锁前）和 AFU（首次解锁后）两种状态。

只要你开机输过一次密码，哪怕重新锁屏，部分保护级别的密钥依然会留在内存里，配合特定漏洞链就能被提取数据。只有彻底关机，才能让手机退回最安全的 BFU 状态。

3.设备密码的位数，决定了暴力破解的物理上限
iPhone 的密码与硬件 UID 绑定，每次尝试被迫耗时约 80 毫秒，无法把闪存拆下来用 GPU 集群并行跑字典，所以看着比较安全。

但这依然取决于密码复杂度。如果跳过次数限制，6 位纯数字密码平均 11 小时就能跑完；而一个 12 位随机大小写字母+数字的密码，穷举时间是：

 8.18 万亿年。

4. 别以为断网了就完事了，USB 也是攻击面
不要把助记词拍成照片或放进备忘录，也不要在日常用过的旧手机上直接断网建钱包，因为无法确认它断网前是否已经中招。
哪怕网络全关，取证设备依然可以通过模拟 USB 外设去攻击内核驱动。

总结一下：

如果你确实想配置一台 iPhone 签名机，Yishi 给出的标准操作是买一台全新的 iPhone 17 或更新机型（不绑日常 Apple ID、不恢复旧备份、只在设置里彻底关掉 Wi-Fi 和蓝牙），

设置 12 位以上的随机字母数字密码，选用真正做到了密钥独立加密保护的钱包 App，平时直接关机存放。

text:
如果不是被起诉，我们永远都不会知道，Anthropic在2021年就已经完美地预言了现在的AI发展。

我刚看完这份 @AnthropicAI  在诉讼中曝光的内部文件，叫《Concise Research Roadmap》，最后更新于2021年7月。

这份文件由Anthropic联创Jared Kaplan撰写，里面还保留了 @DarioAmodei  、 @NotTomBrown  、 @AmandaAskell  、 @ch402  等一批核心研究人员的内部评论。

文件上甚至还标着「Highly Confidential–Attorneys' Eyes Only」（高度机密，仅限律师查阅）。

我仔细看完之后，真的有点感慨。

因为今天我们讨论的Coding Agent、Tool Use、长上下文、RL、自动化反馈，甚至Agent的安全问题，在这份五年前的研究路线图里，基本都已经出现了。

而且远不只是一些模糊的概念。

首先，Anthropic在2021年就已经明确提出，要做一个具备软件工程师能力的AI助手。
在文件第一页，他们就写道，希望开发一个通用AI助手，可以通过对话帮助用户创建、编辑和解释软件。
包括开发浏览器插件、编写函数、发现Bug、设计API、讨论代码风格和最佳实践等等。
最终目标是让AI展现出一名软件工程师同事所具备的能力。
你会发现，这不就是今天Claude Code正在做的事情吗？
更有意思的是，他们当时就认为，要实现这个目标，需要大规模生成模型、长期记忆，以及通过自动化奖励和人类反馈进行强化学习。
甚至连Roadmap都已经想得非常清楚了。

第二，他们当时就专门把RL for Tool Use列成了一项重要研究方向。
研究的核心是让大语言模型学会使用工具，理解环境和目标，并通过强化学习不断改进。
当时他们提出的具体任务包括搜索、printf调试等，还准备研究工具使用能不能让模型获得比监督学习更好的Scaling效果。
今天Agent领域讨论的一大堆问题，五年前他们就已经开始思考了。

第三，最让我意外的是，他们当年甚至就在讨论Coding Agent的产品形态。
Tom Brown提出，代码仓库浏览是一个简单而有价值的工具，可以从这里开始。
Nelson Elhage则表示，如果AI能够主动查找项目中的类型定义，会是一项很强的能力。
Andy Jones进一步提出了两条不同的路线。
一条是打造最优秀的AI程序员，另一条是先验证AI使用工具的能力。
Dario Amodei的回答是：短期优先后者，长期优先前者。
而且同一份文件里，Sam McCandlish就已经开始担心，如何安全地部署非沙箱化工具。
Dario特别强调了部署阶段执行代码的工具。
你再看看今天围绕Coding Agent的Sand box、权限控制和代码执行安全的一系列讨论。
真的很难不感慨。

第四，他们很早就意识到，模型能力和Alignment不能脱节。
Amanda Askell在评论里担心，如果能力研究集中在代码领域，而对齐研究只关注自然语言，那么未来可能会出现模型能力越来越强，但对齐研究无法充分覆盖这些能力的情况。
所以她强调，两者应该紧密结合。
这其实也是今天Agent安全研究面临的重要问题。

我觉得这份文件最有意思的地方，是它让我们重新认识了Anthropic这家公司。

2021年的时候，ChatGPT甚至都还没有发布，整个行业对大语言模型未来能做什么，都还没有今天这么明确的认识。

但Anthropic的这群研究人员，已经把软件工程助手作为通向AGI的一个具体研究目标，并且围绕模型规模、数据、长上下文、工具使用、强化学习和安全，制定了一套相当完整的研究路线。

至少从今天回头看，他们对技术发展方向的判断，确实非常超前。

而且更值得注意的是，这份文件讨论的很多问题，直到2026年都还没有被彻底解决。

五年前他们在思考如何让AI成为软件工程师的同事。

五年后，我们已经开始讨论，如何让AI独立完成整个软件工程任务，甚至参与改进自己的模型和研发系统（AKA：RSI）。

有时候AI的发展看起来快得不可思议，但仔细回头看，你会发现，有些人其实很早就已经知道自己要往哪里走了。

text:
Before you ship a vibe-coded site, make Opus 5.5 audit it like a performance team.

Send 4 subagents across these 20 checks:

*Images + fonts*
•⁠  ⁠Convert images to WebP/AVIF and size them correctly  
•⁠  ⁠Use ⁠ next/image ⁠ for large assets  
•⁠  ⁠Lazy-load below-the-fold media  
•⁠  ⁠Prioritize the main above-the-fold image  
•⁠  ⁠Use framework-native font loading  
•⁠  ⁠Keep fonts limited  
•⁠  ⁠Remove unused third-party scripts  
•⁠  ⁠Delay analytics/chat widgets until after load  

*Frontend*
•⁠  ⁠Run a bundle analyzer  
•⁠  ⁠Replace full-library imports with only what you use  
•⁠  ⁠Dynamically import heavy charts, editors and maps  
•⁠  ⁠Fetch homepage data on the server  
•⁠  ⁠Stream AI responses  
•⁠  ⁠Use skeletons while loading  

*Database + APIs*
•⁠  ⁠Add indexes for filtered/sorted columns and RLS fields  
•⁠  ⁠Use ⁠ (select auth.uid()) ⁠ in RLS policies  
•⁠  ⁠Kill N+1 queries  
•⁠  ⁠Paginate long lists  
•⁠  ⁠Cache shared API responses, never user-specific ones  
•⁠  ⁠Move emails, image processing and reports to background jobs  

*Servers + network*
•⁠  ⁠Keep functions near the database region  
•⁠  ⁠Use static pages or ISR where possible  
•⁠  ⁠Parallelize independent API calls  
•⁠  ⁠Test on low-end Android + slow 4G  

Then paste this:

“Send one subagent per group to check it without editing anything, and note which file each issue is in and which page it affects. Run the database subagent at high effort. Before changing anything, run a production build or preview, then run Lighthouse three times in mobile mode on the homepage and the two or three slowest pages and note the median. Then fix everything yourself from their lists, measure again the same way, and give me the before-and-after numbers. Don’t remove features to gain speed. Ask me before removing dependencies, changing the deploy region, or changing the database.”

其实我们这个行业，最喜欢干的事就是复刻。

有了狗狗币，就有了一大堆 Meme 狗、Meme 猫。

有了 Uniswap，就有了 SushiSwap。

有了 https://t.co/sZ5zzJFOkK，就有了 LetsBonk。

有了 https://t.co/i7VJ044Wgu，就有了 Stars Arena。

有了 ORDI，就有了 SATS、RATS，以及后来一大堆跟风的 BRC-20 铭文。

基本上任何一个新叙事、新模式，只要被市场验证有利可图，很快就会冒出一大堆模仿者。

但是你有没有想过，为什么 TapeOut @TapeOutWorld 出现快两个月了，似乎还没有出现真正意义上的复刻项目，甚至连 $BEM 都没有多少类似概念的竞争代币？

我觉得一个很重要的原因，可能就是这玩意太复杂了。

绝大多数 Crypto 项目的创新，其实更多集中在商业模式、经济模型以及产品机制上，更容易去复刻。

但是 TapeOut @TapeOutWorld 实际上是在尝试从最基础的逻辑门开始，在链上重新构建一套可以制造电路、运行计算、组合处理器，甚至支撑各种应用的基础设施。

你可以复刻它的代币经济模型，可以模仿它的挖矿机制，但想把这一整套东西复刻出来其实很难。

除了基本的开发者懂智能合约外，还要理解数字电路、计算机体系结构，以及如何将这些东西与链结合起来。

复制一个已经存在的产品，却未必能够复制创造这个产品的思维方式，持续创造新东西的能力，以及如此强大的社区凝聚力。

所以在一个绝大多数人都忙着复制别人成功经验的行业里，从底层开始创造新东西的人才是最稀缺的。

当然或许还有一个原因：

就是  TapeOut 或许可以有第二个，但 @Blonskr 这样的脑子，未必能找到第二个。哈哈哈哈。

text:
anthropic git'i bırakmış.

çünkü kendi version control sistemini yazmış. adı da scion. sebebi de yazıyı okuyunca anlaşılıyo.

claude code vb gibi coding agentlar sayesinde artık kod yazmak bottleneck değil, yazılan kodu yönetmek. 

anthropic ekibinin git’inde mayıs 2026'da günde 2 bin 500 merge varken eylülde 30 bini geçmiş. 5 ayda neredeyse 12 kat olmuş. 

monorepo'nun sadece main branch geçmişi 100 gb civarı olmuş. sadece ci için günde 25 milyon checkout yapılıyormuş, agent'lar ve developer'lar hariç. 

git'i ayakta tutmak için yüzlerce mirror çalıştırmak zorunda kalmışlar. yamamışlar, bantlamışlar ama yetmemiş.

çünkü git biz insanlar için geliştirildi. git decentralized bi sistem, her client offline çalışabilsin diye tasarlanmış, herkes repo'nun tam kopyasını taşıyor. ama anthropic'te repo'ya bağlananların neredeyse hepsi zaten hep online olan ai agent'lar ve job'lar. o zaman neden herkes koca repo'yu sırtında taşımak zorunda kalsın ki diye düşünmüşler.

o yüzden commit, merge, rebase, diff ne varsa server'a taşımışlar. client sadece ihtiyacı olan dosyayı çekiyor.

sonuçta şu olmuş: checkout dakikalardan saniyelere inmiş, altyapının cpu ve memory ihtiyacı eski mirror düzenine göre 200 kat azalmış, ci'da da %25 cpu kazanmışlar.

daha ilginci, scion'u ve antique dedikleri code review sistemini 7 kişi, 5 ayda yapmış. 

normalde şirketlerin aylarını hatta belki aylarını alacak bi iş bu.

claude reis önce kod üretimini o kadar hızlandırmış ki altyapı yetmemiş. sonra o altyapının yerine geçecek sistemi yazmayı da hızlandırmış.

ekipteki herkes claude'un kod yazmada kendisinden iyi olduğunu kabul ediyormuş. (hiç ego yapmamışlar(!))

review yaparken satır satır kod okumayı bırakmışlar, "bu değişiklik ne yapmaya çalışıyor" ona bakıyorlarmış.

bu arada scion git'in yerine geçecek bi şey değilmiş zaten bunu kendileri de söylüyor. 

bence asıl mesele git'in eskimesi değil, 

software development lifecycle'ın insan ölçeğinde tasarlanmış olması. binlerce agent aynı anda kod basmaya başlayınca sadece kodu nasıl yazdığımız değil, nasıl sakladığımız, test ettiğimiz ve merge ettiğimiz de değişmek zorunda.

Key allegations from the complaint (N.D. Cal.):

• On or about Sept. 30, OpenAI’s technical surveillance team found a surreptitious audio recording device plugged into a USB port on the back of a TV in an executive conference room. It was concealed in toilet paper, installed around Sept. 28, and its contents were encrypted.

• The room is used for highly confidential technical, commercial, and strategic discussions. Alfozan had no authority to access it or attend meetings there. CCTV showed him near the room on multiple dates beforehand.

• On Oct. 5 he entered the room and appeared to look behind the TV. That same day he left an unattended bag in another room containing his wallet, ID, and a second similar recording device.

• Before installation, he queried internal tools about building addresses, meeting rooms, room capacities, calendars, and locations of leadership and external partner meetings.

• A chatbot account tied to his spouse (sharing multiple identifiers with his own) submitted prompts between Sept. 24–30 about building a continuous audio recorder, encrypting the SD card, concealing the device, adding Wi-Fi/remote access, and the specific device’s MAC address.

He’s been charged with using or attempting to use a device to intercept oral communications (18 U.S.C. § 2511). 

If convicted: up to 5 years, $250,000 fine, and 3 years supervised release.

Arrested Oct. 9, initial appearance Oct. 13, remains in custody. Detention hearing set for Oct. 19.

OpenAI says it used its models to help identify him, coordinated the termination with the FBI (access was progressively restricted beforehand), and has no indications of model-weight, source-code, or customer-data exfiltration. 

U.S. Attorney described it as a national-security matter; FBI has flagged protection of American AI innovation as a high counterintelligence priority.

Friendly reminder that physical + digital insider-threat controls matter even when the goal isn’t classic IP exfiltration. Wiretap charges don’t require successful data theft. Toilet-paper concealment and a second device left in a bag with ID are not sophisticated tradecraft.

(Complaint details drawn from SF Standard reporting, DOJ/USAO Northern District of California statements, and OpenAI’s own post.)

为什么说Gemini写文好，有的大v是不会懂的。什么破折号，外文讲法，雷霆比喻，这些问题的确是有，但为什么即使有这些Gemini依然强大，无伤大雅？
因为写文自己娱乐看的话，这类八股都是可以简单脑内屏蔽的，而如果真的作为交付使用的话，任何负责任的写手必然要走一遍Agent修文流程或者手改流程。
这时候你就会发现，Gemini的八股其实是显式八股，按照规律去除是十分容易的。
而评价一个模型写作好不好，肯定不是看它什么都不改直出写的好不好（真的直出你即使强如opus55也是很难合格的）
是看他核心内容的可用性，整体调性是否符合人类需求。

也就是过滤掉八股之后剩下的东西有没有趣，是否具备符合人类惊喜感期待感与情绪曲线，价值观，这些才是最重要的。

可以这么比较：

Gemini：八股多，去掉八股难度低，剩下精华情感充沛，变化多端，极为美味

Claude Opus46/55：八股极少，整体性很强也不好改，正文中庸细腻，变化略少

其他模型：整体就是由八股和伪人抽象构成的，去掉抽象和八股就什么也剩不下了。

text:
The $DOPE team has taken the original DOPE meme narrative a step further by turning it into a product: a meme-style asset basket that automatically rewards holders with multiple tokens.

33jENUQnjoitkMFpvNJcSHyLAHFWJuHwT6E3E8CNpump 

If DOPE initially gained attention from the AI accident that cost nearly $1,900 and produced just one Doge × Pepe image, the website is now taking that story one step further.

Holders of DOPE automatically receive three reward tokens: ANTHROPIC, DOGE, and PEPE, with no manual claiming required. The project describes this mechanism as “RWA-style rewards” for memes. It is not an RWA in the traditional sense of being backed by real-world assets, but rather a product concept borrowed from the idea of holding one asset and automatically receiving a basket of related assets.

What makes this design interesting is that DOPE is no longer just a hybrid meme character. It now has an additional economic narrative that can continue to spread.

Doge and Pepe represent the two cultural sources of the character, while ANTHROPIC connects it to the original AI API incident. Together, the three names form an easy-to-understand combination: hold a meme accidentally created by AI, and receive tokens associated with its story and origins.

This adds another layer to the narrative beyond simply repeating the story of spending $1,900 to generate one image. The original incident attracts attention, the hybrid character provides recognition, and the reward mechanism attempts to give people an ongoing reason to hold.

From a product perspective, the idea is to encourage users to do more than simply buy and wait for the price to rise. Instead, they receive reward tokens while holding. Automatic distribution with no claiming required also lowers the barrier to participation.

However, it is important to distinguish the design presented on the project’s website from economic value that has actually been verified.

The website displays approximately 549 SOL in reward value and around 125,900 payouts. However, it explicitly labels these figures as an approximate baseline used while the OTC data feed is unreachable, rather than a verified live snapshot. Rewards are distributed in tokens, not directly in SOL. Therefore, these figures cannot be treated as verified cash payouts worth 549 SOL, nor can the actual value of the rewards be determined solely from the number of distributions.

More importantly, the names of the reward tokens and their connection to the narrative do not mean they have stable value. To determine whether this mechanism genuinely strengthens DOPE’s fundamentals, we still need to verify where the rewards come from, how they are distributed, whether distributions continue consistently, and whether the reward tokens have actual market liquidity.

I think the most important question is whether this mechanism can turn one-time narrative-driven attention into a more lasting reason to hold.

If the rewards continue, the rules remain transparent, and the community genuinely creates new content around these three tokens, DOPE could evolve from a meme born out of an AI accident into a meme project with a story, a recognizable character, and a holding mechanism.

But if the rewards are merely short-term marketing, or if their actual value falls significantly short of what the website suggests, the mechanism may simply add another layer of packaging to the existing narrative rather than create a genuinely sustainable economic cycle.

For that reason, I see this update as an attempt to turn DOPE’s narrative into a product, rather than proof that its value-capture mechanism has been validated. The next things worth verifying are the on-chain reward distributions, the source of the rewards, actual liquidity, and whether the mechanism continues operating after the initial speculative hype fades.

DOPE initially gained recognition through an absurd AI story. Now it is trying to give holders another reason to stay through an automatic reward mechanism. A compelling story can get someone to buy for the first time; sustained content creation and a credible reward mechanism are what might convince them to stay.

$DOPE 730k dyor

33jENUQnjoitkMFpvNJcSHyLAHFWJuHwT6E3E8CNpump 

okx wallet:https://t.co/BLzoGWIQOb

The token’s narrative originated from a story that went viral on Reddit’s r/ClaudeAI subreddit.

In short, a user accidentally spent nearly $1,900 on Anthropic’s Claude API, only to end up with a single meme.

Here’s what happened: The user asked Claude Code to write a Python script that would generate different captions for a custom hybrid character combining Doge and Pepe, which he called “DOPE.”

The script was supposed to keep generating captions until it had collected 50 unique ones. The API was only responsible for generating the text, while Python would overlay the captions onto local images. He started the script in the morning, thought the initial results looked decent, and went to work, completely forgetting about it.

However, the script contained several serious bugs. It used the wrong model, applied overly strict duplicate checks, and kept retrying whenever a result was classified as a duplicate. These retries did not count toward the number of accepted captions, while the conversation history continued growing, causing token consumption to explode. There was no cap on the number of attempts, no budget limit, and no prompt caching.

As a result, the script ran continuously for around eight hours, making approximately 2,700 requests and consuming roughly 375 million uncached input tokens plus one million output tokens. The final bill came to nearly $1,900.

And after all that, the result was this low-poly, 3D-rendered Shiba Inu standing in an urban landscape reminiscent of the early GTA games.

text:
Before you sign a lease, a job offer or a software contract, run it through this prompt.

It turns a long document into one page: what you're agreeing to, what it costs, which deadlines can hurt you, and what to ask before signing.

Attach the document to Claude and paste this:

"You are reviewing a document I'm about to sign. I am not a lawyer. Read the entire document before answering.

1.⁠ ⁠Summarize what I'm agreeing to in 5 plain-English bullet points.
2.⁠ ⁠List every payment, fee, deposit, penalty and automatic price increase, with the clause number and the exact amount or formula.
3.⁠ ⁠List every deadline and notice period I have to meet, and what happens if I miss it.
4.⁠ ⁠Flag clauses that are unusual, one-sided or hard to undo, such as auto-renewal, early termination, liability, arbitration and data sharing. Quote each clause and explain the risk in one sentence.
5.⁠ ⁠Tell me what a document like this would normally include that this one is missing.
6.⁠ ⁠Write the 5 questions I should ask before signing, most important first.

Rules: quote the document for every claim. If something is unclear or not in the document, say so instead of guessing. Don't give legal advice. Tell me where I should ask a lawyer."

It won't replace a lawyer. It will tell you what to ask one.

The @BUILDCHAIN_HE project builds this through the EU Digital Building Logbook on Decentralized Knowledge Graph (DKG):

→ Access for architects, contractors, owners and regulators

A building outlasts the people who designed, built and renovated it. author: Eth527
quoted_text:
美股持仓想进加密生态，之前是件麻烦事：卖了再买，要交税、要承担价差；不卖的话，两边账户各管各的，资金效率也上不去。对于真正想把已有组合整体搬过来的投资者，卡点不在交易而在迁移本身。Bitget这次上线的rToken股票转仓，针对的就是这个卡点：
1）它支持 3000多只美股和ETF从外部券商直接转入，外部券商发起无本金交割转出到指定的Alpaca综合账户；
2）股票到账后系统直接按持股数量铸造对应rToken，记入现货账户，用户不需要再做额外转换，全程自动化；
3）转入过程 Bitget 端不收费，处理周期大约10个工作日左右。。

和市场上现有的做法比，差别主要体现在覆盖范围和操作路径上。对持仓更分散、包含不同行业或 ETF的组合来说，Bitget这个就非常适用，全部一次性转仓而不是只能支持有限数量的标的。

更关键的是转仓之后的使用场景：rToken进入现货账户后，可以在统一账户体系里直接作为保证金、用于借贷，或接入理财、跟单、策略机器人等产品，而不必先把底层资产卖掉。

对同时在做加密策略、又希望保留美股敞口的人来说，这意味着原本沉淀在传统券商的仓位，有可能变成可调度的资产，而不是单纯“持有不动”。当然股票价格波动会同步影响抵押价值，相关风险需要自己评估。

从产品定位看，这是在尝试把传统股票组合接入加密平台的统一账户和产品体系。覆盖范围够广、路径够简化、后续使用场景足够原生，才有可能支撑真正的投资组合迁移，而不是只服务单只热门标的的交易需求。

随着代币化股票持续扩张，平台之间的差异会越来越明显地体现在“能不能把现有仓位搬进来、搬进来之后还能做什么”上。Bitget这次把覆盖标范围，自动化和资金复用放在同一套流程里，算是把这个方向往前推了一步。

为配合功能上线，Bitget同步做了总价值 100 万美元的SpaceX 股票代币（rSPCX）奖励活动。奖励按首次转仓金额分档，详情看活动链接：https://t.co/okASmyK4sg

text:
为什么说Gemini写文好，有的大v是不会懂的。什么破折号，外文讲法，雷霆比喻，这些问题的确是有，但为什么即使有这些Gemini依然强大，无伤大雅？
因为写文自己娱乐看的话，这类八股都是可以简单脑内屏蔽的，而如果真的作为交付使用的话，任何负责任的写手必然要走一遍Agent修文流程或者手改流程。
这时候你就会发现，Gemini的八股其实是显式八股，按照规律去除是十分容易的。
而评价一个模型写作好不好，肯定不是看它什么都不改直出写的好不好（真的直出你即使强如opus55也是很难合格的）
是看他核心内容的可用性，整体调性是否符合人类需求。

也就是过滤掉八股之后剩下的东西有没有趣，是否具备符合人类惊喜感期待感与情绪曲线，价值观，这些才是最重要的。

可以这么比较：

Gemini：八股多，去掉八股难度低，剩下精华情感充沛，变化多端，极为美味

Claude Opus46/55：八股极少，整体性很强也不好改，正文中庸细腻，变化略少

其他模型：整体就是由八股和伪人抽象构成的，去掉抽象和八股就什么也剩不下了。

text:
美债逼近6%，为什么越便宜反而越有人卖？

10月7日，30年期美债收益率一度升到5.706%，创下2002年以来的新高。很多小伙伴可能觉得，这么高的收益率，长债是不是可以买了？但巴斯曼提醒，如果20年期收益率突破6%，部分机构反而可能需要加快卖出。

问题出在国债期货的交割规则上。卖方可以从一篮子国债中，选择折算后交割成本最低的那只。这套折算规则以6%的收益率为基准，随着市场利率上升，最适合交割的债券可能换成期限更长、对利率更敏感的债券。

巴斯曼在10月13日的报告中测算，相关交割券的久期已经从约11升到13.24，进一步切换后可能超过17。说人话，基金经理一手仓位没加，但同样幅度的利率变化，可能带来更大的盈亏。

对于有风险上限的机构，仓位变得更敏感，就可能需要减仓或增加对冲。于是收益率越涨，部分机构越要卖，新增卖盘又可能把收益率推得更高。这就是负凸性可能放大下跌的方式。

巴斯曼估算，进一步切换带来的额外利率风险，相当于财政部在四个月里多发行约1,100亿美元的20年期国债。

杠杆还可能把这个过程放大。不少基金借钱买入国债现券，同时卖出期货，赚两者之间的小价差。如果波动加大、保证金提高，或者融资变难，它们就可能卖出现券、买回期货来缩小交易，原本的国债买盘也会变成卖盘。

这里最关键的一点是机构可以继续看好长债，却因为风险额度和现金需求，必须先卖掉。愿意等收益率回落，不代表有能力一直等下去。当初硅谷银行面对的就是类似的问题。

影响也会传到债市之外。长端利率持续走高，企业发债、续借和居民房贷都可能更贵。即使美联储没有继续加息，市场也可能先把融资条件收紧。美股高估值需要更强的利润支撑， bitcoin:native  也可能在机构集中降低风险、补充现金时遭遇卖出。

所以，收益率越高，长期配置的吸引力确实可能越大，但短期价格还要看卖盘有多集中，以及买方有多少资金可以接住。

text:
New post on Eth Research!

Rapidblocks with split proofs: execution proofs that outlive their state

By:
- cskiraly

🔗 https://t.co/sYchLEmpDx

Highlights:
- A monolithic “pre-state root → post-state root” execution proof doesn’t fit Rapidblocks well because blocks execute relative to a Hist set and pipeline ordering, so the exact pre-state a proof refers to may never appear in the canonical chain order.
- Split proofs divide verification into (1) Π_T: expensive EVM correctness from declared inputs to outputs with no state root, plus (2) Π_in and (3) Π_out: cheaper Merkle-style proofs that the inputs match some state root and that applying outputs transforms one root to the next.
- Headers commit to the block’s inputs (the values it reads), not a pre-state root; if later state changes don’t touch those inputs, the same Π_T remains valid across multiple slots—so “proofs outlive their state.”
- The “input rule” replaces the prior Hist-based validity: a block is included if it’s the slot’s chosen value, its proof is valid, its committed inputs are still current at its slot boundary, and its context matches the decided horizon; skips and conflicts propagate only along actual read-dependencies.
- Consensus can run on two tracks: a per-slot ‘block track’ (window vote) where stateless voters check availability, Π_T, and input-currency using horizon roots plus recent access lists, and a slower ‘state track’ where canonical state roots are proven later via recursive Π_out proofs; proofs can even be checked in a later voting round to accommodate proving latency.

ELI5:
Normally, a block proof says “if you start from this exact old snapshot of the blockchain’s state, you end at this new snapshot.” In Rapidblocks, blocks can be reordered or some can be skipped, so that exact snapshot might never exist again—making a single proof hard to reuse. This post proposes splitting the proof into parts: one part proves the transactions correctly turn some specific input values into outputs (without mentioning any state snapshot), and two cheaper parts link those inputs/outputs to actual state snapshots using Merkle proofs. Because the main proof depends only on the input values a block read, it can stay valid even if other unrelated parts of the state change, letting the system agree on blocks first and compute/agree on state roots later.

text:
PRL、QTC 接连大涨：海外大佬和 VC 为什么开始重新押注 PoW？

最近 $QTC 和 $PRL 接连大涨，私信里被问得最多的就是这两个海外热门 PoW 怎么看，以及到底去哪买。

目前能把这两个币一口气全上上的交易所不多，主要是在 @BigONEexchange 上交易，我看了一眼流动性和深度都还不错，想布局的不用去小盘子里硬啃滑点。

自从我分别写了 $QTC 和 $PRL 两篇内容之后，两个项目都经历了一轮明显上涨，也收到了不少朋友的私信。PRL 一度冲到 1.92 美元，QTC 最高冲到 186 美元附近。

今天统一整理一下，这两个被海外投资圈盯上的项目，到底有什么技术优势，背后站着哪些人，最近又取得了哪些实质性进展。

两个项目都选择了比特币的 PoW 路线，却押注了完全不同的未来。

Pearl（PRL）赌的是 AI 算力需求持续爆发，Quantus（QTC）赌的是量子计算最终会威胁现有加密体系。

一个想让挖矿成为 AI 算力经济的一部分，一个想提前建立下一代数字货币的安全标准。这也是我持续关注它们的原因。

先聊 $PRL 。

这个项目最吸引我的地方，是它尝试重新计算 PoW 的经济账。

创始人 Omri Weinstein 和联合创始人 Ilan Komargodski 有复杂性理论、密码学方面的学术背景，团队设计了一套叫 NoisyGEMM 的有用工作量证明机制，把传统挖矿中的哈希竞争改成 AI 计算常用的矩阵乘法，再通过密码学证明验证结果。

理想情况下，一张 GPU 可以在提供 AI 推理服务的同时获得 PRL 区块奖励，同一份计算资源产生两种经济回报。

如果这套机制能大规模落地，矿工就有机会同时赚取 AI 客户支付的美元收入和网络发放的 PRL。

PRL 过去几个月的推进还挺快。

5 月，Together AI 与 Pearl 联合推出 Gemma-4-31B-it-Pearl 推理接口，利用代币排放补贴，将推理价格降低 25% 以上，证明了这个商业模式至少可以做出实际产品。

随后 Pearl 加入 NVIDIA Inception 计划，自建兼容 OpenAI API 的推理平台，已经开放多款模型；技术上继续推进 MoE 模型支持、FP8 浮点计算方案，并与 Attestable 探索可验证 AI 计算。

产业逻辑已经很清晰了：如果 PRL 奖励能覆盖一部分 GPU 运营成本，推理服务商就有降价空间，客户获得更便宜的 AI 服务，矿工还能获得额外收益。

相比单纯讲 AI 概念的代币，我更愿意花时间研究这种有实际产品和成本模型的项目。

再看海外资本和 KOL 的态度，这也是 PRL 最近热度起来的重要原因。

No Limit Holdings 公开表示长期重仓 Pearl，甚至专门发表《Heresy》投资论文，将其视为有潜力成为下一个比特币的项目，还赞助了 Token2049 期间的 Pearl Connect 社区活动。

Dragonfly 合伙人 Tom Schmidt 在 The Rollup 访谈中讨论了这套机制的投资逻辑，Ansem 将其称作 AI 版比特币，DWF Ventures 在 Token2049 复盘中也提到 Pearl 是基金和散户热议的项目。

从技术研究进入海外资金的讨论范围，再到形成社区共识，PRL 的传播路径已经比较清晰。

PRL 的代币经济：

总供应量 21 亿枚，100% 通过挖矿产出，没有传统 VC 预挖、团队代币分配，排放采用平滑递减机制。近期全网算力已达到约 50 EH/s 量级，每天新增约 100 万枚 PRL。

按现在约 1.8 美元的价格，流通市值已超过 6 亿美元，按最大供应量计算的 FDV 接近 38 亿美元，每天新增代币的市值约 180 万美元。

现阶段并非所有挖矿计算都对应真实的付费 AI 需求，早期 Together AI 专属模型目前也已标示不再提供 Serverless API 服务。

Pearl 自营推理平台在推进，但真实订单规模、收入和 PRL 的价值捕获还缺少充分验证。

它已经证明技术方向有吸引力，下一阶段必须证明商业收入能跟上代币估值。

接下来聊 $QTC ，这个项目的逻辑和 PRL 完全不同。

Quantus 在 9 月 9 日上线主网，总量 2100 万枚，定位是抗量子、隐私优先的 PoW 电子现金。它直接采用 NIST 标准化的 ML-DSA 后量子签名，结合零知识证明和 Wormhole 隐私机制，目标是从底层减少未来量子计算对资产所有权的威胁。

比特币即使未来完成抗量子升级，也需要协调大量钱包、托管机构、交易所和用户迁移，已经丢失私钥的资产还会产生额外难题。

QTC 的思路是从创世就采用后量子密码学，省去未来重新迁移整条链的复杂过程。 QTC 最近最重要的两项进展，一项是 NEAR Intents，另一项是 Project Eleven。

10 月 6 日接入 NEAR Intents 后，QTC 可以通过跨链意图交易触达 BTC、ETH、SOL、ZEC 等资产的流动性，对一条刚上线、没有庞大交易生态的新链来说，这相当于补上了早期资产进入网络的关键入口。

10 月 7 日，Project Eleven 宣布 Quantus 成为其 Strongpoint 机构托管平台的开发合作伙伴，计划在 2027 年第一季度支持 QTC，让机构未来可以通过统一的密钥管理、审批和审计体系操作后量子资产。

Token2049 期间，Quantus 还与 NEAR 举办了 Quantum & Privacy Day，Balaji、Zcash 创始人 Zooko、NEAR 联创 Illia、Bitwise CEO Hunter Horsley、Dragonfly 管理合伙人 Haseeb 等人参与相关讨论。

这一圈人的关注，本身就说明抗量子和隐私正在成为海外加密圈的重要研究方向。

QTC 两轮融资合计约 242 万美元:

第一轮融资 165 万美元，对应约 4000 万美元代币估值；

第二轮融资 77 万美元，对应约 1 亿美元代币估值，由前 Coinbase CTO Balaji Srinivasan 领投。

其他投资人包括 AngelList 联创 Babak Nivi、Helius 创始人 Mert 等，Balaji 还被项目联合创始人介绍为顾问。这些人与 Zcash 的支持者圈子高度重合。

Bankless 最近也专门采访创始人 Christopher Smith，讨论比特币的量子迁移难题。我理解这群人的投资逻辑，是继续押注数字现金的隐私、安全和独立货币属性，而 QTC 给了他们一个从零开始设计后量子体系的机会。

但 QTC 的代币经济问题，我上次就批评过，总量 2100 万枚，其中 27% 在创世时直接铸造，约 23% 分配给投资人、创始人和团队，4% 分配给公司相关用途，剩余 73% 通过 PoW 挖矿产生。

绝大部分创世分配设有锁仓，主要部分锁定一年后再用三年线性释放，这能缓和短期抛压，但未来解锁压力始终存在。

现在 QTC 价格约 123 美元，流通只有约 28 万枚，流通市值约 3500 万美元，如果按目前已发行的约 574 万枚计算，对应估值约 7 亿美元，按最终 2100 万枚计算则约 26 亿美元。

PRL 的优势在于团队研究实力、相对公平的挖矿分配，以及已经开始尝试连接真实 AI 推理市场。未来主要看真实付费算力规模、矿工经济模型和商业收入。

QTC 的优势在于后量子密码学、隐私资产定位，以及 Balaji 等投资者和 NEAR、Project Eleven 带来的生态资源。未来主要看用户采用、真实交易需求、市场流动性和 2027 年开始的解锁周期。

PRL 在赌 AI 算力能产生新型货币价值，QTC 在赌未来数字货币必须重新解决安全与隐私问题。

方向都有想象空间，但市场已经开始为未来提前付钱。接下来谁能把预期变成真实需求，谁才有资格走得更远。

写在最后：

这两个项目的叙事和控盘都不错，但也属于典型的早期高波动资产。

如果准备布局，建议根据个人风险偏好采取分批逢低挂单策略。

相比在 DEX 上承受不必要的跨链损耗，直接在 BigONE 挂限价单会更省心一些，现货盘口的挂单承接力也相对可观。再次提醒大家控制好仓位，切勿盲目追高。

⚠️ If the Ledger news has you rethinking hardware wallets, take a breath.

@nunchuk_io just laid out how to plan your self-custody properly, and it’s worth five minutes before you make any moves.

Two of their points are ones we’ve been preaching for years:
1️⃣ Your signer should protect you across more than one attack vector. The tampered Ledgers reportedly had a hidden chip inside the case. Anti-tamper protection would have made that a lot harder to pull off.

Every Keystone ships with it, because your device should be safe before it hits your doorstep. No device stops a determined attacker 100%, but this kind of attack gets very tough to run at scale.

2️⃣ Run multi-vendor multisig. Yes, that means buying hardware from our competitors too. Do it anyway. One compromised device can’t sign alone, so a supply chain attack on one vendor goes nowhere.

One bad batch is no reason to give up cold storage.

Read the post below and send it to the friend who’s panicking right now.
author: KeystoneWallet
quoted_text:
A few words given the recent exploits on hardware signing devices:

• The Ledger supply chain attack represents one of the most sophisticated attacks thus far on the wallet ecosystem. In many ways it’s a lot more sophisticated than the Coldcard RNG exploit, because that one was software only. This one took a cross-border company buyout, tampering with the devices (implanting an eSIM, an LTE module and a CPU) and manufacturing the implants at scale.

• These sorts of attacks have been predicted by early Bitcoiners, but in Bitcoin they remained theoretical or crude until this year. It shows that the level of sophistication of attacks has risen quickly, and what was previously “good enough” advice on wallets and self-custody is no longer sufficient.

• When we started Nunchuk a few years ago, our premise was that multisig, and multi-vendor multisig, needs to become the standard for self-custody in the future. But even we didn’t expect how fast it would materialize. This is likely due to 2 factors: Bitcoin getting more mainstream, and the rise of AI-assisted attacks. This is a Sputnik moment for Bitcoin self-custody. The defenses need to level up.

• Passphrases wouldn’t have helped in the Ledger case, since you are required to enter the passphrase into the device for it to sign any transactions. A compromised device that phones home the seed phrase can also easily phone home the passphrase the moment you enter it.

• Similarly, generating the private key somewhere else (even by rolling dice) and subsequently importing it onto a tampered device wouldn’t save you here. The device can phone home the seed phrase the moment it’s imported.

• Anti-tampering techniques might help, such as transparent casing or bricking the device if it’s tampered with. Or forever displaying a message once the seal is broken. Or using on-device encryption between the internal hardware components. But a dedicated and resourceful enough attacker can still find ways to get around these layers. Tampering and anti-tampering have long been a cat-and-mouse game. In 2008, card readers doctored right off a Chinese production line sent card data and PINs over mobile networks to Pakistan. The Ledger attack is the same playbook, 18 years later. The bigger the target, the more attackers spend on overcoming the defenses.

• You should order directly from the vendors as much as possible, using a PO box for privacy.

• Any setup that relies on a single hardware/software stack or a single vendor should be considered at risk.

• Building your own hardware signers from generic parts is a good option for technical users.

• Multi-vendor multisig should become the standard. Each signer should have a completely independent hardware/software stack from the other signers. The point is that there shouldn’t be any single-point-of-failure anywhere in your setup.

• Many advanced protocols rely on timelocks and the recovery path being a simple singlesig. The recent attacks and exploits should highlight how dangerous this could be. Timelocks simply delay a risk. If a seed is compromised and there’s a timelock involved, the attacker just needs to wait out the timelock. (For Miniscript wallets, there’s the wallet descriptor too, but presumably it also gets sent to the device at some point.) Vault-like protocols face a similar problem: any withdrawal or recovery path that relies on a single key is a potential single point of failure. 

• For our on-chain timelock-assisted wallets, in a few weeks we are adding the option to customize the recovery path to be an M-of-N, so that, if you want, spending would require multiple keys at all points during the wallet’s lifetime.

text:
The Seven Noahide Laws: Rambam and Ramban

Jewish tradition teaches seven foundational commandments for humanity:

1. Do not worship idols.
2. Do not curse G-d.
3. Do not murder.
4. Do not steal.
5. Do not engage in sexual relations prohibited by Noahide law, including adultery and incest.
6. Do not eat flesh taken from a living animal.
7. Establish courts of justice.

According to Rambam, the seventh commandment requires courts to adjudicate violations of the other six. The United States does not uphold that full enforcement standard, since its laws protect some conduct prohibited by Noahide law.

According to Ramban, the seventh commandment has substantive civil requirements of its own, including laws governing property, wages, debts, damages, and commerce. American courts perform these functions and, in that respect, fit within his framework of justice.

The other six commandments remain binding on individuals. Whether governments must enforce them is a further question on every government body individually.

刚才听路飞  @CaptainLufei999     和邵艾伦@AlanShao111   连麦，路飞讲到孙宇晨 @justinsuntron ：孙宇晨最厉害的，就是开天辟地般地直接不装了。不披道德外衣，直接精致利己，开干！

这句话我想了很久，越想越觉得准。

孙宇晨从来没给自己套上道德的枷锁。不装好人，不扮圣人，就是狠，就是精致利己，就是见利忘义。

币圈里很多人，赚的其实是同一种钱，只是嘴上要先披一件道德外衣：去中心化，改变世界，一切为了社区。

孙哥没有披。

他想要流量，就花 457 万美元拍下巴菲特的午餐。他想要话题，就花 620 万美元买下一根香蕉，然后当众吃掉。他想进入美国市场，就把 Tron 带上纳斯达克，自己站上去敲钟。

面子他不太在意，骂声他也都接着。有人说他营销大于技术，他没有去辩解，只是转身继续做事。

很多人看不惯这种方式。但慢慢地也会发现，他可能是第一个把"不要面子"做成方法论的人。

结果就放在那里。全球将近一半的 USDT 跑在波场上，新兴市场的普通人每天都在用这条链转账。骂他的人一直很多，用他的链的人更多。

这大概就是孙哥的逻辑。先把事情做成，对错留给后面再说。

其实这背后也是很朴素的人性。装圣人的人，会有人喜欢，也会有人尊重，但很少有人真的被他吸引。人们心里清楚，那份完美多半是演出来的。反倒是这种不遮不掩的狠人，身上有一种致命的吸引力。因为他真实，因为他敢要，也因为他做到了很多人想做却不敢做的事。

所以他身边始终有一大批拥趸。大家追随的，未必是一个完美的人，而是那股敢在规则边缘往前走的劲。

可以不喜欢他，但很难忽视他。

text:
What $HOOKR Is Really Trying to Do: Give Tokens on RH Chain Their Own Trading Rules

0x18e674231a58c239dc7daedcffe15ec3a24cff5c 

In my view, HOOKR’s significance for Robinhood Chain is not that it adds another token launchpad. It is trying to turn Uniswap v4 Hooks into a set of trading infrastructure that ordinary projects can reuse.

Most token launchpads focus on how to bring a new token to market. HOOKR is trying to solve a different problem: once a token is listed, can its trading rules become more sophisticated? How should fees be distributed? When should tokens be burned? How can LPs be rewarded? Can arbitrage profits be redistributed to traders? Rather than relying entirely on project-operated servers or external bots, these mechanisms can be embedded directly into the trade execution process.

That gives the product potential beyond a conventional launchpad.

Built on Uniswap v4 Hooks, HOOKR uses composable Hook Blocks to let issuers choose different rules for their trading pools, including dynamic fees, Anti-Snipe, Auto Burn, and LP Rewards. The relevant parameters are fixed when a pool is created and cannot be freely changed afterward. The platform also offers two paths: shared Hooks and custom Hooks. Projects can use existing modules directly or deploy their own trading logic.

More importantly, HOOKR is not limited to newly launched tokens. Assets issued elsewhere can also create new Hookr pools. This gives it an opportunity to enter the existing-asset market rather than relying entirely on the number of new tokens launched every day.

This is particularly worth watching for RH Chain. Robinhood Chain is designed for tokenized stocks and other on-chain financial applications. If more assets enter the ecosystem, the market will need more than issuance channels. It will also need more flexible mechanisms for trading, liquidity, and fee distribution.

HOOKR’s design allows different assets to adopt different rules. One pool could distribute part of its trading fees to LPs, another could implement buyback and burn mechanisms, while a pool targeting a specific trading scenario could redirect arbitrage profits. HOOKR provides tools for building markets, rather than a single trading product.

Of course, being able to configure these rules does not mean every asset will automatically have a better market. Complex mechanisms can increase the cost of understanding a product and introduce additional smart contract risks. Whether HOOKR eventually becomes important infrastructure for RH Chain depends on how many projects genuinely need these capabilities, not on how long its feature list becomes.

Its creator, Nodar, previously created DeFiZap and co-founded Zapperfi. His earlier work largely focused on simplifying complex DeFi operations.

DeFiZap aimed to combine protocol interactions that users would otherwise have to complete step by step, reducing the number of actions required and making DeFi easier to access. In 2020, DeFiZap merged with DeFiSnap to form Zapperfi. Nodar was involved in a DeFi product built for real users, rather than simply a token-marketing project.

I think the connection between that experience and HOOKR is more worth examining than the fact that its founder has worked on a well-known project.

Zapper aimed to lower the barrier for users accessing complex financial tools. HOOKR is trying to lower the barrier for developers building complex trading rules. The former combined multiple DeFi operations into easier-to-use workflows; the latter breaks different trading mechanisms into composable, reusable modules.

This does not prove that HOOKR will succeed, but it does suggest that the project is not merely a temporary narrative disconnected from its founder’s previous experience. Nodar previously participated in integrating and popularizing DeFi products. Now, he is trying to take a similar approach into the trading infrastructure layer.

However, if HOOKR relies solely on its official team to keep developing new modules, it could ultimately remain just a launchpad with more features.

The more valuable scenario would be one in which third-party developers can create new Hooks that other issuers can reuse directly, while developers receive a corresponding share of fees when projects adopt their components. Pool activity would then provide feedback, and HOOKR’s development would no longer depend entirely on the official team’s development speed. Instead, it could create an ecosystem driven by developer supply, issuer adoption, and trading activity.

This is the most important dividing line in how I evaluate the project.

If developers only occasionally use a few standard modules supplied by the official team, the ecosystem’s competitive moat will be limited. If more independent developers begin designing new trading mechanisms for different assets, and those components are repeatedly adopted by multiple projects, HOOKR could gradually become infrastructure that other applications depend on.

The official team has already showcased product directions involving external integrations and arbitrage profit recapture. However, it is important to distinguish features that are already live from partnerships that are still under development or awaiting review. A list of partners does not constitute a network effect. The more convincing evidence will be actual trading volume, fee revenue, and component reuse after launch.

HOOKR’s token economics also need to be evaluated based on the revenue the protocol actually receives.

According to the current official documentation, the protocol can take a share of fees generated by certain Hook Blocks, with a default share of 20%. It does not take a cut of the base LP trading fee. Actual revenue depends on which modules a pool enables, whether those modules generate fees, and the applicable revenue-sharing rules.

This means rising platform trading volume does not necessarily translate into a proportional increase in protocol revenue. Even if a pool is highly active, a pool that only charges the base LP fee may not generate corresponding revenue for HOOKR.

The buyback and burn mechanism is designed to connect protocol revenue with the token. But an investment thesis still requires on-chain evidence: how much in fees has actually been collected, how much has been allocated to buybacks, how many tokens have been purchased, and whether the burns have genuinely been executed. Rising trading volume alone is not enough to conclude that demand for the token has strengthened accordingly.

Security is another issue that cannot be overlooked at this stage. HOOKR’s contract source code and testing materials are public, but these materials still need to be verified against specific versions and deployments. Open-source code should not be treated as equivalent to an independent audit. The more flexible the programmable trading rules become, the more important code review and real-world operating records will be.

Ultimately, HOOKR is worth watching because it could move asset trading on RH Chain beyond standardized buying and selling into a layer of composable trading mechanisms. Nodar’s experience with DeFiZap and Zapper provides some relevant background for this product direction, while the development of a genuine developer ecosystem will determine whether HOOKR becomes a feature-rich token launchpad or infrastructure that other projects continue to adopt.

What I will be watching next is not how many new Hooks it launches, but whether third-party developers continue deploying them, whether external projects actually adopt them, and whether protocol revenue can grow sustainably and flow through to HOOKR via verifiable buybacks and burns.

If this cycle works, HOOKR’s value will no longer come merely from short-term activity around new token launches. It will come from growing demand for programmable trading mechanisms as more assets enter RH Chain.

If developer adoption remains limited and revenue continues to depend on a small number of trading pools, then even with an interesting product design, HOOKR will not yet have proven that it can become an indispensable layer of the ecosystem.

For this rally, I'm more inclined to view $HOOKR as Uniswap v4 Hook infrastructure on Rh Chain.

0x18e674231a58c239dc7daedcffe15ec3a24cff5c 

It is expanding from a token launch tool into composable trading infrastructure.

The market appears to be reassessing its ecosystem value.

Unlike a Meme token driven purely by hype, HOOKR has usable products, on-chain trading pools, and a protocol fee mechanism. But that also raises the key question: has the growth in product capabilities translated into sufficient real usage and sustainable buying pressure for the token?

Recent developments have also led me to update my analysis in an important way. HOOKR is not simply adding more Hook modules. It is beginning to connect capital flows, reward distribution, and revenue streams across different trading pools. This is more significant than simply adding token launch features, because it speaks to whether Hookr can evolve from a programmable liquidity pool platform into composable on-chain trading infrastructure.

Hookr’s website now positions the new version as modular infrastructure for Uniswap v4 Hooks. However, the relevant contracts have not yet completed a formal external audit. Product functionality going live and security being independently verified must therefore be evaluated separately.

The Latest Catalysts

1. Moving from individual trading pools to cross-pool connectivity

The most important update is Hookr’s announcement that three contracts connecting different trading pools are now live.

Pool Mesh allows a single vault to provide liquidity to up to four pools for different tokens. Capital can be allocated according to predefined weights or directed toward the pools with the thinnest liquidity. Once a project creates a Mesh, other pools can join it.

This means liquidity no longer has to remain entirely isolated within each pool. For projects operating multiple tokens or trading markets, this mechanism could make capital management more flexible.

Family Pinger allows a single call to automatically execute a group of related operations, including trading Zaps, periodic small fund distributions, and payments owed to a family of pools.

Fee Bridge allows a project to designate an address as a royalty recipient or tax recipient, then distribute the funds it receives in batches to liquidity providers in another pool, with a cap on the amount transferred in each distribution.

The common thread among these three features is that Hookr is beginning to coordinate capital across multiple pools rather than focusing solely on trading rules within individual pools.

If real projects adopt these mechanisms, Hookr’s infrastructure thesis will become much more compelling than a simple launchpad narrative. However, contracts going live only means the functionality is available. It does not mean large-scale adoption or substantial revenue has already materialized.

2. Modular tools and the developer ecosystem continue to expand

Hookr’s newly released HookBook documents 24 ways to combine Uniswap v4 pools with Hook Blocks, covering use cases ranging from fair launches to treasury management. Each combination comes with a full walkthrough, and users can open the Builder with the configuration prefilled in one click.

Hookr has also introduced or announced the following features:

Every live Hook Block can be configured directly in the app and has its own dedicated page.
Developers can submit requests directly through the search interface when they cannot find the module they need.
Swap Reward Mint allows users to create reward tokens within the app and distribute them to traders on every swap.
Multi-pool launches allow different pools to use separate Hook Blocks and different initial quote assets.
Existing tokens can also add Tax + Conversion mechanisms, with the pool page showing who pays each tax.
llms.txt allows AI agents and AI search tools to read Hook Blocks, documentation, and HookBook combinations.

In addition, Hookr has announced support for deploying custom Uniswap v4 Hooks in a single transaction and says the first such Hook is already on-chain. Developers can combine the Hook Blocks they need, deploy their own Hook, and then use Hookr’s launch, routing, and quote-asset tools to create trading pools. Existing tokens can also connect to new pools without modifying the tokens themselves.

These updates may seem scattered, but they point toward the same goal: lowering the barrier to building complex trading mechanisms.

If developers can select modules, combine parameters, deploy pools, and integrate them into their own applications through an SDK, Hookr has the potential to become a development tool for other projects rather than a product that serves only traffic on its own website.

3. Ecosystem integrations are expanding into more use cases

Hookr’s new version supports different quote assets, including ETH, stablecoins, HOOKR, and tokenized stocks. It also provides an SDK and a public module directory, allowing other applications to integrate trading, quoting, and pool creation functionality.

More importantly, Hookr pools can be routed through Uniswap’s own interface and APIs. This means projects do not have to rely entirely on users visiting https://t.co/rbi76Dkjxu directly; they may also attract usage through external trading interfaces.

The project also claims that the new version reduces gas costs for swaps by approximately 47%–70% and token launch costs by around 40%. If these advantages hold up in real transactions, Hookr could attract developers through a better product experience rather than relying purely on subsidies.

Recent project-related information also mentions several integrations:

Saffron is integrating fixed-yield vaults.
ZEALZ plans to launch a zZEC pool with low base fees and LP rewards.
rhook can replay historical trading activity to compare the effects of different trading rules.
hooddomains brings domains into the creator and trading pool experience.
An OpenAI-related project plans to launch tokens with custom rules on Hookr.
Longbow Lend is exploring the use of Hookr pools for liquidations and collateral swaps.

These integrations serve different purposes. Some could increase the number of trading pools, some improve developer tooling, and others attempt to connect Hookr with lending, yield, and trading applications.

If these projects actually launch and generate sustained trading activity, the demand thesis for HOOKR could expand beyond token launch activity into broader ecosystem usage.

However, it is essential to distinguish between an integration being announced, a feature being live, and an integration generating meaningful trading volume. A list of partnerships and a growing number of features do not, by themselves, prove that protocol revenue is increasing.

4. The token value-capture mechanism is becoming clearer

HOOKR’s value proposition is not simply to use all trading fees for buybacks.

In the new version, base LP fees go entirely to liquidity providers. The protocol primarily earns a share of revenue from additional mechanisms such as dynamic fees, Anti-Snipe, LP rewards, and automatic burns. The default revenue-sharing rate is 20%, with the actual rate determined when a pool is created. Pools using the arbitrage value-recapture mechanism also contribute part of their proceeds to the protocol.

The mechanism described by the project involves pooling protocol revenue in a treasury and using it to buy back and burn HOOKR.

If more pools adopt these additional mechanisms and trading volume continues to grow, this could theoretically create a value-capture loop: greater ecosystem usage leads to more protocol revenue, which in turn supports more buybacks and burns.

But this chain of causality still needs to be verified with real data. I will focus on actual protocol revenue, on-chain buyback records, and the amount of tokens burned rather than assuming that every mechanism is already operating at full scale.

What the Market May Be Betting On

I think the market may be betting on three layers of potential.

First, trading activity on Rh Chain will continue to grow, and more projects will need programmable trading rules, positioning Hookr as an important infrastructure entry point.

Second, modular Hooks, HookBook, and the SDK will attract third-party developers. If other projects begin using Hookr to build pools, launch tokens, or develop applications, it could create network effects that extend beyond traffic to Hookr’s own website.

Third, cross-pool capital management and broader ecosystem usage will eventually translate into sustained HOOKR buybacks and burns. For token holders, this is the most important connection between product growth and token value.

Where Things Stand Now

Product fundamentals are strengthening, ecosystem adoption remains unproven, and token value capture has yet to be fully realized.

From a product perspective, HOOKR is clearly more extensible than a single-purpose launch platform. Its modular architecture, pools with multiple quote assets, cross-pool connectors, SDK, custom Hook deployment, and external routing are expanding the range of problems it can solve.

From an adoption perspective, the direction is improving, but it still needs to be validated through sustained trading volume, active developers, and actual usage data from external integrations. The launch of connectors and partnership announcements do not necessarily mean they are already generating substantial trading activity.

From a token value-capture perspective, the mechanism is becoming clearer, but the actual scale of buybacks, the stability of revenue, and the relationship between revenue and token demand still need to be demonstrated with on-chain data. Product upgrades should not be equated with a fully realized improvement in token fundamentals.

Potential Upside Catalysts Ahead

First, real projects begin using the cross-pool connectors. If Pool Mesh helps multiple pools share and coordinate liquidity, Fee Bridge establishes consistent cross-pool revenue distribution, and Family Pinger handles recurring automated payments, that would be much more meaningful than simply adding a few more trading pools.

Second, third-party projects begin building their own products on Hookr. If launch platforms use custom Hooks, trading applications integrate pools through the SDK, and DeFi protocols use its mechanisms for liquidity and yield management, Hookr’s value would no longer depend entirely on how many tokens it launches itself.

Third, protocol revenue and buybacks and burns grow together. This is the key point at which the product narrative could translate into stronger token fundamentals. If real trading activity increases alongside sustained growth in protocol revenue, actual buybacks, and token burns, HOOKR’s long-term valuation thesis would gain much stronger support.

Fourth, additional features launch and attract real usage. Canonical Venue Token, Buy/Sell Block, Market Guard, Zap Relay, Entry Ratio Guarantee, Recovery Reserve, Pay Later, Tax + Conversion, Revenue Router, Vesting Milestone, Market-hours Fee, Limit Orders, Best Route, and Hook Blocks Market could all expand Hookr’s potential use cases.

However, not all these features are live yet. Zero-seed launches, auction-based launches, Floor Bid, Dev Drip, and Usage Fee are also still part of the development roadmap. Whether they become catalysts depends on their eventual launch and adoption, not merely their presence on a roadmap.

Key Risks

First, Hookr’s product capabilities may be ahead of market demand. If developer activity and trading on Rh Chain remain insufficient, even a comprehensive modular system may struggle to generate meaningful protocol revenue.

Second, complex trading rules and cross-pool capital flows increase system complexity. Pool Mesh, Fee Bridge, and similar features need to prove that their fund routing, transfer limits, and exception handling are reliable. More features do not automatically mean lower system risk.

Third, Hook modules are not impossible to replicate. Hookr’s long-term moat must ultimately come from developer adoption, tooling quality, its integration network, and sustained usage—not merely the number of modules it offers.

Fourth, security remains a critical risk. Hookr’s website has not confirmed that the relevant contracts have completed a formal external audit, while the project recently stated that the new version was being submitted for audit. Submitting contracts for an audit does not mean the audit is complete, nor does it guarantee that no vulnerabilities exist.

Finally, even if product usage grows, the token may not appreciate accordingly. If protocol revenue shares remain limited, buybacks are too small, or sustained selling pressure outweighs buying demand, the infrastructure narrative may still fail to translate into token price performance.

My Final Take

The latest batch of updates makes me more optimistic about HOOKR’s product direction.

Previously, its main story was modularizing Uniswap v4 Hooks so that projects could create pools with more flexible, customized trading rules. Now, Pool Mesh, Family Pinger, and Fee Bridge are beginning to connect capital and revenue across multiple pools, while HookBook, the SDK, and custom Hook deployment are lowering the barriers for developers to use these capabilities.

This pushes HOOKR’s potential positioning beyond “a more flexible token launch platform” toward “programmable and composable trading and capital-management infrastructure.”

But product upgrades do not mean token value has already been realized. The key things to track next are whether the connectors see real usage, whether third-party integrations continue to expand, whether protocol revenue grows, and whether buybacks and burns reach a meaningful scale.

If product adoption, protocol revenue, and actual buybacks grow together, HOOKR’s infrastructure narrative will gain much stronger fundamental support. If its features keep expanding but real usage and value capture remain elusive, the token could still be trading on a future that has been priced in too early.
