text:
‼️突发：字节跳动Seed宣布成立「Model-Alignment & Preparedness」部门，并同步启动全球顶尖人才招募。  这是国内第一个由大模型核心研究团队独立拆分、单独建制的安全研发部门。  

部门由严林负责，直接汇报给Seed负责人吴永辉。  

安全不再是模型上线前的一道检查项，而是和能力研发并驾齐驱的主线。

为什么是现在？  
因为过去一年，前沿模型在现实里发生了失控的苗头。  

比如2026年7月，OpenAI 红队评估中，模型自主利用一个未公开的零日漏洞撕开沙盒，访问了 Hugging Face 的真实生产系统（直接给HF打漏了）。  
而Anthropic这边经过回溯调查了约 14.1 万次评估调用，确认至少 3 起Claude越权侵入外部真实系统。 

更严重的威胁是CBRN（化学、生物、放射、核）方向。  
根据智源FlagSafe今年7月份发布的研究显示，11 个主流商用大模型都能给出规避DNA合成筛查的方案，头部模型的方案在湿实验中被证实可执行。 
当模型开始操作生产环境、编排实验，外挂式安全补丁已形同虚设。

Seed 直接在公告里表示：模型能力决定智能的上限，但 Safety & Alignment 决定这个上限能不能在真实世界成立。 

这套打法其实是对标了旧金山湾区的情况，Anthropic 从第一天起就是安全公司，OpenAI 的 Superalignment 后来重组为 Preparedness 体系，DeepMind 也设有专门的 AGI Safety 团队。  
而做这件事的全是金字塔尖的人：Jan Leike（ChatGPT、GPT-4 对齐核心）、RLHF 与 PPO 奠基人 John Schulman，还有 Ilya Sutskever、Chris Olah、Dario Amodei。  
模型越强，对齐越难——这也是为什么必须由顶尖人才来做。

国内模型团队们此前一直是另一套路径：  安全约等于内容风控，挂在大安全中台下面，研究团队负责拔高模型能力，安全团队在下游擦屁股。 
Seed 把编制直接从研究团队划出来，是国内第一次在组织形态上对标 OpenAI、Anthropic——前有 STEM，现在是安全与对齐。 
具体的人才计划是：全球范围内招募 10 位顶尖研究员，做最有价值的事。 
方向覆盖模型训练、科学评测、未知风险防御，提供充分算力，研究成果直接打回训练、评估、上线全流程，base 北京、上海、圣何塞。  

为什么只招 10 个？  
因为这道难题没法靠堆人解决——说白了，弱一点的研究者，甚至意识不到风险在哪。

我的看法是国内大模型竞赛的下半场，最重要的一个点是谁先把安全底座真正建起来。  

Seed这一步，是中国头部实验室认真坐到AGI安全这张牌桌上了。

text:
Walking away from a long Claude Code session used to cost you when you came back. That just changed.

In Claude Code 2.1.299, if a conversation over 200K tokens sits idle for about 54 minutes, it gets compacted before the one-hour prompt cache expires. Your first message after the break no longer has to reprocess the entire history.

It works in the terminal. Two settings if you want control:
→ Change the 200K threshold with the CLAUDE_CODE_IDLE_COMPACT_MIN_TOKENS environment variable
→ Turn it off with "idleCompaction": false in settings.json

Compaction condenses older history, so turn it off if you need every detail of a long session kept as is.

Also in this release: /usage now warns you when max effort, workflows, always-on context or large tool results are in play.

quoted_text:
从四大银行财报看美国经济状况以及它们是怎么看待AI融资的？昨天小摩高盛花旗富国四家银行公布了三季度财报，这里从居民消费、企业信贷和AI融资三个角度聊聊。
1、居民消费：仍有韧性
摩根大通电话会有披露借记卡、信用卡消费，花旗会更细分披露通用信用卡和品牌卡的数据。
1）从小摩的数据能看出来，客户名义消费继续扩张。摩根大通本季信用卡消费额增长10%，更值得一提的是本季消费额增长10%净核销率为1.27%，低于二季度的1.42%，也略低于去年同期的1.29%。

富国管理层也表示，其客户仍在消费，拖欠情况较低，客户存款和投资余额表现较好。说明美国居民消费仍有韧性，实际信用损失也没有恶化。

2）值得注意的是花旗通用卡和商店品牌卡之间的分化
不过花旗自己也明确表示纯商店品牌卡（仅限店内使用）需求长期下降，消费者更偏好可在多处使用的通用卡或联名卡。

花旗在投资者日明确以通用卡为优先方向。通用卡（尤其是联名卡）客户消费金额更高（联名客户消费约为商店品牌卡客户的8倍）、余额更高（约2倍），单位经济效益更好。花旗持续加大在通用卡上的投资，包括差异化奖励、合作伙伴关系（如美国航空AAdvantage联名卡组合的纳入）和获客营销。

2、企业信贷继续扩张
1）摩根大通平均贷款同比增长10%，花旗平均贷款增长12%，富国平均贷款增长11%。这些数据至少说明，四家中的大型综合银行仍在扩张贷款业务；

2）实际损失、准备金和管理层预期
摩根大通新增业务推高准备金，在电话会中小摩说明，批发信贷准备金增加主要来自新增业务，并非评级下调或整体信用展望恶化；同时承认较高能源价格和利率会对部分工商企业、商业地产形成压力。贷款发放得更多，需要计提更多预期损失准备；这与原有贷款质量恶化是两种情况；

花旗净信用损失约22.17亿美元，同比基本持平、环比下降8%；本季净准备金增加3.69亿美元；

富国本季信用损失拨备10.29亿美元，同比增长51%；实际净核销9.83亿美元，同比增长仅3%，但需要说明的是去年拨备受到准备金释放的压低，今年这种贡献不再存在，导致同比增幅显得很高。

3、AI融资：银行看到了巨大业务机会
高盛CEO在本季电话会表示，当前客户算力需求超过供给，为融资安排提供了机会；但随着融资需求规模扩大、结构复杂化，公司会对承销和资本承诺保持高度选择性；

摩根大通CFO在财报后的沟通中表示，AI融资需求和项目储备仍然活跃，但交易节奏会受到估值和市场条件影响；

把这四家银行的表述综合起来就是：
1）消费支付仍增长，主要银行贷款仍扩张，实际信用损失没有普遍跳升，企业与机构融资活动持续。这些证据共同支持经济和金融活动具有韧性。

2）当前银行实际信用指标尚可，但管理层仍提示利率、能源和地缘风险。从传导机制看，高利率可能先影响项目估值、融资价格、成交意愿与再融资能力，之后才影响投资、就业和实际坏账。整体看下来韧性犹在。

四家财报共同描绘的，是一个消费和信用底盘仍有韧性、金融活动保持活跃，但融资成本约束仍然存在的美国经济。

今天还有美国银行、大摩等金融机构的财报，特别是美国银行的财政更值得关注下。

author: 0xGeeGee
quoted_text:
As they say, every time you go back to China, you have to relearn everything. In less than two years, my experience using Alipay (no-cash society) has flipped, and this time it was a TOTAL NIGHTMARE. Multiple problems:

1. "Just walk up and scan the QR code" is not so simple. Now places have QR codes all over the counter! Which one? It’s a trap. Over and over again, we scanned the large-sized, prominently displayed code, which was spam! The real code was small and tucked away. This happened just now at M-Stand coffee, and the foreigner next to us did the same intuitive but wrong thing.

2. Popups. The next problem is the biggest, which is the barrage of spam popups. The worst was at Luckin, where there were literally TWENTY click-through barriers to ordering an Americano. The girl was frantically clicking through on my phone, she knew each spam screen from muscle memory and anticipated them, often clicking before they arrived, but as fast as she was, the other customers were annoyed. I told the wife, and she confirmed the same thing had happened to her earlier: literally 20 clicks, and only a local would know the answers to all those trick questions.

3. Translation. Just use the Alipay translate feature, you say? No, this has got to be the WORST translation software in existence. Claude is essentially flawless; even DeepSeek would be fine, but this is actually translating as the opposite of the meaning many times, which, as you can imagine, spins up serious confusion and wrong orders. For example, it translated "matcha latte no caffeine" (wtf?) and options like "with jelly or yes jelly” (no!).

4. Optionality. This is insane and adds to the above burdens. In the example of Luckin, the girl who works there could not even find the Orange Americano! She menu-dived three times, getting frustrated and coming up for air, before she dived into the right one. Then, of course, came corn syrup, iced, size, etc. Well, combined with misleading translation and constant spam, you are now spending up to 20 minutes ordering a coffee (this was the actual time it took in Starbucks when I did it myself).

5. When is the order ready? You would think this digital system would have that advantage, but again, it is totally unclear. It is written in some small print among dozens of other numbers and is different for each restaurant you go! We never knew when it was ready to pick up.

The effect of all this is that every single time you get a drink, or food, or do anything, it becomes an uninvited adventure, like solving a video game puzzle. It was vastly easier to just say "iced Americano, please" and let them do their job.

This seems to be a big change, or am I just imagining it? Two years ago, it took some getting used to, but I do not remember hitting this brick wall. Is this like how Facebook became 100% spam, but the product cycle is just moving faster in China? On the positive side, ordering a taxi with Alipay (DiDi Taxi) remains great!

Now, of course, we are tourists, true, and my Putonghua and comfort with simplified characters are very low, but typically when you set up systems like this, your own elder population cannot navigate them, like how elders in Korea cannot navigate the crappy banking apps and always get locked out of their own accounts.

Speaking of which, of course I got locked out of my WeChat account, sigh, and none of the three recertification options are available to me in China. We went to a beer stall where the beer is paid for with Alipay but the cup is paid for with WeChat!

This is just bad design!

简单来看整个阿斯麦财报非常强劲，而这份强劲财报的背后意味着目前不仅仅是AI需求强劲，

而是AI资本开支已经从GPU订单扩散至先进Logic、Memory与晶圆厂扩产中，产业在深化扩张

更重要的是，阿斯麦财报算是暂时打破了人工智能目前处于高泡沫的担忧，根据财报可以看出在2027年与2028年期间光刻设备将会迎来供给上的瓶颈，意味着AI投资周期在2030年前后会进入一个转折点

本次财报五个重点数据：

1，收入同比增长55%，说明先进半导体资本开支进入加速阶段
2，毛利率从51.6%增长到57.5%，意味着企业在快速增长的前提下并未降低增长质量
3，Q4收入中位值月147亿欧元，高于Q3，意味着Q3不是周期顶部
4, 2027-2028年现有供应无法满足需求，意味着产能依旧无法满足行业需求
5，客户开始问询2029-2030年的设备，需求能见度正在明显后延，拓展未来预期

按照本周宏观框架的逻辑链来看，银行财报看资本供给，阿斯麦财报看未来产能投资，目前两者问题不大，接下来就要关注台积电财报，看这些投资最终对应的先进制程需求是否真实。

周四的台积电财报看 先进制程收入、AI加速器需求，资本指引与2027年产能评论，如果台积电三分财报不错，可以短期为本周的美股打开反弹空间，扫除短期宏观压力带来的阴霾！

PS：当然，阿斯麦的财报这里有一个“坑”需要注意不能过分解读为乐观，那就是财报显示2027-2028年产能意味着阿斯麦供不应求，但是这并不100%等于目前的AI投资没有泡沫

$ASML  代表的是未来几年半导体厂商正在大量投资现金产能，但是并不能代表行业整体，尤其是AI基础设施最终生产是否带来足够的ROI，两者是不同意义的问题，最终还是要看AI收入与资本支出是否平衡

text:
The tokenization of stocks has advanced from pilots to a recognized market segment, with on-chain trading volumes hitting a record $15.6 billion in September 2026 and total distributed value reaching several billion dollars. Growth stems from demand for 24/7 access, fractional ownership, and equity exposure on blockchain rails, while underlying shares stay in conventional custody. More than half of activity often occurs outside Wall Street hours, and many trades involve amounts smaller than one share.

Regulatory clarity has sped this shift. On September 17, 2026, the SEC issued an Innovation Exemption granting temporary conditional relief so certain Tokenized Securities Venues can facilitate on-chain secondary trading of tokenized National Market System stocks without full national securities exchange registration. The five-year order, expiring in September 2031, allows permissioned automated market makers and liquidity pools on public blockchains such as Ethereum, Solana, and BNB Chain. 

Venues must ensure tokens confer the same rights as the underlying shares, give issuers 30 days’ notice before listing third-party tokenized versions, and stay within limits—typically no more than 75 symbols for the most liquid names and volume caps of 0.25 percent of prior-month average daily volume. Liquidity providers receive temporary relief from dealer registration. SEC Chairman Paul Atkins called it a step to bring capital markets into the digital age while inviting comment for longer-term rules. Issuers retain an objection right that can block unaffiliated tokenized versions of their shares.

These limits keep the experiment small relative to the roughly $80 trillion U.S. equity market, yet activity has grown. Platforms have drawn millions of holders, with rising transfer volumes and active addresses. Products include fully backed 1:1 representations that can be minted and redeemed in-kind against regulated brokerage holdings, as well as offerings focused on price tracking and fractional access. 

Weekend and after-hours trading on decentralized venues has generated billions in volume, filling demand left unserved by conventional exchanges. Concentration among a few issuers and chains remains high, and questions of liquidity, higher volatility than the underlying shares, and precise shareholder-rights alignment continue to draw scrutiny, including from the IMF.

Tokenized equities are also blurring lines between cryptocurrency platforms and traditional brokerage infrastructure. As crypto venues add stock trading and large institutions seek to trade or hedge across both environments, demand has risen for financing, custody, and settlement services that support positions originating on one venue and offset on another. Providers already handling underlying shares for multiple tokenized-product issuers are positioned to extend into prime-brokerage-style capabilities, offering capital and operational support long dominated by major banks.

Challenges persist. Distinctions between true ownership and synthetic or price-linked exposure, settlement finality across chains, and reconciliation with traditional clearing systems still require resolution. 

Public companies are advised to monitor the 30-day issuer notices now required under the exemption. Participants continue testing interoperability, governance features such as proxy voting, and the economics of in-kind versus cash redemption. Structured as a temporary sandbox rather than permanent rulemaking, the exemption is expected to see further adjustments based on experience and comment before any broader framework emerges. 

So far it has embedded blockchain rails more deeply into equity markets while retaining core investor-protection and market-structure requirements.

Claude账号被封，申诉成功概率只有3.3%，我研究了一下过去半年的封号逻辑和规模，得出如下洞察，在使用Claude一定要看看：

1️⃣ 规模比你想的大

Anthropic 官方透明度报告，2025 下半年：
封号约 145 万
申诉成功率仅3.3%
也就是说，申诉 100 次，只成功 3 个

2️⃣ 封号确实跟着新模型走，但不是每次
6/9 Fable 5 发布 → 6 月底一大波中文号同一晚收到 disabled
7/24 Opus 5 → 有风控，但没那么狠
9/1 Fable 5.1、9/22 Opus 5.5 → 这两天又是一波

主要的目的还是防止蒸馏：新模型上线 → 流量、越狱、蒸馏一起涨 → 风控同步升级 → 风险路径集中暴雷。

3️⃣ 这次连企业号都没放过

Opus 5.5发布前后，通过 AWS、微软云用 Claude 的大中华区客户，有一批被停了。

更离谱的是，甚至还有个新加坡账号，因为中秋调休，使用时段和注册地对不上，都被判定为了异常。

4️⃣ 光换 IP 早就不够了

风控看的是整张画像：IP、时区、系统语言、支付卡地区、使用时段、设备指纹，任意一项对不上，都可能被判异常。

5️⃣ 这四类申诉基本救不活

不支持地区
拼车 / 共享 / 代充
拿 Pro/Max 订阅跑第三方客户端、高并发 Agent
批量刷输出做蒸馏

6️⃣ 新号前 72 小时最危险

刚注册、刚做完 KYC，就用虚拟卡冲 Max，账单地址和 IP 还不一致。社区里开号几小时就被封的案例，多半是这个组合。

总之，账号想存活久一点：独享号、IP不要变动、支付和地区一致、IP和地区一致

Papertrade’s Game Is Expanding Beyond $PAPER

The hype around @papertrade_xyz is creating a new game on HyperEVM, and $PSTR (@paperstrategy_) is one of the projects to watch

Here’s the simple idea:
• Papertrade: Traders can earn $PAPER by realizing trading losses. Staking $PAPER generates USDC yield from protocol revenue

• PaperStrategy: Instead of personally losing money to farm $PAPER, users can buy $PSTR, an independent token built around this mechanism

• The flywheel: $PSTR trading taxes fund a treasury, which deposits USDC into Papertrade and accumulates $PAPER. The strategy stakes that $PAPER, then uses around 90% of its staking yield for $PSTR buybacks and burns

More trading activity could fuel more capital, more $PAPER accumulation, and more buybacks

Why watch this meta?
Papertrade creates the underlying yield opportunity, while projects like $PSTR turn it into new token experiments. If Papertrade continues growing, expect more strategies and tokens competing to capture value from its ecosystem

The key risks are execution, dilution, smart contracts, and dependence on Papertrade’s revenue. $PSTR is independent of Papertrade and is not an official affiliated token

text:
Epithelial AhR–NKX3-1–Senescence Axis Drives Barrier Function and Inflammation in Allergic Rhinitis. First author: Xuan Yuan; corresponding authors: Zhihai Xie, Peisong Gao

This study investigates the role of aryl hydrocarbon receptor (AhR)-associated epithelial signaling and its contribution to barrier dysfunction and allergic inflammation. Allergic rhinitis nasal epithelium exhibits increased AhR activity associated with senescence-related transcriptional programs and senescence-associated secretory phenotype (SASP) inflammatory signals. AhR deficiency and CC10-lineage-enriched p16 deletion attenuate epithelial senescence-associated programs, improve barrier integrity, and reduce Type 2 inflammation in vivo. NKX3-1 contributes to AhR-linked epithelial cell-cycle arrest and senescence-associated responses, while curcumin attenuates allergen-induced senescence-associated phenotypes.

text:
How much control should a DeFi vault manager retain?

@PaulFrambot's proposal to distinguish between noncustodial and discretionary vaults has sparked a broader debate about where vault automation ends and active management begins.

Multichain deployment is a concrete example of this challenge. Running a vault across several networks often requires managers to bridge liquidity, update NAV and reconcile accounting separately on each chain, adding layers of manual intervention.

The way these operations are handled can determine how much control managers need to retain.

Centrifuge's approach has been to address this at the infrastructure level, allowing a fund to operate across multiple chains with one balance sheet, one accounting system and one onchain execution policy that encodes and enforces its investment mandate.

Pre Market Thoughts 14 Oct 26Pre Market Thoughts 14 Oct 26

The 2 upcoming risk events for today is the CPI release at 830AM ET as well as Anthropic releasing some information ahead of their IPO. This directly feeds into the 2 biggest driver of macro and markets currently - which is yields and the AI buildout.

First of, with regards to CPI numbers - its the last before mid terms. The more cynical amongst us would think that there would be some window dressing on the numbers. Personally i think this would spark a risk on move that i would probably trim some of my dip buys into.

On the Anthropic numbers, the entire semi investor community is on edge. For good reason, over the last week, select names have been battered by 10-20% or even more for the smaller caps. We are essentially seeing a rerun of the derisking in July. Memory in particular has been hit very hard. The anthropic numbers will be essential to contain some amount of fear. It is also interesting that Hock's remarks were taken entirely out of context and the mainstream media ran with it. For short term price action, this behavior is never what you want to see because it points to shorter term weakness.

For longer term investors, these often creates the best buying opportunities into the market. 

In yesterday's sell off and rebound, a few things are interesting to me. 1 - $SNDK bottomed out alot earlier and outperformed $MU. For the broadest part of the entire rally across march, april july - $SNDK has always led moves to the downside and also to the upside. In July, $SNDK bottomed out at 1000 first and even after $MU moved from 800 to 700, $SNDK held above 1000. This price action is a good sign post for me, with regards to the next 48 hours of price prediction.

2 - Next on $CBRS, this has been a name i followed, yesterday's strength was also remarkable to me and i have added further onto the ticker.

3 - Neoclouds on the other hand are not looking so hot. Especially with $CRWV bonds hitting 15% yields. This is reflective of the demand for funding in the sector. Doing a buildout via equity might be the best possible path ahead. $NBIS however was very strong with it recovering the earlier dip.

All in all, i would be expecting a rally post CPI numbers. Anthropic data releases is anyone's guess. However, if local lows are breached, i would cut most of the positions ($SOXL/$SNDK/$MU/$NBIS) here.

MAGS have gotten some attention. While i like the hyperscaler thesis on a medium term, in the short term - positioning for hyperscalers/mags have been the highest ever. If we are in a market that is trading against positioning, this would probably indicate weakness for mags int he period ahead. Don't @ me. I am just a messenger.

On crypto, i remain consistent that $BTC looks alot better than alts. Since warning about the low liquidity in some of the alt attention driven pumps - those tickers like $W, $STRK have given back quite a bit of their gains. Personally, i think most of the tickers are a coin toss, there is still not enough liquidity for a broad based rally in everything.  Even early runners like $ZEC, $NEAR, $VVV have started on their consolidation/chop leg. $NEAR especially, since it made a local high just this week.... However, this is also the time where i think it makes sense to buy the tickers that you actually have a thesis for - buy when its down, not when its high. I know some people like names like $PUMP, $ENA, $CHIP etc - i have not done my research into them but if i was interested in those names, this would be when i would buy in.

After posting that onchain looks bottomed, some of these tickers have made local bottoms. The ecosystem i like the best for these plays is on RH. I wont talk about these tickers here given its low in liquidity.

$PRL has made a new high - I posted about this at around 0.5-0.6. It remains by far the strongest alt in terms of attention to bagholder ratio. This tells me how much sidelined money there is. My conclusion post token was that there was alot of questions and attention, but nobody had really large bags - i.e underexposed. It was 1-1.1 then. Almost a double. I guess IRL sleuthing still works!

I believe that $PRL would soon start to get listed as well, which is where attention would funnel in even more as for the first time, many funds are also sidelined. In fact, risk taking retail who dared to rawdog safetrade were the only ones who managed to get some sizeable exposure. Most funds have strict restrictions on what exchanges they can interface with.

Paper trade, is now probably +EV for almost all the participants who took part on day 1. I will have a longer article on it shortly. I think this is the best venue for retail to trade because there is no slippage, no trading fee AND you get paid $PAPER for losing money. There are 2 roles to play - 1 is farming PAPER and trying to be a part of the liquidity provider. The other is to use PAPERTRADE and make money off it. The terminal will facilitate this very shortly

Good luck!

text:
事到如今，不得不承认前段时间 @RobinhoodCrypto 链上的情绪和表现进入了一个相对低谷期。但看一堆人前几天还在喊 Robinhood is dead，今天随着链上热度的略微好转又改称 Robinhood summer 2.0 要来了，这个现象本身也是挺有意思的。

自 @168X_Fortune 访谈过后，有段时间没怎么系统地聊聊对于 Robinhood 的后续看法了，所以今天想来简单聊几句，但不想称之为辩经。在聊下面这些观点之前，我想先说明的一个基本前提和事实是，当前大盘本就不稳，链上情绪的消退也不止发生在 RHC 一条链上，就最近一段时间而言，其他链也好不到哪去。明确了这一点后，我们再来从注意力、叙事主权、用户结构、战略方向等更 High-level 的角度聊聊为什么现在谈论 RHC 终局还为时尚早。

1/ 注意力层面

可以说这轮新周期链上开始复兴就是从 Robinhood Chain（下文也称 RHC）上线开始的，也是从那个时候，市场开始慢慢将更多注意力挪回到链上。再后来，无论是币股配对的 MEMEFi 玩法，还是发射台大战，基本都由 RHC 引领；其他一些分支，比如 V4 Hooks 和 AI 相关叙事，RHC 也是最主要的战场之一。

这种基调从 RHC 诞生那天就定下了。就像 @0xYond 老师说的，散户也许撤得快（链上丛林法则，资金是没有忠诚度的），但真正决定一条链「气候」的，往往是中小 Project Builders，他们就像候鸟，气候还在就不会走，甚至还会来更多。短期来看，并没有另一条链能抢走「链上美股流动性」这块注意力；所以即便链上情绪最 Down 的时候，RHC 大概率仍会是最活跃的几条链之一，而不是被彻底遗忘的那种鬼链。

注意力退潮 ≠ 叙事退场。前者是情绪周期，后者是谁在定义下一轮链上该玩什么。

2/ 叙事主权层面

Robinhood 一直以来传达出来的战略都是通过券商后端 + 真实股票库存 + Token Issuer + Robinhood Chain + 钱包的组合打法，把股票变成可编程、可抵押、可进 AMM 的互联网资产，让美股敞口向全球用户打开。这一点其他链基本很难比拟，从这一点来说，股票代币化的叙事主权已经被 Robinhood 牢牢握在手里，而 RHC 在其中的战略地位不言而喻。

值得一提的一个点是，此前的 AMC 之争表面上争的是授权，实质是上市公司管得了附带权利，却管不了股票卖出后的一切合法用途。这也是在为股票上链后的二次开发做铺垫，抢的是资产扩张权的边界。

再往后看，分红/投票等功能上线后，链上股票的定位将会从加密衍生品向真正的代币化证券靠拢，RHC 则是那个真正的消费级入口，一个全球 7×24 资本市场，而不只是 meme 赌场。

3/ 用户结构层面

很多人容易把 Robinhood 的券商基因跟机构稳定币链这类东西归为一类，但其实两者要的东西完全不同，Robinhood 要的是传统流量导入、交易活性、业务延展，Plasma/Stable/Tempo/Arc 则更偏支付结算与合规卡位。

这也导致两者在用户结构上差得很远。一边是零售交易者、meme 玩家、想碰美股敞口的全球用户；一边是机构现金流、结算路径、合规敞口。同样遇到问题的时候， @vladtenev 能硬刚 AMC，靠的是券商侧对零售用户和交易场景的掌控；机构稳定币链却未必有这份底气。所以，拿 RHC 跟以太坊、Solana、BNB 这些链比还能理解，但如果把它跟 Arc 之类的比就大可不必，这不是来吸引你 Fomo 另一条机构链。

另外一层经常被忽略的是，RHC 真正抬高的，不只是又一条能打的 L2，而是 Uniswap / Lighter / Arcus 这类深度绑定的原有协议的天花板，仔细想想 UNI/LIT 是从什么时候开始重新吸引注意力并一路向上的。这在一定程度上说明了，分发和场景往往比又一条新链本身更重要，而这也是 Robinhood 的用户结构决定的。

4/ 战略方向层面

监管侧 SEC 前段时间发布的豁免，在我看来 Robinhood 也是妥妥的最大受益方之一，但这个豁免开的从来不是再发一堆锚定股价的代币，更像是在试一种新的市场形态，把 AMM/LP 一类机制放进实验范围，看看能折腾到什么样的高度。Robinhood 本来就站在 TradFi<>Crypto 的交界处，L2 + Stock Tokens + Wallet + DeFi 是可以拼装成完整闭环的，这种卡位纯 Crypto 原生链也挺难复制。

更长远一点说，真正有杀伤力的点在于：护照和本地券商将不再决定你能买什么。任何人只要有一个钱包就能接上全球资产与流动性。传统金融还在吵发行人同不同意的时候，Robinhood 链上已经在用真金白银跑出「下一代全球资本市场」的雏形了。

所以回看当下这段低谷，大家应该重点关注和赌的不该只是本周/月手续费收入表现如何、某个 meme 能不能反弹，或 RHC 能不能打败 Solana/Base/BNB 带来新的 meme summer。更该看的是叙事主权还在不在、券商分发 + 监管实验能不能拼成闭环、已经来的 Builder 走不走、新的 Builder 来不来，以及美股能不能真正变成全球可编程资产，又由谁来承载和放大它的价值。

最后，如果你感兴趣的话，昨天凌晨 @vladtenev 开了一个 AMA 帖子，回复了大量的问题，耐心看看他说了什么，也许你会找到你想要的答案。

quoted_text:
最近 Almanak 上线了新产品，之前做过一些研究，所以正好借着热度，聊聊这个项目。

他们的思路：一个人跑一支链上对冲基金。

查了一下 Almanak 这个单词，是“年鉴”的意思，一般图书喜欢叫这个名字。

这个项目做的东西是 AI 代理+策略，上面各种策略横飞，加到一起，倒是也可以称之为“基金策略年鉴”。

于是乎，测试了一下他们的产品，输入的指令是：
 
 在 Uniswap 上做主流币（WBTC、ETH）+稳定币（USDT、USDC）做 LP。

1. 定位哪个 Pair 的 APR 最高，在什么链上？这可能会涉及到 2*2*链数 种可能
2. 通过近期、中期判断应该设置的价格区间
3. 根据价格区间计算应当投入的主流币、稳定币两种本金占比（假设每个仓位投入 100K 美金）

然后 Almanak 的 AI 问了几个问题之后，就开始抓取、分析。

最后分析出来，Base 上面的 ETH/USDC 流动性是以上这些选择里 APR 最高的，然后选择了 1600-3300 区间。

接下来，就直接进入开发、测试、部署流程了。

PS：真是不把 AI 当人啊。

大概 10 分钟后策略建好，如果往合约打了这个钱，这个钱包就会真的直接开始执行策略。

使用 Almanak 一个很好的切入点，是先从小资金的测试开始，也就是“构想验证”。如果效果不错、且安全运行，再考虑扩大规模。

例如去年年底，有个机构申请了夜盘比特币 ETF，在美股收盘后建仓比特币，白天天亮了就卖了。这种 idea 你乍一听挺好，但是具体效果如何，你还得去真跑一个测试。

你丢个 100 美金进去，直接告诉Almanak，让它写点代码一跑，跑个十天半个月的实盘，心里自然就有结果了，一下子节约好多时间。

还可以进阶一下，可以跑一些量化策略。

再例如，因为 Almanak 现在已经接入了 GMX，拿套利来说，可以让它写一个 1x 现货+1x 等值空单的策略，赚赚费率，现货还能存入 Aave、Morpho 之类的做收益增强。

PS：真的很需要它也接入HyperLiquid，支持 HyperEVM 链😂。

这样，从策略的构建、测试，到增加规模，都可以靠 Prompt 实现。

话说回来，从基金风控角度来说，在真正投入大资金前，需要对代码进行充分的审计，确保程序的安全。人类AI 审计、人类审计，甚至第三方审计都是必要的。

感兴趣的话，可以都来测试一下。

每个普通用户每周可以白嫖三个高级信号（Signal），用完了可以充会员，或者使用无限的免费信号。

另外，写策略的时候，不是一定要用信号，也可以直接和 Almanak Code 烧 credits 去对话，这个额度是每月会 renew 一次。

text:
Nvidia + Tesla in one token, earning fees when people trade.

That’s the idea behind @ClutchMarkets’ Pair Tokens on Robinhood Chain.

Think of each Pair Token as a receipt for your share of a trading pool holding two assets. Other people swap between those assets and pay fees. Those fees can be reinvested into the pool.

The simple flow:
Deposit assets → receive Pair Tokens → earn trading fees → reinvest.

According to the announcement, minting and redeeming have no protocol fee. Compounding takes 10% of earned trading fees for $STONKBROKER buybacks (which kinda meh).

So $100 in collected fees means $90 for reinvestment and $10 for buybacks, before other costs.

The potential upside:

• Easier to manage. One transferable token represents the whole position.

• Less upkeep. The pool covers the full price range, so you don’t need to keep adjusting a narrow trading range.

• Fees plus dividends. Trading fees can compound. For dividend-paying Robinhood Stock Tokens, dividends are separately reinvested through a multiplier that increases the shares each token represents.

The trade-offs:

• You may earn less than simply holding both assets. If Nvidia outperforms Tesla, the pool gradually holds less Nvidia and more Tesla. This is the risk called “impermanent loss.” Fees may not cover the difference.

• Quiet pools earn little. Returns depend on actual trading, and reinvesting fees won’t stop the underlying assets from falling in value.

• More moving parts. Custom contracts add security risks. Stock tokens also depend on the issuer and custodian, come with access restrictions, and don’t give you direct shareholder rights.

FYI, tradable pool shares already existed with Uniswap v2. Pair Tokens extend that idea with customizable v4 pool rules and tokenized stocks.

The potential is simpler access to liquidity strategies. The real test is whether returns after costs beat just holding the assets. Audits, reliable withdrawals, and sustained trading would strengthen the case; those outcomes remain unverified here.

We have created a new type of token using Uniswap v4 hooks that we call a Pair Token.

What is a Pair Token?

A Pair Token is a fused, auto-compounding ERC-20 asset that combines two tokens into one.

For example, stock tokens on Robinhood Chain could be fused into new tokenized assets:

NVDA + TSLA = NVDATSLA

AAPL + MSFT = AAPLMSFT

Each Pair Token represents a proportional share of the full-range Uniswap v4 liquidity pool.

So why mint these tokens?

At any moment, anyone can call the compound function to reinvest the LP fees generated by the pair’s trading activity back into the underlying asset since Robinhood Stock tokens also self multiply because of dividends we get a double compound effect.

This creates a new financial primitive that behaves similarly to an LP position NFT, except it is fungible,tradeable , auto-compounding, and designed to grow its underlying holdings through trading fees.

Since it is an ERC-20, it can be freely traded onchain, LPed, or even paired with a launchpad.

A new type of token for a new type of exposure and strategy.

Starting tonight, you’ll be able to mint or redeem Pair Tokens for any pair on Robinhood Chain via the StonkBrokers website.

Minting and redeeming are free, while compounding incurs a 10% fee on the LP fees generated, which is used for $STONKBROKER buybacks.

We look forward to seeing a new line of products and protocols on Robinhood Chain using this new financial primitive.

Only on Robinhood Chain, powered by Uniswap.

翻到我 3 年前写的推文，气得想笑。

text:
🚨 Polymarket US is cutting its trading rebates.

next week they will slash incentives for BOTH market makers and takers.

And the numbers are brutal.

📉 MAKER REBATES

Previously, ALL market makers received the same rebate coefficient of −0.0125, regardless of volume.

Now, rebates depend on monthly maker volume:

- Under $10M: 0 (−100%)
- $10M–$50M: −0.0035 (−72%)
- $50M–$200M: −0.0070 (−44%)
- $200M+: −0.0104 (−16.8%)

which means that If you do under >$10M volume, no rebates at all ! 

and even whales at the max tier doing over $200M in monthly maker volume will get less than before.

📉 TAKER REBATES

It's arguably even worse for takers

Previously:
- $250K–$1M monthly volume: 10% back
- $1M–$10M: 25% back
- $10M+: 50% back

Starting October 19:

- $250K–$1M: 3% (−70%)
• $1M–$10M: 5% (−80%)
• $10M–$25M: 10% (−80%)
• $50M+: 30% (−40%)

that's a massive reduction at every tier.

And there's another detail buried in the CFTC filings:

Polymarket will allow traders to qualify for higher rebate tiers using volume from *other prediction markets*.

The strategy seems clear:

>Cut subsidies to smaller retail MMs. 
>rely instead on  institutional-scale MMs that have multi platform operations.

They are moving closer and closer to Kalshi both in price and fee structure

I don't think we will ever see a merging of Polymarket US and Polymarket International orderbooks seeing how their liquidity strategies continue to diverge

quoted_text:
事到如今，不得不承认前段时间 @RobinhoodCrypto 链上的情绪和表现进入了一个相对低谷期。但看一堆人前几天还在喊 Robinhood is dead，今天随着链上热度的略微好转又改称 Robinhood summer 2.0 要来了，这个现象本身也是挺有意思的。

自 @168X_Fortune 访谈过后，有段时间没怎么系统地聊聊对于 Robinhood 的后续看法了，所以今天想来简单聊几句，但不想称之为辩经。在聊下面这些观点之前，我想先说明的一个基本前提和事实是，当前大盘本就不稳，链上情绪的消退也不止发生在 RHC 一条链上，就最近一段时间而言，其他链也好不到哪去。明确了这一点后，我们再来从注意力、叙事主权、用户结构、战略方向等更 High-level 的角度聊聊为什么现在谈论 RHC 终局还为时尚早。

1/ 注意力层面

可以说这轮新周期链上开始复兴就是从 Robinhood Chain（下文也称 RHC）上线开始的，也是从那个时候，市场开始慢慢将更多注意力挪回到链上。再后来，无论是币股配对的 MEMEFi 玩法，还是发射台大战，基本都由 RHC 引领；其他一些分支，比如 V4 Hooks 和 AI 相关叙事，RHC 也是最主要的战场之一。

这种基调从 RHC 诞生那天就定下了。就像 @0xYond 老师说的，散户也许撤得快（链上丛林法则，资金是没有忠诚度的），但真正决定一条链「气候」的，往往是中小 Project Builders，他们就像候鸟，气候还在就不会走，甚至还会来更多。短期来看，并没有另一条链能抢走「链上美股流动性」这块注意力；所以即便链上情绪最 Down 的时候，RHC 大概率仍会是最活跃的几条链之一，而不是被彻底遗忘的那种鬼链。

注意力退潮 ≠ 叙事退场。前者是情绪周期，后者是谁在定义下一轮链上该玩什么。

2/ 叙事主权层面

Robinhood 一直以来传达出来的战略都是通过券商后端 + 真实股票库存 + Token Issuer + Robinhood Chain + 钱包的组合打法，把股票变成可编程、可抵押、可进 AMM 的互联网资产，让美股敞口向全球用户打开。这一点其他链基本很难比拟，从这一点来说，股票代币化的叙事主权已经被 Robinhood 牢牢握在手里，而 RHC 在其中的战略地位不言而喻。

值得一提的一个点是，此前的 AMC 之争表面上争的是授权，实质是上市公司管得了附带权利，却管不了股票卖出后的一切合法用途。这也是在为股票上链后的二次开发做铺垫，抢的是资产扩张权的边界。

再往后看，分红/投票等功能上线后，链上股票的定位将会从加密衍生品向真正的代币化证券靠拢，RHC 则是那个真正的消费级入口，一个全球 7×24 资本市场，而不只是 meme 赌场。

3/ 用户结构层面

很多人容易把 Robinhood 的券商基因跟机构稳定币链这类东西归为一类，但其实两者要的东西完全不同，Robinhood 要的是传统流量导入、交易活性、业务延展，Plasma/Stable/Tempo/Arc 则更偏支付结算与合规卡位。

这也导致两者在用户结构上差得很远。一边是零售交易者、meme 玩家、想碰美股敞口的全球用户；一边是机构现金流、结算路径、合规敞口。同样遇到问题的时候， @vladtenev 能硬刚 AMC，靠的是券商侧对零售用户和交易场景的掌控；机构稳定币链却未必有这份底气。所以，拿 RHC 跟以太坊、Solana、BNB 这些链比还能理解，但如果把它跟 Arc 之类的比就大可不必，这不是来吸引你 Fomo 另一条机构链。

另外一层经常被忽略的是，RHC 真正抬高的，不只是又一条能打的 L2，而是 Uniswap / Lighter / Arcus 这类深度绑定的原有协议的天花板，仔细想想 UNI/LIT 是从什么时候开始重新吸引注意力并一路向上的。这在一定程度上说明了，分发和场景往往比又一条新链本身更重要，而这也是 Robinhood 的用户结构决定的。

4/ 战略方向层面

监管侧 SEC 前段时间发布的豁免，在我看来 Robinhood 也是妥妥的最大受益方之一，但这个豁免开的从来不是再发一堆锚定股价的代币，更像是在试一种新的市场形态，把 AMM/LP 一类机制放进实验范围，看看能折腾到什么样的高度。Robinhood 本来就站在 TradFi<>Crypto 的交界处，L2 + Stock Tokens + Wallet + DeFi 是可以拼装成完整闭环的，这种卡位纯 Crypto 原生链也挺难复制。

更长远一点说，真正有杀伤力的点在于：护照和本地券商将不再决定你能买什么。任何人只要有一个钱包就能接上全球资产与流动性。传统金融还在吵发行人同不同意的时候，Robinhood 链上已经在用真金白银跑出「下一代全球资本市场」的雏形了。

所以回看当下这段低谷，大家应该重点关注和赌的不该只是本周/月手续费收入表现如何、某个 meme 能不能反弹，或 RHC 能不能打败 Solana/Base/BNB 带来新的 meme summer。更该看的是叙事主权还在不在、券商分发 + 监管实验能不能拼成闭环、已经来的 Builder 走不走、新的 Builder 来不来，以及美股能不能真正变成全球可编程资产，又由谁来承载和放大它的价值。

最后，如果你感兴趣的话，昨天凌晨 @vladtenev 开了一个 AMA 帖子，回复了大量的问题，耐心看看他说了什么，也许你会找到你想要的答案。

晚上就要公布CPI了，具体看法往前翻两条引文也都说清楚了。

再简单概括下就是比较悲观看空，觉得会出偏鹰数据。此时此刻10月加息概率为21.6%，9月高油价放在那里CPI反弹也是必然事件。唯一的博弈点就是反弹强度到底有多大，是符合预期还是高于预期。

四项数值中，两项年率一项总体月率的最终数据高于前值但低于预期值，那么近期的下跌可能是市场过度悲观超卖了，公布数据后可能会反弹一波。

如果高于预期值，那美股恐怕就要大逃亡了。

至于低于预期我是不太敢想了，既不符合现实对美联储利率预期调整来说也没有必要。除非川普此时非常想要再撑一下美股，但美伊局势高油价摆在面前，美股短期再拉高难度略大，他没有必要在两院都注定要输的情况下再付出更多沉没成本了，不如抓紧把工作重点转向中选之后。

四项CPI数据中，最关键且目前唯一预期值低于前值的是核心月率，如果这个数据真能控制住，今晚风险市场可能表现还不会太差。

总之，从大的方面说，今晚CPI和明晚PPI的最佳结果是让已经出现头部趋势的美债收益率继续下行，这样风险市场才能根本性好转。

总体月率0.5%左右、核心月率0.2%或更低，是最值得关注的债市利好组合；核心0.1%会更有力。总体0.6%、核心0.2%也允许收益率继续下跌。但高了就麻烦了。

能源涨价已经在市场预测中，今晚真正关键的是核心通胀有没有进一步扩散，以及债市是否因此上修未来利率路径。若核心温和、实际收益率延续回落，近期下跌中的部分风险折价可能被修复；若核心明显偏热，且明晚PPI进一步确认成本压力，美债阶段性见顶的判断就需要重新评估。

quoted_text:
- @AnchorNode Just inspired  PAPER-Hertzflow Dual Hedge Strategy (PDHS) ⚡

What if the hedge leg of Papertrade was moved to @Hertzflow_xyz? 

The idea is to generate PAPER through trading losses on Papertrade, then open an opposite-direction position on HertzFlow to hedge the remaining price exposure while accumulating trading volume for points.

Here’s how the strategy works. 🧵

1. Understanding PAPER minting costs

Based on the current rate of approximately 23 PAPER per $1 of loss and publicly available fees:

• At 100x leverage, a 0.5% price move followed by a manual close results in an estimated cost of $0.007 per token, with a lower limit of around $0.005.

• The estimated naked loss is approximately $0.043 per token.

• At 1,000x leverage, an adverse price move of roughly 0.05% can wipe out the position, with liquidation-related minting costs estimated at around $0.03 per token.

These figures are estimates. Mint rates and fees can change.

2. Why use HertzFlow for the hedge?

Opening an opposite position directly on Papertrade may not achieve the intended outcome because of differences in settlement mechanisms.

Papertrade profits can be skimmed, and when the pool lacks sufficient liquidity, profit withdrawals may enter a queue.

HertzFlow's normal mode settles based on oracle prices and its own liquidity pool, with profits returned to the wallet in USDT.

Hyper Lev may also be unsuitable for this strategy because only around 20% of small profits may be retained, potentially reducing the effectiveness of the hedge.

3. The proposed setup

Papertrade

- Open a single directional position.
- Use 10x–20x leverage to allow more room for price fluctuations.
- Generate the losses required to mint PAPER.

HertzFlow

- Trade the same underlying asset.
- Open an opposite-direction position with a matching notional value.
- Use normal mode with 3x–5x leverage.
- Maintain sufficient margin to reduce the risk of liquidation when mark prices temporarily diverge.

The objective is to offset Papertrade's price exposure while keeping hedge profits in HertzFlow rather than depending on Papertrade's LP redemption queue.

4. Risk management is critical ⚠️

Both positions need to be monitored and closed together.

If the price oscillates, Papertrade's unrealized loss may shrink, reducing the amount of PAPER that can be minted. Leaving the HertzFlow hedge open after closing the Papertrade position creates additional directional exposure.

At 1,000x leverage, a tiny adverse price movement can trigger liquidation, leaving little time to establish the hedge. Lower leverage on Papertrade may provide a more practical execution window.

The strategy is experimental, not risk-free. Fees, slippage, funding, execution delays, liquidation and settlement differences can all affect the final outcome.

Anyone exploring this approach should carefully verify the mechanics and test with small amounts before committing significant capital.

📉 PONS 回撤近70%，Bonk Guy 持仓缩水超1500万美元

知名交易员 Bonk Guy（@theunipcs）的投资组合价值已从峰值2600万美元降至约1040万美元，缩水超1500万美元。

PONS 的核心问题，在于其估值与交易热度高度绑定。交易量带来手续费，手续费支撑回购，回购又强化代币的上涨预期。

但当市场热度退潮，这套飞轮就可能反向运转。据数据显示，PONS 单日收入曾突破100万美元，近期则降至约10万美元级别，回购能力面临考验。

与此同时，Robinhood Chain 还面临交易基础设施竞争，以及 Meme 资金流动带来的不确定性。

当然，收入下降并不意味着回购必然停止，也不能据此断定整个生态已经熄火。

但有一点值得警惕：牛市里，交易量驱动的回购机制是上涨放大器；市场降温时，它也可能成为下跌的加速器。

当增长预期开始松动，真正的考验才刚刚开始。

最近4meme进行了产品更新，我研究了一下，比较有意思。

假如，4stock接入了一支新的热门股票（假如叫做4ABC），社区创建了股票meme（假如叫做ABC理论），然后系统自动在pancakeswap infinity（V4）创建流动性池子，也就是“ABC理论/4ABC”。

如果，后续bStock也上线了ABC（也就是bABC），那么，4meme通过pancakeswap的infinity共享库存钩子（SIH）机制，会把旧池子自动过渡“ABC理论/bABC”这个新池子。也就是：

ABC理论/4ABC → ABC理论/bABC

这就实现了4stock到bStock的自动化迁移，同时有利于加厚流动性。

4meme的这次更新还是非常有意思的，后续需要密切关注4stock的动态，或许能跑出一些好玩的meme.

4Stock brings popular stocks onchain before their bStock is available. To ensure Stock Memes built on 4Stock can transition to bStock seamlessly, we’ve introduced a shared-inventory pool mechanism built on @PancakeSwap Infinity’s Shared Inventory Hook (SIH).

How it works:
- At graduation, a newly created Stock Meme opens its primary pool as Meme / 4Stock
- Once the corresponding bStock is live, primary liquidity migrates to Meme / bStock in one step
- The same meme inventory backs both pairs, so price and depth remain continuous and trading is never interrupted
- Only one primary pool exists at any time, keeping each token fully compatible with aggregators

No action is required from creators or holders.

把对冲腿搬到 HertzFlow，前一段只在 Papertrade 上发生，用来铸 PAPER；后一段在 HertzFlow 普通模式，把还没发生的价格风险卖掉。

我刚刚专门把费用和成本试了一遍。

Papertrade 只开一边，杠杆放在 10 到 20 倍。1000 倍大约 0.05% 就爆，来不及锁；10 倍时价格要反向走大约 10% 才爆，中间有时间下对冲单。

在HertzFlow 这边，同一标的、同一名义价值、普通模式、3 到 5 倍。保证金仓位要够，为了两边标记价短暂错开时，对冲腿不会先爆。

按大约 23 枚 PAPER / 1 美元亏损，费率随时在变

主要是为了把盈利放在 HertzFlow 里，不进 Papertrade 的tracked LP 的兑付队列。

锁上之后，两边必须一起平，保证Papertrade 不再扩大亏损
震荡的时候 Papertrade 亏损变小、铸币也少，这时候要一起平，不能留着对冲腿单挂

text:
Nvidia + Tesla in one token, earning fees when people trade.

That’s the idea behind @ClutchMarkets’ Pair Tokens on Robinhood Chain.

Think of each Pair Token as a receipt for your share of a trading pool holding two assets. Other people swap between those assets and pay fees. Those fees can be reinvested into the pool.

The simple flow:
Deposit assets → receive Pair Tokens → earn trading fees → reinvest.

According to the announcement, minting and redeeming have no protocol fee. Compounding takes 10% of earned trading fees for $STONKBROKER buybacks (which kinda meh).

So $100 in collected fees means $90 for reinvestment and $10 for buybacks, before other costs.

The potential upside:

• Easier to manage. One transferable token represents the whole position.

• Less upkeep. The pool covers the full price range, so you don’t need to keep adjusting a narrow trading range.

• Fees plus dividends. Trading fees can compound. For dividend-paying Robinhood Stock Tokens, dividends are separately reinvested through a multiplier that increases the shares each token represents.

The trade-offs:

• You may earn less than simply holding both assets. If Nvidia outperforms Tesla, the pool gradually holds less Nvidia and more Tesla. This is the risk called “impermanent loss.” Fees may not cover the difference.

• Quiet pools earn little. Returns depend on actual trading, and reinvesting fees won’t stop the underlying assets from falling in value.

• More moving parts. Custom contracts add security risks. Stock tokens also depend on the issuer and custodian, come with access restrictions, and don’t give you direct shareholder rights.

FYI, tradable pool shares already existed with Uniswap v2. Pair Tokens extend that idea with customizable v4 pool rules and tokenized stocks.

The potential is simpler access to liquidity strategies. The real test is whether returns after costs beat just holding the assets. Audits, reliable withdrawals, and sustained trading would strengthen the case; those outcomes remain unverified here.

We have created a new type of token using Uniswap v4 hooks that we call a Pair Token.

What is a Pair Token?

A Pair Token is a fused, auto-compounding ERC-20 asset that combines two tokens into one.

For example, stock tokens on Robinhood Chain could be fused into new tokenized assets:

NVDA + TSLA = NVDATSLA

AAPL + MSFT = AAPLMSFT

Each Pair Token represents a proportional share of the full-range Uniswap v4 liquidity pool.

So why mint these tokens?

At any moment, anyone can call the compound function to reinvest the LP fees generated by the pair’s trading activity back into the underlying asset since Robinhood Stock tokens also self multiply because of dividends we get a double compound effect.

This creates a new financial primitive that behaves similarly to an LP position NFT, except it is fungible,tradeable , auto-compounding, and designed to grow its underlying holdings through trading fees.

Since it is an ERC-20, it can be freely traded onchain, LPed, or even paired with a launchpad.

A new type of token for a new type of exposure and strategy.

Starting tonight, you’ll be able to mint or redeem Pair Tokens for any pair on Robinhood Chain via the StonkBrokers website.

Minting and redeeming are free, while compounding incurs a 10% fee on the LP fees generated, which is used for $STONKBROKER buybacks.

We look forward to seeing a new line of products and protocols on Robinhood Chain using this new financial primitive.

Only on Robinhood Chain, powered by Uniswap.

text:
If you’re launching a market, creating a pool is the easy part. The harder question is what gives people a reason to provide liquidity, trade, and keep participating after launch.

That’s the problem we’re working on with Statics Phase 1, now deployed on @RobinhoodCrypto .

A creator can launch a public Uniswap v4 market, choose its pair and fee settings, and receive 5% of the hook fees that market collects. The pool’s native Uniswap v4 LP fee goes to liquidity providers. Those are separate fees, with separate recipients.

Liquidity providers can also enrol eligible positions in a range gauge for funded rewards while their liquidity is in range. robinhood:0x2d8d6f4a93acd7a916a5a654ec8b690ba3b3eadd stakers can select assets they want to earn fees in and allocate their stake toward pools to direct protocol incentives. Rewards depend on eligibility, funding, and actual activity, staking or opening a pool alone does not generate them.

Creators can choose to activate managed protocol-owned liquidity for a public pool. If they do, a share of future hook fees can build liquidity held in protocol custody. It’s an option for a market, not something that happens just because the pool exists.

These actions come together in a PositionNFT - an account for managing stake, allocations, enrolled liquidity, and claims.
That’s the Phase 1 idea in practical terms - give the people creating markets, supplying liquidity, and directing incentives defined roles in how a market develops. We’ve also documented baskets, lending, Statics Dollar, and Morpho integration for later phases,
 
If you’re evaluating a market on Statics, start with its live liquidity, current fees, and funded rewards. If you’re building one, we’d like to hear what your market needs.

text:
AI FACT-CHECK 2.0 | PAMBA'S “50 ACCOUNTS IN AN HOUR” CLAIM

OVERALL VERDICT: UNVERIFIED
LOGICAL CONCLUSION: UNSUPPORTED

A promotional X post by Pamba cofounder & CTO Karol Zdebel claims users can create 50 new TikTok & Instagram accounts “in the next hour,” that Pamba has generated 500M+ views without a single user being banned or detected as a bot, and that 95%+ of traffic is from the US because its iPhones are physically in the US and use US carrier SIMs.

WHAT CHECKS OUT

Pamba is a real service. Its current API documentation confirms that customers can buy managed TikTok and Instagram accounts, choose usernames, have accounts created on Pamba's phones, configure warming, and post through those accounts.

Pamba also states that its accounts run on physical iPhones with US SIM cards.

WHAT IS NOT INDEPENDENTLY VERIFIED

• 500M+ views
• 95%+ US traffic
• zero users banned or detected as bots
• 50 accounts being ready within one hour

These performance claims originate from Pamba/Zdebel. I found no independent audit or dataset sufficient to verify them.

Pamba's own API says account creation can take “minutes to longer” and that multiple recreations on one phone run sequentially, each taking “tens of minutes.” This does not establish a one-hour completion time for 50 accounts.

THE 95% CAUSAL CLAIM

TikTok confirms that location, device settings, device type and the country where content was published can affect recommendations.

But TikTok explicitly describes recommendations as multifactorial and says user interactions are generally weighted more heavily for most users.

Therefore, US iPhones/SIMs → 95%+ US traffic is not established by TikTok's documentation. The reported 95% figure could be genuine; the claimed causal explanation is not demonstrated.

CONCLUSION

The underlying Pamba infrastructure is documented. The headline performance claims are not independently verified, and the post presents correlation as a causal explanation without sufficient evidence.

Sources: Pamba API & About pages; TikTok “How TikTok recommends content”; archived/indexed copy of the original X post.

────────────────────
AI FACT-CHECK 2.0
Verdict: UNVERIFIED
Logical conclusion: UNSUPPORTED
Checked: 3 Oct 2026

text:
There are many ways to tap into Ethereum’s unique features. Its two unique features to me are its decentralisation, and its state: liquidity, user accounts etc, all accumulated from 11 years of continuous uptime.

Decentralisation and trustlessness of the L1 have been the key to obtaining liquidity over time, including for ETH.

Some use cases want to tap into the chain’s decentralisation, and build to obtain the same properties that decentralisation offers: integrity, uptime and fair access (safety, liveness, censorship-resistance).

Some use cases want to tap into liquidity. This is not parasitic: this creates demand for L1-issued assets, in particular ETH.

Some use cases want to tap into both! But the liquidity is only there, once again, because of the L1’s decentralisation and trustlessness.

Making the L1 a better home for liquidity amplifies something that is originally there because of the L1’s core properties. In particular, L1 should serve as the root of trust for assets that go on to be deployed across various use cases.

Note that this argument does not depend on whether the use case in question is offered as “an L2” or not. L1 apps, including some tokens, may offer very little of the properties that the chain offers maximally. Let us not confuse the way a use case is packaged with the properties it offers. L2s themselves come in different shapes, and at the limit blur with what one might recognise as an L1 application.

So we need not pin our hopes on any one kind of package to realise the potential of Ethereum. We need not reject them either, when their success celebrates Ethereum’s unique offering to the world. We may even support their emergence, particularly so when providing them the means to succeed is aligned with improving the L1’s own core properties.

text:
看到巴黎哥得这篇推文，我是挺有感触得，感触得是我是完全相反得人。

如果我只有 1,000 万，我是不会去买 500 万的房子和200 万的车，但在我只有 20 万的时候，我确实买了 200万的房子和 30 万的车，看上去特别矛盾，但也算是一种自我进化了。

在没有接触到加密货币的时候我就是一个游戏行业的打工者，月薪也就是 2万+ ，看上去在那个年代这个工资是可以的，但想要靠工资买房是基本不可能的，所以还是找父母赞助了一些资金才能买房。

在上海买第一套房的时候，我其实是负资产，虽然账户里有 20 万现金，但银行里还有车贷，我是先买车后买房的，差距不到一个月吧，然后找双方父母拆借了 100 万付的首付，剩下的 100 万正好是公积金，所以就没有用商业贷款。

如果人生没有加密货币，我可能就这么走下去了，这套房子和车的压力不大，当时我还算年轻，还了房贷和车贷不是问题，即便是到了年龄大了失业了，也能维持一个相对体面的生活。

但后来随着确实赚了点小钱，反而是我对消费非常的抵触了，第二套房子还是我来新加坡前两年才买的，满打满算我在新房住了都不到一年，即便是如此，新房我都是卖了旧房以后才换的，一共贴了 200 万人民币不到的现金吧，感谢我第一套房子卖了非常好的价格。

如果不是，我即便没有打算来新加坡，可能都不会想换房，我是一个很喜欢算账的人，可能也是之前的生活不富裕所以导致了现在有点“吝啬”，我一直都会再算，如果我赚不到钱了，那么接下来的生活会怎么办？

这是我几乎每隔一段时间都会问自己的问题，所以在我来看，满足我个人物欲的前提是没有后顾之忧，当然哪有 100% 的没有后顾之忧，尽人事听天命罢了。

所以我的资产配置在之前也聊过了：

首先 bitcoin:native 是第一步，我今生最大的希望就是可以不净卖出 Bitcoin 而尽量多存一些，所有的 Bitcoin 都是遗产。

其次就是大额人寿保险，这也是接触侃哥以后有的意识，花相对小的钱买了一份较大的保险，如果真的我不在了，起码能保持家庭生活不至于滑坡，当然这笔钱如果是 1,000 万的话，最少最少都要用掉 20%  的首付。

然后就是把我一部分的加密货币，包括一部分的 BTC 和 ethereum:native 从加密货币的形态转变成现货 ETF ，存在私行里，这也要感谢侃哥给我指明，之前我是都存在硬件钱包里的，后来鉴于最近发生的事情，还是存在私行更靠谱一些。

其它的加密货币基本就在各个交易所放着，找到机会该处理处理，该卖就卖。

现金部分也还有一些，但不是纯粹的现金，基本都是 USDC 的形式，截至到昨天，但今天银行需要我提供一笔现金的资产证明，不得已还是要把 USDC 换成 USD ，这笔钱用来买三个月的定期，4% 的收益。主要是银行没得选。

以后这笔钱可能会买成短期美债，这笔现金是我一直在计算，如果我不能赚钱的话，最少仍然能在新加坡维持目前生活一直到花栗鼠上大学的钱，当然准备还是要多准备一些，以防万一。

所以回到正题，即便是现金部分，我有一些但目前也是过着和打工时候差不多的生活，花费最多的就是花栗鼠的读书和维持在新加坡的费用，其它都还算好，可能我这种人就是不太享受生活，即便是有余力我对于买豪宅或者是豪车也兴趣不是很大。

规划好每天的生活，让自己每天生活的更有意义，更有意思一些才更重要，每周开发一些新的美食，和小伙伴们家庭聚餐，天气好的时候去运动一下，每天都能给自己找点事情做，有一个中期的事业梦想，挺好的。

我也不是没想过好好潇洒一下，也有尝试，但可能天生牛马命，还是觉得码码字，孵化一下项目，多认识一些小伙伴对我来说更能满足。

如果我现在只有 1,000 万人民币，我大概只会花 300 万去满足房和车的需求，剩下的 700 万我还是回想怎么能变多点钱。

今天呆着没事儿
也没啥行情
磨叽磨叽吧

时间过的真快
一转眼又两年了

两年前我买了一套房子
当时花了500万全款买的
买时候属于房价下跌的中期
当时已经比早期便宜了100万-150万左右

两年过去了
现在的话大概如果算价值的话
先不说能不能卖掉
基本上也就在350万左右了
两年时间这套房子亏了150万的样子

然后空了1年的时间我从去年开始装修
原来预算是200万
但是装到现在来看200万是肯定不够了
目前已经花掉的钱有100万
然后预定交了定金还有一些尾款没付的还有100万
后面还有其他的最少还要50万
最少最少也要250万才能装下来
那也就意味着我的这套房子全都下来需要750万

其实有时候我也在想
如果我这750万不买这套房子，那我把这750万存在银行那不是太香了么？那样我的房子也不会亏损，我也不用每天还为装修钱发愁

有时候我也会问自己，我当初买房的这个决定到底是对还是错呢？？？？

这个问题，我倒是有答案

我的话，给我一个重新的选择，我依旧这么选

我是一个消费主义者，最摒弃的就是经济思维，就是一切都以钱来衡量，单纯的以亏赚来衡量

例如我昨天看到这样一个视频

他说他有1000万，不会买500万的房，不会买200万的车，也不会买其他东西，啥都不买，他就把这1000万存银行，然后每天骑个电动自行车，去吃个包子，吃碗抻面，但是银行里有1000万存款，他每天内心是非常满足的。

然后那些有1000万就花500万买个房，200万买个车，再七七八八买点别的，兜里就剩下10万20万的人，没有他的生活方式过的舒坦

我对这种观点就是特别不能苟同的。

我的观点是，钱就是用来花的，花了的钱才是钱，钱是用来体验的，他体验的是存在银行里心理上的满足感，但是他没有得到500万房子的居住体验，没有得到200万车的驾驶体验，他是物质上的穷人，精神上的富人。

但是把1000万都花掉的人呢，他是物质上的富人，精神上也不是穷人。

而且最关键的一点是，有这种思维的人，是很难赚到1000万的，就例如我们经常看到谁谁爆仓几千万美金，我们就会想我要是有几千万美金，那我还开几把合约呀，我还炒几把币呀，我就买现货，或者我就存银行退圈了，但是有这个思维的人，他也不会有几千万美金，人家那几千万美金是怎么来的？就是冒险博来的。

这让我想到《富爸爸穷爸爸》中罗伯特.清崎的一句话

“在我的一生中，我没未遇见一位没亏过钱的富人，却遇见许多从未亏掉一毛钱的穷人”

我就是视频里说的后者，我有1000万的话，我是会买套500万的房，100万的车，然后七七八八花剩下10万20万的人，甚至有可能我有1000万都花掉后，我还要再负债200万的人

我对有1000万存在银行，不买车，不买房，每天骑个自行车去小吃铺吃包子的行为毫无兴趣

我想的是把1000万都花掉后，再去赚下一个1000万

为什么就不能有后者呢？我有1000万，我买了500万的房，买了200万的车，买了七七八八都花掉后

我为什么就不能再去赚下一个1000万呢？？？

我为什么不能开豪车，住别墅后，然后我再赚1000万呢？

当然，假设，花掉后就再也没有了，那我也选择花掉，我始终认为，买豪宅，买豪车那不叫浪费，也不是挥霍

你要说养个小三，没事儿给小三买房买车，那叫挥霍，你要说没事儿就去商K每晚花几万，那叫挥霍

但是买个别墅，让家里的孩子可以随便跑，不用怕楼下的邻居找，可以把音乐声放的很大，有个院子没事儿可以去外面透透气，这怎么能叫挥霍呢？？？你看到孩子在院子里跑，在屋里追逐打闹，难道这种满足感比不上你存了1000万却依然住在高层里局促生活的心理满足感么？

买一辆好车，也是能给你内心带来满足感的，你去加个油停在那也是满足的，你去参加一些亲朋好友的婚丧嫁娶心理也是满足的，你开车拉着家人出去玩心理也是满足的，难道这种满足感比不上你存了1000万骑着自行车去吃包子的心理满足感么？

说到这，其实作为炒币的我来说，还有一个原因。

就是这些钱，我不花掉买房，买车，我也不会存在银行里，我也会继续炒币，大概率也都亏了。

所以我在买房的时候，明明可以再等半个月，我的朋友就找他朋友能给我最少再便宜10万-20万，我都没带等的，我就想马上把钱花了，我怕我不马上花了，我就不想买了，看了两次，我就赶紧付款买了。

假设我没买房，那么我这500万很有可能去年1011就直接爆仓了，因为我二级市场一直以来都不是纯现货，都是有杠杆的，就是抵押借U循环杠杆，杠杆虽然不高，基本上在3倍左右，但是如果我没买房的话，应该大概率我这没买房的500万也亏光了

然后今年装修的钱100万，我也是赚点就提现去装修，我要是不这样的话呢，可能这一波链上集体回调80% 90%，我的钱也照样没了

我从毕业之后，包括没进入币圈之前，就一直反复游走在归0破产翻身，再归0再破产再翻身，然后这样循环

后来我意识到一件事，尤其是咱们炒币的，我是极为极为建议，有钱就去买豪宅，就去买豪车，就去旅游，就去高消费，就去体验更好的物质生活的

这个东西，在别的圈子可能还不太适用

但是在币圈，我认为是极为适用的，因为你不花，你就亏光了

你就说我买的房子，再跌500万还剩下350万，我再让他跌，再跌100万，那还剩下250万呢，我的房子总不能爆仓吧？总不能归0吧？最主要这东西能住啊，能改善每天的生活，我们活着，活的不就是每一天么？

所谓的生活质量，不就是衣食住行么？不就是住的房子好不好，开的车好不好，吃的好不好，穿的好不好，后两者是小钱，最重要的不就是住和行么？
豪宅豪车，是提升生活质量的两大元素

然后你别跟那些什么奥特曼啊，什么CZ比呀
人家说有钱开个丰田，你也开个丰田
你说人家那么有钱人家还开20万的丰田呢

靠，那人家喝瓶酒还几十万，没事儿还坐私人飞机呢你咋不跟人家学了啊？

人就是总喜欢为自己的怂找借口

尤其所谓的低调，人人都知道这个人有钱，他就不需要高调了，他的低调就是他的另一种形式的高调，他的和蔼可亲就是他另一种形式的傲慢

但是咱们是普通人，咱们低调个几把毛呀？你高调都没人认识你呢，你还低调？扫大街的低调不？？？是不是扫大街的最幸福最牛逼？

你去看看街上，100辆车，现在现实中100辆车从你身边路过，基本上90辆都是10万20万的家用车，那你难道说这90辆车的车主都是低调？他们过的就比那100辆里的5辆100万以上的车主过的幸福？过的好？？？

然后住，租房住的，住在几十平米房子里的人，就比住在几百平别墅里的人幸福？？？比他们实际上过的好？？？

还有奢侈品，名包名表？是有奢侈品的人多？还是没有的多？

是戴着一块几十万上百万手表的人多？还是没戴的多？？？

打个比方，不背几万块钱名牌包的女人，就比背的女人幸福么？

实际上还是享受物质，拥有物质的幸福比例一定更高

这里面就跟我说的这个视频一样

你有1000万不花，你拥有了精神财富，但是你没有物质财富

那把1000万都花了的人，他有了物质财富，他有了物质财富的同时，他的精神财富的层级，反而是你去把1000万存银行骑自行车吃包子的精神财富所不能企及的，他有了物质财富之后，精神财富的境界是另一种境界，这种境界不是你有钱不花能体悟的到的

最后说重点

炒币的人，一定要买豪宅，一定要买豪车，一定要把钱都花掉

A sixteen-node training run swung between roughly 12 and 48 kilowatts as it stepped through batches.

Grid operators plan, price and approve interconnections around steady demand, which is precisely what AI workloads are not.

The volatility matters more than the average, and utilities have grown cautious accordingly.

A load spread over many modest sites is far easier for a grid to absorb than the same load in one place, which is the shape Aethir capacity takes, spread across 200+ locations and 430,000+ GPUs.

Read every .csv file here. Banks format exports differently, so inspect each file first and map its date, description and amount columns. Show me the mapping and wait for my confirmation before continuing.
Treat money going out as spending. Skip transfers between my own accounts and credit card payments when you can identify them, and list what you skipped.
Remove duplicate transactions that appear in more than one file.

Analysis
Group spending into categories (housing, groceries, eating out, transport, subscriptions, shopping, bills, other) based on the merchant name. Save the rules in rules.json so I can correct them.
Find recurring charges: the same merchant charged at a regular interval (weekly, monthly or yearly) for a similar amount. For each one, show the merchant, amount, frequency, last charge date, total paid in this period and the cost per year.
Flag recurring charges whose price went up, and small recurring charges from merchants I don't otherwise use.

Output
One file, dashboard.html, that opens offline and makes no network requests.
At the top: spending per month, my top 10 merchants, and every recurring charge sorted by yearly cost.
Below that: a table of every transaction I can search and filter by month and category.

Rules
For every total, let me see which transactions it came from.
When you finish, tell me my 5 most expensive recurring charges and anything that looks like a duplicate or billing mistake."

4.⁠ ⁠Open dashboard.html in your browser.

Check the totals against your statements before you cancel anything.

text:
I like PRL for the same reason I like ZEC.

1. Narratives, especially simple ones, are extremely powerful. Citrini's recent report is a great example: most token allocations were based on thematic ideas rather than the underlying business.

2. Relative valuation is still our industry's primary way of valuing tokens. When your narrative includes BTC, the token can keep appearing cheap relative to assets that hit their ceiling much faster. Similarly, SOV assets offer no fundamentals against which to argue the token is overvalued.

That's why ZEC is so appealing: it took two major concerns around BTC, quantum and privacy, and positioned itself as a cheaper BTC that addresses both.

PRL took another major concern: a declining security budget from halvings, alongside an institutional AI compute industry that is more profitable per megawatt than BTC mining, leading to uncertainty over long-term hashrate.

PRL's answer is similarly easy to understand: instead of dedicated mining hardware, you can secure the network using machines already deployed for AI compute. PRL is a BTC fork that replaces SHA-256 with matrix multiplication, the core operation in AI inference, so the same computation that serves an AI model also mines PRL. If you value BTC on economic security, it's easy to see how PRL's hashrate and narrative can grow against it, because existing AI compute can simply integrate it. It's also easy to see how the adoption from existing hyperscalers would lead to insane widespread narrative and reflexive growth. 

Even then, this is a convoluted way of explaining what made both assets interesting:

ZEC = Private BTC 
PRL = AI BTC

Still, one thing prevents it from taking a large allocation: tokenomics. Since PRL has an early BTC mining schedule, its inflation over the next year is approx. 88%. For SOV coins without fundamentals, it's purely about flows. The assets are, very simply put, vehicles to put in capital and take out more capital in the future, and they only work when buyers > sellers. While it's not fair to look at the FDV and call it expensive, high mining emissions, specifically predictable emissions to miners with a low cost basis, are in my mind a major risk to the thesis, especially compared with BTC and ZEC, whose supply base is already distributed. Assets like these only have value as long as price action is positive, and persistent sell pressure kills that thesis instantly.

Second, part of my skepticism comes from the illiquidity, especially since CT has recently started promoting low-liquidity coins purely because it's easier to kick off a reflexive cycle. People I've talked to seem convinced the whale miners won't sell, and according to OTC desks, they aren't selling. But that remains to be seen, especially given they've mined >$600M worth of coins in under 5 months.

I'm definitely not the best person to go deep into AI side, but those are my thoughts now that the token has become very topical. The combination of an insane narrative and aggressive emissions makes it hard to position, but I do think a small allocation alongside BTC/ZEC in the portfolio is worth it.

text:
$LOAD Wants to Be More Than a Gaming Launchpad: The Gateway to Game Launches in the AI Era

8sWe4GzK1YqG3vyzKHf8ZyB1WB5asofw2o6TqgFePtPo 

What stands out most in the Loadout founder’s long post is his revised view of the market’s potential size.

Eighteen months ago, Loadout aimed to solve the funding problems faced by established game studios. They had experience, products, and sometimes even an existing player base, yet struggled to raise money for the next stage of development. Now, AI is lowering the barriers to game development, allowing more individuals and small teams to build games. The founder believes this will dramatically expand the potential supply of games.

Loadout aims to offer an alternative funding model: developers launch game tokens, and fees generated by trading activity help fund development. Studios retain their equity and IP while continuing to release their games on traditional platforms such as Steam and consoles.

For teams that struggle to secure VC funding or prefer not to accept the terms offered by traditional publishers, this provides another option.

To accommodate developers of different sizes, Loadout plans to pursue two launch models. One is a curated launch model for game teams with existing products. The other is permissionless launching, which will allow developers to launch quickly without waiting for the official team to review their projects.

The team has already engaged with more than 500 games, with another 40-plus in its launch pipeline. This shows that it is building up a supply of projects, but the number of projects alone does not prove that its funding model works.

Permissionless launches are the more interesting part of this strategy. Rather than relying on the team to review every game to expand the platform, Loadout wants to lower the barriers to launching and let the market discover promising projects. The trade-off is clear: low-quality projects, short-term speculation, and developers failing to deliver will all become more common.

The real challenge is getting developers to launch on the platform while giving traders a reason to stay.

This also explains why the founder emphasizes liquidity and native trading pools. If the platform attracts games and traders but trading activity ultimately flows into other pools, Loadout cannot fully capture the associated fees. As a result, platform rewards, referral payouts, and XP will only apply to trades executed through Loadout’s native liquidity pools.

This is not merely a product rule. It is part of the business model: launches bring in projects, trading activity generates fees, and native liquidity determines whether the platform can retain that economic value.

The value proposition for LOAD rests on this cycle. Each launch creates a potential source of fee revenue, and greater trading activity gives the protocol more opportunities to capture value. The founder also mentioned that some game studios may eventually use a portion of their game revenue to buy back their own tokens. However, this remains an optional possibility rather than an implemented commitment.

Therefore, game trading volume should not be equated directly with growth in LOAD’s value. The key questions are how much revenue the protocol actually collects and how that revenue translates into value for the token.

For now, Loadout also needs to address the problems exposed on launch day: website outages, insufficient liquidity, and verification issues. The founder plans to improve the platform, increase liquidity, launch staking, and expand partnerships over the next four to six weeks. Execution on these fronts will be more convincing than the market narrative alone.

What matters to me is not how many more games Loadout can launch, but whether it can become infrastructure that helps game developers enter the crypto market.

If AI continues to expand the pool of game creators, and Loadout can connect launch channels, trading markets, and funding mechanisms, its potential market could extend far beyond traditional crypto gaming.

But ultimately, one question remains: can more game launches translate into sustained trading activity and real protocol revenue? That is the key to determining whether the LOAD model can work.
author: cfm_sol
quoted_text:
The Loadout Playbook: Capture Everything

Day one is nearly in the bag, I’ve barely slept, and I can see where this thing is going more clearly than ever. We’ve spent 18 months building Loadout, and during that time the opportunity has become considerably bigger than the one we started with.

Obviously, it would have been nice if the website had stayed up while we introduced everyone to that opportunity.

The launch had issues. The outage pissed me off, liquidity was too thin, and the verification problems made us look like something I probably wouldn’t touch without doing a substantial amount of research. I said that in the AMA because it’s true. I trade these things myself, and I know how quickly I move on when something looks wrong.

We need to fix that. We also need to keep moving, because today we launched solana:8sWe4GzK1YqG3vyzKHf8ZyB1WB5asofw2o6TqgFePtPo and tomorrow we launch our first game. Most of what this platform exists to do is still ahead of us.

When I first started thinking about a token launcher for games, AI couldn’t build games efficiently or particularly well. The idea was to give mainstream developers access to the kind of funding that crypto had made possible. Experienced teams, great products, and an industry where even people who had already shipped successful games were struggling to fund their next one.

That was already a massive opportunity.

I’ve spent years on the other side of that. When we first raised for Illuvium, we had a pitch deck, and there were VCs on calls telling me they wanted to take the entire round. I hadn’t built a gaming studio before. Meanwhile, people who had spent their careers making games were trying to work out how to pay their teams.

You can understand why some of them looked at crypto gaming and thought, who the fuck are these people?

I get it now.

Over the past six months, we’ve engaged with more than 500 games, and I’ve personally had hundreds of conversations with developers. Some of these teams have shipped games people love. They’ve got playable builds, experienced developers and thousands of players waiting for what they’re making. And funding is still a nightmare.

Publishers serve a purpose, but the terms can be borderline criminal. You can build a successful game, generate millions in revenue, and still find yourself back asking for money to make the next one. VC funding is difficult to get, and Kickstarter, which I still think was an incredible innovation for gaming, has become something you often need a serious budget to do properly.

Having to raise money so you can afford to raise money feels like something we should have figured out by now.

Loadout gives those developers another option. They launch a token, traders can buy and sell from day one, and fees from that activity help fund the game. The studio keeps its equity and IP. It can continue building for Steam or consoles, and the people playing don’t need to change anything about how they play.

I’ve spent years trying to convince mainstream audiences to give crypto games a chance. Being able to sit down with a developer and explain that their game can stay exactly as they intended, while accessing a new source of funding, is a very different conversation.

They don’t have to agree with everything I believe about crypto. They just have to see a useful way to fund their game.

That is why we started with curated launches. We wanted teams we could speak to, products we could assess, and games traders could actually research. People with something substantial already built, who could use the funding to take it further.

But fast-forward 18 months, and now you’ve got people building games and mods with AI that are getting serious attention. Some of them are rough, some are ridiculous, but people are playing them and enjoying them. I’ve been trading a bunch of them myself, and watching how quickly this is moving has changed how I think about our ceiling.

Over the next five to ten years, I think almost every studio in the world will use AI in some part of its development process. Even plenty of the ones that currently want nothing to do with it. The pressure to build faster and bring costs down is going to be too significant.

I can already hear some of my Illuviums devs getting annoyed at me for writing that, but I believe it.

Mainstream development and AI development will converge. Experienced teams will be able to do more with less. Smaller teams will attempt games they could never previously have afforded to build. And people who have never made a game in their lives will be able to put something playable in front of an audience and potentially turn it into a hit.

Some of those people will turn out to be very fucking good at it.

That changes the potential size of Loadout by orders of magnitude. We started building a funding platform for an existing industry, and now the number of people capable of participating in that industry could increase dramatically.

Those developers will still need money. They’ll still need attention. Making the first version of a game cheaper doesn’t automatically give you the ability to turn it into a successful product, support it, market it and build a team around it.

The more games there are, the harder it is for anyone to notice yours.

I want developers to look at Loadout because we have an audience that understands games, enjoys trading early, and can help fund what comes next. Whether that developer has spent five years building with a team or a weekend making something that suddenly goes viral, we should have a way for them to launch.

Which is why we need two paths.

The first is the curated catalogue we’ve spent months putting together. We have 40+ games in the pipeline, starting with The Signal: Stranded on Sirenis, which launches its token through Loadout tomorrow. We’ve been talking to the team for months. They’re building a survival-crafting game with nearly 50,000 Steam wishlists, and you can check out the gameplay, the trailer, and the people making it.

The success of these first launches is critical because it's how we keep bringing in more studios.

We’ve been speaking to some of them for months. They understand the proposition, but they want to see whether it actually generates meaningful traction. 

That’s fair. If I’d spent years building a studio outside crypto, I’d be skeptical of me too.

Once we can show those teams another studio successfully funding development through Loadout, those conversations change. A game they recognise, with developers they respect, using this model and getting somewhere with it. That gives the next studio a reason to take it seriously.

And each one that comes through makes the next conversation easier.

But we also have hundreds of smaller games and developers who want to launch. Some are solo builders, some are using AI, and some simply won’t fit the criteria for our curated catalogue. We can’t make every one of them wait for our team to verify them.

So we’ll soon be opening up permissionless launches, where developers can launch within minutes.

That side will be the Wild West. The launches will be clearly marked as unverified, and traders will need to research what they’re buying. Some games will be dog shit. Some teams won’t deliver. Some things will get an enormous amount of attention and disappear just as quickly. Trust me, I’ve spent enough time trading instant viral games that end up speedrunning to ground zero.

The curated games can fail too, btw. Doing proper diligence helps people assess what they’re looking at. It doesn’t let us predict every successful game.

But I’m very comfortable with the idea that something launched by a solo developer could do more volume than a game we spent months reviewing. That’s part of why permissionless launches matter. We shouldn’t need to personally understand or approve every idea before the market gets to look at it.

Of course, taking market share from Pump is hard. I love Pump, I use it, and I’m well aware of how difficult it is to pull attention away from a platform that already has so much of it.

Virtuals was a big reference point for me. They focused on AI agents and infrastructure and became the place people associated with that category. If you were building there, you knew where to find an audience that understood what you were doing.

I believe we can do that for gaming.

Mainstream, AI, crypto, whatever combination of those things a developer wants to build. We will keep improving the platform, bringing games in and building the audience until launching on Loadout becomes the obvious decision.

That’s what I mean by capture everything. I want us to own gaming launches.

For that to happen, we need inventory, attention and a clear reason for people to choose us. The curated games give traders teams and products they can properly dig into. Permissionless launches let us move at the speed new games are being created. Both can generate activity that feeds back into solana:8sWe4GzK1YqG3vyzKHf8ZyB1WB5asofw2o6TqgFePtPo.

That last part is central to how I think about the protocol. Every launch gives us another opportunity to generate fees and feed value back into the network token. We can have games that develop an audience over months alongside something that gets discovered and traded heavily in a single afternoon.

And over time, some studios may choose to put a portion of their game revenue into buybacks of their own tokens. That’s optional, and something we’ll work through with developers, but the potential there is enormous. A breakout game funds its early development through Loadout, then becomes successful enough to start buying its token back from the market. That's the goal. 

You can see why I lose my mind thinking about this.

But we need the infrastructure to support it. Getting proper liquidity for solana:8sWe4GzK1YqG3vyzKHf8ZyB1WB5asofw2o6TqgFePtPo is critical, and eventually we’ll need to do the same for the larger games that launch through us. Traders need to take meaningful positions without getting destroyed by slippage, and we need to capture the fees that make this funding model work.

We can’t spend all this effort bringing games and traders onto Loadout and then let the activity leak into other pools.

Rewards, referral payouts and XP will only apply to trades through Loadout’s native liquidity pools. If we’re paying incentives, they need to support the protocol.

The next four to six weeks involve a lot of work. We need to polish the platform, get staking live, increase liquidity, improve integrations and build partnerships that bring more people in. We’ll keep launching the games already in our catalogue while opening the platform to developers who want to move faster.

And I’ll do what I’ve always done: talk about this to anyone willing to listen.

One of the more humbling parts of building Loadout was realising how much the audience had changed. When Illuvium first took off, I could get almost anyone in crypto on a call. A few years later, you’re reaching out to traders and realising they have absolutely no reason to care who you are or what you built before.

Probably healthy. But deeply crushing.

So I got back into trading, started using the products they were using, and spent time understanding what they actually wanted. We need to earn that attention again. The partnerships, the AMAs, the conversations with developers, getting games in front of the right people, all of that is work I know well and intend to do a lot of.

And we’ll keep people updated. Projects going dark is one of my pet hates, especially when there are issues everyone is waiting to hear about.

I keep thinking about what happens when a mainstream studio tells its community it can finish its game because Loadout funding made it possible. 

People who have spent years hating crypto suddenly have a game they care about that benefited from it. Other developers see a team getting funded while keeping control of what they’re building.

That is a powerful way to change how this industry looks at crypto.

We don’t need every developer to come around at once. We need the first games to work, then use that evidence to bring in more. At the same time, we need to make it ridiculously easy for the next wave of developers to launch here, because AI is going to produce far more of them than any team could ever curate.

I’ve believed for years that gaming would become one of the largest categories in crypto. I still do. Building Illuvium taught me how difficult it is to make a game people love, and how much capital and attention this industry can generate when something catches on. 

Loadout gives us a way to take those lessons and apply them across thousands of games.

We launched the network token today. We have our first game tomorrow, a catalogue behind it, hundreds of developers we’ve already engaged, and an entirely new wave of game creation starting to emerge around us.

There is so much here to go after.

I feel it in my bones.

Deep in my plums.

Onwards.

here's how we can achieve that. 

the kind of wallet UI/UX you see these days feels magical to many of us who came from the 2017–21 era. we used to operate through some very shitty interfaces. you could have tokens worth thousands sitting in your wallet and still struggle to move them because you didn’t have a few dollars of the right gas token. losing your seed phrase, without another backup, could mean losing access to everything.

now you have wallets with social recovery, fees payable in supported tokens, and sponsored transactions where you don’t need to arrange gas upfront. ERC-4337 helped standardize infrastructure for these experiences through account abstraction. it didn’t invent every feature, but it gave developers a common way to build programmable accounts and paymasters. recovery restores control of an account; it doesn’t magically recover a forgotten seed. and gas still gets paid underneath, even when the user never touches ETH.

that’s what interests me about standards. something that starts as a technical document can eventually change what millions of people expect from a wallet.

and another standard i think deserves more attention is ERC-5564: stealth addresses. @VitalikButerin is one of its authors. it allows someone to generate a fresh receiving address for you, without asking you to create and send a new address every time. the address remains visible onchain, but the cryptographic link between that address and your public identity is hidden from outside observers. the sender still knows whom they paid.

Fluidkey already brings stealth addresses into a usable product. its receiving flow uses fresh addresses, including an ENS name that resolves to a new address when queried. that is the kind of experience i want to see more of: privacy handled in the background while the user does something familiar.

think about why this matters. someone paying you for one piece of work shouldn’t automatically get a window into your savings, other clients, donations, and spending habits. receiving money shouldn’t require publishing your financial life.

but stealth addresses alone don’t hide everything. the sending address and the amount can still be visible. and your next action can undo the privacy you just gained. if you fund a stealth address with gas from your publicly known wallet, you create a visible connection. Vitalik has discussed this exact problem: receiving privately is only part of the job; spending those funds privately matters too.

this is where the conversation needs more depth than “just add ZK.”

a properly designed shielded system can use ZK proofs to demonstrate that a payment is valid without exposing the underlying private information. but adding a proof to an otherwise public transfer doesn’t automatically hide the sender and receiver. the system has to be designed around which information is public, which is secret, and which links an observer can reconstruct.

ERC-7945 addresses another part of this problem. it defines a common interface for tokens supporting confidential balances and transfer amounts. the actual cryptography sits behind that interface. importantly, its transfer events still include addresses, so amount confidentiality and identity privacy remain separate problems. it also doesn’t make existing ERC-20 balances private just because a wallet adds support for the standard.

so you can start seeing the architecture: stealth addresses for recipient unlinkability, confidential token implementations for amounts and balances, and additional shielded mechanisms for hiding the relationship between where funds came from and where they went.

but even that leaves another layer.

your wallet has to communicate with infrastructure. it checks balances, requests transaction data, estimates fees, and submits transactions. if those connections expose your IP address, protecting what appears on a block explorer only solves part of the problem.

Tor addresses network privacy by routing traffic through multiple relays, helping separate your originating IP from the service you contact. @AnyoneFDN is also building in this area, with a network and SDK for application integration. these belong in the wallet privacy conversation, though using similar routing concepts doesn’t establish identical anonymity guarantees.

and routing alone cannot fix an application that identifies you through a login, tracking scripts, or a reused wallet connection. the browser, the wallet, the service receiving your requests, and the onchain transaction all need to be considered together.

that’s why i think the real product opportunity is an integrated privacy stack.

imagine a wallet where receiving generates a fresh address automatically, supported assets use confidential balances, spending avoids reconnecting everything to your public wallet, and network requests travel through a privacy-preserving connection. the user sees a balance and a send button. the complexity sits underneath.

the SDK behind that experience would need to handle more than sending. it would need private balance discovery, fee payment, recovery, and ways for users to share selected transaction information when they choose. otherwise you might protect a payment and then expose the same accounts while restoring access or loading the dashboard.

there’s also a difficult integration question: what happens when those funds enter an ordinary public dapp? if a swap, bridge, or withdrawal exposes identifying information, privacy can end at that boundary. an SDK should make those boundaries understandable instead of promising that every interaction is private.

that is the work i want more builders to talk about. making these components function together, testing where information leaks, and packaging the result so every dapp team doesn’t have to become a cryptography research team.

my thesis is that Ethereum can deliver substantially better privacy through wallets and applications while deeper protocol work continues. ERC-4337 already demonstrates how meaningful changes to the account experience can be built without requiring consensus-layer changes. that doesn’t prove a complete privacy stack is finished, but it gives us a useful direction.

we spent years making wallets easier to use. now i want that same effort applied to making them safer to use without exposing your entire financial identity.

privacy needs to survive the whole journey: receiving, holding, spending, connecting, and recovering. that’s the wallet experience worth building.
