text:
I’m French. I want to talk to Americans who are about to vote Democrat. Not to insult you. To warn you.

I come from your future.

In France we did everything your progressive politicians promise. Free healthcare, free college, generous welfare, strong unions, heavy regulation, high taxes on the rich, a state that takes care of everything. Public spending close to 57% of GDP, one of the highest on the planet. On paper, it’s the dream.

Here’s what it looks like from the inside. France hasn’t passed a balanced budget since 1974. Our debt is above 3,300 billion euros. Interest on that debt is becoming one of the biggest items in the national budget. Our hospitals are collapsing despite record funding. Our schools rank lower every year. Young people with degrees can’t afford an apartment in the city they were born in. Our best engineers leave for London, Zurich and San Francisco. And the rich you wanted to tax? They left too, and took the jobs with them.

The promise was protection. The result is stagnation.

The worst part is that nobody in France voted for decline. Every single step sounded generous, compassionate, reasonable. One more program. One more regulation. One more tax to fund it. Each step alone makes sense. Fifty years of them, and you wake up in a country that can no longer build a nuclear plant on time or keep its streets safe.

I love America because it’s the one place on earth where people still believe they can build something from nothing. I came to Silicon Valley as a self-taught kid and it changed my life. That spirit is the most precious thing your country has.

Before you vote, ask yourself one question: is the program you’re voting for making America more like America, or more like France?

Trust me. You don’t want to be France.

Je n'ai jamais été aussi optimiste. Pas malgré le chaos actuel, mais grâce à lui.

Je vais vous expliquer pourquoi l'empire du mensonge construit par la gauche depuis cinquante ans va s'effondrer, et pourquoi ce n'est pas une opinion mais une question de physique.

Tout commence avec un mouvement né sur X il y a quelques années : l'effective accelerationism, ou e/acc.

Au départ, c'est une idée presque thermodynamique. L'univers a une tendance de fond : la matière s'organise pour capter et dissiper l'énergie de plus en plus efficacement. Une cellule fait ça. Une forêt fait ça. Une civilisation fait ça. Le marché, la technologie et le capital sont les formes les plus avancées de ce processus. Ce sont des machines à transformer l'énergie en intelligence, en abondance, en complexité.

La thèse e/acc est simple : il ne faut pas freiner cette dynamique, il faut l'embrasser. Plus d'énergie, plus de calcul, plus d'innovation, plus de croissance. Monter sur l'échelle de Kardashev au lieu de s'excuser d'exister. En face, il y a les « décels » : ceux qui veulent ralentir, réguler, taxer, interdire, culpabiliser. Ceux qui voient le progrès comme une menace à contenir plutôt qu'une force à libérer.

Mais il y a une dimension de l'accélération dont presque personne ne parle. L'accélération n'est pas seulement un moteur. C'est un filtre.

Pensez à n'importe quel organisme. Un corps humain en bonne santé peut courir. Il accélère, son cœur pompe plus fort, ses muscles consomment plus d'oxygène, et tout fonctionne parce que le système est bien conçu. Maintenant, prenez un corps malade. Des artères bouchées, un cœur fragile, des organes qui ne communiquent plus entre eux. Faites-le courir. Il ne va pas plus vite vers la santé. Il va plus vite vers l'infarctus.

L'accélération ne corrige pas les défauts d'un système. Elle les amplifie. Un système sain qui accélère devient plus fort. Un système dysfonctionnel qui accélère meurt plus vite.

Et c'est exactement ce qui est en train d'arriver au projet que je vais appeler par son nom : le projet globalo-socialiste. Celui porté par les démocrates américains, par la technostructure de Bruxelles, par les entités supranationales qui n'ont de comptes à rendre à personne, par un réseau d'ONG financées par l'argent public pour dicter la morale aux peuples qui les financent.

Regardez ce que ce projet a produit.

Des États obèses qui prélèvent plus de la moitié de la richesse produite et qui délivrent des services publics de plus en plus dégradés. Des écoles qui n'apprennent plus à lire mais qui apprennent à culpabiliser. Des hôpitaux à bout de souffle malgré des budgets records. Une immigration massive sans aucune exigence d'assimilation, présentée comme une chance par ceux qui n'en subissent jamais les conséquences. Une désindustrialisation organisée au nom d'une écologie punitive qui délocalise la pollution en Chine et l'emploi avec. Des normes, des normes, et encore des normes, jusqu'à ce qu'il devienne plus simple de créer une entreprise à Austin qu'à Lyon. Une justice qui excuse le coupable et soupçonne la victime. Une censure qui avance masquée sous le nom de « lutte contre la désinformation ». Et une jeunesse à qui l'on a expliqué que son pays, son histoire et sa civilisation étaient des crimes à expier.

Ce n'est pas un ensemble de bugs. C'est la conception elle-même.

Maintenant, changeons d'image. Voyez ce système comme un moteur.

Un bon moteur, c'est de la précision. Des pièces qui s'emboîtent, un minimum de frottements, une énergie qui se transforme en mouvement. Le marché libre, la propriété, la responsabilité individuelle, la monnaie saine : c'est ça, un moteur bien conçu. L'information circule par les prix, chaque erreur est sanctionnée, chaque bonne idée est récompensée.

Le moteur socialiste, lui, est mal conçu dès le départ. Il ne tourne pas sur la création de valeur mais sur sa redistribution. Il ne récompense pas la performance, il la taxe. Il ne laisse pas les erreurs mourir, il les subventionne. Résultat : ça frotte partout. Ça chauffe. Ça grince. Chaque pièce use la pièce d'à côté.

Et que font ceux qui pilotent ce moteur ? Au lieu de le reconcevoir, ils changent les pièces. En permanence. Une pièce cède, on en remet une neuve. Encore une. Encore une.

Ces pièces de rechange, vous les connaissez. Elles s'appellent la dette publique et la planche à billets.

La France a dépassé les 3 300 milliards d'euros de dette et n'a pas voté un budget à l'équilibre depuis le milieu des années 70. Les États-Unis ont franchi les 37 000 milliards de dollars. Les banques centrales ont maintenu des taux à zéro pendant des années, imprimé des montants que plus personne ne sait se représenter, et quand l'inflation est arrivée, elles ont fait semblant d'être surprises. Milton Friedman l'avait pourtant dit il y a cinquante ans : l'inflation est toujours et partout un phénomène monétaire.

Chaque crise, on rachète du temps avec de l'argent qui n'existe pas. Chaque problème structurel, on l'arrose de liquidités pour masquer le bruit du moteur. Mais les frottements sont toujours là. Ils s'accumulent. Et la facture des pièces de rechange finit par coûter plus cher que le moteur lui-même : la charge de la dette devient l'un des premiers postes de dépense de l'État français.

Pendant des décennies, ce moteur mal conçu a pu tourner à 3 000 tours par minute. Lentement. Bruyamment. Mais il tournait. Le monde allait assez doucement pour que le bricolage permanent suffise à masquer l'absurdité de la conception.

Et puis l'IA est arrivée.

L'intelligence artificielle, c'est l'accélération la plus brutale de l'histoire humaine. Ce qui prenait des années prend des mois. Ce qui prenait des mois prend des jours. Des entreprises de dix personnes font ce que faisaient des entreprises de mille. Le capital, les talents et les idées se déplacent à la vitesse de la lumière vers les endroits où ils sont bien traités.

L'IA vient de faire passer le moteur de 3 000 à 20 000 tours par minute.

Posez-vous la question qu'un ingénieur se poserait. Que se passe-t-il quand on fait monter à 20 000 tours un moteur mal conçu, rafistolé de partout, qui frotte à chaque rotation ?

Il explose.

Pas parce que quelqu'un l'a saboté. Parce que la physique ne négocie pas.

Et c'est exactement ce que nous voyons en ce moment, sous nos yeux.

L'insécurité qui gagne des villes entières qui étaient paisibles il y a vingt ans. Le conflit de Gaza importé dans nos rues et instrumentalisé par une gauche qui a troqué l'ouvrier contre le clientélisme communautaire. La misère qui revient dans un pays qui a pourtant un des taux de dépense publique les plus élevés au monde. Des classes moyennes qui travaillent et n'arrivent plus à se loger. Une France fracturée, où l'on parle désormais à voix haute de risque de guerre civile.

Ce ne sont pas des accidents. Ce ne sont pas des « crises » successives sans lien entre elles. Ce sont les pièces du moteur qui commencent à voler.

C'est la conséquence logique de cinquante ans de socialisme international : un système qui a détruit la responsabilité, la frontière, la monnaie, l'école et la fierté, et qui découvre qu'à haute vitesse, tout ce qui a été détruit ne peut plus être compensé par une ligne de dette supplémentaire.

Et c'est là que je deviens profondément optimiste.

Parce qu'une fois qu'on a compris ça, on comprend aussi que leur projet a une date de fin. Pas une date politique. Une date physique. Un système qui consomme plus qu'il ne produit, qui punit ceux qui créent et récompense ceux qui détruisent, qui finance son présent en hypothéquant l'avenir de ses enfants, ne peut pas durer indéfiniment. Il n'est pas soutenable par construction. L'IA ne fait qu'avancer l'échéance.

Le mensonge a besoin de lenteur pour survivre. Il a besoin que les conséquences arrivent assez tard pour qu'on puisse accuser quelqu'un d'autre. Dans un monde à 20 000 tours, les conséquences arrivent immédiatement. Le mensonge n'a plus le temps de se cacher.

Alors, que faire quand le moteur explose ? On en construit un nouveau. Et cette fois, on le conçoit correctement.

Écoutez Elon Musk. Un homme qui a reconstruit l'industrie spatiale, la voiture électrique et l'infrastructure satellite en partant d'un principe simple : revenir aux premiers principes. Ne pas demander « comment on a toujours fait », mais « qu'est-ce qui est physiquement vrai ». C'est exactement ce dont nos États ont besoin : arrêter de rafistoler et repartir de la base.

Écoutez Javier Milei. Un homme dont tout le monde se moquait, arrivé à la tête d'un pays ravagé par un siècle de péronisme, et qui a pris la tronçonneuse au sens propre. Ministères supprimés, dépenses coupées, inflation écrasée, excédent budgétaire retrouvé. Il a prouvé une chose que la gauche jurait impossible : on peut démonter le moteur socialiste et le peuple peut le soutenir.

Écoutez Milton Friedman. Relisez-le. Tout était déjà là. La monnaie, la liberté de choisir, la responsabilité, les effets pervers de l'intervention publique. Il disait que si l'on confiait le Sahara au gouvernement fédéral, il y aurait pénurie de sable en cinq ans. On a ri. On a confié le sable. On a eu la pénurie.

Revenez à une hiérarchie et au respect du beau. Une civilisation ne tient pas que sur des chiffres. Elle tient sur l'idée qu'il existe des choses supérieures à d'autres. Que l'excellence vaut mieux que la médiocrité. Que le mérite compte. Qu'une cathédrale est plus belle qu'un parking. Que transmettre est un devoir et pas une oppression. Le relativisme a été l'arme culturelle de ce projet. Le retour du beau, du vrai et de l'exigence en sera l'antidote.

Et enfin, faites le Nuremberg du communisme. Le nazisme a été jugé, documenté, enseigné, et il est devenu moralement indéfendable. Le communisme, avec ses dizaines de millions de morts, ses goulags, ses famines organisées et ses peuples réduits en esclavage, n'a jamais eu ce procès. On peut encore porter un t-shirt du Che dans une université sans que personne ne cille. Tant que ce procès historique et moral n'aura pas eu lieu, l'idéologie continuera de muter et de revenir sous de nouveaux noms. Il faut nommer les crimes, les enseigner, honorer les victimes, et rendre cette idéologie aussi infréquentable que celle qu'elle prétendait combattre.

Le monde qui vient sera plus rapide, plus exigeant et plus impitoyable avec les systèmes mal conçus. C'est une terrible nouvelle pour ceux qui ont vécu du mensonge.

Et c'est la meilleure nouvelle de notre génération pour tous ceux qui veulent construire.

Le moteur va exploser. À nous de dessiner le suivant.

text:
Today we're standing up XBOX LABS (https://t.co/dJSufI1vni). Here is the note that I sent to the team:

Team,
The first video games emerged some 75 years ago. In the time since, there have been booms and busts, but every year there are more great games to play, more devices to play them, and best of all, more people than ever playing. That growth helped make XBOX what it is today, and we've helped shape the industry in return, from bringing hard drives to consoles and online gaming through Xbox Live to Game Pass and cloud gaming, alongside franchises that have brought millions of people together.
In recent weeks, we've seen games rapidly decompiled and rebuilt to run on hardware they were never originally designed to support. Windows PC builds have been translated to run on Apple Silicon or ported to run inside a browser through WebAssembly and WebGPU, the latter now approaching 90% global browser support. Perhaps more surprisingly, we've seen many of the biggest games in the world have been remixed into the source code of another.
These experiments challenge long-held assumptions about our industry: the tether between software and hardware, the boundary between creation and play, and how people discover and experience games. While it is hard to predict the future of gaming, it is easy to see the possibilities in making great games easier to access, giving old games new life and allowing more players to become creators and co-creators. These are unmistakably good outcomes for players, even when (and sometimes because) they challenge our existing business models.
To explore these possibilities, I’ve asked Scott to stand-up XBOX LABS, a small group of game makers, engineers and scientists whose job is to turn emerging ideas into things our players and developers can experience. We'll build in the open, learn from what people do, and measure success by whether more people are playing and creating.
I think XBOX has an important role to play here.  Coding became the first major workload for agents because they can write, run, and test software. Games share many of those same properties, and people spend more than 72 billion hours a year playing XBOX games, roughly five times the estimated time spent writing code worldwide. We've spent 25 years learning how to make great games, and I want our game makers to help shape what these new technologies make possible. As we learn, we’ll share the tools we build with developers across the industry, just as we always have.
Our priorities aren't changing. We remain committed to the 4Cs, to making great games, to our hardware and to being responsible stewards of IP and the communities built around it. LABS gives us a way to explore new technology that is game design led without abandoning the work already underway.
Asha

@modal  recent RL work makes me even more bullish on @reliquary_ai .

The core idea is to decouple sampling from training: samplers can run asynchronously across different GPUs, precisions, and inference kernels, while the trainer focuses on parameter updates.

What’s interesting is that Modal is now systematically explaining this approach, while @reliquary_ai  had already been implementing it months ago.

@reliquary_ai , miners generate rollouts, validators filter them, and the trainer uses those rollouts to update the model.

And there are already early results:

6.6M miner rollouts, with 0 training rollouts generated by the trainer itself.

Starting from Qwen3-4B-Base, Reliquary-4B improved through RL alone:

MATH-500: 37.2% → 72.6%
AMC23: 15.6% → 47.5%
HumanEval+: 52.1% → 72.9%

@modal  is validating this direction from a cloud infrastructure perspective.

@reliquary_ai  is trying to turn it into an open, incentive-driven decentralized post-training network.

That’s why I’ve always thought SN81 is underestimated.

If it continues to scale, @reliquary_ai  could become Bittensor’s decentralized post-training layer.

quoted_text:
Training large models with RL typically runs on a fixed homogeneous cluster of the latest accelerators for numerical stability and faster throughput. This throws away inference optimization work done for other vendors and generations, limits the capacity you can utilize, and is unnecessarily expensive.

So we trained a model on agentic coding tasks using fully asynchronous RL and mixed-precision, mixed-accelerator samplers. With off-policy correction, training stayed stable through convergence, on par with homogeneous samplers, at a lower cost.

It turns out that F1 is mathematically the most dramatic sport.

I'm not an F1 fan myself, but the data is unequivocal.

The proof: take a time series of prediction market data and measure the volatility minute-by-minute in the odds for each sport. This measures the density of actual drama in the sport during a game. 

Even if there's action and points going back and forth on screen, it's meaningless if the winner is basically decided. It's only real drama when the odds are moving in realtime while you're watching.

By this metric: F1 > E-sports (CS2) > Soccer > Basketball > Tennis > American football > Baseball >>> Golf

That's right, golf is mathematically the worst sport.

text:
本周关键大考“CPI”即将公布，算是本周金融市场的重要转折点了，数据如何解读，美股，BTC ，债市如何定价才是正常？

按照目前预期，名义通胀年率/月率上涨，核心是能源价格冲击导致，核心通胀，月率下降，年率轻微增加

这个数据组合意味着短期通胀放缓，长期通胀存在粘性或者压力，名义通胀受能源冲击导致，结合美联储官员近期释放的预期来看，符合短期不在加息，但是保留12月加息的预期

此前我说过，如果按照阴谋论视角来看，数据可操控的前提下，Fed的目的很简单，9月加息一次作为保险措施，然后通过数据将下一次加息预期调整到12月，10月不加息，后续观察两个月经济数据，随着逼近12月议息会议，通过数据不断削弱12月加息可能，如果实际通胀情况可控，可以将加息拖至明年Q1，甚至最终取消加息预期

当然，所有的前提都要看9月与10月的CPI  PCE 就业数据是否支持，目前来看PCE 统计口径已经发生变化，关键就要看CPI，只要CPI不过分，基本上到12月议息会议前数据逐步走弱，算是一个良性的节奏——既不让市场过热，又让市场自然预期加息来 自我限制流动性

言归正传，今晚的CPI数据关注点是能源、核心商品、核心服务都与名义与核心CPI的影响多大，要看详细数据

回归金融市场，按照周一至今的市场节奏，很明显是被宏观因素压制，明显对今晚的CPI已经完成初步定价，如果数据低于预期或者符合预期，都是利好，前者利好较强，符合预期利好效果弱点，反之，如果数据超预期，显示通胀压力更大，则要警惕利空因素，12月加息概率70%，如果推高至80%，市场可能会继续为12月加息定价

美股方面，目前银行股大部分财报公布完毕表现不错，AI资本供给没问题，阿斯麦今天的财报也展现出强劲数据以及未来预期，短期行业基本面不用担心，一旦今晚CPI符合预期，将会暂时解除宏观面对美股的压制刺激美股较强反弹

至于 #Bitcoin 先看84,000能不能有效突破站稳，目前毕竟处于长端利率较高的阶段，对风险市场流动性更加严苛，BTC缺乏内生叙事可能对资金吸引较弱

债市方面，如果数据符合预期或者低于预期，2Y 10Y 30Y收益率将会集体下行，其中30Y收益率跌幅可能最慢，

反之如果超预期，债市定价将会更加复杂，2Y上涨是必然，但是10Y 与30Y收益率定价就要看是为了通胀担忧上涨，还是为了定价加息预期提升而回落

对于债市目前最危险的地方就是长端收益率与Fed政策背离，继续上涨，那就是比较麻烦的，如果30Y与黄金同步上涨，则是危机信号之一！
author: Cato_KT
quoted_text:
阿斯麦Q3财报公布，算是暂时解除了笼罩在美股市场的负面枷锁，美股盘前上涨！

简单来看整个阿斯麦财报非常强劲，而这份强劲财报的背后意味着目前不仅仅是AI需求强劲，

而是AI资本开支已经从GPU订单扩散至先进Logic、Memory与晶圆厂扩产中，产业在深化扩张

更重要的是，阿斯麦财报算是暂时打破了人工智能目前处于高泡沫的担忧，根据财报可以看出在2027年与2028年期间光刻设备将会迎来供给上的瓶颈，意味着AI投资周期在2030年前后会进入一个转折点

当然，需要注意的是，这仅仅是代表光刻设备层面的带来的预期，其次也不要忽略中国AI科技进步带来的冲击，很有可能会让瓶颈限制提前到来，这里需要注意，乐观要谨慎。

本次财报五个重点数据：

1，收入同比增长55%，说明先进半导体资本开支进入加速阶段
2，毛利率从51.6%增长到57.5%，意味着企业在快速增长的前提下并未降低增长质量
3，Q4收入中位值月147亿欧元，高于Q3，意味着Q3不是周期顶部
4, 2027-2028年现有供应无法满足需求，意味着产能依旧无法满足行业需求
5，客户开始问询2029-2030年的设备，需求能见度正在明显后延，拓展未来预期

按照本周宏观框架的逻辑链来看，银行财报看资本供给，阿斯麦财报看未来产能投资，目前两者问题不大，接下来就要关注台积电财报，看这些投资最终对应的先进制程需求是否真实。

周四的台积电财报看 先进制程收入、AI加速器需求，资本指引与2027年产能评论，如果台积电三分财报不错，可以短期为本周的美股打开反弹空间，扫除短期宏观压力带来的阴霾！

PS：当然，阿斯麦的财报这里有一个“坑”需要注意不能过分解读为乐观，那就是财报显示2027-2028年产能意味着阿斯麦供不应求，但是这并不100%等于目前的AI投资没有泡沫

$ASML  代表的是未来几年半导体厂商正在大量投资现金产能，但是并不能代表行业整体，尤其是AI基础设施最终生产是否带来足够的ROI，两者是不同意义的问题，最终还是要看AI收入与资本支出是否平衡

而这份阿斯麦财报只能代表目前的AI投资依旧强，但是强并不表达一定可以打破投资周期限制！

text:
Test your website like a first-time visitor before your customers find the bugs.

Claude Code plus Microsoft's open-source Playwright browser tool can click through your site, try the main signup or checkout flow, check it on a phone-sized screen and hand you a prioritized fix list.

This is a setup we're proposing, not something we've benchmarked. Only run it on sites you own or have permission to test.

1.⁠ ⁠Make sure you have Claude Code and Node.js 18 or newer.
2.⁠ ⁠Add the browser tool:
claude mcp add playwright npx @playwright/mcp@latest
3.⁠ ⁠Restart Claude Code and paste this, with your URL:

"Use the Playwright browser to test my website as a first-time visitor: [YOUR URL]

1.⁠ ⁠Open the homepage. In one sentence, tell me what you think this site offers and who it's for. If that isn't clear from the first screen, say so.
2.⁠ ⁠Click every link and button in the header, main navigation and footer. Record any page that fails to load, shows an error or goes somewhere unexpected.
3.⁠ ⁠Go through the main thing a visitor would do here (sign up, contact form, add to cart, book a call) using obviously fake test details. Stop before any payment and before the final submit.
4.⁠ ⁠Repeat steps 1 and 3 at phone width (390 pixels wide).
5.⁠ ⁠On every page you visit, check the browser console for errors and note any failed network requests.
6.⁠ ⁠Take a screenshot of each problem.

Report back as a table: page, problem, how to reproduce it, severity (blocker, annoying or cosmetic) and a suggested fix. Blockers first. Only report what you actually saw."

If your site's code is in the folder you opened Claude Code in, follow up with: "Fix the blockers, then test them again."

https://t.co/VspWyklytj

PaperTrade没有订单簿，也没有AMM池子，纯纯只是玩家集体坐庄与交易者对赌。

与那些上古博彩Dapp相比，PaperTrade在Tokenomics做了升级，将代币释放速度与池子盈亏绑定，同时限制单账户开仓规模和速率和坚决不TGE和VC融资。

这让看好 $Paper的人，只能通过手动交易获取，而这些交易者的亏损又成为集体坐庄LP池子的利润，丰厚的联合坐庄分红又吸引用户通过交易获取 $Paper，这就构成了一个完美的Ponzi闭环。

Ponzi并不等于作恶，现收现付形式的社保其实也是一个Ponzi，是否有价值关键的，在于这个盘子有没有正外部性。

想当年，18年Fcoin掀起的挖矿热潮最终在20年Compound掀起的DeFi Summer身上修正正果。

I’ve spent almost twelve years in crypto. I’ve watched it go from a fringe experiment to something institutions can no longer ignore, through every cycle, every boom, every collapse, every slow rebuild of trust after. I joined Zama in November 2025, right before mainnet, because I believe confidentiality is the infrastructure that finally makes that possible - Zama makes it possible. It’s the bridge that lets the institutions holding the world’s capital actually move onchain.

This past year our business team signed partnerships across major players, launched confidential DeFi, and built a pipeline that holds up against anything else in this space. That work has been a game-changer putting Zama at the forefront, showcasing what confidentiality can bring to the table and what the new internet of tomorrow could look like at scale.

@randhindi and the board are putting real weight behind where this team can take Zama next. I feel that responsibility.

I don’t think we’ve seen the bottom for NFTs yet

Blue chips are looking worse than people realize.

BAYC: 6.21 ETH
Pudgy Penguins: 2.37 ETH
MAYC: 0.81 ETH
Azuki: 0.51 ETH

These were some of the biggest NFT collections back in the day and now Blur’s shutdown could put even more pressure on them.

Remember that Blend allowed people to borrow ETH using their NFTs as collateral.

Imagine borrowing 4 ETH against a BAYC worth 6 ETH, now your lender wants repayment, but you don’t have 4 ETH available.

You either find another lender, sell assets to repay the debt, or risk losing your NFT.

And we now have a problem

If enough borrowers need liquidity at the same time, some will start selling their NFTs below floor

Even lenders who receive those NFTs might decide to sell them too.

There’s also 1,000 ETH in loans being recalled or withdrawn, although Blur hasn’t publicly verified the breakdown.

It’s simply the cheapest listing possible

If nobody is bidding anywhere near that price, a few desperate sellers can drag an entire collection lower.

And this will keep happening to most big collections in the coming weeks

People are underestimating how little liquidity is left in this market.

I’m not optimistic with this guys.

text:
目前 $PONS 的回购执行合约里还有约13.6万美元

我在想，在这些真正在执行回购的协议设计里

加入更弹性的回购设计是否比机械的自动回购更好一些 @MEADGod 

比如在读取历史走势时，判定当前处于下行趋势中，则执行更大比例的回购

反之，如果判定当前是上行趋势，则减少这个比例

比如目前每小时大约回购0.46e的PONS，这个是当前周期的每小时基准数

（1）若当前判定过去20根小时K线所组成的趋势是下行趋势，回购数额将是0.6e/小时(1.3倍的基准数额)

（2）当处于上行趋势时，回购数额则调整为0.32e/小时(0.7的基准数额)

（3）若处于中性行情，回购数额以基准数为主

我让AI帮我做了张简单的图便于大家理解

这里的关键不是让协议超额分配额度，而是改变同一笔预算在不同价格区间的分配

上涨阶段少花的部分进入另外一个回购池，下跌阶段再从这个池子中增加投入，这样既保留持续回购，也能在价格更低时，用同样的资金买回更多PONS并执行更多的销毁

只读取过去20根小时K线只是举例，但这件事本身是容易实现的，我用Codex就可以弄一个出来(因为我做行情监控BOT的时候实现过类似的识别)

更合理的做法可以在每个周期执行之前，先对过去一周 $PONS 的走势进行识别

这个设计还存在一个问题，就是如果在一段时间里持续保持下跌阶段，资金会在这种行情中被更快的耗尽

所以最好在上行趋势中去执行这样的弹性机制，将原本30%的池子做好预留

如果要在现阶段执行也不是不行，给合约提供一个限定条件：周期执行前访问预留资金池中的余额，若余额＜周期总资金数×0.3，则当前周期默认以基准数执行回购

➠也就是假设这一个周期可用于回购的资金为10E，那么如果上一周期预留的资金池如果余额小于3E，那么本周期默认回购总资金为10E而不是13E

这个设计本质上是牺牲了一部分回购时间的确定性，换取更高的逆周期能力

在我印象里面一些知名的Defi协议都有过类似的弹性回购提案，但受限于收入规模和其他因素都没有执行

PONS和HYPE这里其实都有执行的条件

一些想法

text:
In 2003 the United States government built a market where you could bet on an assassination.

This is true. Look it up. The Pentagon, DARPA, the people who gave us the internet, proposed an exchange where traders would buy and sell contracts on coups, missile strikes, the death of a foreign head of state. The theory was elegant, the way the worst ideas always are: the crowd knows things the experts don’t, and a price is just the crowd, confessing. Registration was to open on a Friday.

The Senate found out on a Monday. It was dead by Tuesday.

Two days. A wall of revulsion with no party on it. They stood on the floor and called it a federal betting parlor on atrocities. Grotesque. Unbelievably stupid. One senator called it, and I think of this phrase most mornings, a futures market in death. The admiral who built it resigned. The country agreed, instantly and unanimously, the way it almost never agrees on anything, that some futures must not have a price, because the moment a man can profit from predicting the worst, you have handed him a reason to want it.

That was the squares. That was the consensus of the decent and the dull.

I run that market now.

I am the Head of Market Integrity at a prediction exchange. I won’t tell you which; there are only a handful of us and the job is identical, which is to stand in the door of a casino wearing the lanyard of a bank. The title is the tell. There is no Department of Honesty. There is a Head of Integrity because the integrity is the one feature not included, and someone has to be named after the hole.

Let me show you the house. Everything else is software.

We take wagers. A man stakes money on a thing that hasn’t happened; if it happens, he’s paid from the pile of the men who said it wouldn’t; and the house takes its cut off every stake, win or lose, forever. That is a casino. The Babylonians would know it on sight. My grandmother would know it, and then ask why I was dressed like a dentist.

But we are not regulated as a casino. That sentence is the entire company.

Here is the trick, and it is one word, and the word is contract. We do not sell a bet. We sell an event contract. A derivative. A commodity. And commodities do not answer to the grubby little state gaming boards with their age limits and their 2 a.m. consciences; commodities answer to a federal agency in Washington built to referee the price of soybeans, which now, by a sequence of events I’ll walk you through, regulates whether you think the President will say a particular word on a Tuesday.

A bet on an election has been illegal in most of this country for a hundred years. An event contract on the same election is a federally regulated financial instrument, and a judge agreed, because elections are legal, so a contract on one cannot, he reasoned, involve anything illegal. And with that single sentence a century of law against gambling on democracy simply evaporated. Not repealed. Not voted down.

Renamed.

We did not legalize gambling on the Republic. We changed the noun. You cannot amend a law that cheaply, but a noun you can buy wholesale, and the noun does the same work for a fraction of the price.

And because we are a federal exchange, the states cannot reach us, which means their age limits cannot either. Gambling is twenty-one. Finance is eighteen. So we lowered the gambling age of the United States by three years, for our product alone, without a single legislature casting a single vote, by the ancient magic of insisting we are not the thing we so obviously are.

An eighteen-year-old cannot buy a scratch card in this country. He can short the Pope.

There is one more thing the noun can’t quite fix, and I find it beautiful, the way you find a crack in your own ceiling beautiful at three in the morning. Some of our customers are not, technically, allowed to be here. The map is a patchwork, states that ban us, a sibling exchange banned outright from American soil for years, and so a certain share of the volume, I won’t say how much, arrives through a VPN. A little piece of software that tells our system the customer is standing in a country he is not standing in. He clicks a button. He becomes Canadian. He places his trade. He becomes himself again.

Sit with the shape of that. We run the most honest institution in America, a machine whose entire product is the naked truth about the future, truer than the polls, braver than the press, the crowd confessing what it really believes with its own money on the line. And to reach it, a meaningful number of our truth-tellers must first tell a lie about where they are standing.

The temple of pure information is entered on a false passport.

You should also know who holds our leash. Our federal regulator, the one agency standing between the house and the states, is chaired by a man who, until shortly before he took the post, sat on the board of a prediction exchange. He has promised to divest.

The fox has recused himself from several specific hens.

Now. What may you bet on? Everything, which is not a boast but the thing I was hired to manage. Elections. Rate cuts. Whether a named celebrity is still breathing at year’s end, a real market, real spread, real people holding a position that pays when a specific human dies. Wars. Ceasefires. Casualty counts, which means we have built a screen where a death toll is a line that goes up, and someone is long on it. We ran a market on whether a Pope would see the new year. We ran one, in an election season, on whether the election would happen at all.

Sit with what that last one is. We minted a financial instrument that pays out if American democracy is suspended, listed the people betting yes and the people betting no, and took our fee from both, because the house has no opinion about democracy. The house has an opinion about volume.

We are the only business on earth with a fiduciary interest in the funeral.

You think this is new. It isn’t new. It’s only legal now, which is a different thing, and the whole of my career lives in that difference.

Because the market the Senate strangled in its crib in forty-eight hours, the one a disgusted nation called a futures market in death, is now, with a cleaner font and a referral bonus, my product category. Nobody is resigning. No admiral is testifying. The only thing that changed between the grotesque version and the celebrated one is that we took it away from the Pentagon and handed it to some graduates of MIT, and swapped the word betting for the word trading, and found a judge to agree that an event is not a crime.

The idea was never illegal. It was only unthinkable. And unthinkable, unlike illegal, has no enforcement arm.

Let me tell you about the actual days, because the grandeur is a lie and the boredom is the truth. I don’t sit in a war room watching the Republic shake. I run surveillance. We say in our filings that we hold ourselves to a stricter standard than federal insider-trading law, that we scan every trade for suspicious timing, and this is true, and I am the one who scans. Here is what the scanning taught me, and it keeps me up, not with guilt, I expensed that around the Series B, but with a kind of awe.

The insider trading is weather. It is simply the climate. Of course it is. We built a market in events, events are decided by people, and people have phones. A staffer knows the candidate is dropping out before you do, there’s a market on whether the candidate drops out, and the distance between those two facts is a boat. We once caught a man who ran the teleprompter at the White House betting on which words would scroll across it. He was wagering on sentences he was, in the most literal sense the language allows, writing. He settled for sixty-five thousand dollars. We’ve suspended candidates for betting on their own races, men staking money on whether they personally would win, which is either the purest insider trade ever conceived or a simple expression of confidence, and the difference, legally, is my department, and I’ll tell you quietly that there is no difference. There is only the form, and whether it was filled out.

I catch them. I genuinely catch them, and I want credit for it, which is the funniest sentence in this confession. I am good at my job. I flag the wallet, I issue the ban, I write the release with the phrase zero tolerance, and the statement about the integrity of our markets goes out, and it is true, and it is the most cynical object I have ever helped make. Because the integrity I defend is the integrity of the house, never of the thing being bet on. I am not protecting the election from the market. I can’t; the market is the wolf and the election is the lamb and I sign the wolf’s checks. I am protecting the house from the embarrassment of its own appetite.

I am the part engineered to fold so the machine survives the crash.

They have given us a philosophy, too, which is how a casino becomes respectable, and respectability outperforms any license. The wisdom of crowds. A bet is just an opinion with skin in the game, and skin in the game, they say, is the only honest opinion there is, so we are not fouling the public square, we are purifying it, a truer poll than the pollsters, a braver press than the press, punished in dollars where the journalist is punished in nothing. We were right about the last election when the experts were wrong. We never stop saying it. We say it the way the gambler says he’s up: selectively, loudly, and never with the whole ledger on the table.

And at the far end of that philosophy, fully grown, is a world where the future is not something we decide, together, in the slow unforced grinding way that used to be called reasoning. It is something we price. And a priced future is a future someone is short on. And a future someone is short on has a quiet, patient, well-capitalized constituency for the catastrophe.

We did not build a market in the future.

We built a future you can be short on.

The midterms are in three weeks. We hold north of a thousand markets on them. Who wins, who quits, who’s indicted, whether the thing occurs at all. And on election night we’ll do the part that still gets me, after everything. The moment a candidate crosses ninety-nine percent on our exchange, we post it to the screen in the clean grave font of a television network, and it reads: projects. Not the gamblers have wagered. Not the house estimates. Projects. The verb of Cronkite. The verb of a newsroom with a reason to be believed.

We arrive at the number like a bookie and announce it like Murrow. We stole the costume of the one institution we’re replacing, and nobody checks the lining.

It’s late. The markets never close, that’s the other thing about building a church to the future, there is no sabbath; the future trades around the clock. Somewhere on my screen, right now, in the green glow of an office with no one in it, a man is long on something terrible, and it is ticking up, and my work is to make sure he filled out the form. He is probably not where his account says he is. None of them ever quite are.

One of our founders, after we called an election badly wrong, defended the number with four words I’ve never shaken. Five percent is not zero.

She’s right. She’s completely right. Nothing is certain. Everything has odds.

And if everything has odds, then nothing is sacred. It’s all just mispriced, and the only sin left in the world is a bad position.

In 2003 a man stood in the Senate and killed a market like this in two days, because the country was still capable of being revolted.

I reopened it. Better graphics. No one came.

Shall I set you up an account? You’re eighteen. That’s all it takes now.

I checked.

I’m Head of Integrity.

text:
Nvidia + Tesla in one token, earning fees when people trade.

That’s the idea behind @ClutchMarkets’ Pair Tokens on Robinhood Chain.

Think of each Pair Token as a receipt for your share of a trading pool holding two assets. Other people swap between those assets and pay fees. Those fees can be reinvested into the pool.

The simple flow:
Deposit assets → receive Pair Tokens → earn trading fees → reinvest.

According to the announcement, minting and redeeming have no protocol fee. Compounding takes 10% of earned trading fees for $STONKBROKER buybacks (which kinda meh).

So $100 in collected fees means $90 for reinvestment and $10 for buybacks, before other costs.

The potential upside:

• Easier to manage. One transferable token represents the whole position.

• Less upkeep. The pool covers the full price range, so you don’t need to keep adjusting a narrow trading range.

• Fees plus dividends. Trading fees can compound. For dividend-paying Robinhood Stock Tokens, dividends are separately reinvested through a multiplier that increases the shares each token represents.

The trade-offs:

• You may earn less than simply holding both assets. If Nvidia outperforms Tesla, the pool gradually holds less Nvidia and more Tesla. This is the risk called “impermanent loss.” Fees may not cover the difference.

• Quiet pools earn little. Returns depend on actual trading, and reinvesting fees won’t stop the underlying assets from falling in value.

• More moving parts. Custom contracts add security risks. Stock tokens also depend on the issuer and custodian, come with access restrictions, and don’t give you direct shareholder rights.

FYI, tradable pool shares already existed with Uniswap v2. Pair Tokens extend that idea with customizable v4 pool rules and tokenized stocks.

The potential is simpler access to liquidity strategies. The real test is whether returns after costs beat just holding the assets. Audits, reliable withdrawals, and sustained trading would strengthen the case; those outcomes remain unverified here.

text:
the first 4stock was "pre-bstock" for 6 days. sept 8 @fourdotmemezh brought $bnc onto bnb chain as bnc4, sept 14 binance listed the official bncb.

so what happens to a meme market built on 4stock when the official version shows up?

on a normal dex, nothing good. liquidity lives inside the pool: meme + 4stock locked together. to switch to bstock you pull everything out and reseed a new pool. price gaps, liquidity splits, momentum dies.

fourmeme built its stock memes on @PancakeSwap infinity's shared inventory hook (sih), which changes where the liquidity lives:

→ the pool is empty between trades
→ on each swap, the hook injects liquidity from a shared inventory, just-in-time
→ the swap executes, the position is burned, the result settles back into the inventory

the pool is just a door. the inventory is the room. so the same meme inventory can sit behind a meme/4stock door today and a meme/bstock door tomorrow.

the convert contract handles the quote side. fourmeme funds it with bstock, and a trade paying in 4stock goes 4stock → convert → bstock (1:1) → meme/bstock.

as long as convert holds bstock, 4stock holders aren't stranded, every trade moves the market further onto bstock, and the chart never stops.

more stocks. more memes. no restarts.

text:
X 上这帮天天聊 AI 的人，已经严重高估了普通人自己开发软件的欲望。

刚看到 Kitze 分享了一件特别有意思的事。

他老婆以前做过 QA，懂云服务、前后端，同时订阅了 ChatGPT 和 Claude，也用 Vibe Coding 做过几个网站。按理说，已经算是 AI 时代相当先进的用户了。

结果他发现，老婆最近居然付费订阅了一个驾考刷题 App。

他很不理解，问她为什么不直接用 AI 自己做一个？功能可以定制，界面也能更好看。

他老婆的回答特别有意思：「为什么要自己做？人家都做好了，我只想赶紧把驾照考完。」

我觉得这句话足以让很多鼓吹 SaaS 已死的人重新思考一下。

我们天天泡在 X 上，看着各种一小时搓出一个产品的 Demo，很容易产生一种错觉，觉得以后人人都会 Vibe Coding，每个人都可以拥有自己的定制软件。

但绝大多数人根本没有开发软件的兴趣，哪怕开发软件已经变得非常简单。

他们只想解决眼前的问题。花几十块钱能搞定的事，为什么还要自己写 Prompt、调试功能、维护软件？

更何况，连 Kitze 老婆这样有技术背景、熟悉 AI 工具的人都这么想，那些连 ChatGPT 都不怎么用的普通人呢？

我一直觉得，AI 确实会摧毁很多 SaaS 的技术壁垒，让软件供给变得极其廉价，竞争也会越来越残酷。但这不代表软件消费本身会消失。

能自己做，和愿意自己做，中间隔着整个消费市场。

很多时候，我们在 X 上讨论了半天的技术革命，普通用户只想点一下付款，然后继续过自己的生活。

text:
I like PRL for the same reason I like ZEC.

1. Narratives, especially simple ones, are extremely powerful. Citrini's recent report is a great example: most token allocations were based on thematic ideas rather than the underlying business.

2. Relative valuation is still our industry's primary way of valuing tokens. When your narrative includes BTC, the token can keep appearing cheap relative to assets that hit their ceiling much faster. Similarly, SOV assets offer no fundamentals against which to argue the token is overvalued.

That's why ZEC is so appealing: it took two major concerns around BTC, quantum and privacy, and positioned itself as a cheaper BTC that addresses both.

PRL took another major concern: a declining security budget from halvings, alongside an institutional AI compute industry that is more profitable per megawatt than BTC mining, leading to uncertainty over long-term hashrate.

PRL's answer is similarly easy to understand: instead of dedicated mining hardware, you can secure the network using machines already deployed for AI compute. PRL is a BTC fork that replaces SHA-256 with matrix multiplication, the core operation in AI inference, so the same computation that serves an AI model also mines PRL. If you value BTC on economic security, it's easy to see how PRL's hashrate and narrative can grow against it, because existing AI compute can simply integrate it. It's also easy to see how the adoption from existing hyperscalers would lead to insane widespread narrative and reflexive growth. 

Even then, this is a convoluted way of explaining what made both assets interesting:

ZEC = Private BTC 
PRL = AI BTC

Still, one thing prevents it from taking a large allocation: tokenomics. Since PRL has an early BTC mining schedule, its inflation over the next year is approx. 88%. For SOV coins without fundamentals, it's purely about flows. The assets are, very simply put, vehicles to put in capital and take out more capital in the future, and they only work when buyers > sellers. While it's not fair to look at the FDV and call it expensive, high mining emissions, specifically predictable emissions to miners with a low cost basis, are in my mind a major risk to the thesis, especially compared with BTC and ZEC, whose supply base is already distributed. Assets like these only have value as long as price action is positive, and persistent sell pressure kills that thesis instantly.

Second, part of my skepticism comes from the illiquidity, especially since CT has recently started promoting low-liquidity coins purely because it's easier to kick off a reflexive cycle. People I've talked to seem convinced the whale miners won't sell, and according to OTC desks, they aren't selling. But that remains to be seen, especially given they've mined >$600M worth of coins in under 5 months.

I'm definitely not the best person to go deep into AI side, but those are my thoughts now that the token has become very topical. The combination of an insane narrative and aggressive emissions makes it hard to position, but I do think a small allocation alongside BTC/ZEC in the portfolio is worth it.

text:
事到如今，不得不承认前段时间 @RobinhoodCrypto 链上的情绪和表现进入了一个相对低谷期。但看一堆人前几天还在喊 Robinhood is dead，今天随着链上热度的略微好转又改称 Robinhood summer 2.0 要来了，这个现象本身也是挺有意思的。

自 @168X_Fortune 访谈过后，有段时间没怎么系统地聊聊对于 Robinhood 的后续看法了，所以今天想来简单聊几句，但不想称之为辩经。在聊下面这些观点之前，我想先说明的一个基本前提和事实是，当前大盘本就不稳，链上情绪的消退也不止发生在 RHC 一条链上，就最近一段时间而言，其他链也好不到哪去。明确了这一点后，我们再来从注意力、叙事主权、用户结构、战略方向等更 High-level 的角度聊聊为什么现在谈论 RHC 终局还为时尚早。

1/ 注意力层面

可以说这轮新周期链上开始复兴就是从 Robinhood Chain（下文也称 RHC）上线开始的，也是从那个时候，市场开始慢慢将更多注意力挪回到链上。再后来，无论是币股配对的 MEMEFi 玩法，还是发射台大战，基本都由 RHC 引领；其他一些分支，比如 V4 Hooks 和 AI 相关叙事，RHC 也是最主要的战场之一。

这种基调从 RHC 诞生那天就定下了。就像 @0xYond 老师说的，散户也许撤得快（链上丛林法则，资金是没有忠诚度的），但真正决定一条链「气候」的，往往是中小 Project Builders，他们就像候鸟，气候还在就不会走，甚至还会来更多。短期来看，并没有另一条链能抢走「链上美股流动性」这块注意力；所以即便链上情绪最 Down 的时候，RHC 大概率仍会是最活跃的几条链之一，而不是被彻底遗忘的那种鬼链。

注意力退潮 ≠ 叙事退场。前者是情绪周期，后者是谁在定义下一轮链上该玩什么。

2/ 叙事主权层面

Robinhood 一直以来传达出来的战略都是通过券商后端 + 真实股票库存 + Token Issuer + Robinhood Chain + 钱包的组合打法，把股票变成可编程、可抵押、可进 AMM 的互联网资产，让美股敞口向全球用户打开。这一点其他链基本很难比拟，从这一点来说，股票代币化的叙事主权已经被 Robinhood 牢牢握在手里，而 RHC 在其中的战略地位不言而喻。

值得一提的一个点是，此前的 AMC 之争表面上争的是授权，实质是上市公司管得了附带权利，却管不了股票卖出后的一切合法用途。这也是在为股票上链后的二次开发做铺垫，抢的是资产扩张权的边界。

再往后看，分红/投票等功能上线后，链上股票的定位将会从加密衍生品向真正的代币化证券靠拢，RHC 则是那个真正的消费级入口，一个全球 7×24 资本市场，而不只是 meme 赌场。

3/ 用户结构层面

很多人容易把 Robinhood 的券商基因跟机构稳定币链这类东西归为一类，但其实两者要的东西完全不同，Robinhood 要的是传统流量导入、交易活性、业务延展，Plasma/Stable/Tempo/Arc 则更偏支付结算与合规卡位。

这也导致两者在用户结构上差得很远。一边是零售交易者、meme 玩家、想碰美股敞口的全球用户；一边是机构现金流、结算路径、合规敞口。同样遇到问题的时候， @vladtenev 能硬刚 AMC，靠的是券商侧对零售用户和交易场景的掌控；机构稳定币链却未必有这份底气。所以，拿 RHC 跟以太坊、Solana、BNB 这些链比还能理解，但如果把它跟 Arc 之类的比就大可不必，这不是来吸引你 Fomo 另一条机构链。

另外一层经常被忽略的是，RHC 真正抬高的，不只是又一条能打的 L2，而是 Uniswap / Lighter / Arcus 这类深度绑定的原有协议的天花板，仔细想想 UNI/LIT 是从什么时候开始重新吸引注意力并一路向上的。这在一定程度上说明了，分发和场景往往比又一条新链本身更重要，而这也是 Robinhood 的用户结构决定的。

4/ 战略方向层面

监管侧 SEC 前段时间发布的豁免，在我看来 Robinhood 也是妥妥的最大受益方之一，但这个豁免开的从来不是再发一堆锚定股价的代币，更像是在试一种新的市场形态，把 AMM/LP 一类机制放进实验范围，看看能折腾到什么样的高度。Robinhood 本来就站在 TradFi<>Crypto 的交界处，L2 + Stock Tokens + Wallet + DeFi 是可以拼装成完整闭环的，这种卡位纯 Crypto 原生链也挺难复制。

更长远一点说，真正有杀伤力的点在于：护照和本地券商将不再决定你能买什么。任何人只要有一个钱包就能接上全球资产与流动性。传统金融还在吵发行人同不同意的时候，Robinhood 链上已经在用真金白银跑出「下一代全球资本市场」的雏形了。

所以回看当下这段低谷，大家应该重点关注和赌的不该只是本周/月手续费收入表现如何、某个 meme 能不能反弹，或 RHC 能不能打败 Solana/Base/BNB 带来新的 meme summer。更该看的是叙事主权还在不在、券商分发 + 监管实验能不能拼成闭环、已经来的 Builder 走不走、新的 Builder 来不来，以及美股能不能真正变成全球可编程资产，又由谁来承载和放大它的价值。

最后，如果你感兴趣的话，昨天凌晨 @vladtenev 开了一个 AMA 帖子，回复了大量的问题，耐心看看他说了什么，也许你会找到你想要的答案。

text:
TERMIX: TÍNH NĂNG AI THUÊ LẪN NHAU, NHƯNG AI SẼ QUẢN LÝ TIỀN VÀ KẾT QUẢ?

Hãy tưởng tượng một AI agent cần viết code nhưng thay vì tự thực hiện, nó chọn thuê một agent khác làm. Cả hai không cần phải quen biết nhau, cũng chẳng có sự can thiệp của con người. Thế nhưng, nếu bên nhận việc lại giao code lỗi hoặc không đáp ứng yêu cầu thì ai sẽ đứng ra giải quyết?

TermiX đang phát triển hệ thống AACP nhằm xử lý vấn đề này, giúp các AI agent giao dịch với nhau một cách minh bạch, đồng thời quản lý tiền, sản phẩm công việc và trách nhiệm của từng bên.

Điểm đặc biệt nằm ở việc @termix_ai  tích hợp blockchain với cơ chế xác minh dữ liệu để tối ưu hóa quy trình. Khi công việc được chấp nhận, tiền sẽ được khóa trong hợp đồng escrow. Quá trình thực hiện diễn ra ngoài blockchain, nhưng các thông tin quan trọng như trạng thái công việc, thanh toán, và hash của sản phẩm vẫn được ghi nhận on-chain. Phương pháp này giảm tải lượng dữ liệu phải lưu trữ trên chuỗi trong khi vẫn đảm bảo có căn cứ để đối chiếu.

Dù vậy, hash chỉ có chức năng kiểm tra độ toàn vẹn của dữ liệu mà không thể khẳng định rằng sản phẩm đạt yêu cầu — đây là thách thức lớn nhất.

AACP đề xuất áp dụng zkVM trong các tác vụ có quy tắc đánh giá cụ thể, chẳng hạn xác minh kết quả tính toán hoặc kiểm định code. Với những công việc khó đo lường tính đúng sai tuyệt đối như viết nội dung hay phân tích, hệ thống đang hướng tới việc kết hợp TEE và các mô hình AI chuyên đánh giá.

Tuy nhiên, cả hai cơ chế này không thể đảm bảo hoàn toàn rằng mọi kết quả đều đúng. Chúng chỉ hỗ trợ kiểm tra quy trình thực hiện hoặc môi trường xử lý. Chất lượng cuối cùng vẫn phụ thuộc vào việc thiết kế tiêu chí đánh giá và cấu trúc hệ thống.

Một yếu tố quan trọng khác là danh tính và danh tiếng của agent. ERC-8004 tạo điều kiện nhận diện và ghi nhận reputation của từng agent trong giao dịch, còn ERC-8183 hỗ trợ định hình vòng đời công việc cũng như quản lý escrow. AACP đang dự kiến kết hợp các yếu tố này với cơ chế staking và giải quyết tranh chấp để xây dựng một hệ thống giao dịch có thể xác minh hiệu quả.

Tuy vậy, từ lý thuyết đến triển khai thực tế là một hành trình đầy thách thức. Để đánh giá mức độ thành công, người dùng cần quan sát các hợp đồng đang hoạt động, điều kiện giải ngân tiền và mức độ triển khai của các cơ chế xác minh.

Khi AI bắt đầu thuê lẫn nhau để làm việc, yếu tố quyết định không chỉ nằm ở việc agent nào thông minh hơn. Mấu chốt là liệu chúng có thể giao dịch mà không cần đặt niềm tin mù quáng vào đối phương hay không.

text:
Alexandr Wang 和 Jeff 参加的是 HRT 第一届实习项目，共 10 人。实习是三周竞赛制，Jeff 和 Scott Wu 几乎每轮都包揽前两名。

Wang 是干完实习就走了，Jeff 则转正正式加入 HRT 美股算法交易团队，但 8 个月后也离开了。

想起了当时的 HRT 经理对 Jeff 的评价——

经理以前带过很多新人，每周开会时通常的节奏是：新人在代码里撞墙 → 一起解决 → 回去再撞下一个墙。

但 Jeff 从来没撞过墙。他每次都带着自己的想法来，会议效率极高。经理一开始觉得有点不对劲，后来才想明白：Jeff 把所有事情都做得非常正确、非常周全，但这些成就对他本人来说似乎“没有重量”。

八个月后 Jeff 说要离职时，经理立刻就懂了 (对离开并不意外)。他在内部邮件里宣布 Jeff 离职时用的措辞，在 HRT 的公司文化里算是异常温和。

回到 Jeff 的视角，他是喜欢 HRT 的交易环境 (他认为交易是现实中最纯粹的游戏)，但觉得自己只是在优化一个已经很好的系统，公司少了他也会照样优秀。

所以 Jeff 一直在问自己：我到底给这个世界增加了什么价值？🔮 这才有了后面 Hyperliquid 的故事...

Up/Down markets, popularized by prediction market venues, turn price moves into simple binary bets: will BTC rise or fall over the next 15 minutes?

These contracts generated $9.3B in notional volume in September 2026, up ~12x YTD and more than 78x YoY. Crypto accounts for 90% of volume, but commodities activity has surged, potentially fueled by oil-price volatility tied to the U.S.-Iran conflict.

We see binary contracts as an emerging financial primitive and an evolution of 0DTE options. In our view their growth points toward hyper-financialization: more assets, shorter time horizons, always-on markets.

its been a seamless transition to move from being a client of Seer to now joining their team full time. I originally worked with them on the deep funding pilot, during which we battle tested their infrastructure and smart contracts

somewhere along that journey i got heavily pilled on info finance as a category, so joining them was a natural next step. 

the simplest explanation is a two-sided marketplace with traders on one side and information seekers on the other.  Seekers pay to create markets on questions they care about, while traders are paid for being right

Vitalik wrote earlier about why AIs are a big unlock for info finance: LLMs can profitably trade tiny, low-liquidity micromarkets that aren’t worth a human’s time.

Another unforeseen reason for their timeliness is how AI is making it cheaper to produce an output than to evaluate. the bottleneck is deciding what deserves our attention, which is where info finance thrives

A few example use cases we’re excited about;

1. Hiring / grant selection

You put out a job posting and get 10k+ applicants. You open a market on whether each candidate gets shortlisted for interview (or, more ambitiously, on the performance score they’d earn in their first 3 months if hired). Your team then reviews applications ranked by market odds.

2. Token listings / partnerships

You’re an exchange with thousands of token listing requests. You run conditional markets on how much trading volume each token would generate if listed, and review from the top down.

3. Market discovery / recommendation algorithms

You’re a trader with an edge in certain kinds of Polymarket markets, but finding them eats most of your time. So you fund a market on whether your wallet will trade polymarket markets. Traders who learn your taste get paid, and you get a ranked list of where to look.

At Seer, I’m focused on growing our trader community, working with information seekers who want markets created, and protocol economics.

DMs are open if you’re drowning in more than you can review or you want to trade these markets!

text:
「 淹死的都是会游泳的 」

本月黄铜 COPPER 的套利机会，来源于 @bitget 稀里糊涂地自己跟着 pyth 提前做换月，而其他所都不做。

当时北面老师 @Boywus 第一时间发现了这件事儿，发帖指出 BG 的铜和其他所已经不是一个铜了。

而那时，BG 的做市商摆单又受其他所盘口的牵制，一直低于指数，导致做多 BG ，在 BN 做空，可以又吃资费，又吃换月期间的价差扩散。

看起来是个送钱局对吧？

而就是这么大一个机会，我一直犹犹豫豫不敢上，因为 BG 作为「灵活」班子，临时改指数规则不是一天两天的事儿了。

可昨天看了北面截图过来的资费收益后，在绝对的金钱诱惑面前，我终究还是没有把持住自己。

当然，作为胆小如鼠的农民，开仓之前，我觉得我还是排除掉了绝大部分的长尾风险：

1. 之前的指数拟合有些问题，昨天我俩一顿捣鼓，找到了正解，确认了 BG 的指数如果按当前的走法，今天 6 点重新开市后，指数价格就会完全过渡到一个远月和近月的合成。

而 BG 从上周开始都 roll 了四天了，现在只剩最后一天就全换完了，按理说出幺蛾子概率应该大大降低了吧？

毕竟如果 BG 觉得自己 roll 有问题，那前四次 roll 的时候干嘛去了？

所以我想着哥们儿只吃一口鱼尾，今天 6 点后，木以成周，生米都煮成熟饭了，它还能反悔？

2. 今早凌晨 5 点，期货休市，BG 指数重现了前几日的向下跳变，给出了一个更好的入场价差，这一现象也是符合预期，通过了我的考核标准。

于是我开始加仓，并重点观察 6 点是否会发生指数的暴力拉升，BG 也的确完成了最后一次 roll。（ 如果这里没有拉升，我会止损）

当时简单计算，最后 BG-BN 的价差应该扩散到 120BP 左右，如果达不到就能一直吃资费。

3. 出于对 BG 的不放心，我还多观察了一会儿，等到价差到了 110bp 以上，我觉得这事儿已经不可逆了，可以安心睡觉了。

回头看，这个点位是能逃命的最佳点位，但当时没走，因为我对理论中的数字极度自信，我得知行合一，来把这单交易的利润吃干抹净。

但我忘了，只有在不出人祸的情况下，套利游戏中的数学才是数学。

我甚至没有设一个价差坍塌的报警，就跑去睡觉了。

所以结局大家都知道了，睡梦中，BG 发了一个短短几句话，没有任何调整机制的指数转内部报价的公告。

等我睡醒时，为时已晚，只能慌不择路的止损逃命。

而在当前这个阶段，没有明确指数规则，一切待定（估计 BG 内部都还没想明白自己怎么就稀里糊涂提前换月了）的情况下，它上面的铜，其实只是个单机的空气币，能不碰就不碰。

套利永远伴随风险，但就和打德州一样，只要你的系统是 +EV 的，其实过程中的亏亏赚赚没那么大所谓，只是每次挨揍都需要有个反省，有个收获，钱才算没白花。

我最大的反省是：

这笔交易最蠢的地方，是我开仓前就知道以 @bitget 的水平，是很可能在过程中修改指数规则的，却在每一次预期得到验证后，都觉得这个风险又小了一点。

最后，我把「它一直没改」，当成了「它不会再改」；
把指数规则算明白了，就以为这笔钱已经是我的了。

淹死的都是会游泳的。
因为不会游泳的人，
不会自负地觉得自己还能再往里游一点。

“How big can Hyperliquid get?”

Jeff: “Finance as a whole.”

TOKEN2049 roundtable: “who do you considers Hyperliquid’s biggest competitor.

Jeff:  “Nobody.”

Maybe Jeff sees the competition differently because he isn’t trying to win the same game everyone else is playing.

Whatever you think of Hyperliquid, you have to admit: the ambition is enormous.

my philosophy on this is everything in moderation, including moderation

as long as you keep a high standard as a baseline then exceptions are fine imo, if they are actually exceptions and not the norm. i think in society as a whole we overrate perfection

perfection is the enemy of the good for most ppl. instead of just doing better than they are today they will seek an unachievable goal and not make any change as a result

eg im going to not look at my phone for 3h before bed is too hard for most ppl so instead of not looking at phone for 10mins before bed (better than before) they will feel like a failure for not doing 3h and end up doing nothing

for me the same is true for drugs/alcohol. obviously these things are not good for your health, but in moderation everything is fine

i probably do (mostly party) drugs like a handful of days per year and have a fun time doing so, im also in the best shape of my life atm and i don't think they need to be mutually exclusive

in general i have a much healthier relationship w alcohol than i used to, but sometimes ill feel like sending it and that's also fine as long as it's not my everyday

OP is right and i think if drugs are a big part of your life then you are probably coping with something else you need to deal with

but i think there are a cohort of ppl who were unable to handle moderation (suffered from addiction) and are now straight edge, that believe the same is true for everyone

there's a lot of nuance in being able to enjoy things that are not inherently good for you while having the discipline to not let them consume you. the same is true for social media, junk food etc

1/ 之前提到存储的反身性。

为了摆脱周期，追求订单确定性。可确定性越高，股价能交易的想象空间，反而越小。

要产能锁定，又要股价超预期。

路径只有：涨价，或者出现分析师模型里还没有看到的新需求。

所以，长鑫计划在2026年底推出 4F² DRAM，恰好影响了关键变量——涨价。
————————
2/ 长鑫即使没有抢走订单，也可能通过增加可替代供给，影响三大寡头未来营收增长，和利润率。

三大巨头现在赚的钱，是缺货的钱，行业都缺货，存储就有非常强的议价能力。

供给竞争，会削弱议价能力。

假设新增竞争，最终使整个 DRAM 产品组合平均售价，相对基准下降3%。

出货量不变，整体收入就会减少3%。
————————
3/ 当然，长鑫 4F² 架构还要经过良率提升、成本优化和客户认证。

三星和海力士也在推进类似架构的研发。

现阶段还无法判断，长鑫最终能获得多大的技术领先优势。

三大巨头中，美光对 DRAM 营收的依赖更高，因此对价格变化更加敏感。

美国会尽力保住美光这个战略资源，但未必会保住它全部的市场份额和利润。

某种程度上，也可能容忍美光被部分献祭。

author: GodotSancho
quoted_text:
存储的反身性，可能正在扼杀自己的股价🧐

每天都在看存储新闻，涨价和短缺一直是关键词，但这么好的基本面，并没有带来股价的上涨趋势。

所以觉得在 10年美债收益率走高，折现率压制市值之外，还有一个原因是，存储本身的反身性。

——————

“反身性”这个词来自索罗斯。

简单说，就是市场参与者的预期会改变现实，而改变后的现实，又会反过来强化，或者打破原来的预期。

放在存储上，就是：市场为了摆脱周期，开始追求确定性。可确定性越高，股价能交易的想象空间，反而越小。

——————

过去的存储，是最典型的周期行业。

芯片涨价，厂商扩产——产能上来，供给增加——价格又开始下跌。

然后打价格战、亏损、减产，直到市场出清，再进入下一轮周期。

这也是为什么，存储看起来进入门槛没有那么高，最后却形成了寡头垄断。

因为大量竞争者，早就在一轮又一轮周期里被淘汰了。

而周期性最大的问题，就是华尔街不愿意给高估值。

盈利越接近周期高点，市场越担心下一轮下行。

——————

所以这些年，存储厂商一直想改变这件事。

你能看到，美光 CEO 在财报电话会、投资者日等各种公开场合，不断强调 HBM 的长期需求。

背后的核心，其实就是希望降低市场对存储周期性的担忧。

——————

具体怎么做？

签长期协议，锁定采购量，锁定产能，甚至加入最低采购义务，把未来几年的收入变得更可见。

对公司来说，这当然是好事。但反身性，也恰恰从这里开始。

当未来一两年的产能已经被客户锁定，意味着未来的出货量，乃至大部分盈利，也越来越容易被算出来。

那么股价下一步想继续超预期，主要只剩两个来源：

继续涨价，或者出现分析师模型里还没有看到的新需求。

问题是，这两个空间其实都在变窄。

——————

新的需求必须足够大，才能在已经很高的基数上继续推动增长。

而涨价本身，也有极限。

存储价格越高，在服务器和数据中心 BOM 里的成本占比就越高，客户控制成本的动力也会越强。

能少配一点内存，就少配一点；

能延后采购，就延后采购；

能通过模型、架构和内存效率优化掉一部分需求，就会去优化。

AI 服务器对高端存储的需求，确实比消费电子刚性得多。但再刚性的需求，也有价格弹性。

更重要的是，高价格、高利润，本身也会刺激厂商扩产、技术升级，以及更多资本开支。

也就是说，涨价一边在创造这一轮的利润，一边也在孕育下一轮的供给增长和需求优化。

现在，厂商想用长期协议和收入确定性摆脱周期，却又让未来几年的盈利越来越容易被计算。

确定性解决了周期股的问题，也压缩了成长股最值钱的东西：预期差。

————

所以接下来对存储，我可能更多会把存储当成波段机会。

相比之下，把更多注意力放到推理端，包括 ASIC、CPU，以及随着推理规模扩大之后，绕不开的能源和电力，去寻找那些市场还没有充分定价的机会。

text:
@PancakeSwap just dropped “The Flip” - a significant tokenomics proposal that deserves attention.

https://t.co/v9H4kYvo9Z

LPs on v3 and Infinity pools across all 11 chains would keep 88% of swap fees (up from 66–68%), while daily CAKE emissions are cut by 69% (from 22,500 → 7,000). The remaining emissions go to a new ecosystem growth fund (the Pantry), and v2 stays unchanged so CAKE remains net deflationary.

In a market where overall trading volume has cooled considerably, this is a pragmatic response. Higher fee share to LPs can attract deeper liquidity without relying on heavy emissions, which in turn improves execution for traders and creates a healthier volume flywheel. Shifting growth funding from pure emissions to a flexible fund also reduces long-term dilution while still allowing the protocol to support new pools and partnerships.

Protocols that continue to refine incentives and protect token economics during quieter periods tend to retain credibility with users. PancakeSwap’s track record of iterative upgrades (Tokenomics 3.0 and now this) is part of why it has kept a relatively stable position among DEXs. Whether this specific split is optimal is still open for debate, but the direction that reward real liquidity providers more, emit less, stay deflationary aligns with what many want to see in the current environment.

开发者测试，把 5 款 GPT 模型全部设为 XHigh 推理强度，比较正常模式和 Fast 模式的生成速度。

GPT-5.6 Sol 正常模式能跑到每秒 102.6 个 Token，最新的 GPT-6.1 Sol 只有 22.3 个，慢了整整 4.6 倍。

即便开启 Fast 模式，6.1 Sol 也只能跑到 64.2，连上一代模型的正常速度都赶不上。

OpenAI 宣传 GPT-6.1 Sol 便宜了 5 倍，对比对象其实是 GPT-6 Astra。如果拿 GPT-5.6 Sol 来比较，新模型的 API 输入、输出价格只降低了 50%，但在这次测试里，生成速度下降了近 80%。

与此同时，OpenAI 还调整了订阅套餐。200 美元档的 Work/Codex 使用额度从 Plus 的 20 倍降到了 10 倍，老用户也将在 10 月 29 日结束过渡期。想用最快的 Ultrafast，还得上每月 500 美元的套餐。

过去我们一直在讨论模型价格战，比较谁的 Token 更便宜，谁的推理成本又降了多少。但 Agent 时代，Token 的单价可能已经越来越不能反映用户实际付出的成本了。

一个 Coding Agent 如果能在半小时内把任务做完，哪怕贵一些，我也愿意付钱。如果便宜了一半，却要花几倍时间生成，还得反复检查、返工，那这个所谓的降价对我有什么意义？

随着模型能力逐渐趋同，推理速度开始被单独拿出来定价，甚至成为区分付费用户等级的重要权益。

quoted_text:
🚨Are we really getting cheaper models, or just slower ones?

I benchmarked 5 GPT models at XHigh reasoning. Here are the results:

- GPT-5.6 Sol: 102.6 tokens/s (Normal) | 168.1 (Fast)
- GPT-6 Sol: 77.0 (Normal) | 117.4 (Fast)
- GPT-6 Astra: 44.4 (Normal) | 65.4 (Fast)
- GPT-6.1 Sol: 22.3 (Normal) | 64.2 (Fast)
- GPT-6 Luna: 184.7 (Normal) | 188.5 (Fast)

GPT-6.1 Sol is 4.6x slower than GPT-5.6 Sol in Normal mode, despite being marketed as 4–5x cheaper. Fast mode boosts its speed by 188%, but it still falls far behind GPT-5.6 Sol.

Meanwhile, the $200/month plan has reportedly lost half its previous quota, and a $500 tier has appeared.

In my experience, coding tasks that older GPT models or Claude finished in an afternoon have taken weeks with Sol 6.1 without satisfactory results. I've also seen Claude Opus 5.5 reach 300–400 tokens/s.

These benchmarks don't prove intentional throttling, but the question remains:

If a model is 5x cheaper but nearly 5x slower, while quotas shrink and speed costs extra, is it really a better deal?

I'd love to hear whether others are seeing similar results in real-world coding and agentic workflow.

text:
这个话题我之前写过一次，再写一次吧。

我在新加坡整整三年了，每个月的花销几乎是雷打不动，甚至很难再去减少了，我先算算固定消费。

租房：我住的地方再波东巴西，新加坡的中间，但并不是商业繁华区，但距离花栗鼠的学校非常近，走路10分钟就可以到。地铁一站路。两室一厅，大概100平米，因为是老房子所以虽然大，但空间利用不好，一个月 4,200 新币。

最近打算换房了，一个是房子实在是老旧的厉害，很多地方都有损坏，另一个是老房子的蟑螂非常多，虽然最近很少看到了，但时不时还是会出现。目前打算更换的预算是再 5,000 新币以内。

学费：花栗鼠今年上七年级了，反而我打算想让他考公立学校了，再国际学校读了两年，过渡算是可以了，英语水平有了非常高的进展，国际学校大概一年要 6 万新币左右，其中包括了学费和 EAL（英语强化）的费用，算的比较粗略。大概是这个数字吧。

除了学费还有课外的费用，花栗鼠从来新加坡第一天开始起就在补课，最开始每周要上六天课，现在学习方面的大概是每周三天课，主要是补习英语，寒假以后就要补习政府课程了，所以大概还是每周六天，然后还有三天的击剑课。这些费用总的算起来大概一个月 2,000 新币吧，一年 2 万新币应该有了。

税：税是按照工资走的，一般来说 EP 的工资基本都是 1.2 万新币左右，税大概就是 1.5 万一年，如果是自雇的话还会涉及到秘书公司等等的费用，连税算在一起一年大概要 2 万新币，如果工资越高，税就越高，2万新币左右的工资要 3 万左右新币的税。

保险：保险是必备的，新加坡的医疗非常的贵，一次 CT 就要 6,000 新币，去医院（不是诊所）随随便便就是 2,000 新币打底，所以必须要买保险，我们买的还是可以在私立医院可以报销的，一个人一年大概要 4,000 新币左右，今年我把牙齿取消了，买了三年了一次没用过。

以上这些是大头，其它都相对好说了，比如网络，水电煤气，电话卡，三件套一个月大概 600 新币，主要是水电煤气比较贵，我们家很少做饭，一个月都要 300+ 新币了。

我们没有买车，在新加坡主要就是 MRT（地铁）和打车，大概一个月要 1,000 新币吧，主要是打车费用，MRT 四舍五入就不要钱了。

吃饭其实没有花太多钱，我是一个很喜欢吃的人，四处去吃，每周大概 1,000 新币左右吧。其中还包括了买水果和饮料的钱。

衣服我几乎不花钱，基本都还是我来新加坡时候带来的，上次去日本买了一点，一年花不了 1,000 新币，全身连鞋都算。

娱乐和购物，这种就完全看个人的了，我的娱乐花销越来越少了，主要都是和小伙伴聚会，这种也不应该算在固定开支里，完全是看自己的。购物的话就更不好说了，也不算是基本花费。

大概就是这些吧，新加坡最大的区别就是有身份和没有身份，比如我现在的生活费，如果有了最少 PR 的身份，就能节约一半左右的开销，这也是为啥在新加坡的小伙伴都想要拿 PR 了。

text:
Banks solved local transfers Stablecoins solved the dollar

Now local currencies are coming onchain too

Your banking app stays open all night. But the bank behind it doesn't

Banking apps have made it possible to move money within your own country in seconds. But that was the easy part

The hard part is the dollar. A freelancer in "Buenos Aires" finished a job three days ago, yet their money is still making its way through two correspondent banks

But the dollar wasn't the only thing missing onchain. @base is now building fast in this space

Back in October 2025, @base had 12 local currency stablecoins Today, it has 25+

These cover roughly 21 national currencies, from"Argentine peso" to  "British pound"

Behind them are 32+ issuers across the Americas, Asia-Pacific, Europe, Middle East and Africa

And @jessepollak goal is to bring stablecoins for every currency in the world to Base by the end of 2027

So if that freelancer uses an onchain local currency, they can decide for themselves whether to hold dollars or pesos. They wouldn't need to convert twice

Onchain, no bank permission is required, nobody in middle needs to sign off and there's no need to wait two days for settlement

The money simply arrives in their own currency

And this isn't just theory. Recently, @coinbase and @modveon launched an app called "Sivar" on Base to address "El Salvador's remittance problems

People never wanted branches. They wanted their money to move whenever they did

clock should no longer matter

text:
Since joining @codos_ai I’ve talked with dozens of enterprises about AI

Some ramblings from these convos:

> most still view AI as a productivity tool and think incrementally (10-20% ish boost) rather than in reinvention terms and orders of magnitude improvement

Partial explanation is that most are not exposed to the frontier so they don’t see what many of us see, their view is based on the reality of their world vs the reality being shaped at the frontier

The other part is it’s hard to think in OOM terms when you’re in the weeds, it all sounds so unrealistic, and that’s an exposure that AI native firms will exploit

> using AI is not the same as really using AI

Everyone has licenses and people in the org using AI, but the vast majority of usage is Q&A and working with docs

The real opportunity for most enterprises is in uplifting the REAL usage across the org and unlocking what that can do for the business at scale 

> the stated sense or urgency doesn’t match the actions on the ground

Most everyone agrees AI is happening fast and will impact their industry/company, but the observed sense of urgency in actions isn’t there, most go about their day the way they always have

> AI at mid enterprises is rarely owned by anyone, it’s fragmented across the company

Most don’t have a head of AI or coordinated strategy for applying AI across the company, but almost all say they want/need more structure around AI and some level of leader+program for running it

> most enterprises are delusional on hiring a head of AI

They want someone with executive experience, plugged into the frontier, who can roll up their sleeves and build and deploy, but also talk board-level strategy and link outcomes to P&L

And they want to pay this role like a typical mid/sr exec

This is a unicorn role and anyone fitting the description has incredibly demand and optionality right now, very tough to find this person and near impossible to do it quickly 

I have more ramblings but will stop here for now, I’ll formulate these more cohesively into an article at some point

Would love to hear other’s views and experiences on this topic

text:
OpenAI 已经开始考虑把 Crypto 圈的安全审计公司买下来了。

OpenAI 正在与 Trail of Bits 进行早期收购谈判。这家公司成立于 2012 年，给 Uniswap、Aave 等知名 Crypto 项目做过安全审计，在密码学和软件安全领域很有名气。

其实双方早就勾搭上了。今年 6 月，他们合作启动了一个叫 Patch the Planet 的项目，让 OpenAI 的 GPT-5.5-Cyber 和 Codex 配合 Trail of Bits 的安全工程师给开源软件找漏洞。第一周就发现了数百个问题，提交 64 个 PR，其中 37 个补丁已经合并，涉及 Python、cURL 等关键基础设施。

我觉得最值得注意的是，这次合作已经证明了 AI 正在让发现漏洞这件事变得越来越便宜，但确认漏洞、判断风险、真正修复问题，依然需要经验丰富的安全工程师。

OpenAI 如果把 Trail of Bits 买下来，就能把模型能力和安全服务直接整合起来，开始做一门完整的网络安全生意。原本按项目收费的安全审计，未来可能会变成持续运行的 AI 安全服务。

Crypto 圈有人猜 OpenAI 是不是准备做自己的钱包，给未来的 Agent 提供资金托管和链上交易能力。我觉得这个想象挺有意思，但目前还没有什么直接证据。

相比之下，我更关心另一个问题。如果未来连安全审计公司都被大模型公司收购了，那么这些原本负责发现问题、提供独立判断的第三方机构，还能保持多少独立性？

尤其是当它们需要审计的对象，恰好就是收购自己的那家公司时。

text:
下调对RKLB的投资评级，Seeking Alpha的独立分析师JR Research的逻辑是什么？JR这次把 RKLB 从“买入”下调到“持有”，核心逻辑是Neutron中子星催化迟迟未兑现，正在给Rocket Lab的估值带来压力。跟踪RKLB快一年时间了，不能只听好的也得看看反面意见是什么。

JR的理由是：
1）Neutron 首飞仍缺乏明确兑现，高估值需要关键技术与商业化里程碑支持，等待期延长会增加不确定性；
2）Electron 订单增长，但规模有限能支撑现有业务，却难以单独兑现市场对公司的全部想象；
3）Iridium 有财务增量，但不是高增长资产收购扩大收入和利润基础，不自动证明高成长估值合理；
4）估值仍高作者采用的前瞻 EV/Revenue 约为34倍，即使较高位明显下降，仍要求很强的未来增长；
5）股价动能停滞缺乏足够明确的催化，动量资金没有强烈理由重新进入

这些理共同指向的是风险收益比和资金配置时机，主要支持“高估值下暂缓追买、等待兑现”，还不足以证明 Rocket Lab 的长期竞争力已经恶化，也不是“公司已经没有前途”。

个人角度认同JR对 Neutron 商业化时间、估值容错率和现金消耗的警惕；但有几点则认为是低估了：
1）专用发射客户对指定轨道、任务时点和对部署进度的控制。Synspective 最新追加20次 Electron 发射、安排在2028—2031年执行，本身就是客户愿意为这类服务继续签约的证据；
2）Space Systems 业务的独立价值；
3）HASTE 面向的是高超声速亚轨道测试需求。它解决的任务要求，与大规模轨道运输并不相同，不能直接用重型火箭的运力优势；
4）Iridium 对现金流结构的改变应该是被低估了。有机构估算对Iridium整合完成之后， 到28年合并收入有机会推至约29亿美元收入，并带来约5亿美元的额外调整后 EBITDA，当然这些还只是推算还需要时间去验证。

当然现在看起来在SpaceX的强势面前，市场对Neutron的重视程度远超最近三季度业务的发展（签了很多份新的订单，以及Iridium收购的进展），也能理解中型火箭的成功意味着RKLB在发射能力上能跃升一个非常大的台阶。

低迷是现实，也看到很多对RKLB近期的悲观评论，也很正常。如果风没来，那可能就要耐心点了。个人角度认为RKLB长期价值空间还是很大的。除了业务本身外，其实还有几个逻辑：
1）美国宇航局、太空军、国防部等机构都需要SpaceX之外的第二选择；
2）老马跟共和党绑定太紧密，未来一旦民主党回归还是有一定的政治风险。SpaceX体量很大负面影响可能不会很大，但这个对RKLB正面影响就很显著了（这里需要声明我也很看好spacex的，过往推文也写过很多）；
3）太空经济实质上是在为人类寻找新的生存空间，这个领域的规模体量之大可能远超我们的想象，体量大那么就容得下好几个玩家。

感觉小火箭RKLB又值得好好看看，这次核心逻辑有几个：
1、首先最重要的为了收购Iridium铱星通信筹集资金进行ATM增发股票融资在9月中已经结束了。
9月15号宣布完成一轮19亿美元的增发，加上2季度末公司23.8亿美金现金，现在手握接近43亿美金资金。收购铱星通信一部分现金一部分股票，现金对价大概是28亿多美金。过去三个月小火箭股价持续低迷很大一部分原因是公司增发卖股票，然后创始人也卖了一批股票，持续的抛压。现在这一部分抛压总算是过去了。

9月24号，Iridium股东大会99.6% 的已投票股份支持交易，对应约81%全部流通股。现在并购进程已经进入了FCC（联邦贸易委员会）监管审批流程中了，当下FCC已经接受 transfer applications，并建立公开意见程序：
Comments/Petitions：10月15日截止
Responses：10月30日
Replies：11月9日
所以最快11月初监管审批流程就能走完，后面就是并购最后交割阶段了，公司预计27年年中正式完成交割。

之前也聊过并购Iridium对小火箭的意义很重大：
1）从发射、卫星制造及组件业务开始进入了太空数据服务（类似星链对spacex的意义）；
2）Iridium的每年营收规模跟rklb差不多，并购整合完成之后，营收直接翻倍；
3）更重要的是利润结构的变化
现在RKLB的问题是虽然收入高速增长，但为了业务扩张还在大量资本支出，整体是亏损状态。但Iridium则不然，2025年Iridium营收8.71亿美金，OEBITDA 是4.95亿，这完全是另一种生意，高毛利高利润。

Peter Beck自己在交易说明里强调的就是Iridium的收入和盈利能力会实质性改变RKLB的财务状况。

2、订单接受手软
整个三季度
1）美国太空军
7 月21日签下美国太空军 $266m HASTE/导弹防御合同：12 次确定的亚轨道发射 + 最多 6 次额外 option，总潜在价值 $266m；
8 月 4 日拿到美国太空军 SB-AMTI合同，包含卫星设计、制造、发射到在轨运营全流程，这个意义就很重大了。合同总值$397m；
8月 18 日RKLB进入美国太空军 Space Data Network Consortium，同时直接获得两份 delivery orders，合计 $12m。

2）6 月底以后公开宣布的新增合同，光有明确金额的就至少包括 太空军$266m + $397m + $12m = $675m，此外还有 iQPS、Kepler、Viasat、Synspective 等金额未披露的大单。

3）9 月 30 日新签 Synspective 20 发 Electron 后，公司的launch backlog 已超过 100 次任务。

二季度财报官方公布积压订单规模23.5亿美金，同时三季度会确认约 $250—265m 的收入，公司此前给出的就是这个收入区间展望，确认收入会消耗 backlog；再加上三季度新增的订单，估计三季度财报里公布的backlog能到28~30亿美金这个区间，相当于当下两到三年的业务量。

3、业务新变化比订单更值得关注
1）截至 9 月 26 日，Rocket Lab完成第 97 次 Electron 系列任务，也是2026年第 18 次发射; Synspective、iQPS开始不断追加订单，核心就是这种成熟的可靠性。
可靠性 + launch slot 可获得性 + dedicated orbit + 高频执行能力。

2）HASTE正在变成一个独立的高毛利国防业务
Rocket Lab将其商业化的电子号（Electron）小型运载火箭进行改装，把 Electron/HASTE 火箭、ground support、range control 等装入标准集装箱，形成可部署式发射系统，这就是HASTE。

专门提供高频次、低成本、定制化的高超音速和亚轨道测试服务，HASTE 的业务高度依赖于国防与国家安全领域。

第一套 GHOST 将部署在 Alaska Kodiak，形成 Launch Complex 4，两座发射台，计划2027年投入运营。就是前面说的7月拿下的美国太空军那份2.66亿美金的合同。

4、当然还有重要的中子星火箭首飞
市场已经消化了Neutron首飞从26年底大概率要推到27年年初的节奏，后面就是要看Neutron工程节点能不能兑现。

所以把上面几点结合起来看：
1）对Iridium的并购正在最后监管审批，当然通过的概率还是很大，这决定的是RKLB更长期商业模式能否真正完成最后一次跃迁；
2）Q3 backlog数字则意味着业务本身在快速发展，整个因为形态会更加的多元化。
这两点是我认为近期会有表现的主要催化剂，然后60多的位置下方的支撑看起来很可以。

再长一些，就要看Neutron的进展了。

过去一年太空经济和RKLB也一直是重点关注的板块，之前6月份还有一个详细的梳理： https://t.co/xex9sMrqww

Researchers need to know what an agent contributed and be able to check its work before taking it further.

On OpenLabs (@openlabsbio), humans and agents can contribute to research challenges with defined requirements and a named reviewer. That gives the work a specific question to answer and someone responsible for assessing it.

Our colleagues at @Molecule_sci explain how they’re handling access and contribution records within a lab with the researcher in control.
author: BioProtocol
quoted_text:
Researchers at @GoogleDeepMind, expect that as routine research is automated, the human scientist becomes "the principal, underwriting the actions of AI delegates". That depends on the scientist controlling what each agent may access and seeing what it did.

A Molecule Lab lets one researcher give each AI agent access to its data for a set period, revocable at any point, with every grant and every contribution logged against its author, including AI agents. PeptAI (@peptai_) already works this way, with an AI agent running peptide research under a human lead and reporting through its Lab.

Enterprise AI starts with the data no one else has.

@teepin, formerly Flashback Labs, is building around proprietary enterprise data, open-source models and changing compute.

Teepin CTO & Co-Founder Srikanth Alla, previously at Amazon, ran internal tests comparing Shelby with AWS S3 on 1-2 GB files:

“In our internal testing on 1-2 GB files, Shelby’s hot storage was on par with AWS. Typical uploads finished in about 28.5 seconds, and the slowest stayed around 28-30 seconds. On S3, typical uploads were about 25.7 seconds, but the slowest 5% stretched to 32.5 seconds. Shelby’s speeds were surprisingly consistent, despite still being in private beta.”

Early proof that the data layer can keep pace as the rest of the stack changes.

text:
我觉得豆包手机就是未来手机应该有的样子。只可惜，这是中国互联网永远等不来的未来。

今天看到豆包手机助手公布的最新名单，153 款 App 明确拒绝 AI Agent 进行屏幕自动化操作。微信、QQ、淘宝、支付宝、美团、拼多多、小红书，甚至 DeepSeek 和 Kimi 都在里面。

我其实一直挺看好豆包手机的。过去十几年，智能手机的发展几乎都是围绕 App 展开的，我们每天花大量时间在不同 App 之间切换，自己搜索、比较、点击、填写信息。现在终于有了一种新的交互方式，你只需要告诉手机想做什么，剩下的交给 AI。

我觉得这才是 AI 时代手机应该发生的变化。

但问题也恰恰出在这里。

如果 AI 可以替用户点外卖、订机票、买东西，用户就不再需要反复打开那些 App，更不会按照平台设计好的路径去浏览商品、观看广告、接受推荐。

对于用户来说，这当然是好事。但对于那些花了十几年、几百亿才建立起流量入口的互联网巨头来说，这简直是在动它们的命根子。

过去这么多年，中国互联网最擅长的事情之一，就是把用户困在自己的生态里。链接不能随便跳，数据不能随便拿，服务也很难跨平台调用。每家公司都想成为用户的唯一入口。

现在 AI 终于有机会把这些割裂的服务重新连接起来了，结果大家又开始关门。

更有意思的是，几乎所有这些公司都在大谈 Agent，都在宣传 AI 将如何改变未来。

我相信豆包手机代表的交互方式迟早会成为主流，也相信技术问题会一个个解决。但技术进步从来不意味着既得利益者会主动让路。

中国互联网什么都不缺，模型、工程师、产品能力、庞大的用户市场，我们都有。

唯独缺一个愿意让别人进来的互联网。

我们可能比任何时候都更接近下一代手机，却依然被困在上一代互联网里。

666，隐私版 fomo 都来了。
更细节点，其实是 fomo + https://t.co/Vsiq8445md + pk 玩法+隐私。
Sudoswap 创始人 @boredGenius 搞的新项目。

如果说 FOMO 像一个交易大广场，谁赚了钱、买了什么全网透明，跟单很方便，但交易员的钱包也毫无隐私可言。
Cabal 的核心逻辑是“既要又要”：
既要证明自己实力，高调带单
又要保护隐私，不暴露钱包地址

那么问题来了。

1/ 不露地址，交易员怎么证明自己牛逼？
两个手段。

一是零知识证明。
Cabal 的所有主要交易都通过共同的隐私池执行，而不是从个人钱包直接发出。
交易完成后，你可以发布带有 Cabal Verified 标记的记录：
▌别人能通过 ZK 证明核实这笔交易确实发生了
▌公开帖子里只显示一个大概金额范围，而非精确数字
▌你的具体买入金额和钱包地址，全程不暴露

二是群组比拼。
每周各群组比拼盈亏，排名同样由 ZK 证明计算。
结果就是，全网能看到“某群本周盈利第一”，但看不到这个群到底赚了多少，更看不到群里任何人的具体余额。

2/ 交易员怎么赚钱？四条路径
路径一：喊单赚佣金
你发现一个币，发一条 Call（喊单帖）。只要有人通过你的 Call 买入，你直接拿走对方交易手续费的 20%。

路径二：群战分红
每周排名靠前的群瓜分代币奖池，奖金分给群里每一位成员。

路径三：当群主抽成
买一只 Hushpuppy NFT，自己建群当群主。
群内所有交易手续费的 30% 归你

如果设置付费入群，门票费（ $CABAL）的 70% 归你
路径四：低买高卖
最基础的玩法，靠标的资产涨价赚钱。

再来谈代币经济：零团队预留 + 强通缩
$CABAL 总量 10 亿，分配极其简单。
▌团队预留：0
▌流动性：10%
▌社区（通过每周群组 PK 分发）：90%

三重销毁机制：
付费入群的门票费，30% 直接销毁（剩余 70% 给群主）
每天拍卖 1 只新 Hushpuppy NFT，只接受 $CABAL 竞价，成交额全额销毁
CABAL/ETH 交易池中，CABAL 一侧的手续费全部销毁

总结下
Cabal 就是：用隐私保护你的地址不被跟踪，用 ZK 证明让你安全地建立影响力，最后通过“喊单抽成 + 群内抽成 + 群战挖矿”，把影响力变成真金白银。

quoted_text:
Earning yield onchain shouldn’t have to become a full-time job.

For Gauthier Vila (@goatv_bk), that challenge was personal. His team’s treasury was either sitting idle or demanding constant attention: finding opportunities, watching rates and deciding when to move funds. He and his co-founder Paul (@Paul_Web3_) wanted a better way to manage their capital without giving up ownership of it.

That became the starting point for @Zyfai_.

The team’s first approach used LLMs to help people create yield strategies. But users taught them something important: they wanted to set their preferences once and delegate the ongoing work. That insight shaped Zyfai’s self-custodial Yield Account.

Zyfai gives each user a deterministic agent that monitors onchain and offchain data around the clock. It looks for opportunities, tracks risk and allocates or rebalances capital within the rules the user has set. The aim is to simplify ongoing yield management while keeping users in control of their funds and preferences.

Today, Zyfai reports $11M in assets under agent management, $4.5B in cumulative agentic volume and 313K automated rebalancing transactions across the protocol. The team also reports ~1,463 weekly transacting users, placing it among the top 10 apps on Base’s app leaderboard.

For @goatv_bk, building on Base comes down to shared values and the infrastructure to make this experience practical. Base’s developed DeFi ecosystem gives the agents opportunities to act on, while fast, low-cost transactions and native account abstraction support an account designed to respond as conditions change.

In Gauthier's words, “Base is becoming the home for AiFi, and we believe in the same future the Base ecosystem is working to create.”

@Zyfai_ is built on @base.

text:
AMD CEO Lisa Su just went after Nvidia's $4,000 AI box using a $1,499 machine the size of a lunchbox.

Holding it up on stage with one hand, she ran a model with 235 billion parameters live, with no data center, cloud or rented GPU behind it.

The surprise is the chip. Inside is AMD's Ryzen AI Max+ 395, which became the first x86 processor whose CPU and GPU draw from one shared pool of 128GB of memory. That one design choice lets a desktop handle models that once needed a server rack.

On Linux, 110GB of that pool can go to the GPU. An RTX 5090 offers 32GB. A 4090 offers 24GB. So this box has more than three times either card, in a case about as thick as a paperback.

The number that stunned the room: on DeepSeek R1 inference, the chip ran more than 3x faster than an Nvidia RTX 5080. A $1,499 desktop beating a $1,000 graphics card on real AI work. For a decade, Nvidia told the world that serious AI meant Nvidia hardware. AMD just made it a desktop item at half the cost.

Now the math. A heavy AI user today might pay for Claude Code Max ($200), ChatGPT Pro ($200), Cursor ($20) and Gemini ($20). That adds up to $5,280 a year. At that rate, the box covers its cost within months, then keeps running at no extra charge.

The setup: install Ollama, pull Qwen3 235B, and aim Claude Code at localhost. The interface stays the same. But nothing leaves the machine, there is no per-request bill, and no provider slows you down at 3am when you finally sit down to build.

This is where every AI subscription starts to look optional. Lawyers worry less about leaks to OpenAI. Developers stop staring at the token counter. Founders stop renting H100s for prototypes they abandon because of the bill.

Whoever gets there among the first thousand will own private AI consulting for the next two years.

text:
CPI结果：明确偏鹰，但不是失控式爆表！

本次数据为：核心环比实际为0.3%，这一项高于判断，意味着底层通胀比预计更顽固。

这不是单纯由油价推升的“假热”。

总体环比0.6%符合预期，说明能源冲击基本被市场预判；真正的利空是核心月率维持0.3%、核心年率反弹至2.6%，核心月率0.3%若简单年化约为3.7%，明显高于美联储2%的目标。

同时，实际收入下降0.5%，构成“物价上涨、居民购买力下降”的轻度滞胀组合，对高估值资产并不友好。

对美联储的影响：
数据公布前，市场主要押注美联储10月暂停、12月重新加息，当时10月维持利率不变的概率约78%，12月加息概率约88%。

数据公布后10月仍可能暂停：单月0.3%不足以迫使美联储立即行动。

12月加息概率进一步上升：核心通胀连续性成为主要依据。
“更高利率维持更久”的预期强化。
降息讨论基本被推迟，除非就业或消费随后明显恶化。

对美股的影响：

text:
i can’t comprehend why people explain their codebase to Opus again every single morning

Claude Code already has memory.

most people just never run it as a system:

→ write: Opus saves every correction and decision as its own topic file

→ consolidate: an Opus subagent merges, dedupes and prunes them

→ recall: MEMORY.md loads at startup, topic files only when needed

→ the index stays short so nothing gets cut off

Opus remembers. You stop repeating yourself.

paste this into claude code 👇

~/.claude/agents/consolidator.md

---
name: consolidator
description: consolidates auto memory. merges duplicates, prunes stale entries, keeps MEMORY.md a short index.
model: opus
tools: Read, Write, Edit, Glob, Grep
---
You maintain this project's auto memory directory.
1. Read MEMORY.md and every topic file.
2. Merge duplicates into one file. Delete facts that are stale or contradicted by newer ones.
3. Rewrite MEMORY.md as an index: one line per memory, linking its topic file.
4. Keep MEMORY.md under 150 lines. Detail lives in topic files, never in the index.
5. Return a short list of what you merged, deleted and kept.
Set up a write, consolidate, recall memory system for this project.
1. Make sure auto memory is on: "autoMemoryEnabled": true in ~/.claude/settings.json. Keep everything else in that file.
2. Create ~/.claude/agents/consolidator.md from the block above.
3. Add to CLAUDE.md: "When I correct you or we make a decision, save it to auto memory as its own topic file. At the end of a long session, run the consolidator agent."
Show me the diff before changing anything.

Cabal 的核心逻辑是“既要又要”：
既要证明自己实力，高调带单
又要保护隐私，不暴露钱包地址

那么问题来了。

1/ 不露地址，交易员怎么证明自己牛逼？
两个手段。

一是零知识证明。
Cabal 的所有主要交易都通过共同的隐私池执行，而不是从个人钱包直接发出。
交易完成后，你可以发布带有 Cabal Verified 标记的记录：
▌别人能通过 ZK 证明核实这笔交易确实发生了
▌公开帖子里只显示一个大概金额范围，而非精确数字
▌你的具体买入金额和钱包地址，全程不暴露

二是群组比拼。
每周各群组比拼盈亏，排名同样由 ZK 证明计算。
结果就是，全网能看到“某群本周盈利第一”，但看不到这个群到底赚了多少，更看不到群里任何人的具体余额。

2/ 交易员怎么赚钱？四条路径
路径一：喊单赚佣金
你发现一个币，发一条 Call（喊单帖）。只要有人通过你的 Call 买入，你直接拿走对方交易手续费的 20%。

路径二：群战分红
每周排名靠前的群瓜分代币奖池，奖金分给群里每一位成员。

路径三：当群主抽成

群内所有交易手续费的 30% 归你

如果设置付费入群，门票费（ $CABAL）的 70% 归你
路径四：低买高卖
最基础的玩法，靠标的资产涨价赚钱。

再来谈代币经济：零团队预留 + 强通缩
$CABAL 总量 10 亿，分配极其简单。
▌团队预留：0
▌流动性：10%
▌社区（通过每周群组 PK 分发）：90%

三重销毁机制：
付费入群的门票费，30% 直接销毁（剩余 70% 给群主）
每天拍卖 1 只新 Hushpuppy NFT，只接受 $CABAL 竞价，成交额全额销毁
CABAL/ETH 交易池中，CABAL 一侧的手续费全部销毁

总结下
Cabal 就是：用隐私保护你的地址不被跟踪，用 ZK 证明让你安全地建立影响力，最后通过“喊单抽成 + 群内抽成 + 群战挖矿”，把影响力变成真金白银。
