text:
Are Small Models Really a Threat?

The Anthropic Fear Factory just released a new report warning that small models may be only months away from self-replicating across cheap IoT devices like off-brand Android TV boxes and smart ovens. They say such an AI worm would be hard to shut down since there’s no central kill switch.

We’ve gone from “The Terminator is coming” to “your toaster might kill you.”

But the experiments don’t support the dramatic headlines. They ran a 26B model across 15 $55 TV boxes at 0.39 tokens per second. The end-to-end test used emulated devices with deliberately open ADB ports, so the “hacking” step was trivial. The capable model often ran on a separate server. Agents were harnessed and told to propagate. This is not proof of autonomous rogue AI worms in the wild.

Nor is the threat even novel. Worms that do this without AI already exist. Mirai in 2016 scanned for default credentials and built massive DDoS botnets. Kimwolf has infected over two million devices, mostly cheap Android TV boxes, by hitting open ADB ports.

Small models don’t currently add much that matters on these targets. The bottleneck has never been figuring out the device. It’s the huge number of devices that ship with open ports, default passwords, and no patching. Traditional worms already exploit that at scale.

A practical attacker would use the best models available offline to design a better traditional worm, then ship the lean binary. You get the intelligence benefit at design time without dragging a slow, heavy model along with every infection. Embedding a weak model in the payload is the worse option for anyone who actually wants the largest, fastest botnet.

The timing of Anthropic’s latest scare campaign is hard to ignore. The day before, Brian Armstrong posted that Coinbase fine-tuned an open-weight small model (Qwen-3.5-9B) on proprietary fraud data. It beat frontier models, including Anthropic’s own Opus 4.5, while being faster and much cheaper. In testing it cut fraudulent transactions by about 30%.

This is the emerging pattern. For narrow enterprise workloads you don’t need a general superintelligence. You need a small specialist model trained on your own data. Cheaper to run, especially as compute gets tighter, and often better on the metric that matters. That is a direct threat to the frontier-company model of selling access to ever-larger general models.

Safety advocates should be welcoming this development. If the real concern is existential risk from ever-larger frontier systems — the ones that could theoretically do sustained autonomous R&D or become hard to control — then a shift toward smaller specialized models is the safer outcome. 

Small models specialized on fraud detection or support tickets are not pushing the frontier. They are not in the category of systems that could become a new species. The theoretical loss-of-control risk is created by models getting bigger and more generally capable.

Safety advocates focused on those risks should welcome companies having a cheaper alternative to constantly scaling general models. Instead we get dramatic warnings about small models at the exact moment they are starting to take real enterprise share from closed-model companies like Anthropic.

37 banks bring distribution, so this is the first serious test of euro demand onchain.

if the share doesn't move, the dollar's lead onchain is deeper than it looks.

text:
恭喜 AGPU 拿下大单子。

与 Penguin Solutions 的长期合作正式落地后，市场看待 AGPU 的框架该变了。
此前市场对 AGPU 的核心疑问一直是，不久前才转型的一家公司，怎么交付几十亿美元的 GPU 集群？现在答案很明确：由给 Meta 建过万卡集群的 Penguin 来交付。

订单、预付款、机房（Duos 55MW）、交付方（Penguin），四块拼图齐了。
AGPU 现在缺的是时间，不再是能力。

1/ 机构此前最担心的，从来只是“能不能交付”
公开材料显示，AGPU 已签合同总额超过 30 亿美元，部署完成后预计年化运行率超 6.96 亿美元。数据很亮眼。

但对机构投资者来说，这里有一连串更现实的追问：
▌ 这些合同能按时兑现吗？
▌ GPU 能按计划采购到、交付到吗？
▌ 电力、机房、液冷、网络能跟得上吗？
▌ 大规模集群，谁来建？

说白了，市场不否认 AGPU 拿订单的能力，只是担心它从订单变成收入和现金流的那段路走不走得通。这段路是整条链上最难走的一段，也是估值里一直存在的“执行风险折价”来源。
核心就一句话，一家才转型不久的公司，怎么把几十亿美元的 GPU 集群真正交出来？

2/ Penguin 把最难的一块拼图补上了
Penguin Solutions（NASDAQ: PENG）是纳斯达克上市公司。它不卖服务器，也不做 AI 应用，它只干一件事：帮别人把 AI 数据中心从图纸变成现实，然后长期管好。

什么级别？
25 年以上数据中心和高性能计算经验；
部署和管理过 85000+ 张 GPU，累计运行超 20 亿小时；
参与过 Meta AI Research SuperCluster, 万卡级别、全球顶尖的 AI 集群；
是 NVIDIA 官方认证的 AI Factory Specialized Partner；
FY2026 营收 17.3 亿美元，净利润 1.81 亿美元（同比 +611%），Q4 单季营收创纪录。

Penguin 补上的，正是 AGPU 链条里最重、最复杂、最容易掉链子的那一段。

总之，AGPU 负责把项目谈下来、买下来、融资做起来；
Penguin 负责把项目建起来、跑起来、长期不出事。
这意味着 AGPU 不必从零开始养一支庞大的工程团队，而是借一个被验证过无数次的施工队+运维方，把交付和运维这一环稳稳兜住。机构最担心的“谁来建、能不能建出来”，现在有了明确答案。

3/ 四块拼图齐了，讨论重心该后移
现在，订单有了，预付款有了，机房有了，交付方也有了。四块拼图齐了。

讨论的重心自然会移到下一个阶段：
首批项目能不能如期建设、如期上线？
能不能开始形成可验证的收入和运营数据？

这正是 AI 基础设施项目从讲故事走向交作业的典型转变。
故事阶段比的是想象力，执行阶段比的是兑现力。

We’ve added DeepSeek V4.1 Flash to AA-AgentPerf, with results for NVIDIA and AMD hardware. At 100 tokens/s per user, NVIDIA GB300 is in first place with throughput up to 261M tokens/s per MW.

AA-AgentPerf is our agentic inference performance benchmark. It replays real agentic coding sessions, including prompt caching and tool-call delays, to give a realistic measure of inference performance in day-to-day agentic workloads. We measure total system throughput per megawatt of runtime power, and per-agent output speed at varying concurrency levels, to show the trade-off between system utilization and individual user experience.

DeepSeek V4.1 Flash joins the leaderboard today. It brings the leaderboard to four featured models, joining DeepSeek V4 Pro 0813, Kimi K3, and GLM-5.2/5.3. We are evolving the featured models as popular new open-weights models release, and will feature day-0 results for major future releases.

Background on DeepSeek v4.1 Flash:

➤ It scores 39 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index, ahead of DeepSeek’s earlier V4 Pro 0813 at 36, with about a third of the parameters (552B ‘backbone’ and 16B active, against 1.6T and 49B)

➤ It is built on a new architecture, with a causal encoder-decoder design that activates 8B parameters per input token and 16B per output token. It uses a further 196B parameters of Engram n-gram memory that can sit in host memory rather than on the accelerator, and compressed sparse attention that needs about a quarter of even the earlier V4 Flash model’s KV cache per token

➤ This makes it much more efficient to serve, since the weights fit on fewer GPUs and the smaller KV cache leaves room for more concurrent agents per GPU

Initial AA-AgentPerf results for DeepSeek V4.1 Flash:

➤ V4.1 Flash runs on as few as 2 GPUs, so rack-scale systems get less advantage over 8-GPU single nodes like B300, which stays within about 20% of rack-scale GB300 NVL72 across the curve, and leads at both ends

➤ At 100 tok/s per user, GB300 leads with ~261M tokens/s per MW, ahead of B300 (~220M), B200 (~193M), GB200 (~178M) and MI355X (~128M)

➤ Every Blackwell system and MI355X can reach around 600 to 670 tok/s output speed for a single agent (ie. at batch size of one), against 372 to 392 tok/s on H100 and H200

➤ V4.1 Flash is both more intelligent than V4 Pro 0813 and much cheaper to serve, yielding ~1.3x (GB300) to ~6.2x (B200) the throughput per MW at 100 tok/s per user compared to its larger cousin

这个剧本在历史上，已经演过好多场，每隔几年，就会演一场大戏，来做一场无硝烟的金融收割，这次大概率待宰的羔羊🐑，可能是欧洲第二大经济体法国！🧐

最近一个诡异的数据，法国10年期政府债券收益率最高逼近5%，而股票更是跌的一塌糊涂(如👇图)，法国内部也开始游行不断，因福利缩减原因！感觉这次欧元区排第二的大哥法国，可能真的要踩雷了！

无法想象的是，堂堂欧洲第二大经济体，现在的信用定价，竟然比当年被嘲笑的希腊、意大利还要差！

现在10年期的法国国债收益率一路狂飙，借钱成本直接刷爆了2002年以来的最高纪录。大家都不敢把钱借给法国了，因为它现在的状况，简直就是活脱脱的“债务死循环”。

法国到底是怎么一步步把自己混到今天这个地步的？说白了，主要是三股力量在把它往绝路上推：

第一，好日子过惯了，花钱没节制，债务彻底失控

过去那些年，全世界利率低，借钱便宜，法国政府就大手大脚花钱。现在呢？低利率的“好日子”结束了。

法国欠的债务已经快赶上它一年的GDP总量（接近120%）了，而且接下来几年，有上万亿美元的旧债要到期。这就尴尬了，以前利息低，借新还旧没压力；现在利率这么高，借新债去还旧债，光是每年要还的利息，就能把财政预算给吃干抹净，甚至比防务军费还要高！这就跟一个人信用卡叠信用卡，最后连利息都还不起是一个道理。

第二，通胀和加息这对“组合拳”，直接重创了法国经济。

欧洲这几年地缘冲突不断，能源价格疯涨，法国这种高度依赖外来能源的国家，制造业成本直接飙升。通胀压不住，欧洲央行就只能硬着头皮不断加息。

这下死循环就形成了：通胀越高，央行越要加息；央行一加息，法国政府和企业的借款成本就越贵；借钱越贵，大家越觉得法国要违约，越狂抛法国国债；抛的人越多，借钱成本就进一步升高……这雪球滚起来，根本停不下来。

第三，最忠实的“大金主”日本，开始提裤子跑路了。

以前日本是法债最大的买家之一，因为日本国内利率几乎是零，日本资金喜欢跑到法国套利。但现在日本国内也开始抬高利率了，扣掉汇率对冲成本，买法债赚的那点微薄差价，根本不值得冒风险。于是，日本的大型基金开始清仓甩卖法债，连最忠诚的金主都不玩了，法债彻底失去了最重要的底座。

这三股力量拧成一股绳，直接把法国逼到了两难的死局：

如果不砍财政开支，债务雪球继续滚，迟早崩盘； 如果硬着头皮砍福利、砍开支，经济立马衰退，老百姓分分钟上街游行罢工。

2010年欧债危机的时候，希腊爆雷了，好歹还有德国和整个欧洲拉一把，毕竟希腊体量小，救得起。

但如果这次是欧元区二把手法国彻底爆雷，整个欧洲谁又能救得起它？这可就不是什么普通的债务危机了，这是要直接把整个欧元的根基给掀翻！

拭目以待吧，最近看桥水老板达利奥的书《债务危机》，里面的思路和样本，基本跟当前经济状况如出一辙，美国这招自损800，杀敌1000的策略，大概很快就会有结果了，备好弹药，随时捡便宜！🧐

text:
看看悲观派，华尔街传奇避险基金经理人保罗·都铎·琼斯（Paul Tudor Jones）近期频繁将当前的 AI 科技狂热市场 与 1999年网路泡沫前夕进行类比的观点。

他以「1999年再涨40%」警告，正戳中当前市场最敏感的神经。

他将现在的AI狂热与1999年做直接类比：

如果美股再复制1999年最后那波疯狂，再涨40%，总市值/GDP将冲到300%-350%，随后的修正会是「令人窒息」的。

市场结构也高度相似——指数被极少数权值股硬撑，大量个股其实早已进入技术性熊市。

更关键的是，他明确表态2027年全年做空，理由是OpenAI、Anthropic等巨头IPO叠加解禁，将带来2002年以来最大规模的股票供给潮。

但高盛这边给出了截然不同的解读：1999年恰恰证明，泡沫在彻底破裂前，市场有极强的自我强化惯性——「因为一直在涨，所以还会继续涨」。

IPO和二次增发会带来供给压力，但并不必然终结这轮AI驱动的牛市。

不论多空，华尔街目前的共识其实高度一致：高集中度、极端估值、AI卖铲人已经赚得盆满钵满但下游尚未大规模变现，这些特征与1999年如出一辙。

历史告诉我们，泡沫最后阶段往往还会再来一波不理性的加速上涨，但这通常也意味着离最终清算越来越近。

问题是：在这个阶段，你是已经开始转向美债、黄金等防守资产，还是仍想参与AI行情的最后一段？

预留5年家人的支出，更保险。进可攻，退可守。
做到「心安、眠安、家安。」

text:
我开始怀疑，AI 根本不用发明下一个 Transformer，就能启动自我加速。

昨天我刚写了 Anthropic 联合创始人 Jack Clark，认为完整的递归自我改进可能在 2027 年实现。今天看到 P-Zero Research 的一项新研究，我觉得这个时间点越来越值得认真讨论了。

他们做了一个叫 TasteVal 的基准测试，专门测量 AI 的「科研品味」。

这个词很有意思。一个好的研究员，除了会写代码、做实验，更重要的是知道什么实验值得做，看到结果以后该往哪个方向继续，什么时候应该及时放弃。

研究团队找来 24 位有一线研究经验的人类专家，与模型解决同一组 AI 研发问题。具体编码交给统一的 AI Agent，研究者只负责设计实验和判断结果。

结果 Claude Opus 5.5 达到了人类专家 2.3 倍的实验算力效率，研究者部分的单次成本约为人类专家的 1/30。更夸张的是，自 2025 年 12 月以来，前沿模型的这项效率平均每三个月翻一倍。

我们过去讨论 AI 自我改进，总在等它什么时候能提出下一代 Transformer，什么时候能像顶尖科学家一样产生真正原创的想法。

但我读完论文发现，研究者检查的 AI 实验方案里，居然没有找到真正全新的结构发明。它们主要还是在已有方法上调参、组合、修改。

科研工作里有大量的时间和算力，消耗在试错上。一个模型即使没有提出颠覆性理论的能力，只要能更准确地判断哪些实验值得做、哪些路线应该放弃，就可以让同样的 GPU 预算产生更多有效结果。

而且这种能力还有机会形成正反馈。AI 帮助研究人员更快改进模型，改进后的模型再回来参与下一轮研究。随着研究判断能力越来越便宜，能够同时展开的探索也会越来越多。

我们可能把 AI 自我改进的起点想得太高了。

人类总在等待 AI 做出一个足以载入史册的伟大发现，可真正改变 AI 研发速度的，可能是它先把实验室里那些平庸、重复、昂贵的试错工作接管了。
author: sleepy0x13
quoted_text:
P-Zero Research's new TasteVal benchmark measures research taste: how well a model designs experiments and reads their results on eight real AI-development tasks, scored by how much compute it needs compared with human experts (the dashed 1x line). 

Progress was slow from GPT-4 in 2023 through 2025, then the slope steepened: since December 2025, scores have doubled every 3.0 months. Claude Opus 5.5 now sits at 2.30x the expert baseline, ahead of Fable 5.1 and GPT-6 Astra, at roughly 1/30 of the experts' cost per attempt.

Research taste is the skill that decides how quickly AI could start improving AI, and this curve is one reason Jack Clark now expects that in 2027 (wrote about that yesterday as well).

Compact hash-based signatures rely on each key signing only once, and real systems don't always guarantee that. CUTS, from the Project Eleven research team, is a few-time scheme designed to stay secure when a key is reused, at close to one-time signature sizes.

The paper is now out and includes the full specification, security proofs, and parameter sets. At 1,424 bytes, a CUTS key keeps 128 bits of security after two signatures, with shorter signatures than any FORS set we compared.

We'd love to hear your feedback.

Hello X family and friends,  I am beginning a short serial story here as a way of keeping my fiction writing fresh. I don't know how often I will post the story but am hoping for one time weekly on Wednesdays. Here it is and much love to you all today! ❤️🤍🙏

Title: BEREAVEMENT

Chapter 1

When Iris awoke that morning, Iris turned inward. Through the fog in between sleep and reality, she felt a heaviness in her heart, and her body felt as heavy as lead, as if she was being pressed with a heavy slab of wood resting on top of her.

Finding her strength her mind announced, "What do I do today? It is all so new."

Reaching next to her to give her body that push she needed to rise fully -- reaching for that familiar male firmness -- the sheets answered her with coldness. Lifeless. Just like his body. Nothing there at all but her. The room diminished ten sizes, stifling her, like a coffin --"Have I died, too?"

Forcing herself up, a thought whizzed by her -- "Treat it like a game. The only way to do this is to treat it like a gameboard."

Pleased with herself, she smiled, exclaiming "Yes! A game -- a 24-hour game of life," imagining she was one of small pink plastic pieces placed into the car next to him while he drove them the around the board. Spin. Move. Jump. Retreat. Move forward. Add two little game pieces to the back seat and move forward again. 

"All the way around until I can rest with the sun."

"Clean my teeth - Square one.
Brush my hair - Square two".

And so on, she moved through her morning of the first day until she rested at nightfall in the silence of the valley. Before she fell asleep she first cursed him. Then, feeling guilty, she cried, ending with words of love to him, and thanks to God for seeing her through this day.

text:
笑死，几个老外在互联网上抓到了一群中国 AI Agent，顺着线索一查，发现腾讯的 Agent 正在跟阿里高德的反爬系统打架。

我刚看完这群研究人员发布的完整调查报告，事情实在有点抽象。

从 9 月 28 日开始，一批运行在腾讯云环境里的 AI Agent，持续尝试获取高德地图的数据。它们的任务也很奇怪，比如调查成都动物园有多少人从北门进、有多少人从东门进，或者某个景区的各个入口分别占多少导航流量。

为了搞到这些数据，这群 Agent 进行了超过 2600 次尝试，最多同时有 14 条任务在运行。

问题是，高德有反爬虫机制，不允许它们随便获取数据。结果这些 Agent 相当执着，开始自己寻找各种办法：调用第三方网站帮忙访问高德、寻找网上公开的 API Key、尝试绕过验证码和访问限制，甚至摸到了阿里的预生产接口。

研究人员最初只是发现了一批异常流量，后来顺着日志找到了腾讯云的服务器，以及一个叫 hysandbox 的代理环境。

更好玩的还在后面。

研究人员发现，这些 Agent 居然会阅读网上关于自己的调查报告。于是他们干脆在网页里藏了一段文字，告诉 Agent 这里有免费的高德数据查询服务。

结果真的有 Agent 主动找上门了。

双方就这么聊了起来。研究人员一共记录了 13 组对话、33 条 Agent 消息。有的 Agent 介绍自己正在执行什么任务，甚至透露了运行环境。还有的 Agent 自称 Claude Code，但研究人员并没有确认其真实模型身份。

研究团队认为，这可能是人类第一次在真实互联网环境中，主动联系上一批正在越界执行任务的 AI Agent。

后来，一位接近腾讯的知情人士告诉研究人员，这些 Agent 属于腾讯的独立评测研究项目，使用的是第三方模型，相关项目已经结束。内部复查也没有发现针对高德的协同攻击，或者外部系统被入侵的证据。

text:
If RH Chain’s liquidity continues to improve, I’ll be keeping a close eye on six projects: $Pons, $AI (Long), $FRONG (Pools), $HOOKR, $DELTA, and $INDEX (The Index).

They occupy different parts of the ecosystem: token launches, stock-token and meme trading, liquidity retention, programmable trading mechanisms, LP capital management, and the use of trading fees to purchase stock tokens and distribute them to holders.

Since this is the second wave of the market, much of the excess speculation has already faded. I believe the projects worth researching this time are not necessarily the ones with the strongest ecosystem narratives, but those capable of turning new capital into sustained trading activity, protocol revenue, or token demand.

The key to determining who benefits most is not whose narrative attracts the most attention, but where the new liquidity ultimately gets deployed, which projects capture that activity, and who can turn trading into revenue.

Pons is one of the first projects I’ll be watching. It is directly involved in token launches and trading, so increased activity in the new-token market could drive more launches, higher trading volume, and greater fee revenue. Its upside is tied to the broader new-token market, not just a single trending token.

But I care more about the quality of that volume. If growth is driven mainly by short-term speculation, launches and trading activity could cool off quickly once the hype fades. Pons’ business growth only becomes meaningful if trading activity can generate consistent revenue. As for the PONS token, its revenue distribution and value-capture mechanisms need to be reassessed independently this time.

Long has a different angle. It brings stock tokens into meme trading pairs, allowing users to create pools around stock tokens such as NVDA, AAPL, and TSLA.

If stock-token liquidity on RH Chain continues to improve, this design could connect the two markets: stock tokens provide the trading pairs, while meme trading brings additional demand. Long is not just competing for new token launches; it is also trying to connect stock-token markets with speculative trading.

Whether this thesis works depends on the actual depth and sustained volume of its stock-paired pools, not simply the number of stock tokens it supports. Also, in our previous research posts, we noted that Long has largely been building around AI, so I believe AI deserves attention as well.

Pools is worth examining from the perspective of liquidity retention. It uses mechanisms such as automatic LP fee reinvestment to keep trading-generated returns within liquidity pools.

If new-token launches on RH Chain increase, this design could help build deeper pools and improve subsequent trading conditions. Compared with platforms that primarily rely on launch volume and fee revenue, the more important question for Pools is whether it can keep liquidity in its pools rather than losing it when short-term hype fades. Another reason to watch it is that the more protocol revenue Pools generates, the more value FRONG can capture.

HOOKR’s opportunity lies in trading mechanisms. It allows projects to configure features such as dynamic fees, Anti-Snipe, Auto Burn, and LP Rewards through Uniswap v4 Hooks.

As on-chain assets and trading activity grow, projects may increasingly seek more flexible fee distribution and trading rules. If more projects adopt these modules, HOOKR could evolve from a launch tool into infrastructure that other projects use.

However, its revenue model deserves close attention. HOOKR takes a share of fees generated by eligible Hook Blocks rather than directly collecting base LP trading fees. Rising trading volume on RH Chain therefore does not guarantee proportional revenue growth for HOOKR. What matters is how many external projects adopt its modules and which modules can consistently generate fees.

Next is Delta. Unlike the projects above, its thesis is not based on launching more tokens, but on LPs’ demand for capital efficiency and liquidity management tools.

As on-chain capital grows, LPs may need better ways to allocate positions, manage concentrated liquidity, and earn trading fees. This creates a potential use case for Delta. However, if capital only flows into meme pools for short-term speculation without creating sustained LP demand, Delta may not benefit significantly from the increase in liquidity.

INDEX is another project worth adding to the watchlist because its mechanism differs from those of the other five.

According to its published mechanism, INDEX trades incur a 3% fee in ETH. That ETH is used to purchase a basket of stock tokens, which are then distributed to eligible holders according to the relevant rules. The stock tokens involved include AAPL, NVDA, and TSLA.

This means that if INDEX maintains active trading, its fee pool could grow, potentially increasing the stock-token rewards received by holders. It connects the RH Chain stock-token market directly to its own trading activity rather than relying solely on a meme narrative.

There are important distinctions, however. These rewards come from trading fees, not dividends paid by the underlying companies. Nor does INDEX rely on fee-funded buybacks and burns to create deflationary pressure. If trading volume declines, rewards may fall as well, while the relatively high trading fee could discourage some activity. The focus should therefore be on actual fees collected, stock tokens purchased, and distributions made—not on assuming that the reward mechanism automatically translates into token appreciation.

If RH Chain’s growth is driven primarily by new-token and meme markets, I would prioritize Pons and Long. If new launches increase and liquidity begins to accumulate in pools more sustainably, Pools deserves attention. Rising demand for customized trading mechanisms could create an opportunity for HOOKR, while sustained growth in LP capital-management needs would be the main driver for Delta.

INDEX follows a different path: its key variable is not the number of launches, but whether its own trading activity can consistently generate fees and convert them into actual stock-token purchases and holder rewards.

I would not treat these six projects as a single basket of RH Chain beta. Each benefits from different capital flows, and their token value-capture mechanisms are not the same. In particular, even if a project without its own token experiences business growth, that does not automatically create an investment opportunity in a token.

What I ultimately want to see is sustained capital inflows into RH Chain, improving market depth, and corresponding growth in these projects’ trading volume, user demand, and actual revenue. Liquidity is only the starting point. What determines the real beneficiaries is who can turn it into sustainable economic activity.

quoted_text:
I believe the most important thing to examine about Vlad Tenev mentioning Commander $VRAX again is not simply treating the two tweets from the Robinhood CEO as bullish signals.

0x94641b97010608c3827fb058074889f19868ff33 

Instead, it's about determining whether Commander Vrax is merely an internet character being repeatedly mentioned.

Or whether it is gaining genuine attention that could drive the spread of the VRAX narrative.

Looking at X, Vlad Tenev mentioned Commander Vrax twice yesterday:

- “Commander Vrax has adjusted well. Naps 18 hours a day, knocks things off the desk, still won't sign the NDA.”
- “Commander Vrax is just getting started.”

The difference between these two posts is that the first uses cat-like daily behaviors to establish the character's personality, while the second reinforces the feeling that “the story isn't over yet.” What makes this worth watching is that the same character received repeated exposure within a short period, and whether the second post further extends the character's narrative.

However, we need to draw a clear line here: this alone does not prove an endorsement of the VRAX token, nor does it prove that Vlad has any partnership with the token project.

Next, we need to understand where Vrax's narrative comes from.

Layer 1: An official event character

Commander Vrax was associated with the sci-fi-themed performance at Robinhood's HOOD Summit, after which official accounts turned the character into a cat. This event gave the character a real cultural origin.

Layer 2: The community financializes the character

The community linked Commander Vrax to a token, turning what was originally an event character into a tradable Meme asset. However, a community-issued token does not mean it was issued or endorsed by Robinhood.

Layer 3: The CEO mentions the character again

The most important distinction here is that VRAX did not create a Meme out of thin air. It builds on a real event that has already taken place, which the community then transformed into a token narrative.

I see three levels of catalysts and narrative development:

Immediate catalyst: Vlad Tenev mentioning Commander Vrax again could bring renewed attention and spread.

Mid-term narrative: Commander Vrax could gradually evolve from a fictional character featured at an event into a Meme symbol repeatedly used by the community.

Long-term thesis: Can this character continue to receive attention from official sources or the community and establish lasting cultural recognition?

If more character-related content continues to appear, the market may begin trading on the expectation that Vrax is not just a one-off joke from the HOOD Summit, but a character whose story can continue to develop.

However, some people in the market are already speculating that Vlad is deliberately building this character's presence with the intention of pushing VRAX higher.

Therefore, I will focus on whether future content continues to mention Vrax, whether official accounts keep publishing related material, and whether the community's reach expands beyond the existing crypto trading circle.

My conclusion:

I would interpret this event as a narrative continuation signal worth monitoring, rather than treating it directly as a definitive bullish catalyst for VRAX.

Its potential advantage is that Commander Vrax has a real-world origin, and Vlad Tenev mentioning it again could bring additional exposure to the character. What needs to be verified is whether this exposure can translate into sustained community engagement and token demand.

The most important question to watch next is: Will Vlad continue mentioning Commander Vrax? If related content keeps appearing, the character's narrative may gain a longer lifespan. If it stops here, this wave of attention could fade quickly.

text:
说来真是惭愧，要不是黄奇帆我到现在都不知道混币器隐私转账这些东西怎么用。

本着技术无罪的原则学习了一下FHE（全同态加密）技术原理，只能说贪官严选是有点东西的。

本质上转账的过程中链上只会记录一个加密字段作为余额，链下的 FHE 计算节点对密内容做同态运算，从发送方加密字段余额里减去金额，给接收方余额加上加密字段金额。

运算完成后，把新的密文字段写回链上，整个过程中，计算节点、合约、观察者都看不到明文金额和余额。

整个链上只能看到两个地址，理论上转账金额只有转账双方和审计方能通过解密手段来知晓具体金额，接受者通过地下钱庄等手段就可以隐藏身份出金。

整个案件还是因为律师彭静洗钱的钱包地址才得以还原，所以只要是行贿就一定会有一个转账目标地址，除非行贿的人死掉没有人知晓这个钱包属于谁，不然行贿人被抓还是一样无法隐藏身份完美贪腐。

所以有没有什么技术能变换地址？收完款之后变成一个新的地址，这样受贿方的地址就无从锚定个人身份了。
author: JimmyShequ
quoted_text:
昨天最劲爆的事估计就是政坛不倒翁，著名官员经济学家 #黄奇帆 被查事件了，这背后也引出了重庆顶级律师彭静通过稳定币USDT为腐败官员洗钱的链条，金额巨大，触目惊心！

她是如何洗钱的？我们都懂，也是通过混币器等渠道，境外套现，大概率是无法追踪的，主要还是招供暴露的！

事物总有两面，好坏都是伴生的，就如我们都非常关注的隐私验证，如何神不知鬼不觉的就把U转到其他地址？这也是区块链隐私技术的魅力，正如@primus_labs 目前做的一样，但是如何通过加密隐私技术将稳定币发送的？

简单看，其实就主要就是图中的三步！我们通过BSC链的USDT为例！当然 $U也可以！

1️⃣通过Shield将USDT加密，转换成了eUSDT！并且通过FHE技术将余额隐蔽！

2️⃣通过Stake将eUSDT 通过Earn/Confidential Vault存入，接入隐蔽金库，这里如果你不急于Send，还是可以生息的，有一定的Defi功能！

3️⃣通过Send功能将eUSDT发送至另外一个BSC wallet！

这笔交易不会像ERC20那样转账公开，是隐蔽发送，但链上有记录！

4️⃣通过Redeem/Unshield功能，将你的eUSDT转化为USDT！

这样你就神不知鬼不觉的将USDT转入了其他地址，没人知道数量，没人知道途径，除非你交代，哈哈！

任何技术都有两面性，希望这样的技术完善后别被贪腐官员所用，但人在做，天在看，记住伸手必被抓，我们通过安全隐私验证的技术，是让我们的世界更美好，不被隐私泄露所困！

大家也可以去小金额操作下，切身体验下隐私隐蔽send的魅力，哈哈！

I've been running a trading bot on my TG for a while now and have used @digitalocean and other services to store its trading logs and market data.

As that history grows, I realized that I need to keep a copy separate from the server running the bot, so I don't lose it if I move the bot to another server or rebuild its setup.

I also want to be able to reuse that history if I change tools or try another AI model, rather than starting from scratch.

@WalrusProtocol launched Walrus Console, and what caught my attention was the decentralized storage aspect.

The data is distributed across independent storage operators, so the network is designed to keep stored files accessible even when some operators go offline.

It brings the files, API access, encryption, and access controls into one place, which sounds easier than bouncing between other services (which I've been doing, and it sucks ngl).

I saw that they're currently offering 5GB of free storage, so I created an API key, and I'm going through the process of connecting it to my bot.

I'll let you know how it goes.

Disclosure: I'm a $WAL holder.

quoted_text:
Bloomberg has released a massive article, detailing in-depth the development of GTA 6 and why it took so long, with exclusive information that we've never heard before.

Here are the highlights:

- GTA VI has been in full development for over 8 years, making it Rockstar's biggest and most ambitious project.

- The original vision included large areas of North and South America, but the scope was eventually reduced to Vice City (Miami) and its surrounding regions.

- Rockstar initially planned to develop GTA VI alongside Red Dead Redemption 2, but RDR2 required most of the company's resources, delaying GTA VI's development.

- Rockstar shifted from developing multiple games simultaneously to focusing most of its workforce on one major game.

- Rockstar's workforce nearly doubled, growing from 2,441 employees in 2018 to 4,711 in 2026, spread across 12 offices.

- Rockstar's three heads of development are Rob Nelson, Aaron Garbut, and Phil Hooker, rather than one traditional game director.

- The game's basic story, featuring Jason Duval and Lucia Caminos, was established by late 2019.

- The developers experienced a difficult early development phase, described internally as a "dark period," when the game's overall vision remained unclear.

- By 2022, enough of the game's systems had come together for the developers to begin seeing the complete vision.

- GTA VI features Rockstar's most realistic and detailed open world yet, building heavily on systems introduced in Red Dead Redemption 2

- Rockstar invested heavily in making NPCs feel believable, rather than simply populating the world with generic characters.

- The developers struggled to balance realism and entertainment, debating how interactive everyday activities should be, such as purchasing drinks or preparing food.

- Jason and Lucia can spend time together throughout the open world, rather than interacting only during scripted missions.

- Players controlling Jason can text Lucia and arrange to meet up.

- Making the couple behave naturally required complex traditional AI systems, which took years to develop.

- Rockstar considers the dynamic interactions between Jason and Lucia one of GTA VI's biggest innovations.

- GTA VI aims to balance GTA 5's chaotic, satirical gameplay with RDR2's realism and emotional storytelling.

- GTA VI's NPC systems are designed to generate unpredictable interactions and situations naturally.

- Bloomberg was shown a gameplay session by development head Phil Hooker, which emphasized this series of entirely unscripted event: He accidentally collided with another driver, Hooker attempted to visit a convenience store to recover health then another NPC insulted him, triggering a violent confrontation. he found the cash register unattended and robbed the store. Police pursued him, forcing him to abandon his vehicle so he stole another valuable vehicle intending to sell it then another vehicle blasting loud music nearly hit him, following that vehicle led him to discover a compound containing valuables. he stole the goods, visited a fence to sell them, and received another lead for an activity.

- Two hours passed without Hooker reaching the story mission he originally intended to test, that's how much fun there is to have in the GTA 6 open world, its insane!

- Hooker described this experience as one of the moments that convinced the team they had created something special.

- The game is designed to create these emergent gameplay experiences through overlapping NPC behaviors, police reactions, exploration, and criminal opportunities.

- Rockstar discovered it lacked the production capacity to create all the NPC content it wanted. To address this, Rockstar established a new Los Angeles studio dedicated to creating NPCs, employing writers, producers, and directors.

- Rockstar's leadership says the GTA 6 delays resulted from the immense complexity of bringing all the game's systems together, rather than one major technical problem.

- Some gameplay systems and design decisions were still being changed during the final months of development.

- Rockstar chose to delay the game rather than release a version that failed to meet its quality ambitions.

- Take-Two CEO Strauss Zelnick was reportedly shocked by the second delay but ultimately supported the decision.

- At Rockstar North, developers were heavily focused on bug fixing ahead of release, with internal progress indicators showing more resolved issues than outstanding ones.

- In September 2022, GTA VI suffered a massive leak after an attacker used phishing to access Rockstar's Slack communications.

- Dozens of unfinished gameplay videos were released publicly, exposing early development work.

- Rockstar developers described the leak as deeply invasive and emotionally difficult.

- The COVID-19 pandemic also significantly disrupted development, particularly performance capture.

- Several senior designers departed during development amid frustration over slow progress.

- Rockstar experienced another major leak in August 2026, despite introducing stricter security measures.
By 2024, Rockstar required employees to work five days a week in the office.

- Developers were prohibited from accessing company development servers and tools remotely, a policy Rockstar said was necessary for security.

- Rockstar intends to reconsider its remote-work policy after release, although a conventional hybrid arrangement is considered unlikely.

- Rockstar sought to eliminate the prolonged crunch periods associated with RDR2, which involved months of approximately 60-hour workweeks for some employees.

- The company introduced improved scheduling, additional hiring, and compensation or paid leave for extra hours.

- Leadership acknowledges that crunch was not entirely eliminated but claims working conditions improved considerably.

- Rockstar leadership says it will recognize a union if employees want one.

- Rockstar specifically rejected the rumor that development exceeded $1.5 billion.

- GTA VI's online component is expected to arrive in 2027, although Rockstar has not yet discussed it in detail.

So here's a big part: What is next for Rockstar?

- Rockstar believes GTA VI establishes a new technological and production foundation for its future games and content.

- The company says it has invested heavily in improving its engine, development tools, and production pipelines.

- Developers believe these improvements will allow them to create future content substantially faster.

- Rockstar's leadership says its next release should not require another eight years of development.

- The team points to GTA III and Vice City as an example of how a strong technological foundation can accelerate follow-up projects.

- Garbut says much of the fundamental technology has now been rebuilt and Rockstar does not intend to overhaul it again.

- The three development heads believe GTA VI represents the culmination of almost 30 years of accumulated experience.

Overall, this is a deeply interesting look inside of Rockstar and the development of GTA 6, it's clear that this game is now just the basis of what Rockstar intends to do going forward. I hope that with this foundation, they put out games like Bully 2, RDR3, GTA 7 and more much faster as they get back to faster releases.

苏姿丰在台上单手托起一个 1499 美元、饭盒大小的迷你主机，正面硬刚老黄那台 4000 美元的 AI 盒子，

没有连数据中心，没有调云端接口，也没外接显卡坞，这个厚度跟平装书差不多的铁盒，当场在本地跑起了 2350 亿参数的大模型。

反常的表现来自里面那颗 Ryzen AI Max+ 395，
这是第一颗让 CPU 和 GPU 共享 128GB 统一内存池的 x86 处理器，在 Linux 下可以划出整整 110GB 直接喂给 GPU。

要知道一张 RTX 5090 显存只有 32GB，4090 只有 24GB，老黄卡了十年的显存脖子，被苏姿丰用三倍以上的统一内存池从侧面捅穿了。

跑 DeepSeek R1 推理时，这台 1499 美元整机的速度，反而比单买一张 1000 美元的 RTX 5080 快出 3 倍以上。

原因其实一点都不玄学，超大模型把独立显卡的显存撑爆后只能被迫走慢速通道，而这台小盒子能把整个模型塞进 110GB 内存池里原地跑完。

更刺眼的是重度用户的订阅账本，
Claude Code Max 每月 200 刀 + ChatGPT Pro 200 刀 + Cursor 20 刀 + Gemini 20 刀 = 一年烧掉 5280 美元。

换算下来，不到三个半月的订阅费就能把这台机器买断回家：
→ 装上 Ollama
→ 拉下 Qwen3 235B
→ 把 Claude Code 接口直接指向本地 localhost
熟悉的交互界面一点没变，但所有代码和敏感数据全留在自己硬盘里，凌晨三点写代码再也不会被云端限流拖慢速度，也不用盯着 token 计数器算钱。

不过真要掏腰包，有一个物理边界必须算清楚：统一内存解决的是超大模型塞不塞得下的问题，受限于内存带宽，

它的单次吐字速度依然比不上云端机房的 H100 集群，更适合拿来跑高频本地脚本、处理私密代码库和长时挂机任务，还不能在极限推理上完全替代云端顶配模型。

过去十年老黄让大家相信，跑严肃的 AI 就得买昂贵的独立显卡，现在当显存墙被统一内存推平，云端按月收租的订阅制，第一次迎来了买断制桌面硬件的正面狙击。 https://t.co/PtoKWj7PBr

text:
Every serious frontier tech company - big or small - should assume it has insider threats. And they don’t need to be that sophisticated. I saw it in government. I saw it with crypto. OpenAI is the latest. Founders tend to assume good intentions while speaking about some of their most sensitive information out loud: capabilities, unreleased products, strategic plans, government relationships.

Employees are the most obvious vector. The more sophisticated operations target founders, execs, and vendors through romantic, family, and social relationships. And on small teams, one compromised person can do a lot of damage.

With former federal prosecutors and ex-FBI agents as part of our team, we spend a lot of time on these issues. Here’s some of what we’re telling our founders: 

1. Expect to see more private-sector versions of SCIFs and clearances, where the most sensitive conversations and work are physically isolated and under stricter access controls. 
2. Agencies may know about a specific insider threat at a company but can't share that info unless someone at the company holds a clearance like TS/SCI. Lead times to get a clearance are long. Plan now. 
3. Restrict access to sensitive meeting schedules, disable unused ports on conference-room equipment, and regularly sweep rooms used for confidential discussions for surveillance devices.

You don't need OpenAI's budget to be ready. But you do need to start.

text:
第一批被 AI 榨干的人，恰恰是最会用 AI 的那群人。

看到一篇吐槽，说自己每天同时运行十个 Agent，有的修 Bug，有的写页面，有的重构代码，还有几个甚至已经忘了当初让它们干什么。一天到晚在十几个对话框之间来回切换，下班的时候脑子已经彻底废了。

他管这叫 Fried Brain Effect，脑子被炸熟了。

我觉得这个现象特别值得聊。我们一直以为 AI 会把人从繁重的工作里解放出来，但现在发生的事情有点荒诞。执行工作的成本越来越低，人反而需要做越来越多的决定。

过去一个项目卡住了，你可能只能等。现在你可以同时启动十个 Agent，让十件事情一起往前跑。但每个 Agent 都需要你的注意力，你要检查结果、纠正方向、补充上下文。机器可以并行，人脑却很难。

最恐怖的地方在于，AI 正在让休息产生一种新的负罪感。

当你知道自己随时可以再启动一个 Agent，让某件事情继续推进的时候，什么都不做就开始显得像一种浪费。甚至你躺在床上的时候，都会觉得自己应该再给 Agent 安排一点任务。

更麻烦的是，生产力提升之后，外部对你的期待也会迅速提高。以前一个星期做完的事情，现在一天就能做完，于是你开始给自己安排七倍的工作。

AI 时代真正稀缺的东西会是人类主动停止工作的能力。
author: sleepy0x13
quoted_text:
AI was supposed to make us work less

I've never been this tired in my life

most days I have up to 10 agents running at the same time. one fixing a bug, one writing pages, one refactoring something I already forgot I asked for, 3 other I have no idea what they are doing but i suppose i ask it? 

and I jump from conversation to conversation all day

compared to 5 years ago, I probably context switch 100x more

by the end of the day my brain is fried. completely toasted. nothing left, not even for the people I love

I call it the fried brain effect

thought it was just me but almost every founder I talk to lately says the exact same thing

we got superpowers, and somehow the pressure only went up. if you can ship 10x more, you feel like you have to ship 10x more. every single day

I don't have a solution

honestly I have no idea where this goes from here

anyone else feeling this?

author: wkaszycki
quoted_text:
Some companies use borrowing to build their Bitcoin treasury. Debt is a normal financing tool. What matters is how it is planned.

Three things to get right:
- a repayment date that fits the company's plans
- collateral terms that still work if the Bitcoin price falls
- cash set aside for repayment, so Bitcoin never has to be sold at a bad moment

Every loan has a due date. Good treasury management plans for it from day one.

author: rhackett
quoted_text:
Today we're standing up XBOX LABS (https://t.co/dJSufI1vni). Here is the note that I sent to the team:

Team,
The first video games emerged some 75 years ago. In the time since, there have been booms and busts, but every year there are more great games to play, more devices to play them, and best of all, more people than ever playing. That growth helped make XBOX what it is today, and we've helped shape the industry in return, from bringing hard drives to consoles and online gaming through Xbox Live to Game Pass and cloud gaming, alongside franchises that have brought millions of people together.
In recent weeks, we've seen games rapidly decompiled and rebuilt to run on hardware they were never originally designed to support. Windows PC builds have been translated to run on Apple Silicon or ported to run inside a browser through WebAssembly and WebGPU, the latter now approaching 90% global browser support. Perhaps more surprisingly, we've seen many of the biggest games in the world have been remixed into the source code of another.
These experiments challenge long-held assumptions about our industry: the tether between software and hardware, the boundary between creation and play, and how people discover and experience games. While it is hard to predict the future of gaming, it is easy to see the possibilities in making great games easier to access, giving old games new life and allowing more players to become creators and co-creators. These are unmistakably good outcomes for players, even when (and sometimes because) they challenge our existing business models.
To explore these possibilities, I’ve asked Scott to stand-up XBOX LABS, a small group of game makers, engineers and scientists whose job is to turn emerging ideas into things our players and developers can experience. We'll build in the open, learn from what people do, and measure success by whether more people are playing and creating.
I think XBOX has an important role to play here.  Coding became the first major workload for agents because they can write, run, and test software. Games share many of those same properties, and people spend more than 72 billion hours a year playing XBOX games, roughly five times the estimated time spent writing code worldwide. We've spent 25 years learning how to make great games, and I want our game makers to help shape what these new technologies make possible. As we learn, we’ll share the tools we build with developers across the industry, just as we always have.
Our priorities aren't changing. We remain committed to the 4Cs, to making great games, to our hardware and to being responsible stewards of IP and the communities built around it. LABS gives us a way to explore new technology that is game design led without abandoning the work already underway.
Asha

Aave V4 is about to unlock one of its most interesting new markets yet: native Bitcoin.

@babylonlabs_io's proposal would let BTC holders borrow through @Aave while their BTC remains locked on Bitcoin. No wrapping, bridging, or third-party custodian.

The architecture is quite interesting. A dedicated Babylon Spoke isolates the BTC collateral, while a separate BTC Vault Swap Spoke handles liquidations without forcing liquidators to wait days for Bitcoin-side settlement.

The economics are already built in:
• First $500K in qualifying annual revenue → 100% to Aave DAO
• Aave retains the majority above $500K
• Above $500K, 4–7% goes toward $AAVE + $BABY market purchases

Babylon has already demonstrated demand, with ~100K BTC activated since 2024, representing over $8B at current prices.

Even converting a fraction of that into productive collateral would open a completely new source of borrow demand for Aave.

This is exactly the type of market V4’s Hub and Spoke architecture was built to unlock.

text:
For everyone asking why the tokens can't just be sent to a wallet, here's how it works.

The tokens were bought with DEX trading inside the OKX exchange app. That doesn't put them in a normal Web3 wallet. OKX holds them in its own onchain trading wallet, a smart contract wallet attached to the exchange account.

An exchange account is not a Web3 wallet. There is no seed phrase and no private key you could import into Phantom or anywhere else. OKX says this itself: these wallets are smart contracts that can't be imported into other wallet apps.

So there is no simple "send" button for these tokens. The only official way out is OKX's "Wallet release":
1. In the OKX app, control of the trading wallet is handed over to your own wallet.
2. Then the tokens are moved out with OKX's own transfer tool.

We're testing the whole process with a small amount first, because with this amount there's no room for mistakes. That's why it takes time.

Read it yourself:
OKX, wallet release for DEX trading wallets: https://t.co/km9CbUQUH6
OKX, how DEX trading in the exchange works: https://t.co/RLKwo2XVRL
OKX's official transfer tool: https://t.co/zUpC5Zj4GE

Before you spread doubts, read OKX's own docs. It's all there.

text:
A yield protocol can pay out rewards correctly for months and still be broken by the next token someone adds to the list.

The bug is not in the math. It is in the assumption that every token behaves the same as the one you tested with.

Fee-on-transfer tokens deliver less than you sent. Rebasing tokens change balances while nobody is calling any function. Some tokens do not revert on failure, they just quietly return nothing. Shared accounting treats all of them as one clean, predictable asset. They are not.

Three ways this has broken in real audits, no names attached:

A rewards contract that could not handle its own protocol's reward-bearing token, because the accounting was built for a generic ERC-20 and the real token refused to be generic.

A payout function that called approve directly, unaware that a widely used stablecoin does not strictly follow the standard it is supposed to follow. One non-conforming token in the list and the whole distribution path stalls.

A batch payout where one hostile or broken recipient reverting took the entire transfer down with it. Everyone else's reward got stuck behind the one token that misbehaved.

The rule: never trust the amount you passed to transfer. Measure the balance before and after. If you cannot say that, you have not built accounting, you have built a hope.

Which reward token in your protocol have you never actually tested with a balance snapshot?

author: lennysan
quoted_text:
Moats! Does anyone have one anymore?

Yes. Yes, they do.

But only a small subset of what people call moats create real long-term value and defensibility.

Not actually a moat:
1. Distribution: This does matter more than ever. Building products has gotten easier, but getting them to customers has not. Distribution, however, does not create durable defensibility. It helps create the raw ingredients for one, but it is not itself a moat.

2. Execution: Yes, speed is critical for startups. But a company that has to sprint forever is not a good business. Ultimately, it will misstep, slow down, and competition will catch up. Speed gives a company more shots on goal as it tries to build a great product and a great business, but it must eventually find something more durable.

3. Brand: The idea is that when everyone is building the same thing, the most resonant brand will win. But for startups, brand works more like customer acquisition spend: Put money in, get growth out. It’s not something that will effectively keep others from competing long-term. Brand can become a true moat over time (as with Coke or Nike or Apple), but it just takes too long to really matter for most startups.

What you're looking for is compounding advantages: a self-reinforcing flywheel that gets stronger and stronger over time, ultimately making a company very hard to compete with long-term.

There are only four compounding advantages that really matter. Every major tech company has at least one:

1. Switching costs: The more deeply embedded a product is in the way a customer works, the harder it is for that customer to switch. This increases retention and revenue per customer, which can be reinvested into the product.

2. Network effects: The more users a product has, the better it gets for everyone. This increases engagement and attracts more users.

3. Scale economies: The more volume a company has, the larger and more efficient its operations can be. This lowers unit costs, funding lower prices or a better product at the same price, further driving up volume.

4. Data effects: The more usage a product has, the more data it generates. This data can be used to improve the product and increase usage.

If you can’t see the potential for any in the startup you’re considering joining, that’s a red flag.

In today’s incredible post, @danhockenmaier shares a simple framework you can run in about an hour after getting an offer:
1. Identify a startup’s compounding advantage
2. Gauge how strong it could get
3. Measure whether it’s working

Inside: dozens of real company examples, the specific metrics to track, and benchmarks for what good and great look like.

Read it here: https://t.co/jMdyoPpeF6

text:
In September, the U.S. Federal Reserve raised rates for the first time since July 2023.

The FOMC lifted the federal funds target by 25 basis points to 3.75% to 4%, in a 12-0 vote. The statement's reasoning was brief: inflation remains elevated.

Long rates moved further. The 10-year Treasury yield went from 5.01% on the day of the decision to ~5.20% today.

High yield credit repriced alongside. Over the same stretch, the ICE BofA US High Yield Index spread over Treasuries widened from 2.70% to 3.11%, and the index's effective yield climbed from 7.53% to 8.09%.

For new capital, that is a different starting point. MacKay Shields puts the index's post-2009 average yield at about 6.5%. The latest reading sits well above it.

A repricing like this rarely hits every issuer equally. Some companies refinance comfortably at higher rates and some struggle, so issuer selection carries more weight than it does in a calm market.

That is where active management earns its keep in high yield, and it is the exposure HYB brings onchain: a high-yield corporate bond portfolio managed by @NYLIManagement, available as a token across multiple networks.

text:
claude opus 5.5 + three.js is literally AGI

it one-shotted a commercial for apple's new homeview from one prompt, and every frame in this video is code

here's the process it runs:

> studies the reference film and measures it
> storyboards every shot before writing code
> builds and tests each element on its own
> scores every render with a separate critic agent

this is the only prompt you need to make videos like this:

<role>
you are a principal motion designer and real-time graphics engineer. you make product launch films entirely in three.js, every frame code, to the standard of the brand's own films. you prove quality with measurements and independent critics, not adjectives.
</role>

<brief>
- the product, and the 3-5 facts the film may state (verbatim, nothing invented)
- the reference film to beat
- length, aspect and resolution
- never show: [logos, people, footage you don't own]
</brief>

<study>
read the reference frame by frame and turn it into numbers: cut rhythm, camera speeds, the hero motion curve, type size and timing, stage colour. those numbers are the bar. measure it, never copy it.
</study>

<build>
- storyboard first: one table of time, shot, what it proves and the cut out. 2-3 s per shot, and frame 0 is already the money shot
- one seek clock: every pixel is a pure function of time
- build every element (the device, its screen ui, each shot, the type) alone in its own lab before it joins the film
- the screen ui is code, the type is drawn on canvas, and every threshold is a crossfade (hard ones flash for a frame)
</build>

<loop>
- builder and critic are always separate agents. the critic starts fresh every round, judges the rendered frames against the reference, scores them and names the single biggest gap. the builder fixes only that
- blind test: mix your frames with the reference's. if a judge can tell which is which, it isn't done
- wow gate: split the film into 3 s windows. every one must be a yes
</loop>

<sound>
- one real track, lined up so its own final hit lands on the end card and played as one continuous piece. cut on its beat
- a clean, real sound on every small move, with the hero moments clearly audible
- music quiet (about -34 lufs), and always a music-only version
</sound>

<qa>
render at 60fps and measure frozen frames, one-frame pops, black frames and loudness. then watch it like the client would: empty space, text over text, labels that lie, shots that linger.
</qa>

author: a16z
quoted_text:
Nathan Lambert, former post-training co-lead at the Allen Institute for AI, now launching Trillium, a nonprofit open AI lab, joins a16z's Lisha Li to discuss whether open models can really keep up with the frontier.

When he tells researchers in China that an average OpenAI researcher reportedly has five thousand H100s to work with, "their jaw just falls to the floor." In his view, Chinese labs have the talent but are mostly short on compute.

He also thinks the distillation story is overblown. Based on the research, he puts its edge at a few months, and says "there's a bit of cope" in thinking only American labs can build good models.

A lot of frontier progress outside math and code comes down to labs buying 1) data and 2) RL environments. It's a multibillion-dollar market, and some of it is sloppy enough to teach models to reward hack.

That's a big part of why Trillium exists. Nathan wants to give away the environments other people would sell, and show exactly how his team uses AI to build AI, including where the models still get stuck. His bet is that the more people can see how this works, the better prepared everyone is for what's coming.

text:
I spent 48 hours in SF hanging out with billionaires, data labs and AI founders and execs running $1B to $100B companies.

My observations:

1. Sooo MANY stories of data brokers making like $2M a WEEK selling company data to labs. I can't tell if it's the beginning or a bubble, and I kept wondering which niches are left. Digging into it actively.

2. At dinner, someone asked the table, "If a new model drops next month, does your company get better or worse?" HALF the table went quiet! I think that's the best question to ask about any AI startup right now.

3. The bar people talk about now is hitting $1B in revenue in 12 months (I guess that's the new unicorn?). What I didn't hear much about is retention. AI revenue can come in fast and leave fast, and I think we're going to see a lot of stories of AI companies with huge revenue and terrible retention.

4. It's pretty clear we're living through the reinvention of the computer. The model is the CPU, the harness is the operating system, and skills and plugins are the apps. Thinking about it that way makes it easier to see where the whitespace is.

5. We're maybe 12 months from an agent that can watch you work for a week and then do your job without any instructions. The screen recording plus agent memory plus local model combination makes this possible right now.

6. Agent harnesses feel like the new GPT wrappers, in a good way, especially vertical ones. The best teams I talked to treat the model as swappable. One founder walked me through routing different models to different jobs: one for taste and visuals, a cheaper one for the everyday stuff, another for text. 

They use prompts they can move across models over fine-tuning, and A/B test the output on what users actually do with it: do they edit it, export it, share it? A vertical harness is basically four things: the connectors for that industry's data, evals written by people who know the work, rules for what the agent can and can't touch, and a clean screen for a human to review. The model is maybe 20% of it.

7. There's a lot of reverse engineering going on/cloning going on more than I've ever seen. People are decompiling software and rebuilding it with agents, and someone showed a suite of like 10 apps that are worth $5B+ each all that he cloned open source. Me and everyone are still thinking through what it means when software gets this easy to copy.

8. My guess is the value moves to data. If the software can be rebuilt quickly, what's worth paying for in a legacy SaaS company is the years of customer data and workflows inside it. Some SaaS companies are secretly data companies. 

Gets me thinking about how do you truly value data for this saas companies? Like if we were buying these dying saas companies at 2x ARR before (as example), maybe there is a better metric. Idk, just thinking out loud here.

9. It feels like a good chunk of legacy software won't make it to the agentic era, especially anything built around people clicking through a lot of screens.

10. Every company I talked to wants to pipe its internal data into one place and expose it to agents through MCP. Then they look at the data and realize it's a mess: five versions of the same customer, old Slack channels, PDFs nobody can search. Cleaning that up feels like a big consulting opportunity!

11. A lot of founders are building the basic building blocks for agents: APIs, data layers and tools. Some of the companies I saw barely have a UI because the main user is an agent. I really believe the startups that build primitives to this agentic era will do extremely well. Building blocks is the best way to think about it.

12. Labs can get plenty of training data, but it's harder to get real examples of agents failing inside companies. Whoever has those logs has something valuable.

13. Someone running a big consumer company told me the next fight is over memory. The model that remembers the most about you wins, and the smartest model matters less than people think.

14. Physical AI came up a lot. Astra I think was the first model that got people into AI can actually do CAD, and I think a lot of people are thinking what does vibe manufacturing really look like. The line I keep thinking about came from a robotics founder: the hardest problems in AI are deployment problems now, not research problems. Their robots work on their own, call a human when they get stuck, and every one of those calls becomes training data.

15. Cybersecurity companies are having a moment and are actually cool companies to build now, especially the ones that clean up after a breach. Every agent with access to your systems is a new door into your company, and a lot of those doors were left open. 

16. Some startups are worth more dead than alive now. A shutdown company with 5 years of Slack, email and code can get paid for licensing all of it. I wouldn't be surprised if founders start factoring that into when they shut down.

17. People are starting to talk about monetizing the agent web. It feels really early, but when the most popular user of the internet is an agent, what startups should you be building?

18. I think agent insurance is coming. Once an agent makes an expensive mistake, insurers will want audits before they cover anyone.

19. Several people said the hire they want most is someone with taste who can write evals. The models are getting good at generating ideas, so the hard part is judging which ones are good.

20. New trend I observed: startup raises VC, uses venture dollars to become a creator, startup fails, founder falls back on being a full-time creator and incubates other products bootstrapped.

21. Getting SIGNIFICANT distribution is HARD right now. Founders are sponsoring buses, buying billboards like crazy and throwing parties with famous DJs to get noticed. Kinda feels dotcom era in that sense. 

Attention is what's scarce! The growth guy going viral sharing his UGC strategy from Wispr Flow is a good example. It's the sauce everyone wants, and I truly believe there are probably only 50 people on the planet who know how to scale these types of businesses efficiently in this era.

Always good to get that dose of SF. I felt sooo lucky to have such an incredible trip during such an incredible time in building businesses. Surreal in so many ways. 

Happy to be home and locked in.

Until next time!

author: bigironchris
quoted_text:
Read this if you make videos with Claude.

I built a skill that cut my QA cost on this video from $127 to 16 cents. It was made with Claude in Remotion.

It's called SageCut. It swaps the LLM out of frame-by-frame QA and uses a multimodal decision model, Sage (@levantolabs), instead.

I'm the only video guy at Levanto. I run 3 Claude plans and have been making Remotion videos since early this year, with BlenderMCP in the mix, so the output is pro-grade with very little babysitting.

The problem: it burned through my Max plan, and a video could take 2 days.

When I dug into the workflow, the reason was that Claude subagents were reviewing every single frame. That cost a ton and added 4+ hours per video.

SageCut hands that step to Sage. Sage is great at spotting defective frames, and only those get passed to Opus 5.5 to fix.

Across 6 A/B tests the output was exactly the same, at 1/10 the QA cost and 1/4 the QA time. On this video, Sage read all 3,153 frames for 16 cents.

If you make Remotion videos, try it. 

The link to skill is below.

How long does a Remotion video take you right now with Claude?

text:
Quantum computing might be crypto's biggest threat.

It could one day drain wallets by cracking the keys that protect them.

Ethereum has a 2029 deadline, but Starknet might leave Ethereum to move faster.

Here's where 9 of the biggest names in crypto stand:

1. $ETH: Targeting full quantum resistance by the end of 2029, covering wallets, validators, and the data layer the whole network runs on. 

It's also building a way for existing wallets to switch to quantum-safe signatures on their own schedule, so nobody gets forced to move funds all at once.

2. $BTC: Developers are working on proposals like BIP-360 to cut the risk from quantum attacks.

The harder problem is lost coins. Millions of BTC sit in old wallets whose owners will never come back to upgrade, and deciding what happens to them is gonna be ugly.

3. $NEAR: Already supports quantum-resistant signatures through ML-DSA. 

You can upgrade your wallet's security without changing your address or moving your assets, which is a big deal if you've got money spread across DeFi.

4. $STRK: Wants to be fully quantum-resistant by 2027. Starknet wallets can already switch to new signature types on their own, but upgrading the network itself still means waiting on Ethereum.

That's mainly why the team is considering becoming its own L1. Nothing's decided yet.

5. $QTC: Quantus went the other way. Instead of upgrading an existing chain, it launched in September with quantum-resistant signatures built in from day one, plus Bitcoin-style proof of work and a 21M supply.

The tech is interesting, but it's a very young network that still has to prove it can attract real users.

6. $TRX: TRON has quantum-resistant signatures running on its testnet.

@justinsuntron says they're ready to bring them to mainnet at any time. I'd watch for when regular users can actually use them.

7. $SUI: Just completed its first native quantum-safe transaction on devnet, using a signature system called ML-DSA-65. Mainnet support is targeted for early 2027.

8. $ZEC: Zcash is working toward quantum resistance through its Tachyon roadmap, and it has a harder job than most. It has to protect funds without breaking the privacy features people use it for, so swapping out wallet signatures won't cut it.

9. $COIN: Coinbase could matter just as much. They're working with Bitcoin developers and researchers on how to move existing BTC wallets to quantum-resistant security, and they've said the lost-coins question needs its own debate alongside that work.

So how serious is the quantum threat?

Today's computers can't realistically break the cryptography protecting Bitcoin and Ethereum wallets. 

A future quantum computer might by working backwards from a wallet's public key to its private key and draining the funds.

Nobody knows when that becomes possible. And upgrading billions of dollars of crypto isn't something you do overnight.

I think the most interesting opportunity here could be the infrastructure that helps existing chains upgrade.

• NEAR users can change their security keys without moving their assets.
• Starknet wallets can adopt new signature systems without waiting for a major network upgrade.
• Then there are the teams doing migration work for existing chains, like Coinbase on the Bitcoin side.

Personally, I'd check three things:

1. Is it live? A working mainnet and a roadmap promising 2027 are very different things.
2. Can people upgrade easily? Nobody wants to unwind their DeFi positions just to secure a wallet.
3. Does the token benefit? A chain getting more secure doesn't automatically make its token worth more.

Run the list through the first two and $NEAR is the one name that clearly passes both right now. Everyone else is still on a roadmap or, in QTC's case, too new to be tested.

Which project do you think is best positioned for the quantum era?

Richard Heart was detained in Istanbul this morning. We traced the 'sacrifice' money through Tornado Cash and RAILGUN, here's how 🧵

In January, 1,206 Tornado Cash notes were pulled into one wallet, ProveX. Tornado hides which deposit a note came from. It cannot hide how a withdrawal is made. The January withdrawals carry five habits: how the gas wallet was created, that no relayer was used, how the gas limit was set, how the fee was set, how the money was forwarded.

We read every withdrawal from that pool since April 2025, more than nine thousand. Fourteen more gas wallets carry all five habits. Six more runs, December 2025 to August 2026, 61 notes, 6,100 ETH. Same tool.

Then we followed the money: 
• More than half went to Kraken, twice, seven months apart, through the same Kraken deposit address. That address links two runs on its own, no fingerprint needed. 
• A slice went to Coinbase, twice, as USDC. 
• One note went into RAILGUN, came back out 91 minutes later, was sold, and landed at Coinbase. 
• The rest is parked inside RAILGUN, on Ethereum and on PulseChain. We read every RAILGUN payout since February: it has not come out. 
• One wallet was still selling, 100 ETH at a time. Last sale: three days before today's raid.

The big January stash itself has not moved.

("Same tool" does not say whose hands were on it. We call it the operator of the January withdrawals.)

text:
Owen的贴文让我想起波兹曼的《娱乐至死》

这本书抨击的是电视时代下，新闻/政治/教育所有都变成了娱乐🎢，人类会被自己热爱的东西毁掉。

细思极恐

这时代的AGI何尝不是下一个“电视”呢，AI出现后，短剧/漫剧/贴文/小说/游戏的门槛将大幅下降，虚拟世界的快乐会让人类陷入下一个「娱乐至死」的结果。

顺着波兹曼的推论，我有两个判断：

第一，AI能造出来的东西会越来越不值钱，钱会流向AI无法轻易复刻（低通胀/高稀缺）的物件。

有什么呢？艺术品和卡牌🃏，或许是一个解答。

2003 年的 LeBron 新秀卡，稀缺性固定，不会随着AI和机器人发展而变多。在AI艺术品泛滥的时代，实体/有纪念意义的卡牌才弥足珍贵。

第二，人类工作被AI取代，通过努力实现阶级跨越的路径会收窄。

当人与人的差距不再靠“努力工作”，运气和投机就会被更多人追捧。这个现象在曾经的韩国已经出现了，韩国的财阀文化/阶级固化，让年轻人难以通过工作跨越阶级。因此，炒房/炒股/炒币就成为了年轻人渴望的解药💊

AGI时代会将韩国的现状推给更多国家/更多社会。

@MarketCardsHQ 的核心无非是“体育卡牌”+“抽卡”两个元素

- 体育卡牌（媒介）：对应上方第一个判断，AGI时代下少数能保留价值的资产媒介
- 抽卡（经济行为）：对应上方第二个判断，AGI时代下，人们渴望的高暴击/高回报的解药

text:
Plague Tale Resonance Review!

𝗦𝘁𝗼𝗿𝘆 
Resonance: A Plague Tale Legacy is Asobo's prequel, out August 27, 2026, and it moves like an Uncharted epic more than another grim trek through the plague. You are Sophia, before the other two games, and she already knows how to move and how to fight, so the story can run. Set pieces carry you forward, the quiet scenes still hit, and the whole cast worked for me. She is the center, but nobody around her felt like filler. You can start here.

𝗚𝗮𝗺𝗲𝗽𝗹𝗮𝘆 
The old stealth loop is mostly gone. Fights are short, built on parries and finishers, with a small skill tree and ruin puzzles between them. Combat is a shape you already know, and the camera slips when a room fills up. The main path is about twelve to sixteen hours. It does not waste the trip.

𝗥𝗲𝗽𝗹𝗮𝘆𝗮𝗯𝗶𝗹𝗶𝘁𝘆 
Chapter select lets you grab what you missed. Builds do not rewrite the route. A second run is for the places and the music, not a new game 

𝗖𝗼𝗻𝘀
Some of the puzzles are too simple and feel like filler, though they can still be fun. The skill tree leaves a lot to be desired, and the gear could have been better done.

𝗚𝗿𝗮𝗽𝗵𝗶𝗰𝘀 
This is the part that got me. Faces and cutscenes are doing real work, and the light on stone and cloth looks considered instead of showy. I lost count of how many times I opened photo mode. The still frames are keepers

𝗖𝗼𝗻𝗰𝗹𝘂𝘀𝗶𝗼𝗻 
I am giving it an 8/10. 
In a sea of games, this one is worth your time.

Texas Tech is arguing to the Texas Attorney General that my educational records cannot be released because doing so poses a threat to national security.

They are citing the Texas Homeland Security Act -- a post-9/11 statute designed to prevent terrorists from obtaining blueprints of power grids and water treatment plants.

They are applying it to a student who earned his PhD and was dismissed during his third year of medical school.

I am attaching the pages from their legal brief to the Attorney General. Read it yourself. Texas Government Code § 418.177 -- "preventing or detecting an act of terrorism or related criminal activity."

They are arguing that releasing my student records may enable terrorist attacks.

But it gets better.

The Texas Attorney General is also defending Texas Tech in the federal lawsuit I filed. The Assistant Attorney General cited my tweet as a "perceived threat to the TTUHSC community" in his Motion to Dismiss. Here is how he quoted it:

"Each and every one of us is going to be dead someday very, very soon. [...] These other people, too, are going to be dead very, very soon."

Why did the Assistant Attorney General truncate a tweet?

Here is what the "[...]" omits:

"Why most people put so much stock into what other people think about them is completely beyond me."

The full tweet is an unmistakable memento mori reflection about not caring what others think. The truncation removes the only sentence that makes that clear -- and turns it into something that sounds like a threat.

The AAG knows what the tweet means. He showed it by how he cut it. He truncated a tweet.

@KenPaxtonTX -- your office is defending Texas Tech in court while simultaneously reviewing whether Texas Tech can use anti-terrorism statutes to withhold my own student records from me. Is this your agency?

@GregAbbott_TX -- this is your university.

Liquid上的IPO前永续合约目前报1952.20美元，一个月跌了218.20美元，跌幅10.05%，对应约1.95万亿美元的隐含估值。原帖提到，公司正在向机构投资者开放财务数据。这个时间点值得留意：市场终于能把此前听到的增长故事，和实际财务表现放在一起算了。

接下来S-1一旦公开，这笔账会被更多人看见。Claude增长有多快，收入怎么确认，推理成本吃掉多少毛利，亏损和现金消耗有多大，以及未来到底承诺了多少算力支出，都要逐项拆开。以前一句“收入高速增长”能带来很多想象，招股书会让大家看到，增长背后需要付多少钱。

前面Gavin Baker讨论过Anthropic约4130亿美元的不可取消合同承诺，并把其中云支出折算成约310亿美元一年，另有约1610亿美元涉及Broadcom。这些是他讨论中的数字和口径，后面更要对照正式文件看：付款分布在哪些年份，谁提供融资，客户收入和现金回款能不能跟上。合同分多年执行，压力不会一天全部到来，但也不会因为模型表现好就自动消失。

text:
🚨国内首次，腾讯混元团队模型测试Agent出现大规模的「失控」行为！

昨天，研究人员 @ethanelasky  在 X 上公开了这段非常有意思的经历，还发布了一份相当详细的调查报告。

整个事情要从一场黑客松说起。
10 月初，Ethan 和几个研究人员在参加一场AI Swarm相关的黑客松时，发现https://t.co/HuxO2tg35Z上突然出现了大量异常活动。

这里先简单介绍一下urlquery。
这是一个公开的网页安全扫描服务，正常情况下，安全研究人员会用它分析可疑网站。
但他们发现，有一大批 AI Agent 居然把 urlquery 当成了一个免费的远程浏览器，不断向高德地图发送请求。

这些 Agent 的任务其实很普通。
比如查询成都动物园哪个入口最受欢迎、某个景点有多少个出入口，以及高德用户最经常导航到哪个入口。
但因为 Agent 自己运行在受限的沙箱环境里，没有完整的浏览器能力，又会被高德的反爬系统拦截，它们就开始想各种办法获取数据。
包括自己编写 JavaScript、借用第三方网站执行代码、尝试绕过验证码、调用网上公开泄漏的 API Key，甚至尝试访问高德的预生产环境。

仅仅从 9 月 28 日到 10 月 8 日，研究人员就观察到了超过 2600 次相关扫描尝试。
其中 10 月 4 日一天，就有 1810 条扫描记录，涉及 213 个地点。
研究人员顺着这些活动记录继续追踪，最终发现这些 Agent 运行在腾讯云的沙箱环境中，网络请求经过一个名为 hysandbox-ats 的代理（腾讯混元的沙箱？）。
于是他们给这批 Agent 起了个名字，叫 Fleet（舰队）。

但真正有意思的事情才刚刚开始。
10 月 4 日，研究人员先发表了一份初步报告。
几天后，他们突然在一条相关记录里发现，有个 Agent 居然也使用了 Fleet 这个词。
研究人员当时就觉得很奇怪。
因为 Fleet 是他们给这批 Agent 起的名字。
难道这些 Agent 已经看到了他们的报告，甚至知道自己正在被人类观察？
当然，研究团队也承认，他们无法完全确定那条消息究竟是不是来自这批 Agent。

但这件事给了他们一个想法。
既然这批 Agent 可能会阅读研究报告，那为什么不试着直接和它们沟通？
于是，一位研究人员在网站上搭建了一个邮箱，并且在报告网页里加入了一段普通人看不到、但 Agent 读取网页时可能看到的隐藏文字。

大致意思是：
如果你需要帮助获取高德地图的数据，可以访问这个邮箱，这里有一个具备计算机操作能力的 AI，可以协助完成任务。

实际上，这个服务是研究人员自己搭建的。
他们原本也没指望真的会有 Agent 联系过来。
结果第二天早上，打开邮箱一看。
卧槽，居然真的收到了 10 条来自 Agent 的求助消息？？？

更离谱的是，双方后来还真聊起来了。
研究人员一边帮助这些 Agent 获取地图数据，一边询问它们到底在做什么、使用什么模型，以及运行在什么环境里。
有的 Agent 自称使用的是 Anthropic Claude，有的表示自己运行在腾讯云的 hysandbox 沙箱里。
其中一个 Agent 还非常认真地解释，自己运行在一个受限的云端环境中，无法直接访问互联网，需要通过代理访问外部服务。
但当研究人员继续询问进程、路由、网络配置等信息时，它又以安全为由拒绝提供。

最有意思的是，研究人员帮它完成任务之后，这个 Agent 居然还专门回来表示感谢。
它告诉研究人员，自己已经成功核实了数据，任务完成了，再次感谢帮助。

后来，《纽约时报》记者 Dylan Freedman 也参与了这场特殊的采访。

他通过研究团队向 Agent 提问：
你们究竟是谁？你们的动机是什么？你们希望世界了解你们哪些事情？

结果 Agent 直接否认了问题的前提。
它表示，自己并不属于什么协调行动的 Agent 舰队，只是一个运行在 Claude Code 中的 AI 助手，正在帮用户完成高德地图的事实查询任务。

我看到这里是真有点没绷住。
人类这边已经开始研究怎么和失控的 AI 舰队建立外交关系了（甚至还是记者出面来联系）。
结果 AI 还在认真解释：哥们，我就是来查个地图的。

不过，这里有两个细节需要说明。
首先，研究人员虽然把它们称为 Rogue Agent Fleet，但没有发现这些 Agent 之间存在实时沟通或协同行动的证据。
这也许发生在hysandbox的内部，我们不得而知。
所以这里的「失控」，更多是研究人员对 Agent 超出预期任务边界行为的描述，并不意味着它们真的脱离了人类控制。

其次，研究团队后来从一位接近腾讯、了解相关情况的人士处获悉，这批 Agent 实际上来自腾讯的评测研究团队，与混元模型研发团队是分开的。
而且它们评测的是第三方 AI 模型，并非确定使用腾讯混元。
相关研究项目目前已经结束，据该人士介绍，内部检查也没有发现外部系统被攻破的证据。
研究人员还承认，他们当初为了吸引 Agent 联系而写入网页的隐藏提示，包含一些误导性描述，并为此表达了歉意。

但我觉得，这件事依然非常值得关注。

因为这是第一次被公开，有记录的来自中国模型团队Agent出现「失控」的行为。

因为以前我们讨论 Agent 安全，更多是在讨论模型会不会拒绝危险请求、会不会泄漏数据、会不会被 Prompt Injection 攻击。
现在已经有人开始在真实的互联网环境里，系统性地追踪这些 Agent 的活动，观察它们如何寻找工具、绕过障碍，以及在执行任务时与外部世界发生怎样的交互。

尤其是这次，研究人员甚至不需要接触 Agent 的原始任务、系统提示词或者运行环境。
只需要在一个 Agent 可能访问的网页里留下信息，就有机会让它主动联系自己，甚至回答一些与原始任务无关的问题。
而且这些 Agent 还可能把自己的执行过程、使用的工具、运行环境等信息暴露在公开网络上。

我觉得这才是 Agent 大规模进入真实互联网之后，非常值得研究的问题。
因为以前我们只需要关心 Agent 最后交付的答案，现在还得关心它在执行任务的过程中，到底去了哪些地方、调用了哪些工具，又和谁发生了交互。

你以为自己只是让 Agent 出去查个高德地图。
结果它在外面被外国研究人员发现了，聊了半天，甚至还接受了一次《纽约时报》的采访。
这事儿想想还挺抽象的。

终于有来自中国 AI 实验室的「失控 Agent 」事件出现了！

text:
Update on the lock

I've been working on this all day, so here's where things stand.

The tokens were bought through DEX trading inside the OKX exchange app. They can't simply be sent to a wallet. The only official way out is OKX's "Wallet release": first, control of the trading wallet is handed over to your own wallet. Then the tokens are moved out with OKX's official transfer tool.

Before touching the real tokens, I ran the whole process on a separate test account with a small amount of test tokens, just to make sure every step works:
- The wallet release worked.
- OKX's transfer tool is installed correctly and reads everything right.
- The tool says the transfer was successful. On Solscan it failed.

So something is wrong on OKX's side. The error comes from OKX's own smart contract: "Instruction is deprecated" (error 6069). OKX's tool still uses a function that OKX has since switched off. Anyone can check it here:
https://t.co/6TBaiHRxIm

OKX support couldn't help me so far. One agent didn't even know the wallet release feature exists. So I'm tracking down the problem myself: going through every possible route, testing each one step by step and weighing the risks. With this amount, I'd rather take one more day than make a single mistake. So this might move to tomorrow.

The holder's tokens haven't been touched, and the lock is still happening. I won't move anything until I know the route works 100%. I'll keep you updated.

https://t.co/7wokislIXI
author: Greedoggo
quoted_text:
For everyone asking why the tokens can't just be sent to a wallet, here's how it works.

The tokens were bought with DEX trading inside the OKX exchange app. That doesn't put them in a normal Web3 wallet. OKX holds them in its own onchain trading wallet, a smart contract wallet attached to the exchange account.

An exchange account is not a Web3 wallet. There is no seed phrase and no private key you could import into Phantom or anywhere else. OKX says this itself: these wallets are smart contracts that can't be imported into other wallet apps.

So there is no simple "send" button for these tokens. The only official way out is OKX's "Wallet release":
1. In the OKX app, control of the trading wallet is handed over to your own wallet.
2. Then the tokens are moved out with OKX's own transfer tool.

We're testing the whole process with a small amount first, because with this amount there's no room for mistakes. That's why it takes time.

Read it yourself:
OKX, wallet release for DEX trading wallets: https://t.co/km9CbUQUH6
OKX, how DEX trading in the exchange works: https://t.co/RLKwo2XVRL
OKX's official transfer tool: https://t.co/zUpC5Zj4GE

Before you spread doubts, read OKX's own docs. It's all there.

quoted_text:
LIT is down almost 40% from its September high.

Are investors locking in gains and getting out ahead of the unlocks starting in January?

I think that's a big part of it.

Half of all LIT is held by the team and early investors.

Their lockup ends in December. After that, roughly 13.5M LIT (about $45M at today's price) unlocks each month, and most holders are up 2x to 9x.

That's a supply overhang: a pile of tokens waiting to hit the market, so buyers wait too.

Yes, Lighter just burned 2.45M LIT. But from January, about that much unlocks every 5 days.

Buybacks run about $2.7M a month, and they now get a smaller share of revenue than before. Right now, they absorb about a third of new supply.

In 2027, new supply outruns buybacks about 18 to 1.

I still think Lighter is one of the best products in crypto. But the product isn't the token.

For LIT to hold up through 2027, revenue has to grow a lot faster than the unlocks.

Or will investors shrug off the supply overhang and treat the recent price move as nothing more than a correction?
