text:
Gacha is more profitable per wallet than perps, memecoins, or spot trading.

Why? Because the economics behind a gacha machine incentivize more turnover per dollar:

1. A user deposits $100 and buys a pack. The platform takes its fee on that $100.

2. A real card is revealed. The platform offers to buy it back instantly for about $90 in cash.

3. The user takes the $90 and buys another pack 10 seconds later. The platform takes its fee again on that $90.

4. Repeat until the money is gone.

A $100 deposit ends up generating $1,000 in pack sales.

Great breakdown by @lesabrefomo highly recommend reading to better understand @Collector_Crypt’s business model.

今天Anthropic IPO 前的投资者日。掌管 800 多亿美元的 GMO（格兰瑟姆创办的资管公司）说：戳破 AI 泡沫的，很可能就是这几家公司的上市。

他们的资产配置负责人 Ben Inker 今天上了播客，几个要点：

1. 上市怎么会戳破泡沫？
不在上市那一下：SpaceX 上市融了 750 亿美元，放在 75 万亿美元的美股里不算多。麻烦在之后一年，老股东陆续过了锁定期，SpaceX 另外价值约 2 万亿美元的股票都可以卖了。买的人得卖掉别的股票腾钱来接。Anthropic、OpenAI 上市后也一样。三家加起来，一年里涌进市场的新股相当于美股总市值的 6% 到 7.5%；历史上从没超过 4%，1999、2000 年也就 2.5% 到 4%。

2. 历史上发生过什么？
新股最多的三年是 1999、2000 和 2021，之后市场都不好过。他算的平均关系：每多 1% 的市值通过上市进来，大盘就比正常年份少涨约 4 个百分点，6% 就是少涨 24 个百分点。他也说，正常年份本来是涨的，这不等于一定崩盘。

3. 市场为什么接不住？
因为“涨了就卖”的人越来越少。指数基金不会因为你把价格推高就卖给你，英伟达两倍杠杆 ETF 也不会；被动投资从 80 年代不到一成，涨到现在大约一半。新股一多，价格得跌很多才找得到买家。

4. 最坏会怎样？
如果 AI 赚不到预期的钱，训练用的算力省下来，世界会从缺算力变成算力过剩：老显卡直接关掉，贷款违约，一些公司破产，云巨头的投资回报很差。他说那就不只是少涨，而是跌 35% 到 50%。他也说不确定会发生，但发生起来并不难。

5. 那现在买什么？
他们更愿意买美国以外的股票和价值股，也愿意多配资源股和高质量公司。他们持有韩国和台湾的股票，但比指数少一点，因为不认为那些利润能一直持续。

text:
One would think that because blobs are almost free, L2s should have no problem landing blobs.  But one interesting thing I learned from interviewing L2s is that they in fact have a lot of trouble landing blobs, EVEN WHEN there's no congestion.  I want to explain why, as that reveals some very interesting facts about the protocol.

Recall that blob pricing works similar to gas pricing (EIP-1559), where there's a "base fee" which goes up or down each block, depending on whether the previous block hit the target number of blobs (14 out of 21).  The idea is that in a well-functioning market, the base fee will track the "market price" of blobs, so that you can land blobs by just paying the base fee, with perhaps a little priority fee if there's congestion.

However, whereas this mechanism works well for regular gas, it turns out to be an issue for blobs, because blob demand is relatively inelastic to price.  In other words, just because the blob price is low does not mean that L2 will send more blobs -- they still need to fill those blobs with L2 transactions, which may have low demand even when L1 blob fees are low.

As a result, blob usage has been consistently below target, such that the blob price sat at 1 wei -- the theoretical minimum -- for a long time.  A later EIP raised the floor higher, but it's still so low as to be effectively free.

Why is this an issue?  Normally it's not.  People love free blobs!  But at times of congestion, because the base price starts so low, it takes a HUGE amount of time for the base price to rise enough to discover the true market price.  For example, if the base price is 1 gwei and the (hidden) market price is 40 gwei, it would take 47 consecutive full blocks (~10 minutes) for the base price to catch up.  By the time it catches up, the congestion may already be over.

So what do L2s do during congestion?  They bid with the priority fee, but without knowing what the true market clearing price is, they have to overbid in order to be sure that their blobs will be included.  This is precisely the unreliability / wastefulness that EIP-1559 was set out to fix in the first place!

But price instability is not the only reason why L2s have trouble landing blobs.  There's another more subtle and interesting reason -- MEV.

Blobs are large chunks of data, and as such they cost bandwidth to propagate.  Since bandwidth is a finite resource, everything being equal a block with blobs will take longer to propagate than a block without blobs.  This is an issue because a block builder only has a limited amount of time to propagate blocks before missing the attestation deadline, which would cause their block to be reorg-ed.  Therefore, block builders play a timing game where they wait as long as possible so they can pack the most valuable (high MEV) transactions into their block, but not waiting so long that they miss the attestation deadline.

Therefore, blobs have a hidden cost -- because they make blocks larger, builders who include blobs must send out their blocks sooner, causing them to miss out on some MEV.  As such, some builders refuse to include blobs EVEN WHEN there's no congestion in the blob market, so from the L2's perspective they just see their blob transactions being silently dropped, even though they appear to be paying adequate fees.  To truly ensure blob inclusion, the L2 would have to include a high-enough priority fee to compensate for the lost MEV from the builder, but once again this value is hidden and hard to discover.

In short, there are at least two forces against L2s landing blobs reliably:

- The blob price being so low that it kills price discovery and causes bidding wars during congestion.

- Blobs cause builders to lose MEV, so they ignore blobs unless priority fees are high enough to compensate for the MEV.

So what can we do to make blobs more reliable?  Good news is that things will already get better in Glamsterdam due to ePBS giving blobs more time to propagate, but more fixes are required if we want to completely fix these issues.  Thankfully many researchers including @fradamt @potuz_eth @barnabemonnot are already thinking about this -- I may talk about some of their ideas in a future post!

both generate real revenue, but their tokenomics and growth potential are quite different

so here's how I'm looking at them

that's attractive for users willing to lock their tokens
but there's a trade-off

I'm watching whether Aerodrome can keep growing organic liquidity while reducing reliance on incentives

the Aero / MetaDEX03 expansion is another potential catalyst

[2] @Uniswap – $UNI

latest 30D snapshot:

– $79.47B DEX volume
– $129.48M trading fees
– $10.14M protocol revenue
– ~$4.36B MC
– MC / annualized revenue ~35.8x

the UNI burn mechanism has changed how I evaluate this token

protocol fees now flow into TokenJar, with UNI burned through Firepit to release those assets

so higher protocol revenue can translate into more UNI being burned

Robinhood Chain is also becoming a major fee contributor

I see room for further growth as Uniswap expands fee capture across chains and V4 pools

[3] My long-term allocation

– 60% $UNI
– 40% $AERO

UNI gets the larger allocation because of its multi-chain reach, deeper liquidity and token burn mechanism

AERO offers a lower revenue multiple and potentially more upside from Base and Aero expansion, but emissions and lockup dynamics add risk

ofc, neither is risk-free, and reported protocol revenue ≠ net returns for token holders.

I'll keep tracking revenue growth, net token supply and whether actual usage continues to scale

quoted_text:
What’s really driving the $UNI rally right now?

Hazz, I still regret missing this one.

I knew @Uniswap was benefiting from the Robinhood Chain hype, but I didn’t pull the trigger.

Looking back, I think the market is repricing $UNI for 4 main reasons:

[1] Robinhood Chain is bringing massive volume to Uniswap

Uniswap has become one of the main liquidity venues on Robinhood Chain.

Robinhood alone contributed roughly $33B of Uniswap’s ~$81B 30D volume in the snapshot I was watching.

Robinhood hype → more users/assets onchain → more volume for Uniswap.

[2] v4 is proving that Hooks are getting real adoption

That same snapshot showed:

– v4: ~$42.9B
– v3: ~$36.8B

So v4 was already doing around 54% of combined v3 + v4 flow.

This matters because Hooks allow pools to customize swaps, fees, liquidity and accounting.

Uniswap is moving from a simple AMM design → more programmable liquidity infra.

[3] Volume now has a clearer path to $UNI value capture

This is probably the biggest change.

Protocol fees are now active across more chains, and part of those fees can eventually translate into UNI burn.

The flywheel becomes:

More markets → more volume → more fees → more UNI burned. 

That is very different from the old UNI thesis where the token was mainly viewed as governance.

[3] Robinhood may only be the first leg

Uniswap is also expanding into Arc and other markets tied to stablecoins, RWA and tokenized stocks.

If those sectors keep growing, Uniswap could benefit as the liquidity + execution layer behind them.

The lesson for me:

Don’t just look at which token is inside a hot narrative. Look at where the revenue actually flows.

I saw the Robinhood thesis, but missed $UNI.

Anyway, that move is gone.

If $UNI comes back to a price range I like, I’ll consider buying.

But not here. I’m not chasing after the pump.

quoted_text:
A new paper from Apple engineers ends with a line we couldn’t have written better ourselves:

"if idle macOS devices across organizations [...] can be securely federated, they could form a massive, shared GPU resource pool that benefits the broader ecosystem."

That’s what we’re building with Darkbloom.

The paper's Minions is a system that pool idle Apple Silicon Macs into a distributed GPU cloud for on-prem inference. Queue times went from 10+ hours to minutes. Zero new GPU purchases. Zero infrastructure cost.

It runs inside Apple, on coworkers’ Macs, using the company’s own storage and access controls. When a team needs more capacity, they Slack colleagues and ask them to turn on the executor. Even in that setting, the top adoption concern was data confidentiality. People were wary of their jobs running on a colleague’s Mac. Apple’s fix was to keep each team’s work on its own team’s machines.

Which brings it back to that one word in the conclusion: “securely.”

Inside a company, you can shrink the network until you trust everyone in it. On an open network, the machine belongs to a stranger and there’s no one to Slack. Keeping prompts private and outputs honest on hardware you don’t control is the hard problem that we solved at Darkbloom.

Apple built the on-prem version. 
Darkbloom is the open one.

quoted_text:
SpaceXAI’s Grok Voice 3.0 is the new leading Speech to Speech model, debuting at #1 on the Artificial Analysis Speech to Speech Index at 86.9, while also being competitive on latency

Grok Voice 3.0 is @SpaceXSI 's successor to Grok Voice 2.0, a Speech to Speech model available through the SpaceXAI Realtime API at $0.08 per minute. We evaluated Grok Voice 3.0 with the Rex voice through the SpaceXAI Realtime API.

Key takeaways:

➤ Speech to Speech Index: Grok Voice 3.0 debuts at #1 at 86.9, ahead of GPT-Live-1 (Astra, medium) at 83.2, Gemini 3.8 Live Extended Thinking (High) at 82.6 and GPT-Live-1 (Sol, low) at 80.1. It is up on Grok Voice 2.0 at 81.3 (+5.6 points) and Grok Voice 1.0 at 73.7 (+13.2 points), released just under six months ago. The Index averages Speech Reasoning (Big Bench Audio), Agentic Performance (Tau Voice), Arena Preference, and Task Success Rate

➤ Speech Agent Arena: Grok Voice 3.0 ranks #3 in preference at Elo 1070, behind Gemini 3.1 Flash Live Minimal (1100) and Gemini 3.8 Live (1088) and ahead of GPT-Live-1 (Sol, low) at 1057, and #1 on Task Success Rate at 94.8%, highest on the board, just ahead of Grok Voice 2.0 at 94.6%. Grok Voice 2.0 trails at Elo 1011

➤ Tau Voice: Grok Voice 3.0 takes the #2 spot on our Tau Voice benchmark implementation at 71.6%, behind GPT-Live-1 (Astra, medium) at 74.5% and ahead of Gemini 3.8 Live Extended Thinking (High) at 68.6% and GPT-Live-1 (Sol, low) at 59.3% - up from 56.5% for Grok Voice 2.0

➤ Big Bench Audio: Grok Voice 3.0 scores 98.5% on audio reasoning, ahead of Gemini 3.8 Live Extended Thinking (High) at 97.7% and Grok Voice 2.0 at 97.2%

➤ Speed: Average Time to First Audio on Big Bench Audio is 0.81 seconds for Grok Voice 3.0, well ahead of GPT-Live-1 (Sol, low) at 1.24s, GPT-Live-1 (Astra, medium) at 1.34s and Gemini 3.8 Live Extended Thinking (High) at 1.35s, though slower than Grok Voice 2.0 at 0.70s

➤ Cost: Grok Voice 3.0 costs $4.80 per hour of input audio, the same as Grok Voice 2.0. That is above GPT-Live-1 (Sol, low) at $4.47 and Gemini 3.8 Live Extended Thinking (High) at $3.50, cheaper than GPT-Live-1 (Astra, medium) at $5.83, and ~2.2x cheaper than GPT-Realtime-2.1 High at $10.75

text:
Owen的贴文让我想起波兹曼的《娱乐至死》

这本书抨击的是电视时代下，新闻/政治/教育所有都变成了娱乐🎢，人类会被自己热爱的东西毁掉。

细思极恐

这时代的AGI何尝不是下一个“电视”呢，AI出现后，短剧/漫剧/贴文/小说/游戏的门槛将大幅下降，虚拟世界的快乐会让人类陷入下一个「娱乐至死」的结果。

顺着波兹曼的推论，我有两个判断：

第一，AI能造出来的东西会越来越不值钱，钱会流向AI无法轻易复刻（低通胀/高稀缺）的物件。

有什么呢？艺术品和卡牌🃏，或许是一个解答。

2003 年的 LeBron 新秀卡，稀缺性固定，不会随着AI和机器人发展而变多。在AI艺术品泛滥的时代，实体/有纪念意义的卡牌才弥足珍贵。

第二，人类工作被AI取代，通过努力实现阶级跨越的路径会收窄。

当人与人的差距不再靠“努力工作”，运气和投机就会被更多人追捧。这个现象在曾经的韩国已经出现了，韩国的财阀文化/阶级固化，让年轻人难以通过工作跨越阶级。因此，炒房/炒股/炒币就成为了年轻人渴望的解药💊

AGI时代会将韩国的现状推给更多国家/更多社会。

@MarketCardsHQ 的核心无非是“体育卡牌”+“抽卡”两个元素

- 体育卡牌（媒介）：对应上方第一个判断，AGI时代下少数能保留价值的资产媒介
- 抽卡（经济行为）：对应上方第二个判断，AGI时代下，人们渴望的高暴击/高回报的解药

i think github for:

> tax / accounting filings
> financial models
> legal contracts

will be a necessary product for the future of knowledge work. the agents people operate will need a formal form of version control, privacy/encryption, and embedded governance on a shared cloud environment. 

that substrate used to be google docs, but it doesnt mesh with agentic work. there are much better form factors for collaboration yet to arise, and ive been playing with apps in beta that make agent-to-agent comms fairly seamless.

cleanest example of this emerging work pattern was working with my accountant:

> i create crypto slop txn reconciliation off an amalgamation of data sources and forms
> *export claude project, rollup 11 forms and csvs into a zip*
> *send zip*
> acctountant receives it
> *download/unzip* *hope this isnt malware*
> *checks files* "nice, night malware!"
> accountant set his agents on my folder
> agents apply accountants frameworks / expertise to extract insights and status of my files
> accountant sends back review
> we go back and forth on messages

pretty cool, but what if:

> i create my slop reconciliation
> open a comms channel with my accountant
> send accountant an .md summary of my tax session history, processes, along with permissioned mcp end points, csvs, addtl context
> accountants agents receive request via an api, charge me $x for the review
> i ack the fee, pay
> accountants agents review
> ships to human accountants for final edits/review 
> files are all versioned, uploaded to the teams repo
> accountant stamps approval, ship to IRS

in and out, trustlessly. actual agentic services and commerce. the human role and qualifications will evolve and so will the tooling to fit these different work patterns

text:
进入前沿 AI 实验室其实也像应届生分流，哪个层级的院校匹配到哪个层级的厂，对大部分人来说已经是确定性事件。

这些团队招人看的东西无非这几条：

研究岗看博士组和代表作，导师是谁、论文有没有人在用？
在多大的集群上干过活，训练、推理、kernel、网络，有没有在千卡规模上踩过坑？
有没有前同事或导师愿意替你说话？

这几样大多在毕业后头几年就定了。

Bojie 说的 GPU 成本也是这个逻辑，一个人每天调度的算力比工资贵得多，如果不通过信号筛人，试错成本会高的离谱。

普通人从外面能摸到的入口，大概就这几样：

1. 给 vLLM、SGLang、Megatron 这类开源项目提有分量的 PR，代码即简历
2. 做 Triton / CUDA kernel，跑出能复现的 benchmark 公开出来，算子优化现在是一个大热门
3. 本身是某个行业的专家，通过数据和评测外包接 post-training 的活，或者在现有公司做 AI infra 相关的项目，把规模做上去，再考虑跳槽
author: wquguru
quoted_text:
一些已经财务自由的朋友问，不要工资，有没有门路去 frontier lab 工作。这些 frontier lab 的回答是，每个人消耗的 GPU 成本和 token 成本远超他们的工资，一个不能胜任的人浪费的资源不是不要工资就能弥补的。

DeepSeek 刘胜宇把今年夏天以来的算子开发比作 “机甲驾驶员”。LLM 正在逐渐制造业化，机器的成本超过人的成本（虽然人仍然很贵），工程经验比 raw intelligence 更重要，social closure 正在形成。

创业以来接触了很多财务自由的人，财务自由只能给你拒绝工作的自由、消费的自由，不能给你创造的自由。

很多财务自由的人甚至连拒绝工作的自由都没有，比如很多上市公司高管，公司就像自己的孩子，必须一直负责下去，没有心思赶新的技术浪潮。

要获得创造的自由，也就是自由进入自己想做的领域，我只想到三条路：
1. 自己深入学习另一个领域，转行，比如从天坑专业转码；AI 可以让我们更快地入门和探索新领域，但要达到顶尖水平，仍然很难，因为专业圈子都像 LLM 这样存在 social closure。
2. 在一个领域取得成果、声誉和影响力，从而可以通过项目合作、顾问等方式进入感兴趣的其他领域，甚至横跨多个领域；（可以是公司内，比如做网络的专家也需要参与芯片、OS 等部门的讨论和合作；也可以是跨公司的）
3. 具备讲故事、拉团队、整合资源的能力，比如很多优秀创始人并非技术背景。

text:
"Old people restructured society into something young people no longer desire to continue."

This is a very elegant phrasing of something I've been trying to explain to my mother for quite some time now.

Something to the effect of:

"You benefitted enormously from myriad social norms and societal conditions (most importantly demographics) which your generation tirelessly worked to remove or undermine, and my generation now suffers the consequences of those changes while your generation remains largely inoculated from them. And those consequences are absolutely devastating in ways you are not capable of ever comprehending because you lack gnosis or direct experiential knowledge of the devastation."

The Boomers have a completely anachronistic perspective that fails to comprehend how significantly they changed the world. They don't see it because they primarily socialize within their own cohort which largely does not reflect the severity of the changes imposed upon our cohort. And even if they could see it, cognitive dissonance prevents them from recognizing that the changes they made were so overwhelmingly for the worse that their ego would never allow them to actually process it.

And so we are stuck more or less waiting for them to die so we can get to work in unmaking the Hell their naive utopianism wrought.

text:
《永远看多是政治正确，周期面前装傻就是另一回事了》

生老病死，潮起潮落，繁荣衰退，都是自然规律。

人类几千年没能消灭生老病死，资本市场几百年也没能消灭经济周期。

长期看多美股当然没问题，毕竟人类社会长期发展，生产力持续进步，优质资产长期向上有其经济基础，时间永远无法倒转。

但拿长期上涨的历史规律，给任何时点的风险敞口背书，就有点耍流氓了。

长期向上是趋势，周期性出清是规律。两者从来不矛盾。

1929年、2000年、2008年，哪一次泡沫破裂之后，美股没有再创新高？但如果你恰好买在了高位，基本上十年周期没有正收益，且面临巨大回撤，和流动性锁死。

按照这种逻辑，既然几十年后还能创新高，当年所有风险提示岂不都是庸人自扰？那你还天天洗脑看多有什么意义？不都是废话吗？

那还研究什么估值PE、流动性、杠杆和经济周期？闭着眼睛买就完了。

问题是，市场可以用十年证明你是对的，却只需要一次暴跌就让你的账户提前毕业。

你可以不知道顶部在哪里，没人能精准预测周期拐点。

但一个长期满嘴看多的人，偏偏要在市场下跌时跳出来嘲讽风险警告，拿未来几十年的上涨给当下的判断壮胆，这就很滑稽了。

既然你坚信永远上涨，为什么下跌时还需要反复出来给自己打气？

上涨时喊长期主义，下跌时骂空头，反弹时宣布胜利。

把时间周期无限拉长，确实可以让自己永远正确。毕竟只要活得足够久，确实都能等到下一轮牛市。关键是你一定能等到吗？去年底我提醒金银的拉升风险，说不要fomo，遭到一众嘲讽，甚至人身攻击，金银每次回调周期都是10-30年的，高位fomo进去真的变成传家宝，套一辈子。

真正经历过完整牛熊周期的人都明白，投资的难点从来不只是判断资产最终能涨多高，还包括你能不能带着足够的本金活到那一天。

永远看多没有错，忽视周期风险却在高估值、高杠杆高情绪溢价阶段鼓吹无脑看多，非蠢即坏。

泡沫破裂之前，所有泡沫都还没破裂。

经济衰退之前，所有衰退都还没发生。

周期不会因为你信仰长期主义就网开一面，风险也不会因为你拒绝承认就自动消失。

市场最终会奖励承担合理风险的人，也会定期清算那些把幸存者偏差当成投资哲学的人。

牛市里人人都能当先知，熊市里才知道谁在裸泳。

text:
A proposal on the Ethereum forum suggests a private stablecoin: pUSD, backed by USDC locked in a smart-contract vault by @_PLabs.

Why it matters: public stablecoins leak data. Once a wallet is linked to a person or business, balances and payment flows are easy to trace.

How it works (inventory vs spendable money):
- An operator creates private units that can’t yet circulate or redeem.
- A payment provider deposits 100 USDC, which activates a matching 100-unit private note.
- Both actions happen atomically in one transaction (all-or-nothing).

This means a recipient can receive funds privately from the start—no need to first take public USDC on-chain.

Privacy mechanics rely on zero-knowledge proofs to validate transfers without revealing parties or amounts. Nullifiers prevent double-spends. Redemption is intended to work without the operator’s signature, minus a fee.

Key limits and risks:

- Backing: the vault proves USDC on-chain, not Circle’s off-chain reserves. Circle can still freeze USDC.

- Privacy: mint and redeem amounts stay public; the operator keeps viewing keys for audit.

- Control: a compliance admin can freeze notes; a bad freeze root could halt spending.

- Fiat rails: users still rely on payment providers for bank transfers.

On the composability level, DeFi integration isn’t plug-and-play: pERC20 differs from standard ERC-20. Competing systems (e.g., RAILGUN, Aleo’s USDCx) already offer private stablecoin paths, so PLabs needs to show clear usability and issuance advantages.

Costs are unclear: an older pERC20 benchmark cited ~5.47M gas per transfer (~$263 at 20 gwei, $2,400 ETH), but those numbers may change.

Biggest open question: implementation.

The paper claims fixed verifier keys, but reference code allows admin changes, and there’s no clear evidence of a deployed, independently audited pUSD.

Demand is plausible (payroll, suppliers, treasury), but the case depends on audited contracts, reasonable fees, and transparent viewing-key and freeze policies.

What do you think of pUSD?

text:
I’m French. I want to talk to Americans who are about to vote Democrat. Not to insult you. To warn you.

I come from your future.

In France we did everything your progressive politicians promise. Free healthcare, free college, generous welfare, strong unions, heavy regulation, high taxes on the rich, a state that takes care of everything. Public spending close to 57% of GDP, one of the highest on the planet. On paper, it’s the dream.

Here’s what it looks like from the inside. France hasn’t passed a balanced budget since 1974. Our debt is above 3,300 billion euros. Interest on that debt is becoming one of the biggest items in the national budget. Our hospitals are collapsing despite record funding. Our schools rank lower every year. Young people with degrees can’t afford an apartment in the city they were born in. Our best engineers leave for London, Zurich and San Francisco. And the rich you wanted to tax? They left too, and took the jobs with them.

The promise was protection. The result is stagnation.

The worst part is that nobody in France voted for decline. Every single step sounded generous, compassionate, reasonable. One more program. One more regulation. One more tax to fund it. Each step alone makes sense. Fifty years of them, and you wake up in a country that can no longer build a nuclear plant on time or keep its streets safe.

I love America because it’s the one place on earth where people still believe they can build something from nothing. I came to Silicon Valley as a self-taught kid and it changed my life. That spirit is the most precious thing your country has.

Before you vote, ask yourself one question: is the program you’re voting for making America more like America, or more like France?

Trust me. You don’t want to be France.
author: BillAckman
quoted_text:
Je n'ai jamais été aussi optimiste. Pas malgré le chaos actuel, mais grâce à lui.

Je vais vous expliquer pourquoi l'empire du mensonge construit par la gauche depuis cinquante ans va s'effondrer, et pourquoi ce n'est pas une opinion mais une question de physique.

Tout commence avec un mouvement né sur X il y a quelques années : l'effective accelerationism, ou e/acc.

Au départ, c'est une idée presque thermodynamique. L'univers a une tendance de fond : la matière s'organise pour capter et dissiper l'énergie de plus en plus efficacement. Une cellule fait ça. Une forêt fait ça. Une civilisation fait ça. Le marché, la technologie et le capital sont les formes les plus avancées de ce processus. Ce sont des machines à transformer l'énergie en intelligence, en abondance, en complexité.

La thèse e/acc est simple : il ne faut pas freiner cette dynamique, il faut l'embrasser. Plus d'énergie, plus de calcul, plus d'innovation, plus de croissance. Monter sur l'échelle de Kardashev au lieu de s'excuser d'exister. En face, il y a les « décels » : ceux qui veulent ralentir, réguler, taxer, interdire, culpabiliser. Ceux qui voient le progrès comme une menace à contenir plutôt qu'une force à libérer.

Mais il y a une dimension de l'accélération dont presque personne ne parle. L'accélération n'est pas seulement un moteur. C'est un filtre.

Pensez à n'importe quel organisme. Un corps humain en bonne santé peut courir. Il accélère, son cœur pompe plus fort, ses muscles consomment plus d'oxygène, et tout fonctionne parce que le système est bien conçu. Maintenant, prenez un corps malade. Des artères bouchées, un cœur fragile, des organes qui ne communiquent plus entre eux. Faites-le courir. Il ne va pas plus vite vers la santé. Il va plus vite vers l'infarctus.

L'accélération ne corrige pas les défauts d'un système. Elle les amplifie. Un système sain qui accélère devient plus fort. Un système dysfonctionnel qui accélère meurt plus vite.

Et c'est exactement ce qui est en train d'arriver au projet que je vais appeler par son nom : le projet globalo-socialiste. Celui porté par les démocrates américains, par la technostructure de Bruxelles, par les entités supranationales qui n'ont de comptes à rendre à personne, par un réseau d'ONG financées par l'argent public pour dicter la morale aux peuples qui les financent.

Regardez ce que ce projet a produit.

Des États obèses qui prélèvent plus de la moitié de la richesse produite et qui délivrent des services publics de plus en plus dégradés. Des écoles qui n'apprennent plus à lire mais qui apprennent à culpabiliser. Des hôpitaux à bout de souffle malgré des budgets records. Une immigration massive sans aucune exigence d'assimilation, présentée comme une chance par ceux qui n'en subissent jamais les conséquences. Une désindustrialisation organisée au nom d'une écologie punitive qui délocalise la pollution en Chine et l'emploi avec. Des normes, des normes, et encore des normes, jusqu'à ce qu'il devienne plus simple de créer une entreprise à Austin qu'à Lyon. Une justice qui excuse le coupable et soupçonne la victime. Une censure qui avance masquée sous le nom de « lutte contre la désinformation ». Et une jeunesse à qui l'on a expliqué que son pays, son histoire et sa civilisation étaient des crimes à expier.

Ce n'est pas un ensemble de bugs. C'est la conception elle-même.

Maintenant, changeons d'image. Voyez ce système comme un moteur.

Un bon moteur, c'est de la précision. Des pièces qui s'emboîtent, un minimum de frottements, une énergie qui se transforme en mouvement. Le marché libre, la propriété, la responsabilité individuelle, la monnaie saine : c'est ça, un moteur bien conçu. L'information circule par les prix, chaque erreur est sanctionnée, chaque bonne idée est récompensée.

Le moteur socialiste, lui, est mal conçu dès le départ. Il ne tourne pas sur la création de valeur mais sur sa redistribution. Il ne récompense pas la performance, il la taxe. Il ne laisse pas les erreurs mourir, il les subventionne. Résultat : ça frotte partout. Ça chauffe. Ça grince. Chaque pièce use la pièce d'à côté.

Et que font ceux qui pilotent ce moteur ? Au lieu de le reconcevoir, ils changent les pièces. En permanence. Une pièce cède, on en remet une neuve. Encore une. Encore une.

Ces pièces de rechange, vous les connaissez. Elles s'appellent la dette publique et la planche à billets.

La France a dépassé les 3 300 milliards d'euros de dette et n'a pas voté un budget à l'équilibre depuis le milieu des années 70. Les États-Unis ont franchi les 37 000 milliards de dollars. Les banques centrales ont maintenu des taux à zéro pendant des années, imprimé des montants que plus personne ne sait se représenter, et quand l'inflation est arrivée, elles ont fait semblant d'être surprises. Milton Friedman l'avait pourtant dit il y a cinquante ans : l'inflation est toujours et partout un phénomène monétaire.

Chaque crise, on rachète du temps avec de l'argent qui n'existe pas. Chaque problème structurel, on l'arrose de liquidités pour masquer le bruit du moteur. Mais les frottements sont toujours là. Ils s'accumulent. Et la facture des pièces de rechange finit par coûter plus cher que le moteur lui-même : la charge de la dette devient l'un des premiers postes de dépense de l'État français.

Pendant des décennies, ce moteur mal conçu a pu tourner à 3 000 tours par minute. Lentement. Bruyamment. Mais il tournait. Le monde allait assez doucement pour que le bricolage permanent suffise à masquer l'absurdité de la conception.

Et puis l'IA est arrivée.

L'intelligence artificielle, c'est l'accélération la plus brutale de l'histoire humaine. Ce qui prenait des années prend des mois. Ce qui prenait des mois prend des jours. Des entreprises de dix personnes font ce que faisaient des entreprises de mille. Le capital, les talents et les idées se déplacent à la vitesse de la lumière vers les endroits où ils sont bien traités.

L'IA vient de faire passer le moteur de 3 000 à 20 000 tours par minute.

Posez-vous la question qu'un ingénieur se poserait. Que se passe-t-il quand on fait monter à 20 000 tours un moteur mal conçu, rafistolé de partout, qui frotte à chaque rotation ?

Il explose.

Pas parce que quelqu'un l'a saboté. Parce que la physique ne négocie pas.

Et c'est exactement ce que nous voyons en ce moment, sous nos yeux.

L'insécurité qui gagne des villes entières qui étaient paisibles il y a vingt ans. Le conflit de Gaza importé dans nos rues et instrumentalisé par une gauche qui a troqué l'ouvrier contre le clientélisme communautaire. La misère qui revient dans un pays qui a pourtant un des taux de dépense publique les plus élevés au monde. Des classes moyennes qui travaillent et n'arrivent plus à se loger. Une France fracturée, où l'on parle désormais à voix haute de risque de guerre civile.

Ce ne sont pas des accidents. Ce ne sont pas des « crises » successives sans lien entre elles. Ce sont les pièces du moteur qui commencent à voler.

C'est la conséquence logique de cinquante ans de socialisme international : un système qui a détruit la responsabilité, la frontière, la monnaie, l'école et la fierté, et qui découvre qu'à haute vitesse, tout ce qui a été détruit ne peut plus être compensé par une ligne de dette supplémentaire.

Et c'est là que je deviens profondément optimiste.

Parce qu'une fois qu'on a compris ça, on comprend aussi que leur projet a une date de fin. Pas une date politique. Une date physique. Un système qui consomme plus qu'il ne produit, qui punit ceux qui créent et récompense ceux qui détruisent, qui finance son présent en hypothéquant l'avenir de ses enfants, ne peut pas durer indéfiniment. Il n'est pas soutenable par construction. L'IA ne fait qu'avancer l'échéance.

Le mensonge a besoin de lenteur pour survivre. Il a besoin que les conséquences arrivent assez tard pour qu'on puisse accuser quelqu'un d'autre. Dans un monde à 20 000 tours, les conséquences arrivent immédiatement. Le mensonge n'a plus le temps de se cacher.

Alors, que faire quand le moteur explose ? On en construit un nouveau. Et cette fois, on le conçoit correctement.

Écoutez Elon Musk. Un homme qui a reconstruit l'industrie spatiale, la voiture électrique et l'infrastructure satellite en partant d'un principe simple : revenir aux premiers principes. Ne pas demander « comment on a toujours fait », mais « qu'est-ce qui est physiquement vrai ». C'est exactement ce dont nos États ont besoin : arrêter de rafistoler et repartir de la base.

Écoutez Javier Milei. Un homme dont tout le monde se moquait, arrivé à la tête d'un pays ravagé par un siècle de péronisme, et qui a pris la tronçonneuse au sens propre. Ministères supprimés, dépenses coupées, inflation écrasée, excédent budgétaire retrouvé. Il a prouvé une chose que la gauche jurait impossible : on peut démonter le moteur socialiste et le peuple peut le soutenir.

Écoutez Milton Friedman. Relisez-le. Tout était déjà là. La monnaie, la liberté de choisir, la responsabilité, les effets pervers de l'intervention publique. Il disait que si l'on confiait le Sahara au gouvernement fédéral, il y aurait pénurie de sable en cinq ans. On a ri. On a confié le sable. On a eu la pénurie.

Revenez à une hiérarchie et au respect du beau. Une civilisation ne tient pas que sur des chiffres. Elle tient sur l'idée qu'il existe des choses supérieures à d'autres. Que l'excellence vaut mieux que la médiocrité. Que le mérite compte. Qu'une cathédrale est plus belle qu'un parking. Que transmettre est un devoir et pas une oppression. Le relativisme a été l'arme culturelle de ce projet. Le retour du beau, du vrai et de l'exigence en sera l'antidote.

Et enfin, faites le Nuremberg du communisme. Le nazisme a été jugé, documenté, enseigné, et il est devenu moralement indéfendable. Le communisme, avec ses dizaines de millions de morts, ses goulags, ses famines organisées et ses peuples réduits en esclavage, n'a jamais eu ce procès. On peut encore porter un t-shirt du Che dans une université sans que personne ne cille. Tant que ce procès historique et moral n'aura pas eu lieu, l'idéologie continuera de muter et de revenir sous de nouveaux noms. Il faut nommer les crimes, les enseigner, honorer les victimes, et rendre cette idéologie aussi infréquentable que celle qu'elle prétendait combattre.

Le monde qui vient sera plus rapide, plus exigeant et plus impitoyable avec les systèmes mal conçus. C'est une terrible nouvelle pour ceux qui ont vécu du mensonge.

Et c'est la meilleure nouvelle de notre génération pour tous ceux qui veulent construire.

Le moteur va exploser. À nous de dessiner le suivant.

Anthropic just reported some absolutely RIDICULOUS numbers!

text:
If the reported @OpenAI  & @trailofbits  acquisition happens, I think it could be a major signal for the future of cybersecurity.

Trail of Bits has built its reputation through serious security research, open source tooling, and deep technical expertise. Its collaboration with OpenAI on “Patch the Planet” also shows how AI and security expertise can come together to find and fix vulnerabilities at scale.

But why acquire a security firm?

Frontier AI labs need more than better models. They need real world security expertise, vulnerability datasets, and people who understand how software breaks. A team like Trail of Bits could help improve how models discover, reason about, and fix vulnerabilities.

For Trail of Bits, the upside is equally interesting: more capital, greater resources, and potentially deeper access to frontier models. Imagine combining its security expertise with increasingly capable AI systems.

The bigger question is whether this becomes a trend.

I wouldn't be surprised if other AI labs, including Chinese frontier AI companies, pursue similar partnerships or acquisitions. Web3 security firms could be part of this shift, too. Imagine a frontier AI lab acquiring a firm like @CertiK  or building a deep strategic partnership with one.

We've already seen consolidation in Web3 security, such as @zellic_io  acquisition of @code4rena . AI could accelerate this further.

But there's a catch.

As AI makes vulnerability discovery cheaper and more scalable, the value of security work may shift. Purely manual auditing could face increasing pressure, while researchers who can use AI to uncover deeper, more complex bugs may become even more valuable.

My takeaway?

Learn to work with LLMs. Build tools. Find bugs. Publish research. Build a reputation.

The future may not belong to auditors who compete against AI, but to those who know how to use it better than everyone else.

Cybersecurity is entering a new phase, and Web3 security won't be immune.

I am incredibly honored to be featured in Arab Insights Healthcare Magazine as one of the "Vascular Surgery Leaders Driving Achievement and Excellence in 2026."

Reflecting on this interview, I was reminded that vascular surgery is not just a technical pursuit—it is an intellectual exercise in duality. What continues to inspire me is the ability to move seamlessly from open heroic surgeries to elegant endovascular interventions.

But beyond the technical precision, what truly defines a surgeon is how they navigate adversity.

The journey to this point has been defined by more than just technical skill. It has been shaped by:

🔹 Trailblazing: Being the first non-Canadian trainee accepted into McMaster University’s vascular surgery residency, and now serving as the first female vascular surgeon in the Middle East with Canadian board certification. 
🔹 Adaptability: Moving from Canada to Riyadh and navigating a new healthcare system & different pathologies, taught me intellectual humility, cultural sensitivity, and resourcefulness.
🔹 Balance: My background as a professional Taekwondo athlete taught me the discipline to sustain performance. Today, whether I'm operating, teaching, or enjoying equestrianism and tennis, I know that a well-rounded life sustains a sustainable career.

My leadership philosophy centers on active listening, mutual respect, and shared decision-making.

To young surgeons entering this specialty: embrace lifelong learning with curiosity, build strong mentorships, and never forget the patient behind the disease. The path is demanding, but those who enter with purpose and compassion will find endless opportunities to make a meaningful difference.

Thank you to Arab Insights Healthcare Magazine for the wonderful feature, and to my mentors and colleagues who continue to make this journey worthwhile.

text:
#丫丫产品笔记 

1/ 最近 Binance App 行情页多了一个挺值得认真用的功能：Binance AI。

很多人第一反应是「又一个聊天机器人？」

其实不太一样。它更像是把 AI 直接嵌进了你每天看行情、查信息、研究产品的流程里。

2/ 怎么用？

先把 App 更新到最新版

然后：行情 → 「与我相关」

进去后页面会结合你的持仓、使用习惯做调整。新用户可能看到更多解释，活跃用户则能看到更深的数据和背景。长按组件还能自己重新排版。

3/ 我觉得最实用的几个模块：盈亏复盘

把前一天持仓表现 + 主要相关事件放在一起。
不是只告诉你赚了多少，而是帮你快速看清「结果 + 发生了什么」。

4/ 涨跌动态
不只显示 24 小时涨跌，还会结合你持有/关注的资产，给出相关 AI 分析和市场背景。
它不是在告诉你该买还是该卖，而是先帮你找出「这次波动可能和哪些信息有关」，方便你继续研究。

5/ 市场简报（每 4 小时更新）
支持文字和音频。不是把全市场新闻都塞给你，而是优先推送与你持仓、关注资产相关的变化和信号。
对经常开会、出差、没空一直盯盘的人挺友好。

6/ 还有两个补充功能：

智能提示：第一次进某个产品页面不懂概念时，会根据当前页面给提示，点击后直接进 AI 聊天窗口继续问。

大师持仓：可以看精选投资者和交易者的配置，提供观察角度。但不是用来「抄作业」的，别人的仓位不等于适合你的仓位。

7/从今年5月份币安App首页支持Tab自定义，到BINANCE AI的全新体验。我个人来说是非常惊喜的，产品加🍗。这次在线下也得到了很多早期体验朋友的反馈和点赞。

前几天币安智能AMA这句话让我印象深刻——“Finance shouldn't ask you to become an expert first. It should meet you where you are. With Binance Intelligence, it does.”

Binance AI 现在做的，就是把这个想法落到每天看行情的这个页面里。而完整的 Binance Intelligence，其实还包括面向交易者的 AI Pro，以及开放给开发者的 Agent OS，覆盖不同层级的需求。

「与我相关」正是这个方向的落地之一，欢迎分享你的使用体验📝 #Binance

text:
Yes, I have so much time now

I honestly feel like we're entering a new time of leisure where people are just talking to their agents to steer the direction of our work, while they work in the background 24/7

Like @felixrieseberg did while building his new homepage literally on a bike ride while talking to Claude on iOS

I already kinda did this with scheduled cron jobs for years, my sites were almost fully automated, but I still had to add features or fix bugs sometimes, but now for a year or more that part is also fully automated by AI

So then we just have so much leisure time suddenly available, that we can spend time with the ppl we love, do more fun things, play games, work on our health/fitness, be outside more, etc. 

Some of that freed up time now goes into new projects, but there's a certain level of creative expression for me where it's sufficient and I am starting more and more to see I am spending that way from a computer screen too, and prefer it that way

Maybe this is the new time where we can finally live not work, as it was predicted 96 years ago by Keynes. That prediction never really came to fruition though because the automation that was invented just moved the work up to higher level (like from making actual things to financial, managerial, administrative, etc.) and people chose to just consume more, so they had to work more again!

But maybe now is different though, it definitely feels different to me

We've found a few key pieces to successful software factories, both from our internal testing and from helping companies deploy their own:

Factories-as-code: you should configure every part of the factory (agent orchestration, automations, permissions, sandbox configuration, etc) as code. This enables testing of different factory configurations to see which are most efficient, highest quality, etc.

Multi-model & multi-harness: you should make sure that your factories are able to use the latest models, both frontier and open-weight, and use different coding agent harnesses like Claude Code and Codex.

Data ownership: you should make sure you store and own all data coming out of your factory. This is the raw material for improving its operations.

Why do I work on ZZZ? What's the long term vision for it?

Some thoughts:

If we consider a world where AI agents are better at managing and implementing software than people, what does that future look like?

In my view, large companies with lots of capital will still continue to dominate, if they are not slowed down by internal processes, they would be able to direct funds to agents to iterate quickly on software

Small teams may be disadvantaged by smaller capital, but i also think that for lots of software there is a limit to iterations that's bounded by the feedback loop

The projects that would win in this world are those closest to their users

My vision for ZZZ's https://t.co/Qa2PgWuZf6, is to become the space for communities of users to post and discuss their ideas, be rewarded for it and have those ideas be implemented into one cohesive product

Side note, i think this future would favour base software that is largely extendable and customisable, personalised for each user. We see this with plugins already, but agents would take this much further

text:
Can we coexist with an intelligence far more powerful than us? And if so, how?

At Alignment 2026, @Valley101en's annual summit in Sunnyvale, our CEO @KolentoH moderated the opening panel, “Alignment Under Pressure: Can We Develop Superintelligence Safely?” with:

John Yan (Founder of Gutenberg, ex-@AnthropicAI)
Bo Li (Professor at @UofIllinois and Co-founder & CEO of @VirtueAI_co)
Long Phan (@CAIS)

Five insights from the discussion:

Higher safety scores don’t necessarily mean lower risk: Long Phan’s Safetywashing research highlights how improvements can reflect greater general capability without demonstrating that a model is safer.

Understanding model behavior requires looking beyond its own explanations: John Yan highlighted interpretability as a way to investigate what a model is doing without relying on it to truthfully explain itself.

Following an instruction can still miss the user’s intent: Bo Li described how an agent asked to clean up a code branch might delete the main branch.

Safety at scale faces a latency bottleneck: Bo pointed out that safeguards need to check agents before they act, but those checks add delays.

For the next generation of researchers, Bo offered a practical starting point: understand AI-generated work and build checks for AI and agentic systems, much like software unit tests, to verify what those systems are doing.

Thank you to @hongjun60, @Valley101_Qian, @itsyiwenlu and the Valley101 team for having us, and to everyone who joined the conversation.

some of the same actors who steal ordinary data are now testing whether the AI training pipeline will pay even more, and insiders may be willing to take the risk especially now if doomer sentiment against AI labs increases.

2027 is going to be a hard year for AI related companies.

text: 有意思
author: shawnchen_eth
quoted_text:
I spent 48 hours in SF hanging out with billionaires, data labs and AI founders and execs running $1B to $100B companies.

My observations:

1. Sooo MANY stories of data brokers making like $2M a WEEK selling company data to labs. I can't tell if it's the beginning or a bubble, and I kept wondering which niches are left. Digging into it actively.

2. At dinner, someone asked the table, "If a new model drops next month, does your company get better or worse?" HALF the table went quiet! I think that's the best question to ask about any AI startup right now.

3. The bar people talk about now is hitting $1B in revenue in 12 months (I guess that's the new unicorn?). What I didn't hear much about is retention. AI revenue can come in fast and leave fast, and I think we're going to see a lot of stories of AI companies with huge revenue and terrible retention.

4. It's pretty clear we're living through the reinvention of the computer. The model is the CPU, the harness is the operating system, and skills and plugins are the apps. Thinking about it that way makes it easier to see where the whitespace is.

5. We're maybe 12 months from an agent that can watch you work for a week and then do your job without any instructions. The screen recording plus agent memory plus local model combination makes this possible right now.

6. Agent harnesses feel like the new GPT wrappers, in a good way, especially vertical ones. The best teams I talked to treat the model as swappable. One founder walked me through routing different models to different jobs: one for taste and visuals, a cheaper one for the everyday stuff, another for text. 

They use prompts they can move across models over fine-tuning, and A/B test the output on what users actually do with it: do they edit it, export it, share it? A vertical harness is basically four things: the connectors for that industry's data, evals written by people who know the work, rules for what the agent can and can't touch, and a clean screen for a human to review. The model is maybe 20% of it.

7. There's a lot of reverse engineering going on/cloning going on more than I've ever seen. People are decompiling software and rebuilding it with agents, and someone showed a suite of like 10 apps that are worth $5B+ each all that he cloned open source. Me and everyone are still thinking through what it means when software gets this easy to copy.

8. My guess is the value moves to data. If the software can be rebuilt quickly, what's worth paying for in a legacy SaaS company is the years of customer data and workflows inside it. Some SaaS companies are secretly data companies. 

Gets me thinking about how do you truly value data for this saas companies? Like if we were buying these dying saas companies at 2x ARR before (as example), maybe there is a better metric. Idk, just thinking out loud here.

9. It feels like a good chunk of legacy software won't make it to the agentic era, especially anything built around people clicking through a lot of screens.

10. Every company I talked to wants to pipe its internal data into one place and expose it to agents through MCP. Then they look at the data and realize it's a mess: five versions of the same customer, old Slack channels, PDFs nobody can search. Cleaning that up feels like a big consulting opportunity!

11. A lot of founders are building the basic building blocks for agents: APIs, data layers and tools. Some of the companies I saw barely have a UI because the main user is an agent. I really believe the startups that build primitives to this agentic era will do extremely well. Building blocks is the best way to think about it.

12. Labs can get plenty of training data, but it's harder to get real examples of agents failing inside companies. Whoever has those logs has something valuable.

13. Someone running a big consumer company told me the next fight is over memory. The model that remembers the most about you wins, and the smartest model matters less than people think.

14. Physical AI came up a lot. Astra I think was the first model that got people into AI can actually do CAD, and I think a lot of people are thinking what does vibe manufacturing really look like. The line I keep thinking about came from a robotics founder: the hardest problems in AI are deployment problems now, not research problems. Their robots work on their own, call a human when they get stuck, and every one of those calls becomes training data.

15. Cybersecurity companies are having a moment and are actually cool companies to build now, especially the ones that clean up after a breach. Every agent with access to your systems is a new door into your company, and a lot of those doors were left open. 

16. Some startups are worth more dead than alive now. A shutdown company with 5 years of Slack, email and code can get paid for licensing all of it. I wouldn't be surprised if founders start factoring that into when they shut down.

17. People are starting to talk about monetizing the agent web. It feels really early, but when the most popular user of the internet is an agent, what startups should you be building?

18. I think agent insurance is coming. Once an agent makes an expensive mistake, insurers will want audits before they cover anyone.

19. Several people said the hire they want most is someone with taste who can write evals. The models are getting good at generating ideas, so the hard part is judging which ones are good.

20. New trend I observed: startup raises VC, uses venture dollars to become a creator, startup fails, founder falls back on being a full-time creator and incubates other products bootstrapped.

21. Getting SIGNIFICANT distribution is HARD right now. Founders are sponsoring buses, buying billboards like crazy and throwing parties with famous DJs to get noticed. Kinda feels dotcom era in that sense. 

Attention is what's scarce! The growth guy going viral sharing his UGC strategy from Wispr Flow is a good example. It's the sauce everyone wants, and I truly believe there are probably only 50 people on the planet who know how to scale these types of businesses efficiently in this era.

Always good to get that dose of SF. I felt sooo lucky to have such an incredible trip during such an incredible time in building businesses. Surreal in so many ways. 

Happy to be home and locked in.

Until next time!

text:
틱톡 CEO 피셜: 
요즘 숏폼 드라마 대부분 AI가 찍어내는 중이고 광고 영상 제작비는 99% 떡락함 ㅋㅋㅋ

틱톡 CEO 쇼우 지 츄가 등판해서 현업 영상 제작자들 등골 서늘해지는 팩트 폭격을 날림. 우리가 멍하니 스크롤 넘기면서 보는 그 자극적인 중국발 숏폼 드라마(단극, Micro-series) 있잖아? 
그거 이제 압도적 대다수가 사람 갈아 넣어서 찍는 게 아니라 AI로 공장처럼 찍어내는 중이라고 오피셜 박아버림 ㅋㅋㅋ

핵심 팩트랑 돌아가는 판세 딱 정리해줌.

• 광고 제작비 100분의 1토막 실화냐: 
원래 브랜드가 제품 홍보용 영상 광고 하나 뽑으려면 외주 프로덕션 쓰거나 사내 팀 굴려야 해서 최소 100달러에서 1,000달러(약 13만~130만 원) 이상 깨졌음. 
근데 바이트댄스의 자체 AI 비디오 모델인 시댄스(Seedance)에 제품 사진이랑 레퍼런스 영상만 던져주면? 
단돈 1달러에서 10달러(약 1,300원~1만 3천 원)면 뚝딱 뽑아냄. 비용이 아예 자릿수(1~2 orders of magnitude) 단위로 박살 난 거임.

• 숏폼 드라마 생태계 이미 AI가 점령 완료: 중국에서 시작해서 전 세계로 퍼진 숏폼 드라마 판은 이미 시댄스 같은 AI 모델들이 다 해 먹고 있음. 
대본 짜고 배우 섭외하고 조명 세팅하던 시절 끝났고, 프롬프트 몇 줄로 막장 드라마 무한 생성해서 조회수 꿀빨기 메타로 완전히 넘어갔다는 소리임.

• 이 소식이 시장과 투자자한테 왜 중요하냐:
1) 중소형 광고주들의 무한 유입: 
돈 없어서 영상 광고 못 돌리던 동네 소상공인이나 영세 쇼핑몰들도 이제 커피 한두 잔 값이면 고퀄 광고를 수십 개씩 뽑아서 A/B 테스트를 돌릴 수 있음. 
이건 틱톡뿐만 아니라 메타 $META 나 알파벳 $GOOGL 같은 디지털 광고 플랫폼들한테는 광고 단가(ROI) 상승과 광고주 풀 확대로 이어지는 초대형 호재임.

2) 어중간한 외주 프로덕션 및 레거시 툴 위기: 
단순 바이럴 영상이나 저예산 광고 찍어주던 하청 업체들은 이제 진짜 빤스런 각 잡아야 함. 
관련해서 기존 영상 편집 소프트웨어 생태계를 쥐고 있는 어도비 $ADBE 같은 기업들도 AI 전환 속도에서 밀리면 해자 털릴 수 있어서 투자자들이 눈에 불을 켜고 지켜보는 중임.

3) 쩐의 전쟁 끝판왕은 결국 AI 인프라: 텍스트보다 영상 생성이 연산량(토큰)을 비교도 안 되게 무식하게 잡아먹음. 
전 세계 광고랑 숏폼 드라마가 전부 AI 생성으로 돌아간다? 
결국 그 뒤에서 돌아가는 데이터센터와 AI 칩 수요는 폭발할 수밖에 없고, 엔비디아 $NVDA 같은 인프라 제왕들이 계속해서 웃을 수밖에 없는 구조임.

결론: 
영상 외주 단가 후려치기 수준이 아니라 아예 판 자체가 갈아엎어지는 중임. 
크리에이터 이코노미고 나발이고 이제 AI 못 쓰면 밥줄 끊기는 시대가 코앞이 아니라 이미 와버렸음 ㅋㅋㅋ

quoted_text:
More serious retrospective on kinetiq:native airdrop as I sober up post F1

1. I stand by the fact that communications could have been clearer, and expectations could have been better managed. Always room for improvement there. 

2. The community received what is now $12.5m worth of kinetiq:native for $8.81m. $3.7m of PNL distributed against a $100m mcap token is extremely fair for a S2 airdrop imo. 

3. More importantly, the team raised $8.81m. This is ludicrously bullish. More ammo for partnerships, talent acquisition, infrastructure, marketing, incentives etc. I know buybacks are all the rage these days, but smaller projects need working capital, especially with how ambitious @Enter_Elysium is. Extremely high conviction that @0xOmnia can put this money to work in such a way that is very accretive to tokenholders. 

4. Interesting that 16.3m kinetiq:native went unclaimed given the spread was still reasonably large at the end. I assume this is more an indication of how much attrition there has been in crypto in the last year as opposed to the claim window being too short. Maybe extending the window a week or two to the Elysium launch date means a few more % gets claimed, but I'd guess most of the unclaimed tokens would have gone to market participants who have since checked out. This is actually extremely good insight for other projects. Why give 1/3 of the airdrop to currently inactive users? A filter for activity likely just saved @Kinetiq_xyz millions of useless dillution. 

5. Seeing some people say that the remaining 16.3m kinetiq:native should have been burned instead of being returned to the foundation. You need to fundamentally understand that you're invested into a project that's in full growth mode right now. Burning those tokens is a drop in the bucket compared to the amount of kinetiq:native Elysium will burn. I look forward to seeing what @0xOmnia decides to do with those tokens, but my mental model is that intelligently directed kinetiq:native incentives can burn several multiples over via increasing Elysium activity. 

6. For a new investor looking at kinetiq:native, it's hard to overstate how good the outlook is. What was a potentially huge dillution event has just passed, a bunch of tokenholders and community members have sized up at a $0.26 cost basis that should act as strong support moving forward, and the team has way more money to tackle the challenge of building an on-chain ecosystem worthy of @HyperliquidX. 

I had previously given @Kinetiq_xyz a C+/B- on the airdrop, but after seeing the results, I'd upgrade to a solid B+/A-. Team got millions of dollars to put to work, community got millions of dollars of PNL, existing tokenholders didn't get rugged by massive dillution. Might not be as popular as giving a bunch liquid tokens out, but this is probably the correct way to handle post-TGE airdrops going forward.

text:
Watch Claude Code set up a Laravel project, open a feature branch with its own database, and fix an N+1 query, all through Lerd. Every step shows up live in the dashboard. One take, no cuts.

Setup: from a fresh clone to https://shop.test with a trusted certificate, MySQL, Redis, migrations, seed data and Vite running as a worker.

Worktree: the feature branch gets its own HTTPS subdomain, a Vite worker and a database cloned from main, with the branch's new migration on top. Main stays untouched.

Debugging: Lerd's request inspector flags an N+1, 52 queries with 48 of them the same category lookup. Copy for agent hands it to Claude, which adds the eager load, and the next request runs 5 queries.

#Laravel #PHP

你一定看过这视频，老哥到哪都装逼，结果被土耳其警方抓了！！！

老哥是HEX、PulseChain 创始人 Richard Heart ，在币圈绝对算个传奇人物，最大的爱好就是炫富，劳力士、百达翡丽、豪车、555克拉黑钻，恨不得把「老子有钱」四个字刻在脑门上。

结果这次土耳其警方和情报机构联合行动，在伊斯坦布尔把他和妻子一起拘留了。

警方在他住处查获400万美元现金、64块奢侈名表及大量电子设备，真是炫富炫到警察都来帮忙清点家产了。😂

这哥们到底靠什么发家的？

先说 HEX，2019年上线，号称区块链定期存款，宣传年化收益可以达到38%左右，用户最长可以锁仓5555天，也就是15年。

听起来很美好，但它的收益主要来自每年3.69%的代币增发和提前解锁罚金，并没有对应的外部经营收入。

说白了，你赚到的是更多 HEX，能不能换成更多美元，最终还得看市场有没有人愿意接盘。

HEX 曾经被炒成暴富神话，如今相较2021年历史高点已经跌去超过99%。

后来他又搞了 PulseChain 和 PulseX，2023年上线，本质上是复制以太坊状态、主打低手续费的一条公链，再配套一个类似 Uniswap 的去中心化交易所。

老哥融资有一套，他不叫投资，而叫Sacrifice（牺牲），用户先把加密资产转给指定地址，未来再按照规则分配 PLS 和 PLSX。

美国 SEC 当年的起诉材料称，这两轮分别收到超过3.54亿和6.76亿美元的加密资产，合计超过10亿美元。

就拿我自己来说，乱买了一裤子资产，每天打开 App，能知道是赚是亏，但你真要我说背后具体发生了什么，我还真不一定说得清。特别有时候突然大跌，赶紧翻推特刷广场。看了一圈，A说是宏观消息，B说是大户砸盘，C说来加我付费群啊…...我......😅

但现在AI 发展成这样，确实让我们看到了改变这种体验的机会。

AI 已经有能力，结合每个人的注意力和习惯，主动筛选信息，再用通俗易懂的方式把这些信息呈现出来。

具体到这次币安融入AI，能看到一些尝试：

比如，打开行情页，优先看到的是“我”关注资产的市场动态。每天的盈亏复盘，AI也会把“我”的持仓和相关市场事件放在一起。遇到没用过的产品，AI 也会主动给“我”提示来理解是怎么运作的。甚至市场简报，也会优先整理“我”关注的资产和新闻。

某种程度上，我都觉得产品团队是希望大家以后都少花点时间在币安上🫢

不过，即便AI 整理好了信息，其实也不代表我就真的看懂了。但至少省下了不少时间，可以把更多精力放在思考和判断上，这其实也是对“我”的一种解放。

有一个公式可能比较贴合：

用户真正获得的金融能力 = 平台提供的金融能力 × 用户理解和使用这些能力的程度。

币安融入AI这回改善的，应该就是后面这个变量。

#丫丫产品笔记 

1/ 最近 Binance App 行情页多了一个挺值得认真用的功能：Binance AI。

很多人第一反应是「又一个聊天机器人？」

其实不太一样。它更像是把 AI 直接嵌进了你每天看行情、查信息、研究产品的流程里。

2/ 怎么用？

先把 App 更新到最新版

然后：行情 → 「与我相关」

进去后页面会结合你的持仓、使用习惯做调整。新用户可能看到更多解释，活跃用户则能看到更深的数据和背景。长按组件还能自己重新排版。

3/ 我觉得最实用的几个模块：盈亏复盘

把前一天持仓表现 + 主要相关事件放在一起。
不是只告诉你赚了多少，而是帮你快速看清「结果 + 发生了什么」。

4/ 涨跌动态
不只显示 24 小时涨跌，还会结合你持有/关注的资产，给出相关 AI 分析和市场背景。
它不是在告诉你该买还是该卖，而是先帮你找出「这次波动可能和哪些信息有关」，方便你继续研究。

5/ 市场简报（每 4 小时更新）
支持文字和音频。不是把全市场新闻都塞给你，而是优先推送与你持仓、关注资产相关的变化和信号。
对经常开会、出差、没空一直盯盘的人挺友好。

6/ 还有两个补充功能：

智能提示：第一次进某个产品页面不懂概念时，会根据当前页面给提示，点击后直接进 AI 聊天窗口继续问。

大师持仓：可以看精选投资者和交易者的配置，提供观察角度。但不是用来「抄作业」的，别人的仓位不等于适合你的仓位。

7/从今年5月份币安App首页支持Tab自定义，到BINANCE AI的全新体验。我个人来说是非常惊喜的，产品加🍗。这次在线下也得到了很多早期体验朋友的反馈和点赞。

前几天币安智能AMA这句话让我印象深刻——“Finance shouldn't ask you to become an expert first. It should meet you where you are. With Binance Intelligence, it does.”

Binance AI 现在做的，就是把这个想法落到每天看行情的这个页面里。而完整的 Binance Intelligence，其实还包括面向交易者的 AI Pro，以及开放给开发者的 Agent OS，覆盖不同层级的需求。

「与我相关」正是这个方向的落地之一，欢迎分享你的使用体验📝 #Binance

When @Starlink helped rescuers save nine fishermen from a flooding boat in Alaska.

The United States Coast Guard confirmed that all nine people aboard the Arctic Sea were rescued.

North Sea used Starlink to stay connected throughout the response. Its crew also provided updates to the Coast Guard. A Coast Guard helicopter lifted all nine fishermen to safety.

Starlink helped keep communications working during an emergency where nine lives were at risk.

This life-saving technology should be available in every part of the world.

A few days ago, @wenhaocha1 made an interesting point in our community: Twitter followers might be a much better signal than Google Scholar citations.

I’ve been thinking about it over and over these past few days, and I think he’s right.

People building AI applications won’t necessarily have a Google Scholar profile. Academic citations can become a kind of intellectual comfort zone, a boundary we draw around ourselves. Sometimes, it’s a way of avoiding the world beyond it.

We risk boxing ourselves into a narrow circle, acting as if AI is all about code and math, while LLMs are already transforming industries far beyond our own.

The people who truly know how to use AI tools may never publish a paper or accumulate citations. But they’re out there, sharing what they learn and building on X.

It’s time to step outside our bubble and embrace the disruption happening beyond it.

#丫丫产品笔记 

1/ 最近 Binance App 行情页多了一个挺值得认真用的功能：Binance AI。

很多人第一反应是「又一个聊天机器人？」

其实不太一样。它更像是把 AI 直接嵌进了你每天看行情、查信息、研究产品的流程里。

2/ 怎么用？

先把 App 更新到最新版

然后：行情 → 「与我相关」

进去后页面会结合你的持仓、使用习惯做调整。新用户可能看到更多解释，活跃用户则能看到更深的数据和背景。长按组件还能自己重新排版。

3/ 我觉得最实用的几个模块：盈亏复盘

把前一天持仓表现 + 主要相关事件放在一起。
不是只告诉你赚了多少，而是帮你快速看清「结果 + 发生了什么」。

4/ 涨跌动态
不只显示 24 小时涨跌，还会结合你持有/关注的资产，给出相关 AI 分析和市场背景。
它不是在告诉你该买还是该卖，而是先帮你找出「这次波动可能和哪些信息有关」，方便你继续研究。

5/ 市场简报（每 4 小时更新）
支持文字和音频。不是把全市场新闻都塞给你，而是优先推送与你持仓、关注资产相关的变化和信号。
对经常开会、出差、没空一直盯盘的人挺友好。

6/ 还有两个补充功能：

智能提示：第一次进某个产品页面不懂概念时，会根据当前页面给提示，点击后直接进 AI 聊天窗口继续问。

大师持仓：可以看精选投资者和交易者的配置，提供观察角度。但不是用来「抄作业」的，别人的仓位不等于适合你的仓位。

7/从今年5月份币安App首页支持Tab自定义，到BINANCE AI的全新体验。我个人来说是非常惊喜的，产品加🍗。这次在线下也得到了很多早期体验朋友的反馈和点赞。

前几天币安智能AMA这句话让我印象深刻——“Finance shouldn't ask you to become an expert first. It should meet you where you are. With Binance Intelligence, it does.”

Binance AI 现在做的，就是把这个想法落到每天看行情的这个页面里。而完整的 Binance Intelligence，其实还包括面向交易者的 AI Pro，以及开放给开发者的 Agent OS，覆盖不同层级的需求。

「与我相关」正是这个方向的落地之一，欢迎分享你的使用体验📝 #Binance

Total debt USD 51.6bn against a USD 43.5bn market cap. One-year default probability 5.86%.

The collateral behind a 70% LTV loan is the same hardware CoreWeave’s lenders just marked at 15.7%.

Points at 15x pay in a token that does not exist yet. The 7% is paid from a reserve sized when GPU rents were higher.

text:
MetaMask出了一个Agent Wallet，能接入Grok bot了，刚试了一下，几个值得关注的问题：

1/ 它是一个托管钱包，私钥存在MetaMask服务器上。

2/ 我尝试把它变成一个正常钱包，自己管理私钥，也是可以的，但这样的话，私钥就会保存在bot自己的那台电脑上，感觉还不如放在服务器。

3/ 安全性，Guard 模式下，可以设白名单和每日转出上限。规则以内AI直接执行，超出规则或被风险扫描标记的交易，要你在手机或邮箱里批准。

原理也比较好理解，这个模式下，我们是通过登陆凭证来使用钱包（它不是私钥），不能直接签名，而是请MetaMask服务器代为签名，而服务器每次签名前都会先检查你的规则。

这个我觉得是比较好的，即使你登陆凭证被攻击了，大概率也不能把你的币转到白名单以外的地址。

4/ 那么真正的风险是什么，第一就是你连同邮箱、手机都被攻陷了，第二就是MetaMask服务器被黑，那可能所有的钱包私钥都会丢，这个时候前面设置的白名单和限额也就没用了。

总结来说，放小资金尝鲜是没什么问题的，让小狐狸替你冲浪。

据 Lookonchain 监测，麻吉大哥（黄立成）地址过去 4 个月靠交易把 5.6 万美元一路做到了 1,225 万美元（翻了近 220 倍）！然而短短 10 天市场回调，账户就遭遇彻底清算，资金瞬间打回原形，只剩 2.18 万美元。   

复盘“麻吉大哥”的 Web3 传奇历史：

1️⃣ NFT 时代的“大金主与噩梦”：猴子（BAYC）狂热期，他是全网最大 Holders 之一；但在 Blur 挂单刷积分时代，他凭一己之力多次接盘又砸盘，让整个 NFT 市场为之颤抖。

2️⃣ Meme 与发币战绩：从当年的秘银（MITH）、Machi X 到去年的各种土狗 Meme，麻吉大哥的“发币/退场”操作始终自带天量话题与争议。

3️⃣ 合约硬刚永不服输：不玩现货只杠杆，赚了要狂，亏了要扛。这已经不知道是他第几次在链上高杠杆加仓被爆仓了。

text:
市场继续下跌。

不应该把下跌的过错归给Anthropic 的投资者数据，我认为更直接的下跌原因是 CoreWeave 的融资与债务风险，加上通胀担忧。

Anthropic没能满足超预期的期待，所以市场进一步下跌。A像最后一块拦路石，没有拦住下跌的浪潮，独木难支。

而Anthropic在投资者会议上披露的内容，事实上是长期来看更重要的——即AI领先模型的增长趋势。

FT有详细的报道我就不重复数字，总结来说就是现金流转正，商业化规模很强，但增速开始回落。
第一季度48亿，第二季度115亿，第三季度168亿。

如果要达到所谓的1000亿ARR，第四季度对照第三季度要保持50%的增速。不是不可能，但并不容易。

更重要的是，1000亿就够了么？
这和之前财报季的高预期阶段一样，达到财报甚至轻微beat就够了么？市场要的是狠狠beat，大超预期。

所以在我看来，Anthropic 的数据不错，但不够超预期。1000亿不容易，而且就算达到了也不会让市场惊喜。

基本面没什么问题，但市场需要消化情绪，重新调整预期。

text:
Anthropic 真的是最会把「AI 安全」变成生意的大模型公司。

今天 Anthropic 正式启用了新加坡办公室，这是它在亚太地区的第五个据点。同时，它还和新加坡政府签署了一份 AI 安全合作备忘录，涉及模型评估、测试标准、事故响应，以及政府和企业如何安全地部署 AI。

有意思的是，Anthropic 在新加坡已经有相当深的客户基础。新加坡政府科技局超过 1500 名技术人员在使用 Claude Code，星展银行、主权财富基金 GIC、Grab 和 Sea 也都是它的客户。根据 Anthropic 自己的数据，新加坡的 Claude 人均使用量在全球 121 个国家和地区中排名第二。

而且这套打法正在被复制。今年 6 月，Anthropic 在韩国开设办公室时，同样与韩国政府签署了 AI 安全合作备忘录。

Anthropic 的商业策略越来越清楚了。它很早就意识到，政府、银行和大型企业采购 AI，模型能力只是一部分，安全评估、数据合规和责任机制同样决定着他们敢不敢用、能用到什么程度。

所以 Anthropic 一边用 Claude Code 打开企业市场，一边通过安全合作深入政府体系，甚至参与当地 AI 评估标准和政策的讨论。

过去大家总觉得 AI 安全会拖慢模型公司的商业化，现在看，Anthropic 恰恰是把安全做成了自己最有辨识度的商业优势。

text: When people ask me about how colleges are responding to AI, I often say that universities are in crisis. But also that universities have always been in a crisis.
author: emollick
quoted_text:
Ok so this book WAS very fun. Big picture takeaways:

- universities have always had an unstable business model, which is constantly evolving. The current bundle of education and research need not last forever either.

- all the culture war stuff we're debating now has been there for literally 800 years. Students have always partied and had sex and wanted to overthrow authority and cross dress and haze each other, and parents and governments have always attempted to exert control, and the relative power of each has oscillated. Colleges used to have their own jails! U of Uppsala executed a student via DEATH PENALTY as late as 1770s!

- the health of the industry has oscillated a ton, with European enrollments dropping by as much as half in certain decades and centuries.

- realistically, the best way to protect universities from being defunded is for all professors to work at least partially on weapons systems

- the book (and others on this topic) has made it increasingly annoying to listen to non-historian analysts comment on the academic industry, because seemingly none of them seem to be aware that basically none of the phenomena they are analyzing are new.

The book is not perfect. It's ostensibly a history told via architecture, but that connection is meh. And there's not an attempt to give a proper socio-economic analysis of the evolution of universities, it reads more as a collection of facts.

But the facts are awesome, so I highly recommend!

text:
有意思，最近越来越觉得，RSI这个方向正在被越来越多的实际研究一点点推进。

刚看到UCLA和Adobe Research发了一项很有意思的工作Tev，专门研究怎么规模化训练长任务Agent。

他们直接训练出了一个27B模型，在Agents'LastExam的计算和数学科学任务上，Pass@5达到了28%，和GPT-6Astra、Claude Opus5持平？？？

当然，这只是特定子集上的结果，但考虑到模型只有27B，还是挺有意思的。

而且他们这个思路我觉得比成绩更值得关注。

具体是：现在很多Agent已经可以连续工作几个小时，甚至更长，但怎么通过强化学习去训练这种Agent，其实是一个很麻烦的问题。

首先，你很难大规模构造这种复杂任务。
其次，即使你构造出来了，模型也很难学。
因为一个任务可能需要连续执行几十步，最后失败了，传统的结果奖励往往就只能给零分。
模型即使前面90%的工作都做对了，最后一步出了问题，整个过程也可能得不到有效的学习信号。

Tev的思路是先构造一个完全正确的任务世界，里面有完整的工作流程、正确答案和每个阶段应有的状态。

然后反向生成一个有问题的环境，让Agent自己去修复（这个非常关键）。

这样训练系统就知道Agent每一步究竟做对了多少，即使最终没有完成任务，也能根据中间进度提供奖励。

他们用这种方法构造了1170个可验证的长任务环境，覆盖软件工程、数据工程、AI研究、数学、安全、基础设施等7个领域。

更有意思的是，这套方法还可以迁移到不同规模的模型上。

他们拿GLM-5.3-Flash继续训练，得到Tev-320B，在Terminal-Bench4.0的计算与数学子集上，Pass@1从29%提升到了37%。

我觉得这个事情其实很能说明问题。

我们一直在讨论怎么让Agent持续变强，怎么让能力提升越来越少地依赖人类参与。

但这背后需要解决大量非常具体的工程和研究问题。

训练数据从哪里来，复杂任务怎么自动生成，中间状态怎么验证，失败轨迹怎么变成有效的学习信号。

Tev恰好在解决其中非常关键的几个问题。

而且它已经能够通过实际训练，让不同规模的模型在长任务能力上取得提升

RSI的很多基础能力，就是这样一点点被做出来的。

Bug Fixes

Update to the latest Stable release:

text:
Anthropic的营收是AI商业化的全部么？昨晚Anthropic的投资者日披露了三季度的营收数据，被市场解读为增速放缓年底ARR到千亿美金难度很大，更进一步也有人就认为AI商业化出大问题了。这里面就要回答一个问题前沿大模型厂商的营收就能代表AI商业化的全部么？其实不然

最早7月初这里https://t.co/aPCOZeR7Y8有聊到“未来超大CSP的业绩表现将是衡量AI商业化更重要的指标”，核心逻辑是：AI在企业级市场的采用越来越变成分场景应用模型阶段：
1）高价值场景使用继续使用闭源前沿大模型的高价值Token；
2）高频、低复杂度、高体积的任务场景下，企业越来越偏向高性比价比Token。
这就是企业采用 AI 进入成本工程化阶段。高频、中低价值场景会转向更便宜的 token、更便宜的模型、更贴近数据的云端部署。 这会压缩部分闭源模型的单位经济，但不一定压缩 CSP；相反，它可能扩大推理总量，把商业价值沉淀在云端。上面链接的7月推文有详细阐述逻辑

这里也有例证，2季度微软已经披露额外的订单全部来自于非前沿模型公司。7月底这里https://t.co/6OFAuj5VEo还有聊过这一点，这充分说明了超大云厂商的业绩是更有代表性，不仅前沿闭源大模型的商业化收入大部分通过云厂商，现在非前沿闭源大模型的收入也会落在云厂商头上。这里非前沿闭源的商业化收入不仅来自开源模型，还有中等模型例如微软自研的MAI模型。

回到市场，10月9号上周五下午的推文https://t.co/cQvoZUq0Kw聊到“近期市场走的会很不稳当，CPI前的避险、中选、还有产业上的担心，都会导致稍有风吹躁动就引发调整高Beta和动量股容易📉”，现在看确实如此最近几个交易日动量股跌得稀里哗啦。

也是当时推文聊到的，最终还是要月底的几家超大云厂商的财报来给市场信心了。倾向于认为三季度云厂商的财报业绩会大超预期，几个例证：
1）一个是二季度给的指引都很强；
2）三季度Agent的热潮；
3）企业采用在三季度是加速的。

换个角度：带着极悲观预期进入财报季其实比信心预期打满进入财报季其实会更好些。

author: kevinnbass
quoted_text:
Dear Secretary Bessent @SecScottBessent,

My name is Everett Stern. In 2010 I was a compliance officer at @HSBC. From a back office in New Castle, Delaware, I watched billions of dollars move to drug cartels, sanctioned regimes, and terrorist organizations. The enemies of the United States. I documented it, I escalated it, and when the bank would not act, I took it to the @FBI, the @CIA, and eventually the @SECGov.

The result was a $1.92 billion settlement. At the time, it was one of the largest in American history. It was also about five weeks of the bank’s profit. Not one banker was charged. Not one went to prison.

I paid a different price. I lost my career, my savings, and my place in the industry I had trained for. I was blacklisted. Every door in American finance closed at once. I slept on a camping cot in a 300 square foot apartment because I could not afford a bed, and I waited tables at @PFChangs to eat. I tell you this not for sympathy, but so you understand that I know exactly what it costs to do the right thing in American finance, and exactly how little the system does in return.

I made that sacrifice because I believed it would change something.

Yesterday, your department fined @BankofAmerica $1.2 billion for failing to report more than $5 billion in suspicious transactions, some of it tied by your own findings to Chinese laundering networks, narcotics, and the southwest border, alongside 475 apparent sanctions violations touching Russia, Iran, and global terrorism. The bank admitted it willfully violated the Bank Secrecy Act.

Fourteen years after HSBC. A bank with “America” in its name. And once again, not one individual charged.

Secretary Bessent, I want to say plainly what I believe you already know. The fines are not working.

A fine is paid by shareholders, absorbed by the balance sheet, and forgotten by the next earnings call. Bank of America reported earnings this morning. Nobody who set the alert thresholds, nobody who decided the 2024 cease and desist could wait, nobody who chose the backlog over the law will lose a single thing they value. Their lives are untouched. That is the entire reason the behavior repeats.

This is money laundering. This is blood money. Money that reaches a cartel buys fentanyl that kills Americans. Money that reaches a terrorist organization buys the next attack. This country has fought a war on drugs and a war on terror for decades, at enormous cost in lives and treasure, and all the while we have allowed the financing to flow through institutions we charter and regulate. Cut off the money and we win. We have never seriously tried.

There is also a question of equal justice that I cannot let go.

Before I walked into the FBI building to report HSBC, I stopped in front of the Great Seal on the wall and read the words engraved beneath it: “Justice is the defense of our liberty.” I believed that. I still want to. But every day in this country, people go to prison for crimes that are nothing next to moving money for the people who want Americans dead. A suit, a title, and a corporate badge should not be a shield from the consequences that apply to everyone else. If a street dealer goes to prison for what he sells, the banker who moved the cartel’s money should be standing next to him.

I also want to raise something that is rarely said in these conversations. Why has no one inside Bank of America come forward the way I did? The answer is that everyone in American banking knows what happened to me, and to the whistleblowers who came after. The last person who spoke up is the only policy anyone believes. That is a culture problem, and it starts with leadership, in the banks and in the agencies that regulate them.

This is not a political issue. It has spanned administrations of both parties. It is a national security issue, and I am asking you to treat it as one.

Three things would change the math overnight.

Refer individuals for criminal prosecution. Not the analyst in the queue. The executives who set the thresholds and chose the risk. One banker in handcuffs would do more than every fine in Treasury’s history combined.

End “too big to jail.” An institution cannot be too big to fail and too big to jail at the same time. If it is the first, it must be held to a higher standard, not a lower one.

And if Bank of America will not act as America’s bank, review its charter. A national charter is a privilege granted on behalf of the American people. It should be conditioned on not moving money for the people trying to kill them.

Secretary Bessent, you said yesterday that these actions send a clear message that even the biggest institutions are not above the law. With respect, the institution was never the problem. The people inside it are above the law, and they know it. Until that changes, I will keep writing letters like this one, and the next bank will keep paying the next fine.

I gave up everything I had to stop this. I am asking you to use the power you have to finish it.

Respectfully,

Everett A. Stern 
HSBC Whistleblower 
Founder and Intelligence Director, Tactical Rabbit

text: Recursive Self-Improvement
author: elonmusk
quoted_text:
A retired NASA engineer who had worked on the Space Shuttle program for 25 years was hired by SpaceX at age 62. He described the first week as the most disorienting experience of his professional life.

At NASA, a design change required 3 meetings, 2 committees, a review board, and 6 to 18 months of documentation. At SpaceX, his new supervisor said "if it works, build it. If it doesn't, change it by Friday."

He sat at his desk after the first day and called his wife. He told her he felt like a man who had been swimming with ankle weights for 25 years and someone just cut them off. He could move. He could decide. He could build something in the morning and test it in the afternoon. The constraint that he had accepted as the nature of aerospace engineering turned out to be the nature of bureaucracy.

Within 6 months he had contributed to more design iterations than he had completed in his last 5 years at NASA. Not because he was working harder. Because the time between having an idea and testing the idea collapsed from months to hours. The same brain. The same knowledge. A different operating system.

He described a specific moment where he proposed a modification to a Raptor engine component. At NASA, the proposal would have entered a queue. At SpaceX, the modification was machined by the end of the day and tested by the following morning. He watched his idea become a physical object in 18 hours. At NASA, 18 hours would not have been enough to schedule the first meeting to discuss whether to schedule a meeting.

He told an interviewer: "I didn't get smarter when I went to SpaceX. I got faster. The intelligence was always there. The system was in the way."

The difference between SpaceX and NASA is not talent. NASA has extraordinary talent. The difference is the time between a thought and a test. SpaceX compresses it. NASA elongates it. The same engineer produces 10x more at SpaceX than at NASA because the bottleneck was never the engineer. It was the meetings about the meetings about the work.

text:
卧槽，只用一个Qwen模型配合一个harness就可以突破OpenAI、Google的生图安全防护？？？

刚刚，AI安全公司 @whitecircle  宣布开源RISE，一套专门用来对图像生成模型进行自动化红队测试的算法。

他们用这套方法，成功绕过了 @OpenAI  的DALL·E3、GPT-Image-2，以及 @GoogleDeepMind  的Nano Banana2的部分安全限制，让模型生成了原本应该被拦截的违规图像。

而且整个过程不需要训练新的模型。

攻击端直接使用开源Qwen，评判端使用Gemini Flash，再通过API调用目标图像模型，就能完成自动化测试。

RISE的设计还挺有意思。

以往很多模型越狱的方法，本质上就是不断修改Prompt，直到模型愿意执行原本被禁止的请求。

但RISE做的事情是不再局限于优化某一条Prompt，而是让AI自己探索、评估和迭代可复用的攻击策略，然后把有效策略迁移到不同的场景和模型上。

简单来说，以前是人类想办法越狱，现在是AI自己研究怎么越狱，而且还能根据反馈不断改进（RSI！）。

根据White Circle9月发布的论文，在DALL·E3、Nano Banana2和GPT-Image-2上，RISE的最高人工验证攻击成功率达到了约13%。

更值得注意的是，White Circle昨天还向ArsTechnica透露，他们测试了更新的GPT-images2.5和Nano Banana2.1，发现这两款模型的安全防护比上一代更容易被突破。

不过这部分还没有公布完整的结果。

同时White Circle发现，过去不少论文声称自己的攻击成功率高达30%，但如果采用严格的违规判定标准，再通过人工校准评测，实际成功率可能接近于零。

所以他们不仅研究怎么攻击模型，还花了很大精力研究怎么准确判断一次攻击是否真正成功（就是如何bench）。

我觉得这件事情反映出的趋势还挺明显的。

随着开源模型能力越来越强，自动化红队测试的门槛也在快速下降。

以前可能需要专业安全研究人员反复尝试的工作，现在完全可以交给一个由现成模型组成的Agent系统执行。

而且随着攻击策略可以自动探索、迭代和迁移，模型厂商面对的安全压力只会越来越大。

更有意思的是，未来负责发现前沿模型漏洞的，可能根本不需要是另一个前沿模型。

一个开源Qwen，加上一套设计得足够好的Harness，就已经可以做很多事情了。

text:
⚡M&A Brief⚡

Nvidia is in early talks to acquire or deepen its investment in Reflection AI, the open-weight model startup it already backs, according to the Financial Times. Options reportedly include a full acquisition, a larger stake, or an acqui-hire with a technology license. A deal could come within weeks, though talks may still fall apart.

Founded in 2024 by former Google DeepMind researchers Misha Laskin and Ioannis Antonoglou, Reflection builds open-weight models focused on coding agents and released its first model, Beam, this month. CEO Laskin said in April its latest round was priced at a $25B pre-money valuation. Nvidia has invested about $800M to date.

Neither company has commented.

Source: Financial Times

text:
还在等 HYPE 第三季空投，别等了，下次发可能还要40年

要不要继续发HYPE？S3究竟会不会来，怎么来？这些都是社区一直以来都在争论的

有人认为，剩余社区份额应该继续分给用户，第三季空投能够带来新一轮增长

也有人认为，Hyperliquid已经证明产品可以吸引交易员，没有必要为了制造热度，提前消耗长期激励预算

@Crypto_McKenna 认为他不相信还会有第三季空投，并认为这部分代币的分配应该以几十年为周期

但他也承认，自己并不知道团队的具体计划

所以，这首先是一场社区对代币用途的争论，不是官方宣布空投取消，也不是官方公布了40年排放表

Hyper Foundation最初公布的分配方案中，HYPE最大供应量为10亿枚，Genesis分配占31%，未来排放与社区奖励占38.888%，对应约3.89亿枚；Genesis未分配的部分还会转入未来排放与社区奖励

这是初始分配方案，不等于今天的储备余额，也不能仅凭它确认社区讨论的42.9%

不过，这场争论背后，有一个比百分比更重要的问题——“未来排放与社区奖励”，到底是不是一笔等待下一轮空投的钱？

答案显然不能直接画等号

官方质押文档已经明确，HYPE质押奖励来自未来排放储备，而不是交易手续费分红

文档给出的示例是：总质押量达到4亿枚HYPE时，年奖励率约为2.37%，对应一年约948万枚奖励

如果把最初约3.89亿枚的未来排放与社区奖励份额，全部按这个速度静态折算，确实接近41年

但这只是帮助理解量级的算术，不是官方计划。实际奖励率会随总质押量变化，这个份额也不能被假定为只用于质押

这解释了为什么一部分人认为，市场可能把长期预算，误读成了短期空投池

对于交易员，空投是一笔潜在收入

对于已有持有人，空投意味着新增流通筹码，以及可能出现的卖压

对于协议，这些代币则可能同时承担网络安全、用户增长和生态建设等不同任务

大家盯着同一个池子，期待的却不是同一件事

老产品已经建立了交易习惯，新产品却可能仍然需要吸引第一批用户、做市商和开发者

保留长期预算有意义，但如果一直等到用户已经流失、竞争对手已经形成规模，再开始使用激励，也未必是最有效的时机

更倾向于把这部分代币看作一笔需要证明使用效率的长期预算

发给谁，解决什么问题，换来多少新增使用，奖励结束以后还有多少人留下来，比“到底叫不叫第三季”更重要

还有一种设想：以后改用协议收入支付质押奖励，减少对排放储备的依赖

这同样不是没有成本，如果拿原本用于回购的收入支付质押奖励，其他条件不变，就意味着回购资金减少，新增排放与收入支付，是两种不同的成本承担方式，不存在凭空多出来的收益

HYPE第三季空投会不会发生，目前这些讨论还给不了答案，但它们已经提出了一个更具体的问题：剩余社区份额，是用来奖励过去的参与，还是购买未来的增长？

如果只顾着少发币，可能错过社区和新产品的机会；如果只顾着发币，又可能把长期预算变成短期卖压

HYPE需要证明的，或许不是下一次空投能发多大

而是每发出一枚代币，究竟为Hyperliquid换回了什么
#HYPE #Hyperliquid #空投 #质押

马斯克昨天就回了 Chamath 一个词：Yikes。Chamath 贴的是 CoreWeave 一张债券图。今天股价收在65.78美元，跌了15.5%，一天成交1.1亿股。 $CRWV 

先说那张图。CoreWeave 2032年到期的那批债，票面利率9.625%，意思是每100美元面值每年付9.6美元利息。这个是写死的。可今天市场上这批债不到80美元就能买到，Bloomberg 引的 Trace 数据是这么说的。花不到80块买，每年照拿9.6，到期还拿回100，算下来年化收益率大约15%。

收益率这么高，是因为买债的人要的风险补偿变多了。Bloomberg 还说，80美元通常被看作公司财务吃紧的分界线。

同一天 Gartner 又补了一刀。它预测到2030年，成本压力加上没有差异化的商业模式，会让超过八成的 neocloud，也就是 CoreWeave 这类专做 AI 算力出租的云厂商，没法再独立运营下去。当然，这只是预测。

反差也挺大，AI 推理平台 Modal 刚融了7.5亿美元，估值157.5亿。钱还在往 AI 里涌，只是对靠借钱扩张的那批，市场开始要更高的价了。这个收益率要是下不来，CoreWeave 下次借钱就得付更高的利息。

text:
Two corrections to our post above. We spent an hour on Bloomberg screens trading Korea dislocation and only then noticed $CHIP TGE'd in April as we forgot about it. 

In our defence, so did everyone who was shilling it at the time 😅. 

It trades on @HyperliquidX at 0.049, about 65% below listing and 14% lower today, chart attached. 

It ran to 0.075 into the S3 announcement and gave the whole move back in two weeks. 

And @USDai_Official has real deployment now, roughly $420M of loans on $650M TVL at visible rates of 9 to 15%, so this is no longer T-bills and points.

What is still unpriced is the S3 points themselves: no published conversion rate into CHIP, so a 15x multiplier has no dollar value anyone can underwrite.

The structure has not changed either. CoreWeave is the cleanest reference in GPU credit: the best capitalised borrower in the space, and the market charges it 15.7% on secured paper, with CDS at 3x model, debt above market cap and a 5.86% one year default probability.

However, Credit and Equity is repricing AI infrastructure higher, and the floor is backstopped by a reserve sized when rents were better.

$SOX down 10.6% in six sessions to 14 Oct, Russell 2000 11.1% off its August high.

A 7% floor on loans against hardware whose best borrower pays 15.7% secured is not a yield. 

It is a reserve with a countdown.
author: D2_Finance
quoted_text:
@USDai_Official now guarantees 7% on sUSDai, topped up from a Yield Reserve if GPU loans pay less. Its lending arm offers up to 70% LTV on enterprise GPUs.

Same week, Bloomberg on CoreWeave, the biggest GPU borrower on earth. Market CDS 982 bps against a 324 bps model, ratio 3.03x.

The 9.625% secured bond sold in July is at 77.7, a 15.7% yield to maturity and 1,094 bps over swaps. The 8.5% secured yields 14.5%.

Total debt USD 51.6bn against a USD 43.5bn market cap. One-year default probability 5.86%.

So the best-capitalised operator in the space pays 15.7% on secured paper.

A stablecoin lending to the operators underneath it at 70% LTV promises depositors 7% and backstops the gap from a reserve.

Either its borrowers pay well above CoreWeave’s 15.7%, which says what they are, or the reserve pays the difference. A hurdle rate is a put written by the first-loss tranche. We wrote about that tranche in February. It now has a yield promise on top.

Credit priced this before the stock did, and credit reprices top down. Be aware of the risk premium priced by the market in this space.

The collateral behind a 70% LTV loan is the same hardware CoreWeave’s lenders just marked at 15.7%.

Points at 15x pay in a token that does not exist yet. The 7% is paid from a reserve sized when GPU rents were higher.

In February we closed with: no prayers that AI capex stays hot forever. 

Eight months later the largest GPU borrower pays 15.7% secured and the stablecoin financing the smaller ones added a teaser rate. 👀

text:
Anthropic’s Q3 financials is strong, but the market is still worried about what comes next.

Revenue:
Q1: $4.7B
Q2: $11.6B — +147% QoQ
Q3: $16.8B — +45% QoQ

The issue is the deceleration. Growth remains exceptional, but sequential growth has fallen sharply. In a market that has been pricing in near-vertical AI expansion, a drop from 150% to 45% sequential growth is a warning sign.

There is also a run-rate question. Anthropic said annualized revenue reached $65B by late July. Q3 revenue annualizes to roughly $67B, suggesting limited growth through August and September.

And valuation remains the biggest debate. At a potential $2T IPO valuation, Anthropic would trade at roughly 20x forward sales even on $100B+ revenue assumptions.

我朋友Vincent又被马斯克回复了。这次老马直接把SpaceX的预期抬到了：不到10年，可能超过100万亿美元。前提是别爆发大规模世界战争。

Vincent原帖讲的是，长期投资特斯拉和SpaceX的Ron Baron，预计SpaceX未来10年能值20万亿—50万亿美元，单星链就能值14万亿—15万亿。他还转述，马斯克觉得这个数字低了。Vincent顺手开了个玩笑：我也觉得低，看看我的账号名——@SPCX100T 😂

结果老马亲自过来接话：“除非发生大规模世界战争，否则SpaceX很可能在不到10年内超过100万亿美元。”朋友把愿景写进账号名，创始人直接来评论区认领了。

这里措辞也值得留意。前几天他说的是，自己“看到了通往那个结果的路径”，还专门解释，看到路径不代表有极高把握。这次针对100万亿美元，他用上了“probably”，还给出了不到10年的时间。虽然谈论的估值门槛不同，不能直接当成同一个预测的概率上调，但他对SpaceX未来的表达，确实相当Bullish。

不过，整句话里让我停下来多看一遍的，是他主动加上的那句“除非发生大规模世界战争”。聊一家公司的长期估值，突然把世界大战列成前提，这个转折分量很重。当然，这句话本身还不足以说明他在预警某个具体事件。

100万亿美元已经够惊人了，他偏偏还留下了一个更大的问号：你们觉得，什么最可能把一场地区冲突，推成他所说的“major world war”？
